Completed 3 to 5 cycles of induction therapy and reached at least partial response
ECOG performance status of 0 or 1
Willing and able to follow the lifestyle restrictions in the protocol
not_for: Frailty index of 2 or higher on the Myeloma Geriatric Assessment
Known allergy, hypersensitivity, or intolerance to the study treatment or its active agents
Ongoing grade 2 or higher non-hematologic toxicity from induction therapy (except grade 2 bortezomib-related peripheral neuropathy)
Needs continuous supplemental oxygen

NCT05045066.summary_en: This early phase 1 study looks at how common low vitamin D is in Black/African American men with prostate cancer that is localized, locally recurrent, or metastatic, and how low vitamin D affects the immune system. Patients with low vitamin D3 levels take cholecalciferol by mouth once daily for 8 weeks, as long as there is no unacceptable toxicity, and blood samples are collected throughout the study. The record does not state a primary outcome measure; it aims to find out whether vitamin D replacement normalizes immune function.
NCT05045066.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1 temprana examina qué tan común es el nivel bajo de vitamina D en hombres afroamericanos con cáncer de próstata localizado, recurrente localmente o metastásico, y cómo la vitamina D baja afecta el sistema inmunitario. Los pacientes con niveles bajos de vitamina D3 toman colecalciferol por vía oral una vez al día durante 8 semanas, siempre que no haya toxicidad inaceptable, y se recolectan muestras de sangre durante todo el estudio. El registro no indica una medida de resultado principal; el estudio busca saber si la reposición de vitamina D normaliza la función inmunitaria.
who_for: African American males aged 18 or older
Previous localized, locally recurrent, or metastatic prostate cancer
Vitamin D level below 30 ng/ml at registration
not_for: Known hypersensitivity to vitamin D
End-stage renal failure on dialysis
Liver cirrhosis
History of hypercalcemia (high blood calcium)
Taking a vitamin D or multivitamin with more than 400 IU daily in the past month

NCT07807345.summary_en: This Phase 1 study tests STRO-006, an antibody drug conjugate that targets integrin beta-6, alone and with pembrolizumab, in adults with refractory recurrent or metastatic solid tumors. STRO-006 is given by intravenous infusion, and the record does not state how long or how often. The study looks at safety, tolerability, how the drug moves through the body, and early anti-tumor activity.
NCT07807345.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1 evalúa STRO-006, un conjugado anticuerpo-fármaco que se dirige a la integrina beta-6, solo y junto con pembrolizumab, en adultos con tumores sólidos refractarios, recurrentes o metastásicos. STRO-006 se administra por infusión intravenosa; el registro no indica por cuánto tiempo ni con qué frecuencia. El estudio evalúa la seguridad, la tolerabilidad, cómo se distribuye el fármaco en el organismo y la actividad antitumoral temprana.
who_for: Adults 18 or older with refractory recurrent or metastatic solid tumors of the listed types
Life expectancy of at least 3 months
ECOG performance status 0 to 1
Measurable disease per RECIST v1.1
Adequate blood and organ function
not_for: Prior treatment with an ADC that has a TOP1 inhibitor payload
Chemotherapy within 2 weeks or immunotherapy within 3 weeks before first dose
Untreated or active brain metastases or leptomeningeal disease
Active interstitial lung disease, or active or recent pneumonitis within 6 months
Concurrent participation in another therapeutic treatment trial
cancer_types: head and neck squamous cell carcinoma

NCT07619339.summary_en: This study tests tepotinib combined with ivonescimab in non-small cell lung cancer that has MET exon 14 skipping and is advanced or recurrent. Tepotinib is taken by mouth at 225 mg or 450 mg once daily, and ivonescimab is given through an IV every 3 weeks, for up to 24 months of ivonescimab treatment. The study focuses on safety and finding the best tepotinib dose with few or mild side effects; a formal primary outcome is not stated, and it is a Phase 1 pilot study.
NCT07619339.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa tepotinib combinado con ivonescimab en cáncer de pulmón de células no pequeñas con salto del exón 14 de MET que es avanzado o recurrente. El tepotinib se toma por vía oral a 225 mg o 450 mg una vez al día, y el ivonescimab se administra por vena cada 3 semanas, durante hasta 24 meses de tratamiento con ivonescimab. El estudio se enfoca en la seguridad y en encontrar la mejor dosis de tepotinib con pocos efectos secundarios o leves; no se indica un resultado principal formal, y es un estudio piloto de fase 1.
who_for: Pathologically confirmed non-small cell lung cancer.
MET exon 14 skipping confirmed by an FDA-approved assay in a certified lab.
Advanced or recurrent disease with measurable disease by RECIST 1.1.
Age 18 or older with ECOG performance status of 2 or less.
Adequate blood counts, kidney, liver and clotting function as defined by the study.
not_for: Other actionable alterations such as EGFR, ALK, ROS1, RET, KRAS, HER2 or BRAF V600E.
Prior angiogenesis inhibitor therapy, such as bevacizumab or ramucirumab.
Untreated or active brain metastases or leptomeningeal disease, unless specific conditions are met.
Interstitial lung disease requiring steroid treatment, or prior grade 3 or higher immune-related side effect.
Recent serious bleeding, clotting, heart events, or inflammatory bowel disease within the stated time windows.

NCT05215353.summary_en: The study compares music therapy with cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) to see which may reduce anxiety in people who have had cancer. Both treatments are given virtually through Zoom, as seven weekly 60-minute sessions. The record does not state a main outcome; the study is Phase 4.
NCT05215353.summary_es: El estudio compara la terapia con música y la terapia cognitivo-conductual (TCC) para ver cuál puede reducir la ansiedad en personas que han tenido cáncer. Ambos tratamientos se dan de forma virtual por Zoom, en siete sesiones semanales de 60 minutos. El registro no indica un resultado principal; el estudio es de Fase 4.
who_for: Age 18 or older and English- or Spanish-speaking.
Prior cancer diagnosis of any type or stage, and free of cancer or with stable disease without progression.
Score of 8 or higher on the HADS anxiety subscale.
Anxiety symptoms lasting at least one month.
Access to Zoom and a quiet, private location.
not_for: Active cancer treatment completed less than one month before enrollment (maintenance hormonal or targeted therapy allowed).
Active suicidal thoughts, bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, or substance abuse.
Blessed cognitive score of 10 or higher.
Seven or more recent music therapy or CBT sessions for anxiety within six months.
Unable to give their own informed consent.

NCT05231122.summary_en: This Phase 2 randomized trial tests pembrolizumab and bevacizumab with or without the anti-CD40 agent CDX-1140 in recurrent ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer. Patients receive pembrolizumab and bevacizumab through an IV on day 1 of each 3-week cycle, and one group also receives CDX-1140 IV over 90 minutes, with cycles repeating until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. The main outcome measure is not stated in the record; the study is Phase 2.
NCT05231122.summary_es: Este ensayo aleatorizado de fase 2 evalúa pembrolizumab y bevacizumab con o sin el agente anti-CD40 CDX-1140 en cáncer de ovario, de trompa de Falopio o peritoneal primario que ha recidivado. Los pacientes reciben pembrolizumab y bevacizumab por vía intravenosa el día 1 de cada ciclo de 3 semanas, y un grupo también recibe CDX-1140 por vía intravenosa durante 90 minutos; los ciclos se repiten hasta la progresión de la enfermedad o toxicidad inaceptable. El resultado principal no está indicado en el registro; el estudio es de fase 2.
who_for: Age 18 years or older.
Recurrent serous, endometrioid, or clear cell epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer.
Platinum-sensitive or platinum-resistant disease, with no more than 4 prior lines of treatment.
Measurable disease by RECIST 1.1 and ECOG performance status 0 or 1.
BRCA status must be known.
not_for: Primary platinum-refractory disease.
Nonepithelial, borderline, mucinous, or carcinosarcoma tumors.
Progression on prior immune checkpoint blockade therapy.
Prior therapy with any anti-CD40 antibody.
Active autoimmune disease needing systemic treatment in the past 2 years, or active HIV.

NCT05804227.summary_en: This early phase 1 trial tests whether the study drug ulixertinib can cross the blood-brain barrier in people with recurrent MAPK-activated gliomas. Ulixertinib is taken by mouth twice a day; in the surgical group it is taken for two weeks before tumor removal on about day 14, and in the non-surgical group it is taken continuously in 28-day cycles. The main outcome measure is not stated in the record, and the study is listed as early phase 1.
NCT05804227.summary_es: Este ensayo de fase temprana 1 evalúa si el medicamento en estudio, ulixertinib, puede atravesar la barrera hematoencefálica en personas con gliomas activados por MAPK recurrentes. Ulixertinib se toma por vía oral dos veces al día; en el grupo quirúrgico se toma durante dos semanas antes de extirpar el tumor, alrededor del día 14, y en el grupo no quirúrgico se toma de forma continua en ciclos de 28 días. El resultado principal no se indica en el registro, y el estudio figura como fase temprana 1.
who_for: Adults 18 or older for the surgical group; people 12 or older for the non-surgical group
Recurrent MAPK-activated glioma, mixed glioma, or glioneural tumor
Tumor with RAS/RAF/MEK/ERK pathway mutation or activation shown by a report
Progressive disease by RANO criteria, with prior radiation or chemotherapy depending on tumor grade
Karnofsky performance status of 60 or higher and adequate organ function
not_for: Active infection requiring systemic therapy
Bevacizumab treatment within 3 months before enrollment
Currently in another investigational study
Pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning pregnancy during the trial
Retinal vein occlusion or central serous retinopathy, or risk of them

NCT06580002.summary_en: This phase 2a pilot trial tests riluzole against a placebo to see how it affects circulating BDNF levels in people with cancer-related cognitive impairment. The study includes people with many cancer types, including breast cancer, sarcoma, gastric cancer, lung cancer, head and neck cancer, and colorectal cancer. Participants take riluzole 50 mg by mouth twice daily (every 12 hours) for 8 weeks, or a matching placebo capsule on the same schedule. The study measures the effect on circulating BDNF levels, which is the main outcome stated.
NCT06580002.summary_es: Este ensayo piloto de fase 2a compara riluzol con un placebo para observar cómo afecta los niveles circulantes de BDNF en personas con deterioro cognitivo relacionado con el cáncer. El estudio incluye personas con varios tipos de cáncer, entre ellos cáncer de mama, sarcoma, cáncer gástrico, cáncer de pulmón, cáncer de cabeza y cuello, y cáncer colorrectal. Los participantes toman riluzol de 50 mg por vía oral dos veces al día (cada 12 horas) durante 8 semanas, o una cápsula de placebo con el mismo horario. El estudio mide el efecto sobre los niveles circulantes de BDNF, que es el resultado principal indicado.
who_for: Adults 18 or older who feel cognition has worsened since cancer treatment or brain radiation.
Cohort A: breast cancer treatment, or non-breast cancer with anthracycline, platinum, or other anticancer therapy in the past 3 years, and no prior brain radiat
Cohort B: prior radiotherapy or radiosurgery to the brain, with life expectancy over 6 months.
Able to give informed consent and complete questionnaires and computer tests in English, Chinese, Korean, Vietnamese, or Spanish.
not_for: Primary brain tumors or brain metastases (Cohort A), or high grade glioma (Cohort B).
Unwilling to complete the neuropsychological assessments needed for the study.
Pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning to become pregnant during the study.
Suspected hypersensitivity to riluzole, current smoking, cannabis use, or taking listed interacting medicines.
AST or ALT at least 3 times the upper limit of normal, or serious conditions the investigator judges would preclude participation.

NCT05891769.summary_en: This study tests 18F Fluorocholine, a PET isotope bound to choline, in people with suspected parathyroid adenoma whose 99mTc Sestamibi SPECT/CT scan was negative or equivocal. Each participant receives one intravenous dose of 18F Fluorocholine (5 mCi ± 20%), and about 45 to 60 minutes later has a low-dose CT scan and a PET scan from the skull base to mid thighs. The main outcome is not stated in the record; the study phase is Phase 2/Phase 3.
NCT05891769.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa 18F Fluorocholine, un isótopo PET unido a colina, en personas con sospecha de adenoma paratiroideo cuya gammagrafía SPECT/CT con 99mTc Sestamibi fue negativa o dudosa. Cada participante recibe una dosis intravenosa de 18F Fluorocholine (5 mCi ± 20%) y, aproximadamente de 45 a 60 minutos después, una TC de baja dosis y un PET desde la base del cráneo hasta la mitad de los muslos. El resultado principal no se indica en el registro; el estudio es de fase 2/fase 3.
who_for: Suspected parathyroid adenoma with high calcium and normal or high parathyroid hormone.
Negative or equivocal 99mTc Sestamibi SPECT/CT scan.
Able to give written consent.
Karnofsky performance status above 50, or an equivalent ECOG/WHO score.
Total bilirubin and liver enzymes within the stated limits.
not_for: Younger than 18 years at the time of radiotracer dose.
Creatinine clearance below 60 mL/min or serum creatinine above 1.5 times the upper limit of normal.
QTcF above 470 msec on ECG, or congenital long QT syndrome.
Pregnant women, per the radiology department policy.

NCT05417594.summary_en: This study tests AZD9574, a drug taken by mouth, alone and combined with other anti-cancer drugs, in people with advanced solid cancers that have come back or grown. AZD9574 is taken by mouth, temozolomide is taken by mouth, and trastuzumab deruxtecan and datopotamab deruxtecan are given into a vein, and how often and for how long these are given is not stated. This is a Phase 1/Phase 2 study that aims to measure safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics and preliminary efficacy.
NCT05417594.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa AZD9574, un medicamento que se toma por vía oral, solo y combinado con otros medicamentos contra el cáncer, en personas con cánceres sólidos avanzados que han reaparecido o progresado. AZD9574 se toma por vía oral, la temozolomida también se toma por vía oral, y el trastuzumab deruxtecan y el datopotamab deruxtecan se administran por vía intravenosa; la frecuencia y la duración de estos tratamientos no se indican. Es un estudio de Fase 1/Fase 2 que busca medir la seguridad, la tolerabilidad, la farmacocinética, la farmacodinamia y la eficacia preliminar.
who_for: Progressive cancer at enrollment, with ECOG performance status not worse over the previous 2 weeks.
Adequate organ and marrow function.
Certain advanced ovarian, breast, prostate or pancreatic cancers with a predicted loss-of-function change in BRCA1, BRCA2, PALB2, RAD51C or RAD51D.
IDH1/2-mutant glioma that is suitable for temozolomide, progressed after radiation and one prior alkylating chemotherapy.
Some modules require HER2-positive, HER2-low or HER2-ultralow advanced cancer, depending on the cohort.

NCT06185751.summary_en: This Phase 1 study tests WS-CART-CS1, a CAR-T cell therapy that targets CS1 (SLAMF7), in adults with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma. Participants have a leukapheresis procedure, then receive cyclophosphamide and fludarabine by IV on Days -5 to -3, and WS-CART-CS1 is infused on Day 0; hospitalization is 7 days. The study measures safety and preliminary anti-myeloma effects, but the primary outcome measure is not stated in the record.
NCT06185751.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1 evalúa WS-CART-CS1, una terapia con células CAR-T dirigida a CS1 (SLAMF7), en adultos con mieloma múltiple recidivante o refractario. Los participantes se someten a una aféresis de leucocitos y luego reciben ciclofosfamida y fludarabina por vía intravenosa los días -5 a -3, y WS-CART-CS1 se infunde el día 0; la hospitalización dura 7 días. El estudio mide la seguridad y los efectos preliminares contra el mieloma, pero la medida principal de resultado no se indica en el registro.
who_for: Relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma after 3 or more prior lines of therapy.
Prior proteasome inhibitor, anti-CD38 therapy, and anti-BCMA therapy required.
Measurable disease by protein levels, biopsy-proven plasmacytoma, or bone marrow plasma cell criteria.
Age 18 or older with ECOG performance status of 1 or better.
Adequate kidney, liver, lung, and heart function, with LVEF of at least 45%.
not_for: Systemic myeloma therapy within 14 days before planned leukapheresis.
Other cancer history, except treated non-melanoma skin cancer or cancer treated over 2 years earlier with no evidence of disease.
Currently receiving other investigational agents, or cellular therapy within 8 weeks of conditioning.
Prior Grade 3 cytokine release syndrome or ICANS with other CAR-T therapy, including BCMA CAR.
Active hepatitis B or C, HIV, uncontrolled infection, pregnancy, or breastfeeding.

NCT07147231.summary_en: This Phase 1/Phase 2 trial tests pidnarulex (CX-5461) given together with cemiplimab (REGN2810) in refractory microsatellite stable colorectal cancer. In the arm that receives both drugs, cemiplimab is given IV over 30 minutes on days 1 and 15, and pidnarulex is given IV over 60 minutes on days 1 and 8 of each 28-day cycle, for up to 26 cycles. The record does not state a main outcome measure; the study is listed as Phase 1/Phase 2.
NCT07147231.summary_es: Este ensayo de fase 1/fase 2 evalúa pidnarulex (CX-5461) administrado junto con cemiplimab (REGN2810) en cáncer colorrectal estable para microsatélites refractario. En el brazo que recibe ambos medicamentos, cemiplimab se administra por vía intravenosa durante 30 minutos los días 1 y 15, y pidnarulex por vía intravenosa durante 60 minutos los días 1 y 8 de cada ciclo de 28 días, hasta 26 ciclos. El registro no indica una medida de resultado principal; el estudio figura como fase 1/fase 2.
who_for: Colorectal adenocarcinoma that is unresectable or metastatic, with no effective standard treatment left
Measurable disease by RECIST version 1.1
Proficient mismatch repair (pMMR) or not microsatellite-high (non-MSI-H) tumor status
Progressed on or intolerant to fluoropyrimidine, oxaliplatin, irinotecan, bevacizumab, and an EGFR inhibitor
Age 18 or older with ECOG performance status 2 or better
not_for: Prior RNA polymerase inhibitor, G quadruplex stabilizer, or immunotherapy, including PD-1 or PD-L1 inhibitors
Active autoimmune disease needing systemic treatment in the past 2 years
Current use of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or strong CYP3A4 inducers
Currently receiving other investigational agents
Pregnant or breastfeeding women

NCT04598009.summary_en: This Phase II study tests binimetinib together with imatinib in people with unresectable stage III or IV KIT-mutant melanoma. Binimetinib is taken by mouth twice a day and imatinib once a day, on days 1 to 28 of each 28-day cycle. The main outcome measure is not stated; the study is a Phase II trial.
NCT04598009.summary_es: Este estudio de fase II evalúa binimetinib junto con imatinib en personas con melanoma KIT mutado, en estadio III o IV, que no se puede extirpar con cirugía. Binimetinib se toma por vía oral dos veces al día e imatinib una vez al día, en los días 1 a 28 de cada ciclo de 28 días. La medida principal de resultado no se indica; el estudio es de fase II.
who_for: Performance status of 2 or better (ECOG), or Karnofsky 60% or higher.
Confirmed melanoma that is unresectable, stage III or IV, and not suitable for local therapy.
Measurable disease by RECIST v1.1 criteria.
KIT-mutant melanoma confirmed by a CLIA-certified test.
Progressed on prior standard therapy, or unable to tolerate it, per the investigator's opinion.
not_for: Systemic anticancer or antibody therapy within 3-4 weeks, or radiation within 2 weeks, before study start.
Another investigational agent within 14 days or 5 half-lives, whichever is shorter.
Recent heart attack, bypass or stent within 6 months, heart failure, or LVEF below 50%.
Blood clot or stroke within 12 weeks of first dose, with some exceptions.
Pregnancy or breastfeeding, or inability to swallow and keep down study drugs.

NCT06251544.summary_en: This Phase 1 study tests HTR2 T cells, which are T cells engineered to recognize HER2 and that also include a TRAIL-R2-targeting component and IL15, in people with metastatic or locally recurrent unresectable HER2-expressing breast cancer. Arm A is given without lymphodepletion at dose levels of 1.00E+06 or 1.00E+07 cells, and Arm B is given with lymphodepletion at dose levels of 1.00E+07 or 1.00E+08 cells; how often doses are given is not stated. The study aims to find the highest safe dose, how long the cells last in the body, the side effects, and whether the cells can fight and kill HER2-expressing breast cancer cells.
NCT06251544.summary_es: Este estudio de Fase 1 evalúa las células T HTR2, que son células T modificadas para reconocer HER2 y que también incluyen un componente dirigido a TRAIL-R2 y IL15, en personas con cáncer de mama metastásico o recurrente localmente no resecable que expresa HER2. El Brazo A se administra sin linfodepleción en niveles de dosis de 1.00E+06 o 1.00E+07 células, y el Brazo B se administra con linfodepleción en niveles de dosis de 1.00E+07 o 1.00E+08 células; la frecuencia de las dosis no se indica. El estudio busca encontrar la dosis más alta segura, cuánto tiempo permanecen las células en el cuerpo, los efectos secundarios y si las células pueden combatir y destruir las células de cáncer de mama que expresan HER2.
who_for: Age 18 to 80 years with metastatic or locally recurrent unresectable HER2-expressing breast cancer
Disease progressed after standard first-line therapy
HER2 expression 1+, 2+ or 3+ by IHC
Measurable or evaluable disease per RECIST 1.1
ECOG performance status 2 or less
not_for: Pregnant or breastfeeding
Active, uncontrolled bacterial, viral or fungal infection
Systemic corticosteroids above 0.5 mg/kg/day prednisone equivalent
LVEF below 55%
Progressing brain metastases

NCT06697301.summary_en: This study tests EIK1001 with pembrolizumab, compared with placebo with pembrolizumab, as first-line therapy for advanced melanoma. How EIK1001 is given, and how often, is not stated. The main outcome is not stated; this is a Phase 2/3 study.
NCT06697301.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa EIK1001 combinado con pembrolizumab, comparado con placebo más pembrolizumab, como tratamiento de primera línea para melanoma avanzado. El registro no indica cómo se administra EIK1001 ni con qué frecuencia. El registro no indica la medida principal de resultado; es un estudio de fase 2/3.
who_for: Adults 18 or older with stage 3 unresectable or stage 4 metastatic melanoma eligible for pembrolizumab.
Measurable disease on CT or MRI by RECIST 1.1.
ECOG performance status of 0 to 1.
Life expectancy of at least 3 months.
Known BRAF V600 status, or willing to have BRAF V600 testing.
not_for: Melanoma of ocular origin.
Systemic therapy for advanced melanoma before the first study dose, with exceptions for adjuvant or neoadjuvant therapy.
Grade 3 or higher adverse event during prior anti-PD-1 therapy.
Known active brain metastases or carcinomatous meningitis.
Active autoimmune disease needing systemic treatment in the past 2 years, or chronic steroid or immunosuppressive use.

NCT05365581.summary_en: This Phase 1 study tests ASP2138, given alone or with other cancer drugs, in adults with stomach, gastroesophageal junction, or pancreatic cancer whose tumors express CLDN18.2. ASP2138 is given into a vein (intravenous infusion) or under the skin (subcutaneous injection), with doses increased in small groups; how long or how often it is given is not stated. The study measures safety and tolerability and aims to find a suitable dose; a formal main outcome measure is not stated.
NCT05365581.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1 evalúa ASP2138, administrado solo o con otros medicamentos contra el cáncer, en adultos con cáncer de estómago, de la unión gastroesofágica o de páncreas cuyos tumores expresan CLDN18.2. ASP2138 se administra por vena (infusión intravenosa) o debajo de la piel (inyección subcutánea), con dosis que aumentan en grupos pequeños; no se indica cuánto tiempo ni con qué frecuencia se administra. El estudio mide la seguridad y la tolerabilidad y busca encontrar una dosis adecuada; no se indica una medida de resultado principal formal.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older with locally advanced unresectable or metastatic stomach, GEJ, or pancreatic adenocarcinoma
Tumor sample positive for CLDN18.2 by central immunohistochemistry testing
Measurable disease by RECIST 1.1 within 28 days before first dose
ECOG performance status of 0 or 1
Predicted life expectancy of at least 12 weeks
not_for: Need for medicines that suppress the immune system
Blockages or bleeding in the gut
Specific uncontrollable cancers or specific infections
Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH)
New York Heart Association Class III or IV heart condition

NCT07560865.summary_en: The study tests FT536, an allogeneic natural killer (NK) cell immunotherapy, in adults with recurrent WHO Grade 4 astrocytoma. FT536 is injected once into the tumor during a biopsy procedure, at doses of 1 x 10^7, 2 x 10^7, or 6 x 10^7 cells per dose, and maximum safe surgical resection follows between Study Day 8 and 15. The primary outcome is not stated; this is a Phase 1 study that compares tumor samples taken before and after the injection.
NCT07560865.summary_es: El estudio evalúa FT536, una inmunoterapia alogénica con células asesinas naturales (NK), en adultos con astrocitoma recurrente de grado 4 de la OMS. FT536 se inyecta una sola vez dentro del tumor durante un procedimiento de biopsia, en dosis de 1 x 10^7, 2 x 10^7 o 6 x 10^7 células por dosis, y luego se realiza una resección quirúrgica máxima segura entre los días 8 y 15 del estudio. La medida principal de resultado no se indica; es un estudio de fase 1 que compara muestras de tumor tomadas antes y después de la inyección.
who_for: Adults aged 18 to 75 years at consent.
Histologically confirmed WHO Grade 4 astrocytoma with first or second recurrence on MRI.
Gross tumor resection must be feasible as judged by the investigator and neurosurgeon.
Completed standard treatment, including surgery, radiation, and temozolomide with or without tumor treating fields.
Karnofsky performance status of 70 or higher, off dexamethasone or on 2 mg daily or less.
not_for: Need for urgent neurosurgery, high intracranial pressure, or uncontrolled seizures.
History of myelodysplastic syndrome or acute myeloid leukemia.
Radiographic evidence of leptomeningeal disease.
Prior bevacizumab or any other cellular therapy.
Any condition requiring systemic immunosuppressive therapy.

NCT07441681.summary_en: This phase III trial compares radiation with cetuximab to radiation with carboplatin and paclitaxel in adults with locally advanced head and neck squamous cell cancer who cannot receive cisplatin. Intensity-modulated radiation therapy (IMRT) is given 5 days per week for 35 treatments, and cetuximab or carboplatin and paclitaxel is given intravenously on day 1 of each 7-day cycle for up to 7 cycles, if the disease does not progress and side effects are acceptable. The main outcome is not stated; the record lists this as a phase 3 trial.
NCT07441681.summary_es: Este ensayo de fase III compara radioterapia con cetuximab frente a radioterapia con carboplatino y paclitaxel en adultos con cáncer de cabeza y cuello de células escamosas localmente avanzado que no pueden recibir cisplatino. La radioterapia de intensidad modulada (IMRT) se administra 5 días por semana durante 35 tratamientos, y el cetuximab o el carboplatino con paclitaxel se administran por vía intravenosa el día 1 de cada ciclo de 7 días, hasta 7 ciclos, si la enfermedad no progresa y los efectos secundarios son aceptables. El resultado principal no se indica en el registro; el registro señala que este es un ensayo de fase 3.
who_for: Previously untreated, unresected squamous cell cancer of the larynx, hypopharynx, oropharynx, or oral cavity
Locally advanced disease at AJCC 9th edition stage II to IVB, depending on site and p16 status
Contraindication to cisplatin, such as creatinine clearance under 60 mL/min, grade 2 or higher nerve damage, or hearing loss
Age 70 or older with HNCIG omega score under 0.80, or under 70 with omega under 0.80, Charlson score of at least 1, and G-8 score of 14 or less
Age 18 or older, and not pregnant or nursing
not_for: Prior systemic therapy for this head and neck cancer
Prior radiation to the same region that would overlap with the planned radiation fields
Prior surgery for this head and neck cancer
Cannot safely receive the radiation and drug regimens per FDA labeling and investigator judgment
Pregnant or nursing
cancer_types: head and neck squamous cell carcinoma

NCT04906434.summary_en: The study tests ABSK-011, a medicine taken by mouth, in adults with advanced solid tumors, including advanced liver cancer. Patients take ABSK-011 once daily or twice daily in repeated 28-day cycles, after a single-dose run-in period; the total length of treatment is not stated. The study measures safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics (how the body processes the drug), and it is a Phase 1 trial.
NCT04906434.summary_es: El estudio evalúa ABSK-011, un medicamento oral, en adultos con tumores sólidos avanzados, incluido el cáncer de hígado avanzado. Los pacientes toman ABSK-011 una vez al día o dos veces al día en ciclos repetidos de 28 días, después de una dosis única inicial; la duración total del tratamiento no se indica en el registro. El estudio mide la seguridad, la tolerancia y la farmacocinética del medicamento (cómo lo procesa el cuerpo), y es un estudio de Fase 1.
who_for: Male or female, aged 18 to 75 years.
Advanced solid tumor or advanced liver cancer that progressed on, did not tolerate, or has no standard therapy (escalation part).
Liver cancer at BCLC stage B or C with Child-Pugh score 5 to 6 (escalation) or 5 to 7 (expansion).
Expansion part: positive FGF19 overexpression test on archived tissue or biopsy, and at least one measurable lesion.
ECOG performance status 0 to 1 and life expectancy of at least 3 months.
not_for: Previous treatment with FGFR4 or pan-FGFR pathway inhibitors.
Known active brain or central nervous system metastases (stable cases may be allowed).
Liver tumor volume that is 50% or more of the whole liver.
Inability to take oral medicine or factors that significantly prevent drug absorption.
Active hepatitis C infection needing treatment, hepatitis B and C co-infection, or positive HIV test.

NCT07061964.summary_en: This phase II study tests pembrolizumab given with photon beam radiation therapy in people with muscle invasive bladder cancer whose tumor responded to chemotherapy before surgery. The goal is to help patients avoid surgical removal of the bladder. Pembrolizumab is given by IV over 30 minutes on day 1 of each 21-day cycle, for up to 18 cycles, and radiation is given Monday through Friday for up to 20 treatments. The record states the total study duration is 12 months, including neoadjuvant therapy, and it does not state a primary outcome measure.
NCT07061964.summary_es: Este estudio de fase II evalúa pembrolizumab administrado junto con radioterapia de haz de fotones en personas con cáncer de vejiga que invade el músculo, cuyo tumor respondió a la quimioterapia previa a la cirugía. El objetivo es ayudar a los pacientes a evitar la extirpación quirúrgica de la vejiga. El pembrolizumab se administra por vía intravenosa durante 30 minutos el día 1 de cada ciclo de 21 días, hasta 18 ciclos, y la radiación se aplica de lunes a viernes hasta 20 tratamientos. El registro indica que la duración total del estudio es de 12 meses, incluida la terapia neoadyuvante, y no indica una medida de resultado principal.
who_for: Muscle invasive urothelial carcinoma of the bladder, staged cT2 to T4a, node negative, with no distant spread
Diagnosed within 180 days before starting neoadjuvant therapy
Received 3 to 6 cycles of an FDA approved neoadjuvant chemotherapy regimen for muscle invasive bladder cancer
Clinically T0 to T1 disease after neoadjuvant therapy, confirmed by TURBT and biopsies
Age 18 or older with Zubrod performance status 0 to 2
not_for: Small cell, neuroendocrine, or plasmacytoid variant on any pathology
Prior pelvic radiotherapy
Prior PD-1, PD-L1, PD-L2, or CTLA-4 antibody therapy, other than neoadjuvant treatment for this bladder cancer
Pregnant or nursing
Other cancer or malignancy that could interfere with safety or efficacy, per treating physician, or steroid doses above 10 mg prednisone daily

NCT04165772.summary_en: This Phase 2 study tests TSR-042 or dostarlimab, given before standard chemoradiation and surgery, in people with locally advanced mismatch repair deficient solid tumors, including rectal and endometrial cancer. The study drug is given by IV infusion over 30 minutes every 3 weeks for up to 6 months (9 cycles of 21 days), and capecitabine is taken by mouth with radiation therapy (infusional 5-FU is an alternative if oral medicine cannot be tolerated). The record says the study looks at whether the treatment is effective and at its safety, and the primary outcome is not stated.
NCT04165772.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 evalúa TSR-042 o dostarlimab, administrados antes de la quimiorradiación y la cirugía estándar, en personas con tumores sólidos localmente avanzados con deficiencia en la reparación de errores de apareamiento, incluido el cáncer de recto y el cáncer endometrial. El medicamento del estudio se administra por infusión intravenosa durante 30 minutos cada 3 semanas, por hasta 6 meses (9 ciclos de 21 días), y la capecitabina se toma por vía oral junto con radioterapia (el 5-FU en infusión es una alternativa si no se puede tolerar el medicamento oral). El registro indica que el estudio analiza si el tratamiento es eficaz y su seguridad, y el resultado principal no está indicado.
who_for: Age 18 or older with ECOG performance status 0 or 1.
Locally advanced solid tumor, or endometrial cancer clinically FIGO stage I or II (cohort 3).
Tumor shows mismatch repair deficiency or MSI-H status.
No evidence of distant metastases; disease is measurable or clinically evaluable.
Adequate blood counts, kidney, liver and clotting lab values.
not_for: Metastatic or recurrent disease.
Prior radiation, chemotherapy, or surgery for the tumor.
Prior therapy targeting T-cell co-stimulation or checkpoint pathways (cohorts 1 and 3).
History of interstitial lung disease.
Known HIV, active hepatitis B or C, or pregnancy or breastfeeding.

NCT07294677.summary_en: The study tests adding capivasertib to venetoclax and low-intensity chemotherapy (mini-hyperCVD) in adults with relapsed or refractory acute leukemia of lymphoid type or lymphoblastic lymphoma. Capivasertib is taken by mouth twice daily on a 4 days on, 3 days off schedule, venetoclax is taken by mouth once daily, and mini-hyperCVD is given in 8 cycles, about every 28 days. The study aims to assess the safety of this combination, and the record lists it as Phase 1/2.
NCT07294677.summary_es: El estudio evalúa agregar capivasertib a venetoclax y a quimioterapia de baja intensidad (mini-hyperCVD) en adultos con leucemia aguda de tipo linfoide o linfoma linfoblástico recidivante o refractario. El capivasertib se toma por vía oral dos veces al día con un esquema de 4 días con tratamiento y 3 días sin él, el venetoclax se toma por vía oral una vez al día, y el mini-hyperCVD se administra en 8 ciclos, aproximadamente cada 28 días. El estudio busca evaluar la seguridad de esta combinación, y el registro indica que es de Fase 1/2.
who_for: Relapsed or refractory acute lymphoid leukemia or lymphoblastic lymphoma (cohorts 1 and 2).
At least 5% leukemic blasts in bone marrow or blood (cohorts 1 and 2).
Previously untreated patients aged 40 or older with at least 20% blasts (cohort 3).
Age 18 or older, with ECOG performance status 0-2.
Adequate organ function per protocol criteria.
not_for: Ph-positive acute lymphoblastic leukemia or Burkitt leukemia/lymphoma.
Pregnant or breastfeeding.
Uncontrolled infection.
Known active hepatitis B or C, or uncontrolled HIV.
Uncontrolled diabetes, or insulin-dependent diabetes.

NCT07116057.summary_en: This Phase 1 study tests MOv19-BBz CAR T cells, which are a patient's own T cells engineered to target folate receptor alpha (FRa), in people with metastatic or recurrent non-small cell lung cancer. Patients receive one dose of the CAR T cells by intrapleural infusion (directly into the chest lining) after lymphodepleting chemotherapy, and checkpoint inhibitors may start at least 28 days later. The study aims to assess safety, feasibility and preliminary efficacy.
NCT07116057.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1 evalúa las células CAR T MOv19-BBz, que son células T propias del paciente modificadas para atacar el receptor de folato alfa (FRa), en personas con cáncer de pulmón de células no pequeñas metastásico o recurrente. Los pacientes reciben una sola dosis de las células CAR T por infusión intrapleural (directamente en la membrana que recubre el pulmón) después de quimioterapia de linfodepleción, y los inhibidores de puntos de control pueden iniciarse al menos 28 días después. El estudio tiene como objetivos evaluar la seguridad, la factibilidad y la eficacia preliminar.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older
Metastatic or recurrent lung adenocarcinoma with a malignant pleural effusion
Failed at least one prior line of standard therapy for advanced disease
Tumor FRa expression of at least 10% by IHC, with archived tumor tissue available
ECOG performance status of 0 or 1
not_for: Pleural effusion that cannot be drained with standard approaches
Significant lung disease, such as lymphangitic spread, radiation pneumonitis or interstitial lung disease
Active hepatitis B or hepatitis C infection
Dependence on systemic steroids or immunosuppressant medications
Pregnant or nursing patients

NCT07095452.summary_en: This study tests etentamig given with daratumumab, compared with daratumumab, lenalidomide, and dexamethasone (DRd), in adults with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma who are not eligible for transplant. Etentamig is given as an intravenous infusion or a subcutaneous injection, with daratumumab given as a subcutaneous injection, until the recommended phase 3 dose, and the study lasts about 16 years. The study measures adverse events, change in disease activity, and pharmacokinetics, according to the brief summary; this is a Phase 2/3 study.
NCT07095452.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa etentamig administrado con daratumumab, comparado con daratumumab, lenalidomida y dexametasona (DRd), en adultos con mieloma múltiple recién diagnosticado que no son elegibles para trasplante. El etentamig se administra como infusión intravenosa o inyección subcutánea, y el daratumumab como inyección subcutánea, hasta la dosis recomendada para fase 3; el estudio dura aproximadamente 16 años. El estudio mide los eventos adversos, el cambio en la actividad de la enfermedad y la farmacocinética, según el resumen breve; es un estudio de Fase 2/3.
who_for: Newly diagnosed multiple myeloma, confirmed by IMWG criteria
Investigator judges not suitable for high-dose chemotherapy and stem cell transplant
Frailty index score of 1 or higher
Measurable disease within 28 days before enrollment
Age 18 years or older
not_for: Prior systemic therapy or stem cell transplant for myeloma, except a short course of corticosteroids
Investigational treatment within 30 days or 5 half-lives before first dose, or currently in another study
Known active central nervous system involvement of myeloma
Clinically significant kidney, nerve, psychiatric, hormone, metabolic, immune, lung, or liver disease in the last 6 months that would affect participation

NCT06961955.summary_en: This study compares a 5-day course with a 9-day course of whole breast radiation therapy with a boost for early-stage breast cancer. Participants receive hypofractionated radiation therapy, given over either 5 days or 9 days. The main outcome is not stated; this is a Phase 2 randomized trial.
NCT06961955.summary_es: Este estudio compara un curso de 5 días con un curso de 9 días de radioterapia de toda la mama con refuerzo (boost) para el cáncer de mama en etapa temprana. Los participantes reciben radioterapia hipofraccionada, administrada en un curso de 5 días o de 9 días. El resultado principal no se indica; es un ensayo aleatorizado de fase 2.
who_for: Women aged 18 or older with invasive breast cancer or ductal carcinoma in situ.
Stage T0 to T3, N0, M0 by AJCC v8, with T0 N0 allowed if whole breast radiation is recommended.
Lumpectomy within 84 days before radiation starts, with negative inked margins.
At least one listed risk factor, such as grade 3 histology, age 50 or younger, or tumor larger than 2 cm.
ECOG performance status 2 or less, or KPS 50 or more.
not_for: Bilateral breast cancer.
Prior chest radiation or prior chemotherapy.
Recurrent disease, known metastases, or node-positive disease.
Prior breast malignancy in either breast.
Uncontrolled significant illness, such as heart failure, or a stroke, heart attack, or blood clot within 3 months.
cancer_types: ductal carcinoma in situ of the breast

NCT05819892.summary_en: This Phase 1 study tests chemoradiation followed by chemotherapy plus dostarlimab for stage IIIC, node-positive endometrial cancer. Participants receive chemotherapy for 6 cycles, and dostarlimab is given by IV starting at cycle 3 for up to 2 years, as long as the disease does not get worse or toxicity is not acceptable. The study measures safety and tolerability, as stated in the title, and no other outcome measure is stated.
NCT05819892.summary_es: Este estudio de Fase 1 evalúa quimiorradiación seguida de quimioterapia más dostarlimab para cáncer endometrial en estadio IIIC con ganglios positivos. Los participantes reciben quimioterapia durante 6 ciclos, y el dostarlimab se administra por vía intravenosa desde el ciclo 3 por hasta 2 años, mientras la enfermedad no empeore y la toxicidad sea aceptable. El estudio mide la seguridad y la tolerabilidad, según indica el título, y no se establece ninguna otra medida de resultado.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older.
Surgically staged stage IIIC, pathologically confirmed endometrial cancer, eligible for adjuvant chemoradiation followed by chemotherapy.
Enrolled within 8 weeks of surgery and started treatment within 10 weeks of surgery.
ECOG performance status of 0 or 1.
Adequate blood counts, kidney, liver, and clotting function within 14 days before enrollment.
not_for: Prior anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1, or anti-CTLA-4 antibody therapy.
Severe allergic reaction to monoclonal antibodies or dostarlimab.
Active or recurring autoimmune disease, or history of interstitial lung disease or non-radiation pneumonitis.
Daily steroids or other immunosuppressive therapy within 7 days before enrollment, or immunodeficiency.
Known HIV, clinically significant liver disease, or uncontrolled intercurrent illness.

NCT06203210.summary_en: This Phase 3 study compares ifinatamab deruxtecan (I-DXd), a B7-H3 antibody drug conjugate, with treatment of physician's choice in adults with relapsed small cell lung cancer. I-DXd is given as 12 mg/kg intravenously on Day 1 of each 21-day cycle, until progression, unacceptable toxicity, or other stop criteria in the protocol are met. The record states that the study compares efficacy and safety, but it does not state a primary outcome.
NCT06203210.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 3 compara ifinatamab deruxtecan (I-DXd), un conjugado anticuerpo-fármaco dirigido a B7-H3, con el tratamiento a criterio del médico en adultos con cáncer de pulmón de células pequeñas recidivante. I-DXd se administra a 12 mg/kg por vía intravenosa el día 1 de cada ciclo de 21 días, hasta la progresión, toxicidad inaceptable u otros criterios de suspensión definidos en el protocolo. El registro indica que el estudio compara la eficacia y la seguridad, pero no indica un desenlace primario.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older with extensive-stage small cell lung cancer.
Received only one prior platinum-based systemic therapy line for small cell lung cancer, with at least 2 cycles.
Chemotherapy-free interval of at least 30 days from end of platinum to radiologic progression.
At least one measurable lesion according to RECIST v1.1.
ECOG performance status of 1 or less within 7 days before Cycle 1 Day 1.
not_for: Prior treatment with B7-H3 targeted agents, including I-DXd.
Prior discontinuation of an exatecan-derivative antibody drug conjugate due to treatment-related toxicity.
Prior treatment with any study comparator drug or any topoisomerase I inhibitor.
Stroke, transient ischemic attack, or other arterial thromboembolic event within the past 6 months.
Current or past interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis, or suspected interstitial lung disease that cannot be ruled out.

NCT07529808.summary_en: BHB810 is being tested in adults with advanced gastric or gastroesophageal junction (GEJ) adenocarcinoma. This is a Phase 1/2 study. BHB810 is given as an IV infusion every 2 weeks while participants are on study treatment. The study mainly looks at how safe BHB810 is, and it also looks at how well it works, how it moves through the body, and how the body reacts to it.
NCT07529808.summary_es: BHB810 se está probando en adultos con adenocarcinoma avanzado de estómago o de la unión gastroesofágica (GEJ). Es un estudio de Fase 1/2. BHB810 se administra por infusión intravenosa cada 2 semanas mientras los participantes reciben el tratamiento del estudio. El estudio se enfoca principalmente en qué tan seguro es BHB810, y también observa qué tan bien funciona, cómo se mueve por el cuerpo y cómo reacciona el organismo ante él.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older, or the legal age of consent where the study takes place.
Advanced gastric or GEJ adenocarcinoma that progressed, did not respond to treatment, or has no standard curative therapy.
At least one measurable target lesion at baseline per RECIST 1.1.
Tumor tissue available; fresh biopsies needed for backfill cohorts and Phase 2.
CDH17-positive by central testing for Phase 1 backfill cohorts and Phase 2 participants.
not_for: Prior CDH17-directed therapy or an antibody drug conjugate with an auristatin (MMAE or MMAF).
Recent chemotherapy, targeted therapy, monoclonal antibody, or immune checkpoint inhibitor within the stated time windows.
Known allergy to BHB810 or its excipients, or left ventricular ejection fraction below 50%.
QTc above 470 msec, or a medication known to prolong QT/QTc.
Pregnant or breastfeeding, planning pregnancy, or known or suspected untreated brain metastases, leptomeningeal disease, or spinal cord compression.

NCT06246968.summary_en: This study tests pembrolizumab with or without ablation (cryoablation or histotripsy) in people with metastatic or locally advanced triple negative breast cancer. Pembrolizumab is given at 200 mg every 3 weeks as part of standard care, and participants are randomly assigned in a 2 to 1 ratio to ablation plus pembrolizumab or pembrolizumab alone. The main outcome is not stated; the study is Phase 1.
NCT06246968.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa pembrolizumab con o sin ablación (crioablación o histotripsia) en personas con cáncer de mama triple negativo metastásico o localmente avanzado. El pembrolizumab se administra a 200 mg cada 3 semanas como parte del tratamiento estándar, y los participantes se asignan al azar en una proporción de 2 a 1 a ablación más pembrolizumab o solo pembrolizumab. El resultado principal no está indicado; el estudio es de Fase 1.
who_for: Age 18 or older
Confirmed triple negative breast cancer that is metastatic or locally advanced and inoperable
At least one site suitable for cryoablation, at least 1.5 cm in size
Physically fit to undergo ablation under usual clinical practice
Planned pembrolizumab as first, second, or third line therapy
not_for: Not eligible for a PD-1 inhibitor according to the patient's medical oncologist
No disease that can be treated with ablation
Pembrolizumab not planned as part of standard of care

NCT05024552.summary_en: This Phase 1 study tests Vyxeos (a liposomal form of cytarabine and daunorubicin) given with gilteritinib in adults with relapsed or refractory FLT3-mutated acute myeloid leukemia. Vyxeos is given as an intravenous infusion over 90 minutes on days 1, 3 and 5 of induction, and gilteritinib is taken by mouth daily on days 6 to 19 of induction. The record does not state the main outcome measure; the study is a Phase 1 study.
NCT05024552.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1 evalúa Vyxeos (una forma liposomal de citarabina y daunorrubicina) administrado junto con gilteritinib en adultos con leucemia mieloide aguda recidivante o refractaria con mutación FLT3. Vyxeos se administra como infusión intravenosa durante 90 minutos los días 1, 3 y 5 de la inducción, y el gilteritinib se toma por vía oral todos los días del 6 al 19 de la inducción. El registro no indica la medida de resultado principal; el estudio es de fase 1.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older with FLT3-ITD or FLT3-TKD mutated AML (non-M3).
AML that has relapsed or not responded to at least one prior AML treatment.
ECOG performance status of 2 or better.
Left ventricular ejection fraction of 50% or higher.
Able to take oral medication and follow the medication plan.
not_for: Documented central nervous system involvement of AML.
AML that progressed while on prior gilteritinib therapy.
White blood cell count of 50,000 or higher when study treatment begins.
Grade 3 or higher graft versus host disease after transplant.
Other cancers needing current treatment, with listed exceptions.

NCT06741085.summary_en: This study compares stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) given after about 3 months of osimertinib with osimertinib alone, in non-small cell lung cancer that has spread to the brain. Osimertinib is taken by mouth, and SRS is given as a single dose or in several doses, with schedules that depend on the size of the brain lesion (for example, 18Gy x 1 or 21Gy x 1 for lesions under 20mm, and 9Gy x 3, 6Gy x 5, or 5Gy x 5 for lesions 20mm or larger); how long osimertinib is taken is not stated. The study measures quality of life using questionnaires, and this is a Phase 2 study.
NCT06741085.summary_es: Este estudio compara la radiocirugía estereotáxica (SRS) administrada después de unos 3 meses de osimertinib con osimertinib solo, en cáncer de pulmón de células no pequeñas que se ha diseminado al cerebro. El osimertinib se toma por vía oral, y la SRS se administra en una sola dosis o en varias dosis, con esquemas que dependen del tamaño de la lesión cerebral (por ejemplo, 18Gy x 1 o 21Gy x 1 para lesiones menores de 20mm, y 9Gy x 3, 6Gy x 5 o 5Gy x 5 para lesiones de 20mm o más); no se indica por cuánto tiempo se toma el osimertinib. El estudio mide la calidad de vida mediante cuestionarios, y es un estudio de Fase 2.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older.
Non-small cell lung cancer with an EGFR activating mutation, confirmed at the enrolling institution.
At least one intact brain metastasis visible on contrast MRI of the brain.
Not yet started TKI therapy, or started TKI no more than 3 months before enrollment.
For randomization: detectable brain lesions that are not growing and may be viable residual disease.
not_for: Prior brain-directed radiation therapy.
Evidence of leptomeningeal disease on MRI of the spine or lumbar puncture cytology.
Neurologic symptoms or a lesion in the brainstem, motor strip, or other eloquent area that needs immediate SRS.
Active blood cancer or a second solid tumor known to spread to the brain.
Pregnant, breastfeeding, or of childbearing potential without highly effective contraception.

NCT04575935.summary_en: This phase 3 trial compares minimally invasive surgery (MIS) with laparotomy, an open surgery, in people with stage IIIC or IV ovarian, primary peritoneal, or fallopian tube cancer who received chemotherapy before surgery. MIS uses small incisions and is done within 6 weeks after the last cycle of chemotherapy given before surgery, and standard chemotherapy is given again within 6 weeks after surgery. The record does not state a primary outcome; the summary says the study looks at how long before the disease returns and at quality of life after surgery.
NCT04575935.summary_es: Este ensayo de fase 3 compara la cirugía mínimamente invasiva (MIS) con la laparotomía, una cirugía abierta, en personas con cáncer de ovario, peritoneo primario o trompa de Falopio en etapa IIIC o IV que recibieron quimioterapia antes de la cirugía. La MIS usa incisiones pequeñas y se realiza dentro de las 6 semanas posteriores al último ciclo de quimioterapia previa a la cirugía, y se administra quimioterapia estándar nuevamente dentro de las 6 semanas posteriores a la cirugía. El registro no indica un resultado principal; el resumen dice que el estudio analiza cuánto tiempo pasa antes de que la enfermedad regrese y la calidad de vida después de la cirugía.
who_for: Adults 18 or older with stage IIIC or IV high-grade ovarian, peritoneal, or fallopian tube cancer.
Considered a surgical candidate after 3 to 4 cycles of platinum-based chemotherapy.
Complete radiologic resolution of disease outside the abdomen; pleural effusion allowed at PI discretion.
CA-125 normalized or at most 500, with a planned diagnostic laparoscopy if applicable.
ECOG performance status 0 to 2, surgery within 6 weeks of last chemotherapy cycle.
not_for: Tumor not suitable for minimally invasive removal on pre-operative imaging.
Ascites not improving during chemotherapy (trace ascites allowed).
Tumor involvement of bowel, colon or rectum, diaphragm, spleen, liver, or mesentery.
Inability to tolerate prolonged Trendelenburg position or pneumoperitoneum.
Psychological, family, social, or geographic barriers to follow-up, or other contraindication to MIS.

NCT04913285.summary_en: This Phase 1/1b study is testing KIN-2787 (also called exarafenib), alone or with binimetinib, in adults with BRAF or NRAS mutation-positive solid tumors, including non-small cell lung cancer and melanoma. KIN-2787 is taken by mouth twice daily in 28-day cycles, and binimetinib is also taken by mouth, with an intermittent cohort taking it twice daily for 5 days on and 2 days off in each 28-day cycle. The study measures safety, tolerability, how the body processes the drug (pharmacokinetics), and preliminary antitumor activity.
NCT04913285.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1/1b evalúa KIN-2787 (también llamado exarafenib), solo o con binimetinib, en adultos con tumores sólidos que tienen una mutación en BRAF o NRAS, incluidos el cáncer de pulmón de células no pequeñas y el melanoma. KIN-2787 se toma por vía oral dos veces al día en ciclos de 28 días, y binimetinib también se toma por vía oral; en una cohorte intermitente se toma dos veces al día durante 5 días seguidos y luego 2 días de descanso en cada ciclo de 28 días. El estudio mide la seguridad, la tolerancia, cómo el organismo procesa el fármaco (farmacocinética) y la actividad preliminar contra el tumor.
who_for: Metastatic or advanced solid tumor.
Known BRAF Class I, II, or III alteration, or melanoma with an NRAS mutation, confirmed by tumor tissue or ctDNA testing.
Measurable disease, or evaluable disease in Part A only, by RECIST v1.1.
ECOG performance status 0 to 1.
Adequate organ function and able to swallow, retain, and absorb oral medicines.
not_for: Other active cancer treated within 3 years before enrollment.
In Part B dose expansion, prior approved or in-development BRAF, MEK, or MAPK-directed inhibitor therapy.
GI disease that prevents oral medicine, causes malabsorption, needs IV feeding, or is uncontrolled inflammatory GI disease.
Active, uncontrolled bacterial, fungal, or viral infection, or positive, known, or suspected SARS-CoV-2.
Pregnant or breastfeeding women.

NCT06119685.summary_en: This Phase 1/2 study tests IDP-023, an NK cell therapy, alone or combined with rituximab, daratumumab, isatuximab, or interleukin-2, in adults with advanced blood cancers, including relapsed or refractory non-Hodgkin lymphoma and multiple myeloma. The record does not state how IDP-023 is given, how often, or for how long, but it describes single-dose and multiple-dose groups. The study measures safety, tolerability and preliminary antitumor activity.
NCT06119685.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1/2 evalúa IDP-023, una terapia con células NK, sola o combinada con rituximab, daratumumab, isatuximab o interleucina-2, en adultos con cánceres de la sangre avanzados, incluidos el linfoma no Hodgkin y el mieloma múltiple recidivantes o refractarios. El registro no indica la vía, la frecuencia ni la duración de la administración, pero describe grupos con una dosis única y grupos con varias dosis. El estudio mide la seguridad, la tolerabilidad y la actividad antitumoral preliminar.
who_for: Adults aged 18 years or older
Multiple myeloma that has returned or did not respond, after at least 3 prior lines of therapy
Non-Hodgkin lymphoma that has returned or did not respond, after failing at least 2 lines of chemotherapy
ECOG performance status of 0 or 1
Investigator-judged life expectancy greater than 12 weeks
not_for: Impaired cardiac function or clinically significant heart disease
HIV infection, active hepatitis B, or hepatitis C infection
Active SARS-CoV-2 infection
Untreated brain, central nervous system, or epidural tumor metastasis

NCT06483048.summary_en: This phase 1 trial tests the safety, side effects, and best dose of MUC1-activated T cells, made from the patient's own blood, in people with relapsed or resistant ovarian cancer. The T cells are given by IV on day 0, or on days 0 and 21, after leukapheresis and IV cyclophosphamide or bendamustine given before the T cells. The study measures safety, side effects, and the best dose.
NCT06483048.summary_es: Este ensayo de fase 1 evalúa la seguridad, los efectos secundarios y la mejor dosis de células T activadas con MUC1, elaboradas a partir de la sangre de la propia paciente, en personas con cáncer de ovario recidivante o resistente. Las células T se administran por vía intravenosa el día 0, o los días 0 y 21, después de una leucaféresis y de cyclophosphamide o bendamustina por vía intravenosa administradas antes de las células T. El estudio mide la seguridad, los efectos secundarios y la mejor dosis.
who_for: Age 18 or older with epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, carcinosarcoma, or primary peritoneal cancer.
Relapsed or refractory disease after at least one prior line of platinum chemotherapy.
Measurable disease, with at least one lesion of 1 cm or more on imaging.
MUC1 expression on tumor cells by immunohistochemistry, with a staining score above 0.
ECOG performance status of 0 or 1.
not_for: Pregnant or nursing persons, or those of childbearing potential not using birth control.
Prior treatment targeting MUC1.
Clinically unresolved brain metastases.
Myocardial infarction within 6 months, or heart failure needing ongoing treatment.
Active autoimmune disease needing systemic treatment within 30 days.

NCT05312255.summary_en: This study tests non-chemotherapy approaches, including strength training, activity tracking, intermittent fasting, and the beta-blocker propranolol, in people with multiple myeloma or smoldering myeloma. Strength training is done online twice a week with a Fitbit for 6 months (9 months in one group), fasting is done for 1 month, and propranolol is taken by mouth twice a day for 3 months. The record does not state a main outcome measure; the study phase is listed as NA (not applicable).
NCT05312255.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa intervenciones sin quimioterapia, como entrenamiento de fuerza, seguimiento de actividad física, ayuno intermitente y el betabloqueador propranolol, en personas con mieloma múltiple o mieloma latente. El entrenamiento de fuerza se hace en línea dos veces por semana con un Fitbit durante 6 meses (9 meses en un grupo), el ayuno se realiza durante 1 mes y el propranolol se toma por vía oral dos veces al día durante 3 meses. El registro no indica una medida de resultado principal; la fase del estudio aparece como NA (no aplica).
who_for: Age 18 years or older.
Smoldering multiple myeloma, multiple myeloma, or plasma cell leukemia (modules A to C).
Non-transfusion-dependent low-risk MDS (module D).
ECOG performance status 0 to 1 or 0 to 2, depending on module.
Access to a computer or tablet with camera, microphone, speakers, and internet (physical activity modules).
not_for: Major heart, lung, or active infectious conditions that would make participation unsafe.
Current symptomatic pathological fractures or unstable bones (physical activity modules).
Current beta-blocker use or use within 3 months (beta-blocker module).
Conditions that contraindicate beta-blockers, such as low blood pressure or severe asthma or COPD.
Pregnant or nursing participants (beta-blocker module).

NCT07469891.summary_en: The study tests PRT12396, an investigational drug, in people with polycythemia vera or myelofibrosis, which are types of myeloproliferative neoplasms. It is given as a capsule by mouth twice a day, swallowed whole with water, and may be taken one hour before or two hours after meals; how long treatment lasts is not stated. The study measures safety, tolerability, how the body processes the drug, and early signs of effect, and it aims to find the maximum tolerated dose; it is a Phase 1 study.
NCT07469891.summary_es: El estudio evalúa PRT12396, un medicamento en investigación, en personas con policitemia vera o mielofibrosis, que son tipos de neoplasias mieloproliferativas. Se administra en cápsulas por vía oral dos veces al día, tragadas enteras con agua, y puede tomarse una hora antes o dos horas después de las comidas; la duración del tratamiento no se indica. El estudio mide la seguridad, la tolerabilidad, cómo el cuerpo procesa el medicamento y las primeras señales de efecto, y busca encontrar la dosis máxima tolerada; es un estudio de Fase 1.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older with polycythemia vera or myelofibrosis confirmed by WHO 2016 or ICC/WHO 2022 criteria
Documented JAK2 V617 mutation
ECOG performance status of 0 to 1
Estimated life expectancy of at least 12 weeks per investigator
Adequate blood count, kidney and liver function, and bone marrow reserve
not_for: Another malignancy within the past 3 years, unless considered cured with low risk of recurrence
Prior systemic therapy for PV or MF, or prior or planned allogeneic stem-cell transplant
Pregnancy or breastfeeding
Use of strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors or inducers, or acid-reducing agents that cannot be stopped
Participation in another interventional clinical study

NCT06588478.summary_en: This study tests pirtobrutinib in people with relapsed or refractory chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) or small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL). The drug is taken by mouth, with three dose levels tested in Part 1; how often doses are taken is not stated. Part 1 is expected to last about 3 years and Part 2 up to 2 years, and the study assesses efficacy and safety, but the specific main outcome measure is not stated; it is a Phase 2 study.
NCT06588478.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa pirtobrutinib en personas con leucemia linfocítica crónica (LLC) o linfoma linfocítico de células pequeñas (LLPC) en recaída o refractarios. El medicamento se toma por vía oral, con tres dosis diferentes probadas en la Parte 1; la frecuencia de las dosis no se indica. La Parte 1 dura unos 3 años y la Parte 2 hasta 2 años, y el estudio evalúa la eficacia y la seguridad, aunque la medida de resultado principal específica no se indica; es un estudio de fase 2.
who_for: Confirmed chronic lymphocytic leukemia or small lymphocytic lymphoma under iwCLL 2018 criteria.
Part 1: 1 to 3 prior lines of CLL/SLL treatment, including a covalent BTK inhibitor.
Part 2: no prior CLL/SLL treatment and a 17p deletion.
Need for therapy under iwCLL 2018 criteria.
ECOG performance status 0 to 2 and able to swallow oral medication.
not_for: Prior treatment with a BTK degrader or a noncovalent BTK inhibitor.
Grade 3 or higher bleeding caused by a BTK inhibitor.
Known or suspected Richter's transformation.
Known or suspected central nervous system involvement by CLL/SLL.
Another cancer within 3 years before randomization, with some exceptions.

NCT06260033.summary_en: This Phase II trial tests stereotactic body radiation therapy (SBRT) and fluoroestradiol (FES) PET/CT imaging in patients with oligoprogressive, estrogen receptor positive metastatic breast cancer. SBRT is given in 3 or 5 treatment fractions within 3 weeks, and F-18 16 Alpha-Fluoroestradiol is given by IV, with FES PET/CT scans at 12 and 24 weeks. The main outcome is not stated; the study is Phase II.
NCT06260033.summary_es: Este estudio de fase II prueba la radioterapia corporal estereotáxica (SBRT) y las imágenes PET/CT con fluoroestradiol (FES) en pacientes con cáncer de mama metastásico positivo para receptores de estrógeno y progresión limitada. La SBRT se administra en 3 o 5 fracciones durante 3 semanas, y el F-18 16 Alfa-Fluoroestradiol se administra por vía intravenosa, con exploraciones PET/CT con FES a las 12 y 24 semanas. El resultado principal no se indica en el registro; el estudio es de fase II.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older
Estrogen receptor positive metastatic breast cancer with progression in 1 to 4 lesions
ECOG performance status of 2 or lower
SBRT must be feasible for all progressing lesions
Able to read and understand English or Spanish for questionnaires
not_for: Has had one to three lines of systemic therapy for metastatic disease
Progression in more than 4 lesions, including current pleural effusion, ascites or lymphangitic lung spread
Only liver metastases
Intracranial disease progression or current leptomeningeal disease
Pregnant or breastfeeding

NCT03618550.summary_en: This study tests pembrolizumab combined with GVD (gemcitabine, vinorelbine, and liposomal doxorubicin) in relapsed or refractory Hodgkin lymphoma. Pembrolizumab is given by IV infusion on day 1 and GVD on days 1 and 8 of each 3-week cycle, for 2 to 4 cycles before stem cell collection. The main outcome is not stated in the record; this is a Phase 2 study.
NCT03618550.summary_es: Este estudio prueba pembrolizumab combinado con GVD (gemcitabina, vinorelbina y doxorrubicina liposomal) en linfoma de Hodgkin recidivante o refractario. El pembrolizumab se administra por infusión intravenosa el día 1, y GVD los días 1 y 8, de cada ciclo de 3 semanas, durante 2 a 4 ciclos antes de la recolección de células madre. El resultado principal no está indicado en el registro; es un estudio de Fase 2.
who_for: Classical Hodgkin lymphoma that has come back or did not respond to treatment, proven by biopsy
Age 18 or older and able to give written consent
Measurable disease on a PET scan before starting treatment
ECOG performance status of 0 or 1
Adequate blood, kidney, liver, lung, heart and clotting function
not_for: Known pregnancy or breastfeeding
Radiotherapy within 2 weeks before starting study treatment
Known active brain or spinal cord metastases or carcinomatous meningitis
Active autoimmune disease needing systemic treatment in the past 2 years
Active HIV, hepatitis B, or hepatitis C

NCT04150640.summary_en: This Phase 2 study tests a combination of 5-fluorouracil (5-FU), oxaliplatin, and liposomal irinotecan (nal-IRI) with immunotherapy, plus trastuzumab for HER2-positive tumors, in advanced esophageal or gastric adenocarcinoma. The drugs are given by intravenous infusion on day 1 and day 15 of each cycle, and cycles last 28 days (42 days in one cohort). The record does not state a primary outcome; it describes evaluating efficacy and safety.
NCT04150640.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 evalúa una combinación de 5-fluorouracilo (5-FU), oxaliplatino e irinotecán liposomal (nal-IRI) con inmunoterapia, más trastuzumab en tumores HER2 positivos, en adenocarcinoma avanzado de esófago o estómago. Los medicamentos se administran por infusión intravenosa el día 1 y el día 15 de cada ciclo, y los ciclos duran 28 días (42 días en una cohorte). El registro no indica un resultado principal; describe la evaluación de la eficacia y la seguridad.
who_for: Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 0 to 2
Locally advanced or metastatic esophageal or gastric adenocarcinoma confirmed by biopsy or cytology
HER2 status and PD-L1 CPS status must be known before treatment
Measurable disease by RECIST v1.1 and no prior systemic therapy for advanced disease
Age 18 years or older with adequate organ function
not_for: Known hypersensitivity to 5-FU, oxaliplatin, platinum agents, or liposomal product components
Known dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase (DPD) deficiency
Other active malignancy requiring treatment within the last 2 years
Current therapy with another investigational agent
Known active brain metastases or carcinomatous meningitis, or known HIV

NCT07284433.summary_en: This study tests Allo-QuadCAR01-T, an off-the-shelf CAR-T cell therapy made from donor cells, in adults with relapsed or refractory B-cell cancers, including diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. Participants get chemotherapy with cyclophosphamide and fludarabine by IV over 3 days, then one IV infusion of the study therapy on Day 1, and are followed for up to 15 years. The main outcomes are safety and complete response rate at Week 13, and the study is Phase 1/2.
NCT07284433.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa Allo-QuadCAR01-T, una terapia CAR-T lista para usar elaborada con células de donante, en adultos con cánceres de células B recidivantes o refractarios, incluido el linfoma difuso de células B grandes. Los participantes reciben quimioterapia con ciclofosfamida y fludarabina por vía intravenosa durante 3 días, luego una sola infusión intravenosa del tratamiento del estudio el Día 1, y se les da seguimiento por hasta 15 años. Los resultados principales son la seguridad y la tasa de respuesta completa en la Semana 13, y el estudio es de Fase 1/2.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older
Relapsed or refractory B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma or chronic lymphocytic leukemia
Received at least 2 prior lines of therapy
ECOG performance status 0-1
Adequate heart, liver and kidney function, and HLA B/C match with donor cells
not_for: Active CNS involvement, including PCNSL, in dose escalation cohorts
CAR-T within 3 months of screening, or Grade 3 or higher ICAHT from prior CAR-T
Prior allogeneic stem cell transplant or solid organ transplant
History of GvHD or post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder
Pregnant or breastfeeding

NCT05419076.summary_en: This study is testing stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) for brain metastases that have spread from small cell lung cancer. SRS is given as radiation, with a dose that may range from 16 to 30 Gy in 1 to 5 treatments, chosen by the radiation oncologist, and participants have a lumbar puncture to collect spinal fluid at enrollment, with an optional repeat at 3 months. The record does not state a main outcome measure; it is a Phase II study described as assessing the efficacy of SRS.
NCT05419076.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa la radiocirugía estereotáctica (SRS) para metástasis cerebrales que se han extendido desde el cáncer de pulmón de células pequeñas. La SRS se administra como radiación, con una dosis que puede estar entre 16 y 30 Gy en 1 a 5 tratamientos, según decida el oncólogo radioterapeuta, y los participantes se someten a una punción lumbar para recolectar líquido cefalorraquídeo al inscribirse, con una repetición opcional a los 3 meses. El registro no indica una medida de resultado principal; es un estudio de Fase II que se describe como una evaluación de la eficacia de la SRS.
who_for: Small cell lung cancer confirmed by tissue examination.
Up to 20 brain metastases seen on contrast-enhanced MRI.
Age 18 or older.
Performance status KPS 60-100 or ECOG 0-2.
Patient or legal representative able to give informed consent.
not_for: Unable to have contrast-enhanced MRI of the brain.
Leptomeningeal disease confirmed by lumbar puncture, brain MRI, or spine MRI.
Pregnant or breastfeeding women.
Prior brain-directed radiotherapy.
Uncontrolled systemic disease with no reasonable treatment options likely to result in death, seen on imaging within 3 months before enrollment.

NCT07766187.summary_en: This Phase 2 study is testing whether adding histotripsy, a focused ultrasound treatment, to durvalumab works in people with advanced intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma. Durvalumab is given by IV infusion on day 1 of each 28-day cycle, and histotripsy is performed on Cycle 1 Day 8, with participants followed until progression for up to 5 years. The study measures whether adding histotripsy increases immune response and the safety of the combination.
NCT07766187.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 evalúa si agregar histotricia, un tratamiento con ultrasonido enfocado, a durvalumab funciona en personas con colangiocarcinoma intrahepático avanzado. El durvalumab se administra por infusión intravenosa el día 1 de cada ciclo de 28 días, y la histotricia se realiza el día 8 del ciclo 1; los participantes son seguidos hasta la progresión por hasta 5 años. El estudio mide si agregar histotricia aumenta la respuesta inmunitaria y la seguridad de la combinación.
who_for: Diagnosed with intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma confirmed by a prior biopsy.
Disease controlled after 18 weeks of gemcitabine and/or cisplatin plus durvalumab.
Tumor suitable for liver biopsy and histotripsy; solitary tumor at least 2.0 cm.
Tumor unresectable or not a surgical candidate.
Child-Pugh score A or B (up to B8) and ECOG performance status 0-2.
not_for: Target tumor previously treated with ablation, embolization, or radiation.
Bleeding disorder or uncorrectable coagulopathy.
History of interstitial lung disease or non-infectious pneumonitis.
Active autoimmune disease needing systemic treatment in the past 2 years.
Untreated central nervous system metastasis, or live vaccine within 28 days of durvalumab.

NCT06184516.summary_en: This study tests a decision tool that sorts women having radical cystectomy for bladder urothelial carcinoma into "favorable" or "unfavorable" groups. Women in the favorable group have a reproductive organ sparing radical cystectomy, and women in the unfavorable group have a standard radical cystectomy; how long or how often is not stated. The main outcome is not stated in the record; this is a Phase 2 study.
NCT06184516.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa una herramienta de decisión que clasifica a mujeres que se someterán a una cistectomía radical por carcinoma urotelial de vejiga en los grupos "favorable" o "desfavorable". Las mujeres del grupo favorable reciben una cistectomía radical que conserva los órganos reproductivos, y las del grupo desfavorable reciben una cistectomía radical estándar; la duración o frecuencia no se indica. El resultado principal no se indica en el registro; se trata de un estudio de Fase 2.
who_for: Adult women aged 18 or older with histologically proven urothelial carcinoma of the bladder
Surgical candidate for radical cystectomy
Able to have a pelvic MRI that meets the stated minimum standards
At least one of: anterior vagina, uterus, fallopian tubes, or ovaries present
ECOG performance status of 0 to 2
not_for: Regional or distant metastatic disease
Non-urothelial bladder cancer
Other known active malignancies that may confound recurrence rates
Known germline BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation
Pregnant or breastfeeding

NCT05389293.summary_en: This study tests mosunetuzumab alone or with zanubrutinib in adults with newly diagnosed follicular lymphoma who need systemic therapy. Mosunetuzumab is given under the skin, with step-up doses in cycle 1 and then a 45 mg dose each 3-week cycle, and zanubrutinib is given continuously for 12 months in cohort 2. The record does not state the main outcome measure; this is a Phase 2 study.
NCT05389293.summary_es: Este estudio prueba mosunetuzumab solo o con zanubrutinib en adultos con linfoma folicular recién diagnosticado que necesitan tratamiento sistémico. El mosunetuzumab se administra debajo de la piel, con dosis escalonadas en el ciclo 1 y luego una dosis de 45 mg en cada ciclo de 3 semanas, y el zanubrutinib se administra de forma continua durante 12 meses en la cohorte 2. El registro no indica la medida principal de resultado; el estudio es de fase 2.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older with newly diagnosed follicular lymphoma grade 1, 2, or 3A that has not been treated.
Need for systemic therapy, such as bulky disease, certain symptoms, or low blood counts caused by lymphoma.
ECOG performance status of 0, 1, or 2.
Considered a candidate for chemoimmunotherapy by the treating physician.
At least one measurable lesion on CT or MRI scan.
not_for: Follicular lymphoma grade 3B or transformed follicular lymphoma.
Any prior anti-lymphoma therapy.
Current or prior central nervous system lymphoma.
Pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning pregnancy during the study.
Known active infection, or positive results on certain hepatitis B, hepatitis C, or HIV tests.

NCT07325721.summary_en: This study tests hypofractionated radiation therapy combined with a microboost technique in adult men with high-risk, very high-risk, or pelvic lymph node positive prostate cancer. Radiation is given in 25 fractions: the prostate receives 68 Gy, elective lymph nodes receive 45 Gy, and up to three dominant nodules receive a microboost of 70-83 Gy; participation lasts about 6 weeks, with follow-up every three months for two years, then twice yearly for years 3 to 5. The record does not state a primary outcome measure; it is a Phase 2 study that evaluates safety and effectiveness.
NCT07325721.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa la radioterapia hipofraccionada combinada con una técnica de microrrefuerzo (microboost) en hombres adultos con cáncer de próstata de alto riesgo, muy alto riesgo o con ganglios linfáticos pélvicos positivos. La radiación se administra en 25 fracciones: la próstata recibe 68 Gy, los ganglios linfáticos electivos reciben 45 Gy y hasta tres nódulos dominantes reciben un microrrefuerzo de 70-83 Gy; la participación dura aproximadamente 6 semanas, con seguimiento cada tres meses durante dos años y luego dos veces al año en los años 3 a 5. El registro no indica una medida de resultado principal; es un estudio de fase 2 que evalúa la seguridad y la eficacia.
who_for: Adult men 18 years or older with previously untreated prostate cancer.
High-risk, very high-risk, or pelvic lymph node positive disease without spread outside the pelvic nodes.
Able to have pelvic radiotherapy and prostate or pelvic MRI, with at least one MRI target rated PI-RADS 4 or higher.
ECOG performance status 0 to 2.
Willing and eligible to take long-term androgen deprivation therapy for 12 to 36 months.
not_for: Testosterone supplementation, unless stopped by registration.
