VS-7375 is taken by mouth, and combination arms also use cetuximab, carboplatin with pemetrexed and pembrolizumab, gemcitabine with nab-paclitaxel, pembrolizumab, or defactinib; how long or how often these are given is not stated. The study measures safety and tolerability at escalating doses to find a recommended phase 2 dose in the early phase, and treatment efficacy in the phase 2 groups.
NCT07020221.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa VS-7375, un inhibidor oral de KRAS G12D (ON/OFF), solo y en combinación con otros medicamentos, en adultos con tumores sólidos avanzados que tienen una mutación de KRAS G12D, incluidos el cáncer de páncreas, de pulmón y colorrectal. VS-7375 se toma por vía oral, y los grupos de combinación también usan cetuximab, carboplatino con pemetrexed y pembrolizumab, gemcitabina con nab-paclitaxel, pembrolizumab o defactinib; no se indica cuánto tiempo ni con qué frecuencia se administran. El estudio mide la seguridad y la tolerabilidad con dosis crecientes para determinar una dosis recomendada para la fase 2 en la etapa inicial, y la eficacia del tratamiento en los grupos de fase 2.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older.
Locally advanced unresectable or metastatic solid tumor with a KRAS G12D mutation.
Measurable disease according to RECIST v1.1.
ECOG performance status 0 or 1.
Recovered from side effects of previous therapies to grade 1 or less, or to baseline.
not_for: Prior treatment with direct RAS inhibitors.
Symptomatic, untreated, or actively growing brain metastases.
Inability to swallow oral medications.
Chemotherapy, targeted therapy, or radiation (except palliative radiation) within 4 weeks or 5 half-lives before Cycle 1 Day 1.
Pregnant or breastfeeding.

NCT04483206.summary_en: This phase 1 study tests a personalized dose of melphalan given before a stem cell transplant in people with multiple myeloma. Patients receive high-dose melphalan IV over 30 minutes on day -3, then a second melphalan IV dose over 30 minutes on day -1 that is set using blood level (pharmacokinetic) analysis, followed by stem cell infusion on day 0. The study looks at the best dose and the side effects of melphalan.
NCT04483206.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1 prueba una dosis personalizada de melfalán administrada antes de un trasplante de células madre en personas con mieloma múltiple. Los pacientes reciben melfalán IV en dosis alta durante 30 minutos el día -3, luego una segunda dosis IV de melfalán durante 30 minutos el día -1, ajustada según el análisis de los niveles de melfalán en sangre (farmacocinética), y después la infusión de células madre el día 0. El estudio busca determinar la mejor dosis y los efectos secundarios del melfalán.
who_for: Clinical diagnosis of a plasma cell neoplasm that needs treatment, per the treating physician
Phase A: at least 2 prior lines of therapy and estimated kidney filtration (eGFR by Cockcroft-Gault) above 40 mL/min
Phase B: transplant must be part of first-line therapy
Absolute neutrophil count at least 1000/uL and platelets at least 100,000
ECOG performance status 2 or less (Karnofsky 60% or higher); able to understand and sign informed consent
not_for: Progressive disease or clinical relapse before the planned melphalan infusion on day -3
Serious heart problems, such as NYHA class III or IV heart failure, heart attack within 6 months, or QTc above 480 msec
HIV positive, with limited exceptions; hepatitis B surface antigen positive; or hepatitis C without sustained virologic response
POEMS syndrome, AL amyloidosis, or Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia
Pregnant or breastfeeding

NCT05345002.summary_en: This Phase 2 study tests all-trans retinoic acid (ATRA) combined with retifanlimab, a PD-1 inhibitor, in people with recurrent IDH-mutant glioma. ATRA is taken by mouth at 45 mg/m2 per day in two divided doses on days 1 to 14 of each 28-day cycle, and retifanlimab is given by IV at 500 mg on day 1 of each cycle. Treatment continues until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, or 2 years from the first dose, whichever comes first, and the main outcome is not stated.
NCT05345002.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 evalúa el ácido all-trans retinoico (ATRA) combinado con retifanlimab, un inhibidor de PD-1, en personas con glioma recurrente con mutación IDH. El ATRA se toma por vía oral a 45 mg/m2 al día, en dos dosis divididas, durante los días 1 a 14 de cada ciclo de 28 días, y el retifanlimab se administra por vía intravenosa a 500 mg el día 1 de cada ciclo. El tratamiento continúa hasta la progresión de la enfermedad, toxicidad inaceptable o 2 años desde la primera dosis, lo que ocurra primero, y el resultado principal no está indicado.
who_for: Progressive or recurrent astrocytoma or oligodendroglioma after at least one prior alkylating chemotherapy
Tumor has a known IDH1 or IDH2 mutation confirmed by DNA sequencing
Age 18 or older
Karnofsky performance status of 60 or higher
Measurable disease on MRI for those with contrast-enhancing tumor, or a surgical indication for surgical arms
not_for: Contrast-enhancing tumor in the brainstem or spinal cord
Diffuse leptomeningeal disease
Bevacizumab within the last 3 months
Immunosuppressive medicine other than steroids within 6 months of starting study drug
Active hepatitis B or C, or HIV on antiretroviral therapy

NCT07167381.summary_en: This study tests the xDRIVE Functional Precision Medicine and Artificial Intelligence tumor profiling test in patients with relapsed or refractory cancers in Florida. The test is a diagnostic test, not a drug, and it uses tumor tissue plus a blood or buccal swab sample; results go to the physician, who may use them to guide the next treatment, and how often or how long is not stated. The study measures patient clinical benefit and health economic impacts, as a feasibility study.
NCT07167381.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa la prueba de perfil tumoral xDRIVE de Medicina de Precisión Funcional e Inteligencia Artificial en pacientes con cáncer recidivante o refractario en Florida. La prueba es un examen diagnóstico, no un medicamento, y utiliza una muestra de tejido tumoral más una muestra de sangre o de frotis bucal; los resultados se entregan al médico, quien puede usarlos para guiar el siguiente tratamiento, y la frecuencia o duración no está indicada. El estudio mide el beneficio clínico para el paciente y los impactos económicos en salud, como estudio de factibilidad.
who_for: Recurrent or refractory cancer; adults 18 or older, or children under 18 (ages 7–17 must sign assent).
Received at least one prior line of standard cancer therapy, with treatment and outcome information available.
Adults with sufficient health to undergo cancer therapy (performance status 0, 1, or 2).
Scheduled for or recently had a tumor biopsy, excision, or resection.
Willing to give a blood sample or buccal swab for normal-tissue comparison.
not_for: No malignant tissue available or accessible for testing.
Malignant tissue amount too small (under 0.3 g for resections, or biopsies without malignant tissue).
Insufficient malignant tissue in peripheral blood or bone marrow aspirate samples.
Insufficient health indicators to undergo therapeutic intervention.

NCT07693751.summary_en: This study tests SOT109, an antibody aimed at CDH17 linked to a payload called exatecan, in people with advanced, unresectable or metastatic colorectal cancer. SOT109 is given into a vein (IV) over about 30 minutes (±15 minutes) once every 21 days. The study has two parts, and the record does not state a primary outcome; it is a Phase 1/2 study of safety, pharmacokinetics and preliminary efficacy, with Part A looking at safety and dose levels and Part B comparing two safe dose levels for benefit and risk.
NCT07693751.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa SOT109, un anticuerpo dirigido a CDH17 unido a una carga llamada exatecán, en personas con cáncer colorrectal avanzado, no resecable o metastásico. SOT109 se administra por vena (IV) durante unos 30 minutos (±15 minutos), una vez cada 21 días. El estudio tiene dos partes, y el registro no indica una medida de resultado principal; es un estudio de fase 1/2 de seguridad, farmacocinética y eficacia preliminar, en el que la Parte A evalúa la seguridad y las dosis, y la Parte B compara dos dosis seguras para determinar el equilibrio entre beneficio y riesgo.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older who can give written informed consent.
Advanced unresectable or metastatic colorectal cancer, confirmed by tissue or cell testing.
ECOG performance score 0-1; score of 2 to be discussed with the sponsor.
Progressed on fluoropyrimidines, oxaliplatin, irinotecan and bevacizumab, with no further standard treatment options.
Blood counts, kidney, liver, heart and other lab values within the protocol limits.
not_for: Radiation therapy within 14 days before the first dose, or unrecovered side effects from it.
Systemic therapy for metastatic cancer other than colorectal cancer, apart from listed exceptions.
History of interstitial pneumonitis or pulmonary fibrosis.
Symptomatic central nervous system tumors, or peripheral sensory neuropathy grade 2 or higher.
Recent serious heart events, or a history of inflammatory bowel disease.

NCT07822399.summary_en: The study tests MGC030, an antibody-drug conjugate, in people with advanced solid tumors, including urothelial, colorectal, gastric or gastroesophageal, esophageal, and pancreatic cancer. Study treatment is given initially every 3 weeks, and the route of administration is not stated. The study measures side effects and whether the cancer shrinks, stays stable, or stops progressing, and it is a Phase 1 study.
NCT07822399.summary_es: El estudio evalúa MGC030, un conjugado anticuerpo-fármaco, en personas con tumores sólidos avanzados, incluidos cáncer urotelial, colorrectal, gástrico o de la unión gastroesofágica, esofágico y pancreático. El tratamiento del estudio se administra inicialmente cada 3 semanas, y la vía de administración no está indicada. El estudio mide los efectos secundarios y si el cáncer se reduce, se mantiene estable o deja de progresar, y es un estudio de Fase 1.
who_for: Unresectable, locally advanced or metastatic urothelial, colorectal, gastric/GEJ, esophageal, or pancreatic cancer.
Cancer that is refractory to standard therapy, or for which standard therapy does not exist, is intolerable, or was refused (dose escalation).
Expansion groups require progression after specified prior systemic therapy lines for each cancer type.
At least one lesion measurable by RECIST v1.1.
Available archival or FFPE tumor tissue, or willingness to undergo a biopsy.
not_for: Active brain metastases or leptomeningeal metastases.
Prior stem cell, tissue, or solid organ transplant.
Another malignancy that required treatment within the past 2 years, with listed exceptions.
Prior treatment with topoisomerase 1-based ADCs for cancer.
Active viral, bacterial, or fungal infection.

NCT07558733.summary_en: This study tests sapanisertib and serabelisib (PIKTOR), given with fulvestrant and/or other anticancer therapies, in people with HR+/HER2- advanced or metastatic breast cancer. Serabelisib and sapanisertib are taken by mouth, and fulvestrant is given as an injection into the muscle; how often and for how long are not stated. The study evaluates safety and preliminary effectiveness, and it is a Phase 1/2 dose-escalation trial.
NCT07558733.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa sapanisertib y serabelisib (PIKTOR), administrados con fulvestrant y/u otras terapias contra el cáncer, en personas con cáncer de mama HR+/HER2- avanzado o metastásico. Serabelisib y sapanisertib se toman por vía oral, y fulvestrant se administra como inyección en el músculo; la frecuencia y la duración no se indican. El estudio evalúa la seguridad y la eficacia preliminar, y es un ensayo de escalada de dosis de Fase 1/2.
who_for: Confirmed HR+/HER2- breast cancer.
Advanced or recurrent disease that cannot be cured with surgery or radiation.
Received at least one prior systemic therapy.
At least one measurable or evaluable lesion under RECIST v1.1.
ECOG performance status of 1 or less at screening.
not_for: Triple-negative breast cancer.
Brain or central nervous system metastases, unless treated and off steroids for at least 4 weeks.
Prior PI3K, AKT, mTORC1/2, or dual PI3K/mTOR inhibitor.
Other active malignancy within the past 24 months, with some exceptions.
Concurrent participation in another therapeutic clinical trial.

NCT06529731.summary_en: This study tests interferon gamma-1b (ACTIMMUNE) given together with donor leukocyte infusion (DLI) in adults whose acute myeloid leukemia or myelodysplastic syndromes returned after an allogeneic stem cell transplant. Interferon gamma-1b is given as 100 mcg three times a week for 4 weeks, then the same schedule for 4 more weeks, then 100 mcg weekly for 4 weeks. DLI doses are given based on clinical assessment, with the first dose at 10^6 CD3+ cells/kg and a possible second dose at 10^7 CD3+ cells/kg in the haploidentical cohort. The record does not state a main outcome measure; it is a Phase 2 study that aims to confirm efficacy seen in a prior Phase 1 trial and to evaluate safety.
NCT06529731.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa el interferón gamma-1b (ACTIMMUNE) administrado junto con infusión de linfocitos del donante (DLI) en adultos con leucemia mieloide aguda o síndromes mielodisplásicos que recayeron después de un trasplante alogénico de células madre. El interferón gamma-1b se administra a 100 mcg tres veces por semana durante 4 semanas, luego con el mismo esquema por 4 semanas más, y después 100 mcg semanales por 4 semanas. Las dosis de DLI se administran según la evaluación clínica, con una primera dosis de 10^6 células CD3+/kg y una posible segunda dosis de 10^7 células CD3+/kg en la cohorte de donante haploidéntico. El registro no indica un resultado principal; es un estudio de Fase 2 que busca confirmar la eficacia observada en un estudio previo de Fase 1 y evaluar la seguridad.
who_for: Age 18 years or older.
Acute myeloid leukemia or myelodysplastic syndromes that relapsed after allogeneic stem cell transplant, with measurable disease.
ECOG performance status 0 to 2.
A donor lymphocyte infusion is available, or the donor is willing to undergo apheresis.
Willing to give signed consent, follow study procedures, and use contraception as required.
not_for: Grade 3 or 4 acute GVHD at enrollment, or a history of grade 4 acute GVHD.
Moderate or severe chronic GVHD at enrollment.
Known hypersensitivity to interferon gamma or E. coli-derived products.
Certain heart, lung, seizure, liver, or kidney conditions as listed, such as AST or ALT above 5 times ULN or CrCl below 30 mL/min.
Positive pregnancy test or currently breastfeeding.

NCT07585266.summary_en: The study compares velzatinib with imatinib, the standard treatment, in adults with previously untreated gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST) that have spread or cannot be surgically removed. The method of giving each drug and how long or how often it is given are not stated. The study aims to see whether velzatinib can delay disease worsening and is safe and well tolerated, but the main outcome measure is not stated; this is a Phase 3 study.
NCT07585266.summary_es: El estudio compara velzatinib con imatinib, el tratamiento estándar, en adultos con tumores del estroma gastrointestinal (GIST) sin tratamiento previo que se han diseminado o no se pueden extirpar con cirugía. La forma de administrar cada medicamento y con qué duración o frecuencia se dan no se indica. El estudio busca saber si velzatinib puede retrasar el empeoramiento de la enfermedad y si es seguro y bien tolerado, pero la medida principal de resultado no se indica; es un estudio de Fase 3.
who_for: Adults aged 18 or older, or the legal age of consent where the study takes place.
GIST that is metastatic and/or surgically unresectable, confirmed by biopsy or cytology.
No prior systemic therapy for the metastatic or unresectable GIST.
Tumor tissue can be provided to the central laboratory.
At least one target lesion, with ECOG performance status of 1 or less.
not_for: Another malignancy that progressed or needed active treatment within the past 24 months, with listed exceptions.
Clinically significant GI problems that may alter absorption, or major stomach or bowel resection.
Major surgery within 14 days before the first dose of study treatment.
Untreated or progressing brain or central nervous system metastases.
Clinically significant cardiac disease within 6 months, QTc over 480 ms, or long QT syndrome.

NCT07206056.summary_en: This study tests tulmimetostat (DZR123) given with JSB462 (luxdegalutamide) in men with progressive metastatic castrate resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC). In Part 2, the combination is compared with standard of care. Tulmimetostat and JSB462 are both given once a day (QD); the length of treatment is not stated. The main outcome measure is not stated; the study is Phase I/II.
NCT07206056.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa tulmimetostat (DZR123) combinado con JSB462 (luxdegalutamida) en hombres con cáncer de próstata metastásico resistente a la castración (mCRPC) progresivo. En la Parte 2, la combinación se compara con el tratamiento estándar. Tulmimetostat y JSB462 se administran una vez al día (QD); la duración del tratamiento no se indica. El resultado principal que se mide no se indica; el estudio es de Fase I/II.
who_for: Adult men aged 18 years or older.
Prostate adenocarcinoma without neuroendocrine or small cell features.
At least one metastatic lesion on recent imaging.
Progressive mCRPC with castrate testosterone levels.
Progressed on at least one prior second-generation ARPI (Part 2: taxane-naive in mCRPC).
not_for: Previous treatment with any PRC2 or EED inhibitor.
Previous treatment with an AR-targeting protein degrader.
Known hypersensitivity to study treatment components.
Investigational agent within 28 days before study entry.
Prior radioligand therapy in mCRPC (Part 1a is an exception).

NCT06576037.summary_en: This Phase 1 study tests CBP-1019 combined with FOLFOX, with or without bevacizumab, pembrolizumab, or enzalutamide, in adults with metastatic solid tumors of epithelial origin that overexpress TRPV6. Study drugs are given on an outpatient basis: CBP-1019, oxaliplatin, leucovorin, 5-fluorouracil, bevacizumab, and pembrolizumab are given into a vein (IV), and enzalutamide is taken by mouth, with duration and frequency not stated. The record says the study evaluates safety and efficacy, but no specific primary outcome measure is listed.
NCT06576037.summary_es: Este estudio de Fase 1 evalúa CBP-1019 combinado con FOLFOX, con o sin bevacizumab, pembrolizumab o enzalutamida, en adultos con tumores sólidos metastásicos de origen epitelial que sobreexpresan TRPV6. Los medicamentos del estudio se administran de forma ambulatoria: CBP-1019, oxaliplatino, leucovorina, 5-fluorouracilo, bevacizumab y pembrolizumab se administran por vena (IV), y la enzalutamida se toma por vía oral; la duración y la frecuencia no se indican. El registro indica que el estudio evalúa la seguridad y la eficacia, pero no se enumera una medida de resultado principal específica.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older with metastatic or unresectable epithelial-origin cancer, other than ovarian cancer.
Prior standard therapy received, with disease progression or intolerable toxicity afterward.
Measurable disease of at least 1 cm, except prostate cancer patients who meet specified progression criteria.
Expansion cohorts include metastatic pancreatic or colorectal cancer with an oxaliplatin and irinotecan-free interval of at least 4 months, prior anti-PD-(L)1 t
ECOG performance status of 1 or less, adequate blood counts and organ function, and willingness to provide baseline tumor tissue.
not_for: Active infection requiring IV antibiotics, or symptomatic heart failure (NYHA Class III or IV).
Heart attack, unstable angina, stroke, or transient ischemic attack within 6 months before enrollment.
Congenital long QT syndrome, prior torsade de pointes, or family history of unexplained sudden death.
Known allergy to the study drugs or their components.
Major surgery within 28 days or minor surgery within 7 days before study entry, or a live vaccine within 30 days before the first dose.

NCT07645651.summary_en: This study tests samuraciclib, a CDK7 inhibitor, in people with resectable, borderline resectable, or locally advanced basal pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. Patients take samuraciclib by mouth once a day for 14 days while on study, and treatment continues if the disease does not progress and side effects are acceptable. The stated purpose is to evaluate safety and efficacy; a specific primary outcome is not stated, and the study is listed as Phase 1.
NCT07645651.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa samuraciclib, un inhibidor de CDK7, en personas con adenocarcinoma ductal pancreático basal resecable, limítrofemente resecable o localmente avanzado. Los pacientes toman samuraciclib por vía oral una vez al día durante 14 días mientras están en el estudio, y el tratamiento continúa si la enfermedad no progresa y los efectos secundarios son aceptables. El propósito indicado es evaluar la seguridad y la eficacia; no se indica un desenlace principal específico, y el estudio figura como Fase 1.
who_for: Confirmed pancreatic adenocarcinoma classified as basal (GATA6-negative and HMGA2-positive tumor).
Resectable, borderline resectable, or locally advanced pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma with no metastatic disease.
Age 18 or older and able to understand and sign written consent.
ECOG performance status 0 to 1.
Blood counts, kidney function, and liver function within the stated limits.
not_for: Prior radiation.
Unable to tolerate oral medication, per the principal investigator.
Currently receiving other investigational agents.
Pregnant, breastfeeding, or nursing.
Active infection, uncontrolled illness, or known active hepatitis B or C.

NCT05766371.summary_en: This study tests pembrolizumab given together with 177Lu-PSMA-617, a PSMA-targeted radionuclide therapy, in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. Pembrolizumab is given IV at 400 mg every 6 weeks, and 177Lu-PSMA-617 is given by IV infusion at 7.4 GBq on Cycle 1 Day 1 and 6 weeks later, then at the first later PSA rise, for up to six total doses with at least 6 weeks between doses. The main outcome is not stated; this is a Phase 2 study.
NCT05766371.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa pembrolizumab administrado junto con 177Lu-PSMA-617, una terapia con radionúclidos dirigida a PSMA, en hombres con cáncer de próstata metastásico resistente a la castración. El pembrolizumab se administra por vía intravenosa a 400 mg cada 6 semanas, y el 177Lu-PSMA-617 se administra por infusión intravenosa de 7.4 GBq el Día 1 del Ciclo 1 y 6 semanas después, y luego en el primer aumento posterior del PSA, hasta seis dosis en total, con al menos 6 semanas entre dosis. El resultado principal no está indicado; este es un estudio de Fase 2.
who_for: Men 18 years or older with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer that is progressing.
Prior progression on at least one second generation androgen signaling inhibitor.
At least one PSMA PET-avid lesion on the screening scan.
ECOG performance status of 1 or lower.
Adequate blood cell counts, liver function, and kidney function.
not_for: De novo small cell neuroendocrine prostate cancer.
Prior anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1, or anti-PD-L2 therapy, or other T-cell checkpoint agent therapy.
Prior PSMA-directed radiotherapy.
Untreated brain metastases at study entry.
Active autoimmune disease that required systemic treatment within the past 2 years.

NCT05751434.summary_en: This Phase 2 study tests exercise therapy, mainly walking, in men with localized prostate cancer who are on active surveillance. Participants do individualized walking, up to 5 sessions per week, for a total of 225 to 300 minutes per week, until their next standard prostate biopsy, which is about 6 to 12 months away. The study aims to measure effects on molecular, imaging, and pathology markers compared with usual care.
NCT05751434.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 evalúa la terapia con ejercicio, principalmente caminar, en hombres con cáncer de próstata localizado que están en vigilancia activa. Los participantes hacen caminatas individualizadas, hasta 5 sesiones por semana, con un total de 225 a 300 minutos por semana, hasta su próxima biopsia de próstata estándar, que ocurre en unos 6 a 12 meses. El estudio busca medir los efectos sobre marcadores moleculares, radiológicos y patológicos en comparación con la atención habitual.
who_for: Men aged 18 or older.
Histologically confirmed localized prostate cancer undergoing active surveillance.
Not meeting national exercise guidelines (under 150 minutes per week of moderate or vigorous exercise) based on 7-day tracking.
Cleared for exercise by exercise physiologist ECG review and the PAR-Q+ questionnaire.
BMI under 40 kg/m².
not_for: Enrolled in another program that may alter exercise effects on tumor outcomes, such as a weight loss program.
Neoadjuvant anticancer treatment of any kind for prostate cancer in the last 5 years.
Systemic anticancer therapy in the last 15 years.
Distant metastatic malignancy of any kind.
Other condition or illness that the investigator judges makes the person a poor candidate.

NCT05498428.summary_en: This Phase 2 study tests amivantamab given under the skin as a co-formulation with recombinant human hyaluronidase PH20, in combination with other drugs, for advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer, including EGFR-mutated disease. Amivantamab is given as a subcutaneous injection, and in the first-line EGFR exon19del or L858R cohort it is given on Cycle 1 Days 1, 8, 15 and 22 and then on Days 1 and 15 of each 28-day cycle, with lazertinib 240 mg by mouth once daily. The study measures anti-tumor activity and safety.
NCT05498428.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 prueba amivantamab administrado debajo de la piel como una co-formulación con la hialuronidasa humana recombinante PH20, en combinación con otros medicamentos, para el cáncer de pulmón de células no pequeñas avanzado o metastásico, incluida la enfermedad con mutación de EGFR. Amivantamab se administra como inyección subcutánea y, en la cohorte de primera línea con mutación EGFR exón 19 o L858R, se aplica en el Ciclo 1, días 1, 8, 15 y 22, y luego en los días 1 y 15 de cada ciclo de 28 días, junto con lazertinib 240 mg por vía oral una vez al día. El estudio mide la actividad antitumoral y la seguridad.
who_for: Advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer that cannot be cured with surgery or chemoradiation.
EGFR exon 19 deletion or exon 21 L858R mutation (most cohorts).
EGFR exon 20 insertion mutation (cohort 2).
No prior systemic therapy for advanced or metastatic lung cancer (cohorts 1, 2, 5 and 6).
Disease progressed after osimertinib or after amivantamab plus lazertinib (cohorts 3, 3b and 7); ECOG 0 or 1.
not_for: Interstitial lung disease, including drug-induced ILD or radiation pneumonitis.
History of allergy to any excipients of the study products in the enrolled cohort.
Squamous non-small cell lung cancer (cohorts 2, 3, 3b and 7).
Cohort 4 requires current amivantamab IV every 2 weeks for at least 8 weeks.
Remaining exclusion criteria not stated (record text is cut off).

NCT06134232.summary_en: This Phase 2 study tests one extra infusion of sipuleucel-T, given after commercial PROVENGE, in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. Sipuleucel-T is given as an intravenous infusion, one time, 6 to 9 months after receiving commercial PROVENGE. The study aims to measure immune response.
NCT06134232.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 evalúa una infusión adicional de sipuleucel-T, administrada después de PROVENGE comercial, en hombres con cáncer de próstata metastásico resistente a la castración. Sipuleucel-T se administra por vía intravenosa, una sola vez, entre 6 y 9 meses después de recibir PROVENGE comercial. El estudio busca medir la respuesta inmunitaria.
who_for: Men aged 18 or older with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer that is asymptomatic or minimally symptomatic
Clinically indicated for PROVENGE and qualified for an on-label PROVENGE infusion
Received all 3 PROVENGE infusions before randomization
Gave written informed consent and have estimated life expectancy of at least 12 months
not_for: Not clinically indicated for PROVENGE treatment
Need for systemic chronic immunosuppressive therapy, such as steroids, GM-CSF or G-CSF, or recent vaccinations
Uncontrolled illness, including active infection or psychiatric illness that would limit study compliance
Currently on experimental or investigational therapy

NCT07643012.summary_en: This study tests moderately hypofractionated, MR-guided adaptive pelvic intensity-modulated radiation therapy (IMRT) given as adjuvant treatment for endometrial cancer. The radiation is delivered by an MR-linac in a total dose of 42 Gy over 15 fractions, with daily MRI guidance and plan adjustments as needed, and vaginal brachytherapy may follow at the physician's discretion. The study aims to evaluate safety, tolerability and preliminary efficacy.
NCT07643012.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa la radioterapia pélvica de intensidad modulada (IMRT) adaptativa guiada por resonancia magnética, con dosis moderadamente hipofraccionada, como tratamiento adyuvante para el cáncer de endometrio. La radiación se administra con un equipo MR-linac, en una dosis total de 42 Gy en 15 fracciones, con resonancia magnética diaria y ajustes del plan según sea necesario; la braquiterapia vaginal puede aplicarse después, a criterio del médico. El estudio busca evaluar la seguridad, la tolerabilidad y la eficacia preliminar.
who_for: Confirmed endometrial carcinoma of an eligible type (endometrioid, serous, clear cell, carcinosarcoma or dedifferentiated).
Indication for adjuvant pelvic radiation based on ASTRO and GOG-99 high-intermediate-risk features.
Age 18 or older and able to give informed consent.
Eligible for adjuvant systemic therapy if needed, with at least 3 weeks between chemotherapy and radiation.
Willing and able to complete the EORTC QLQ-C30 and EN-24 questionnaires in a validated language.
not_for: Prior pelvic radiotherapy.
Contraindication to pelvic radiotherapy, such as active connective tissue disorder or inflammatory bowel disease.
Hip prosthesis that would compromise treatment planning or delivery.

NCT06758401.summary_en: This Phase 3 study compares sigvotatug vedotin plus pembrolizumab with pembrolizumab alone as first-line treatment for non-small cell lung cancer in which at least 50% of tumor cells express PD-L1. All participants receive pembrolizumab by IV infusion once every 6 weeks for up to about two years, and half also receive sigvotatug vedotin by IV infusion once every 2 weeks, continued until the cancer is no longer responding. The main outcome is not stated; the study is Phase 3.
NCT06758401.summary_es: Este estudio de Fase 3 compara sigvotatug vedotin más pembrolizumab con pembrolizumab solo como tratamiento de primera línea para el cáncer de pulmón de células no pequeñas en el que al menos el 50% de las células tumorales expresan PD-L1. Todos los participantes reciben pembrolizumab por infusión intravenosa una vez cada 6 semanas durante hasta aproximadamente dos años, y la mitad también recibe sigvotatug vedotin por infusión intravenosa una vez cada 2 semanas, que continúa mientras el cáncer siga respondiendo. El resultado principal no se indica en el registro; el estudio es de Fase 3.
who_for: Stage IIIB or IIIC NSCLC that is not a candidate for surgery or definitive chemoradiation, or stage IV NSCLC.
PD-L1 expression in at least 50% of tumor cells, by local testing.
Appropriate candidate for pembrolizumab monotherapy per local guidelines.
Measurable disease based on RECIST v1.1.
Age 18 years or older.
not_for: Known EGFR, ALK, ROS1, NTRK, BRAF, RET, or MET alterations with approved first-line therapy available locally.
Large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma.
Prior systemic therapy for advanced NSCLC, including anti-PD-(L)1 therapy, with exceptions for adjuvant or neoadjuvant treatment.
Active central nervous system lesions, with some exceptions for treated or small brain metastases.
Noninfectious or drug-induced interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis, or DLCO below 50% predicted.

NCT06469281.summary_en: This study tests 27T51, an experimental CAR T cell therapy that targets the MUC16 protein, in adults with recurrent or hard-to-treat epithelial ovarian, primary peritoneal, or fallopian tube cancer. 27T51 is given by intravenous (IV) infusion, alone or with cemiplimab and bevacizumab, which are also given by IV infusion; how often and for how long is not stated. The record does not state a main outcome measure; it is a Phase 1 study with stated aims of testing safety and finding the highest dose without unacceptable side effects.
NCT06469281.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa 27T51, una terapia experimental con células CAR T que actúa contra la proteína MUC16, en adultos con cáncer de ovario epitelial, carcinoma peritoneal primario o cáncer de trompa de Falopio recurrente o difícil de tratar. El 27T51 se administra por infusión intravenosa (IV), solo o con cemiplimab y bevacizumab, que también se administran por infusión IV; la frecuencia y la duración no están indicadas. El registro no indica una medida de resultado principal; es un estudio de Fase 1 con objetivos declarados de evaluar la seguridad y encontrar la dosis más alta sin efectos secundarios inaceptables.
who_for: ECOG performance status of 1 or lower
Histological diagnosis of epithelial ovarian, primary peritoneal, or fallopian tube cancer
Recurrent or refractory disease, as described in the protocol
Serum CA-125 at least 2 times the upper limit of normal
At least one measurable tumor lesion by RECIST 1.1 and expected survival of at least 3 months
not_for: Inadequate heart, kidney, or liver function, as described in the protocol
Absolute lymphocyte count below 100 cells/μL at time of leukapheresis
Grade 2 or higher hemorrhage within 30 days, or inadequate coagulation parameters
Clinically relevant central nervous system pathology, as described in the protocol
Significant autoimmune disease needing systemic immunosuppression within 2 years, or prior cellular or gene therapy

NCT04871607.summary_en: This Phase 2 study tests yttrium-90 labeled anti-CD25 antibody combined with BEAM chemotherapy before stem cell transplant in adults with Hodgkin lymphoma that is refractory or has relapsed. The antibody is given by IV on day -14, and chemotherapy (carmustine, etoposide, cytarabine, and melphalan) is given from day -6 to day -1. Stem cells are infused on day 0, and G-CSF is given from day 5 until neutrophil recovery or as the treating physician judges. The main outcome is not stated in the record; the study is listed as Phase 2.
NCT04871607.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 evalúa un anticuerpo anti-CD25 marcado con itrio-90 combinado con quimioterapia BEAM antes de un trasplante de células madre en adultos con linfoma de Hodgkin refractario o recidivante. El anticuerpo se administra por vía intravenosa el día -14, y la quimioterapia (carmustina, etopósido, citarabina y melfalán) se administra del día -6 al día -1. Las células madre se infunden el día 0, y el G-CSF se administra desde el día 5 hasta la recuperación de neutrófilos o según el criterio del médico tratante. El resultado principal no se indica en el registro; el estudio aparece como fase 2.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older with Karnofsky performance status of 70% or higher and life expectancy of at least 6 months.
Histologically confirmed Hodgkin lymphoma that is high-risk relapsed or refractory, such as primary refractory disease or relapse within 1 year of frontline the
Not in complete remission at the time of transplant, or relapse after PD-1 blockade or brentuximab vedotin as initial therapy.
At least 2.0 x 10^6 CD34 cells/kg of own stem cells collected by apheresis before enrollment.
Adequate kidney, liver, heart, and lung function, and agreement to use effective birth control during the study.
not_for: Planned brentuximab vedotin consolidation after transplant.
Prior high-dose chemotherapy with autologous stem cell transplant, or prior allogeneic transplant.
Active cancer other than Hodgkin lymphoma, or myelodysplasia.
Active hepatitis B or C, or hepatitis B surface antigen positive; HIV-positive unless criteria are met.
Pregnancy or breastfeeding, or lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma.

NCT05472792.summary_en: This study compares two treatments after lumpectomy for low-risk breast cancer in women age 65 and older: accelerated partial breast irradiation alone, or endocrine therapy alone. Accelerated partial breast irradiation is given as 5 fractions every other day to the lumpectomy cavity, and endocrine therapy is chosen by the treating medical oncologist with an aim of 5 years, as tolerated. The main outcome is quality of life at 1 year after lumpectomy, and this is a Phase 2 study.
NCT05472792.summary_es: Este estudio compara dos tratamientos después de la lumpectomía en mujeres de 65 años o más con cáncer de mama de bajo riesgo: radioterapia parcial acelerada de la mama sola, o terapia endocrina sola. La radioterapia parcial acelerada se administra en 5 fracciones, un día sí y otro no, en la cavidad de la lumpectomía. La terapia endocrina la elige el oncólogo tratante, con una duración objetivo de 5 años, según la tolerancia de la paciente. El resultado principal es la calidad de vida a 1 año después de la lumpectomía, y es un estudio de fase 2.
who_for: Women age 65 or older with newly diagnosed invasive breast cancer.
Pathological T1 stage tumor, grade 1 or 2, and node-negative.
Estrogen or progesterone receptor positive (at least 10%).
HER2 negative by the stated lab criteria.
Breast-conserving surgery completed, with final margins of at least 2 mm and no lymphovascular invasion.
not_for: Chemotherapy before or after surgery during the study.
Current anti-hormone treatment, or hormone replacement not stopped within 30 days of randomization.
Multifocal or multicentric tumor, or synchronous bilateral breast cancer.
Clinical or imaging evidence of distant spread, or prior breast or thoracic radiation.
Autoimmune conditions with radiation risks, or uncontrolled medical conditions.

NCT06169371.summary_en: This Phase 4 study tests abemaciclib, given with endocrine therapy, as adjuvant treatment for early-stage, hormone receptor-positive (HR+), HER2-negative breast cancer. Patients take abemaciclib by mouth twice a day, starting at 50 mg in week 1, 100 mg in week 2, and 150 mg from week 3. After study treatment, patients may stay on abemaciclib plus endocrine therapy at their treating providers' discretion. The main outcome measure is not stated; this is a single-arm Phase 4 study.
NCT06169371.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 4 evalúa abemaciclib, administrado junto con terapia endocrina, como tratamiento adyuvante para el cáncer de mama temprano, positivo para receptores hormonales (HR+) y negativo para HER2. Los pacientes toman abemaciclib por vía oral dos veces al día, comenzando con 50 mg en la semana 1, 100 mg en la semana 2 y 150 mg desde la semana 3. Después del tratamiento del estudio, los pacientes pueden continuar con abemaciclib más terapia endocrina según el criterio de sus médicos tratantes. El resultado principal no está indicado en el registro; se trata de un estudio de fase 4 de un solo brazo.
who_for: Performance status score of 0 to 2 on the ECOG scale.
Early-stage HR-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer confirmed by biopsy and prescribed adjuvant abemaciclib.
Able to give written informed consent and HIPAA authorization.
Women who could become pregnant must have a negative pregnancy test and not be pregnant or breastfeeding.
Able to understand and follow study procedures for the full length of the study.
not_for: Chronic history of diarrhea.
Active infection requiring systemic therapy.
Uncontrolled HIV/AIDS or active viral hepatitis.
Pregnant or nursing.
Prior or current cancer that could interfere with safety or efficacy assessment, as judged by the treating oncologist.

NCT07617363.summary_en: This phase 1 study tests ATRN-119 (also called mosipasertib), an ATR inhibitor taken by mouth, alone and with decitabine, in people with TP53-mutated acute myeloid leukemia or higher-risk myelodysplastic syndrome. ATRN-119 is taken by mouth once a day on days 1 to 28 of each 28-day cycle, and decitabine is given by vein on days 1 to 5 of each cycle in the combination part, with up to 24 cycles allowed. The main goal is to find the maximum tolerated dose and recommended dose for expansion of ATRN-119 plus decitabine.
NCT07617363.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1 evalúa ATRN-119 (también llamado mosipasertib), un inhibidor de ATR que se toma por vía oral, solo y con decitabina, en personas con leucemia mieloide aguda o síndrome mielodisplásico de alto riesgo con mutación en TP53. ATRN-119 se toma por vía oral una vez al día en los días 1 a 28 de cada ciclo de 28 días, y la decitabina se administra por vena en los días 1 a 5 de cada ciclo en la parte de combinación, con un máximo de 24 ciclos. El objetivo principal es encontrar la dosis máxima tolerada y la dosis recomendada para la expansión de ATRN-119 más decitabina.
who_for: Diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia or higher-risk myelodysplastic syndrome.
TP53 mutation, TP53 or chromosome 17p deletion, or high p53 staining, shown by standard tests.
Relapsed or not responding after prior treatment, meeting the stated prior-therapy criteria.
At least 18 years old with performance status of 2 or better.
Adequate liver and kidney function, and agreement to use contraception if able to become pregnant or father a child.
not_for: Active leukemia involvement of the brain or central nervous system that needs treatment.
Active graft-versus-host disease needing systemic immunosuppressive therapy, other than low-dose steroids.
Currently receiving any other investigational agent.
Pregnant or breastfeeding.
Uncontrolled infection, symptomatic heart failure, or other uncontrolled illness that the study team considers significant.

NCT06682793.summary_en: This study tests A2B395, an allogeneic logic-gated CAR T-cell product, in adults with solid tumors that express EGFR and have lost HLA-A*02, including colorectal, lung, head and neck, breast, and kidney cancers. Participants receive a preconditioning lymphodepletion regimen, then a single intravenous dose of A2B395 on day 0. The Phase 1 main question is the recommended dose that is safe for patients, and the Phase 2 main question is whether that dose kills solid tumor cells and protects healthy cells.
NCT06682793.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa A2B395, un producto de células CAR T alogénicas de compuerta lógica, en adultos con tumores sólidos que expresan EGFR y han perdido HLA-A*02, incluidos cáncer colorrectal, de pulmón, de cabeza y cuello, de mama y de riñón. Los participantes reciben un régimen de preacondicionamiento con linfodepleción y luego una sola dosis intravenosa de A2B395 el día 0. La pregunta principal de la Fase 1 es la dosis recomendada que es segura para los pacientes, y la de la Fase 2 es si esa dosis destruye las células tumorales y protege las células sanas.
who_for: Enrolled in the BASECAMP-1 study, with tumor tissue showing HLA-A*02 loss by NGS.
Recurrent, unresectable, locally advanced, or metastatic CRC, NSCLC, HNSCC, TNBC, RCC, or other EGFR-expressing solid tumors.
Measurable disease, with lesions of at least 1.0 cm by CT.
ECOG performance status of 0 to 1 and life expectancy of at least 3 months.
Willing to follow the study schedule, including long-term safety follow-up.
not_for: Disease suitable for local therapy or standard therapy that is therapeutic and not palliative.
Prior allogeneic stem cell transplant or prior solid organ transplant.
Cancer therapy within 3 weeks, or radiotherapy within 28 days, of A2B395 infusion.
Significant cardiac disease within 6 months, or new symptomatic PE or DVT within 3 months.
Pregnant or breastfeeding, or of childbearing potential and not willing to use birth control through 6 months after infusion.
cancer_types: head and neck squamous cell carcinoma

NCT07602842.summary_en: This study is testing IDP-001, a drug given to people with advanced or metastatic squamous and non-squamous lung cancer and other squamous cell solid tumors. IDP-001 is given as an intravenous (IV) infusion, and how often and for how long are not stated. The study measures safety, tolerability, how the drug moves through the body (pharmacokinetics), and early signs of antitumor activity.
NCT07602842.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa IDP-001, un medicamento que se administra a personas con cáncer de pulmón avanzado o metastásico, de tipo escamoso y no escamoso, y otros tumores sólidos de células escamosas. IDP-001 se administra por infusión intravenosa (IV), y no se indica con qué frecuencia ni durante cuánto tiempo. El estudio mide la seguridad, la tolerabilidad, cómo se distribuye el medicamento en el cuerpo (farmacocinética) y las primeras señales de actividad antitumoral.
who_for: Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0 to 1
Histologically confirmed advanced, metastatic, or recurrent solid tumor not amenable to surgery or other approved therapy
Measurable disease per RECIST v1.1
Willing to provide tumor biopsies
Life expectancy greater than 12 weeks
not_for: Clinically significant cardiac disease
Active hepatitis B, hepatitis C, or HIV, or uncontrolled infection needing IV treatment
Active autoimmune disease
Pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning pregnancy
History of interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis requiring systemic steroids
cancer_types: head and neck squamous cell carcinoma

NCT06010342.summary_en: This study tests TL118 in solid tumors that have an NTRK gene fusion. TL118 is taken by mouth as a capsule, 252 mg twice daily, in 28-day cycles. The main goal is to evaluate how well TL118 works (efficacy); the specific outcome measure is not stated, and this is a Phase 2 study.
NCT06010342.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa TL118 en tumores sólidos que tienen una fusión del gen NTRK. TL118 se toma por vía oral en cápsulas, 252 mg dos veces al día, en ciclos de 28 días. El objetivo principal es evaluar qué tan bien funciona TL118 (eficacia); la medida específica de resultado no se indica, y es un estudio de Fase 2.
who_for: Adults aged 18 years or older.
Locally advanced or metastatic solid tumor with an NTRK1, NTRK2 or NTRK3 gene fusion, without a second cancer driver.
Disease progressed during or after prior treatment, or not suitable for standard therapy in the investigator's opinion.
At least one measurable lesion.
ECOG score of 0, 1 or 2, and life expectancy over 3 months.
not_for: Systemic anti-tumor therapy within 3 weeks before enrollment, or immunotherapy within 4 weeks.
Prior TRK inhibitor treatment, except stopped for less than 28 days due to intolerable toxicity.
Active central nervous system metastases.
Other primary malignant tumors within 3 years, with listed exceptions.
Uncontrolled active infection, or unresolved toxicity above Grade 1 from prior therapy.

NCT06850623.summary_en: This study tests Acoustic Cluster Therapy (ACT) with the drug PS101 and ultrasound, given together with modified FOLFIRINOX chemotherapy, for locally advanced pancreatic cancer. How the treatment is given, and how often or for how long, is not stated. The main outcome measure is not stated; this is a Phase 2 study.
NCT06850623.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa la Terapia Acústica por Racimos (ACT, por sus siglas en inglés) con el medicamento PS101 y ultrasonido, administrada junto con quimioterapia FOLFIRINOX modificada, para el cáncer de páncreas localmente avanzado. No se indica cómo se administra el tratamiento, ni con qué frecuencia o por cuánto tiempo. No se indica la medida de resultado principal; este es un estudio de Fase 2.
who_for: Not suitable for primary curative surgery, with inoperable locally advanced or borderline resectable pancreatic cancer
Considered suitable for mFOLFIRINOX by the investigator
Aged 18 years or older
not_for: Any prior anti-cancer treatment for pancreatic cancer, such as chemotherapy, surgery or radiation

NCT06500273.summary_en: This study tests cemacabtagene ansegedleucel (cema-cel), an allogeneic CD19 CAR T cell therapy, as consolidation for adults with large B-cell lymphoma who have minimal residual disease after first-line therapy. Participants who are randomized to treatment receive cema-cel after a lymphodepletion regimen of fludarabine and cyclophosphamide; the dose schedule and treatment duration are not stated. The study assesses efficacy and safety compared with observation, and the primary outcome is not stated; it is a Phase 2 trial.
NCT06500273.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa cemacabtagene ansegedleucel (cema-cel), una terapia con células CAR T alogénicas dirigidas a CD19, como consolidación en adultos con linfoma de células B grandes que tienen enfermedad residual mínima después de la primera línea de tratamiento. Los participantes asignados al tratamiento reciben cema-cel después de un régimen de linfodepleción con fludarabina y ciclofosfamida; el esquema de dosis y la duración del tratamiento no se indican. El estudio evalúa la eficacia y la seguridad en comparación con la observación, el resultado principal no se indica, y es un ensayo de Fase 2.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older with large B-cell lymphoma confirmed by pathology.
Completed standard first-line therapy with complete response, or partial response suitable for observation, on PET/CT.
Positive minimal residual disease result on the Foresight CLARITY test.
ECOG performance status of 0 or 1.
Adequate blood, kidney, liver, lung, and heart function.
not_for: Central nervous system involvement, transformed lymphoma, or T-cell/histiocyte rich large B-cell lymphoma.
Prior treatment with anti-CD19 targeted therapy.
Anti-cancer treatment, including radiation, after end-of-treatment PET/CT or MRD testing.
Active clinically significant autoimmune disease, or active systemic infection requiring systemic treatment.
Another primary malignancy or bone marrow disorder within 3 years before enrollment.

NCT07283822.summary_en: This phase 2 study tests ruxolitinib added to pembrolizumab in adults with relapsed or refractory Hodgkin or non-Hodgkin lymphoma. Ruxolitinib is taken by mouth at 20 mg twice daily, and pembrolizumab is given into a vein at 200 mg every 21 days, both for as long as the disease responds, up to one year (17 cycles). The record does not state a primary outcome measure; its stated purpose is to determine whether the combination is safe and effective.
NCT07283822.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 evalúa ruxolitinib añadido a pembrolizumab en adultos con linfoma de Hodgkin o no Hodgkin recidivante o refractario. El ruxolitinib se toma por vía oral a 20 mg dos veces al día, y el pembrolizumab se administra por vena a 200 mg cada 21 días, ambos mientras la enfermedad responda, hasta un año (17 ciclos). El registro no indica una medida de resultado principal; su objetivo declarado es determinar si la combinación es segura y eficaz.
who_for: Relapsed or refractory Hodgkin, PMBCL, gray zone, or T-cell lymphoma, as listed in the record.
Received at least one prior systemic therapy line; some subtypes require prior CD30-directed therapy.
Age 18 to 95 years.
Measurable disease on PET-CT performed within 4 weeks.
ECOG 0-2 or Karnofsky score of 50 or higher, with adequate blood counts and organ function.
not_for: Diagnosis of adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma.
Active central nervous system disease.
Autoimmune disease that requires systemic treatment.
Pregnant or breastfeeding, or expected to conceive during the study.
Severe (grade 3 or higher) hypersensitivity to pembrolizumab or ruxolitinib.

NCT06841354.summary_en: This Phase 3 study tests sacituzumab tirumotecan (Sac-TMT, MK-2870) alone or with pembrolizumab (MK-3475) in people with previously untreated, locally recurrent unresectable or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer. Sac-TMT is given by IV infusion at 4 mg/kg every 2 weeks until disease progression, toxicity or discontinuation, and pembrolizumab is given by IV infusion at 400 mg every 6 weeks for up to 18 doses (up to about 2 years) in the combination arm, while the comparison arm receives physician's choice chemotherapy. The main goal is to learn whether people live longer overall or live longer without the cancer growing or spreading, compared with chemotherapy.
NCT06841354.summary_es: Este estudio de Fase 3 evalúa sacituzumab tirumotecan (Sac-TMT, MK-2870) solo o con pembrolizumab (MK-3475) en personas con cáncer de mama triple negativo, localmente recurrente no resecable o metastásico, que no han recibido tratamiento previo. Sac-TMT se administra por infusión intravenosa a 4 mg/kg cada 2 semanas hasta progresión de la enfermedad, toxicidad o suspensión, y pembrolizumab se administra por infusión intravenosa a 400 mg cada 6 semanas, hasta 18 dosis (hasta unos 2 años) en el brazo de combinación, mientras que el brazo de comparación recibe quimioterapia elegida por el médico. El objetivo principal es saber si las personas viven más tiempo en general o más tiempo sin que el cáncer crezca o se propague, en comparación con la quimioterapia.
who_for: Locally recurrent unresectable or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer that cannot be treated with curative intent
No prior systemic treatment for locally recurrent unresectable or metastatic breast cancer
Candidate for pembrolizumab plus paclitaxel, nab-paclitaxel, or gemcitabine plus carboplatin
Prior early-stage treatment completed at least 6 months before first recurrence
Hepatitis B or C allowed if antiviral treatment or viral control criteria are met
not_for: Breast cancer that can be treated with curative intent
Triple-negative breast cancer with PD-L1 CPS 10 or higher
Grade 2 or higher peripheral neuropathy
Known active brain metastases or carcinomatous meningitis (stable treated brain metastases allowed)
Active or prior inflammatory bowel disease, or severe dry eye or corneal disease

NCT06343805.summary_en: This Phase 1 study tests LY5830966, a type II JAK2 inhibitor, in people with myelofibrosis who were previously treated with a type I JAK2 inhibitor. LY5830966 is taken by mouth at several dose levels, and the duration and how often it is taken are not stated. The study measures safety, tolerability, how the drug moves through the body (pharmacokinetics), clinical activity, and changes in biomarkers.
NCT06343805.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1 evalúa LY5830966, un inhibidor de JAK2 de tipo II, en personas con mielofibrosis que recibieron antes un inhibidor de JAK2 de tipo I. LY5830966 se toma por vía oral en varios niveles de dosis, y la duración y la frecuencia no se indican. El estudio mide la seguridad, la tolerabilidad, cómo el medicamento se distribuye en el organismo, la actividad clínica y los cambios en los biomarcadores.
who_for: Diagnosis of primary myelofibrosis, post-polycythemia vera myelofibrosis, or post-essential thrombocythemia myelofibrosis.
Previously treated with at least one type I JAK2 inhibitor, with no response or relapse after a response.
Estimated spleen volume of at least 450 cubic centimeters.
Symptom score requirement on the MFSAF form (total symptom score of 10 or more, or at least 2 symptoms scored 3 or more).
Age 18 or older with ECOG performance score of 0 to 3.
not_for: Splenectomy or splenic irradiation within the past 3 months.
Need for a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor as a concomitant medication.
Peripheral neuropathy of grade 2 or higher.
Active, uncontrolled systemic infection or active hepatitis B or C.
Chemotherapy in the previous 4 weeks, or a history of noninfectious pneumonitis or interstitial lung disease.

NCT07400029.summary_en: This study tests obecabtagene autoleucel (obe-cel) as consolidation treatment in adults with B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) that is in first complete remission without measurable residual disease. It is given as an infusion about 3 days (plus or minus 1 day) after lymphodepleting chemotherapy, and the number of doses and total treatment length are not stated. The main outcome measure is not stated; this is a Phase II study.
NCT07400029.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa obecabtagene autoleucel (obe-cel) como tratamiento de consolidación en adultos con leucemia linfoblástica aguda (LLA) de células B que está en primera remisión completa sin enfermedad residual medible. Se administra como infusión aproximadamente 3 días (más o menos 1 día) después de la quimioterapia linfodepletiva, y el número de dosis y la duración total del tratamiento no se indican. La medida principal de resultado no se indica; este es un estudio de Fase II.
who_for: Adults aged 40 or older; ages 30-39 allowed with high-risk comorbidities or poor chemotherapy tolerability
CD19-positive B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia
In MRD-negative complete remission or complete remission with incomplete hematologic recovery at screening
Adequate liver, kidney, oxygen and heart function, and ECOG performance status 0-2
Philadelphia chromosome-negative or positive disease (Ph-positive is an exploratory cohort)
not_for: Burkitt leukemia or lymphoma
Measurable extramedullary (outside the bone marrow) disease at screening
Recent high-dose corticosteroids or certain other recent cancer medicines, within stated time limits
Uncontrolled active infection at leukapheresis or CAR T cell infusion
Positive tests for HIV, hepatitis B or C, HTLV, or syphilis

NCT05879146.summary_en: This Phase 2 study tests nirogacestat, a drug taken by mouth, in adults with desmoid tumors (also called aggressive fibromatosis). Participants take nirogacestat every day in each 28-day cycle, either once a day or twice a day about 12 hours apart, depending on when they enroll. The record does not state a main outcome; it says the study aims to learn about the safety and effects of the drug.
NCT05879146.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 prueba nirogacestat, un medicamento que se toma por vía oral, en adultos con tumores desmoides (también llamados fibromatosis agresiva). Los participantes toman nirogacestat todos los días durante cada ciclo de 28 días, una vez al día o dos veces al día con unas 12 horas de diferencia, según la fecha de inscripción. El registro no indica el resultado principal; describe el objetivo del estudio como conocer la seguridad y los efectos del medicamento.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older.
Desmoid tumor confirmed by tissue exam, with tumor growth on imaging within the past 18 months.
New or previously treated disease; prior treatment must have stopped at least 28 days earlier.
ECOG performance status of 2 or better.
Adequate blood, liver and kidney test results, and able to swallow tablets.
not_for: Pregnant or breastfeeding women.
Known allergy to nirogacestat or its ingredients.
Familial adenomatous polyposis.
Unable to have repeated biopsies or MRI scans.
Brain metastases or another cancer that could interfere with the study.

NCT07079631.summary_en: This study tests BNT314 together with pumitamig (BNT327) and chemotherapy in people with metastatic colorectal cancer. Most study drugs are given by intravenous infusion, and one chemotherapy drug can be given by mouth; how long or how often is not stated. The main outcome measured is not stated in the record; the study is Phase 1/2.
NCT07079631.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa BNT314 en combinación con pumitamig (BNT327) y quimioterapia en personas con cáncer colorrectal metastásico. La mayoría de los medicamentos del estudio se administran por infusión intravenosa, y un medicamento de quimioterapia puede tomarse por vía oral; la duración o la frecuencia no se indican. El resultado principal que se mide no se indica en el registro; el estudio es de fase 1/2.
who_for: Unresectable adenocarcinoma of the colon or rectum, confirmed by tumor tissue
Non-MSI-H or pMMR colorectal cancer confirmed by approved or local testing
Measurable disease according to RECIST v1.1
ECOG performance status of 0 or 1 and life expectancy of at least 12 weeks
Age 18 years or older
not_for: Confirmed MSI-H or dMMR colorectal cancer
Prior EpCAM or 4-1BB targeted therapy or immunotherapy
Prior immune checkpoint inhibitor or PD-L1/VEGF bispecific antibody
Candidate for locoregional treatment with curative (radical) intent, per investigator
Left ventricular ejection fraction below 50%

NCT04623931.summary_en: This phase II trial tests temozolomide and radiation therapy in adults with IDH wildtype gliomas, including IDH wildtype glioblastoma. Patients take temozolomide by mouth daily during 6 weeks of radiation therapy given 5 days a week, then continue temozolomide by mouth for 12 months if the disease does not progress and side effects are acceptable. The main outcome is not stated in the record; this is a phase II trial.
NCT04623931.summary_es: Este ensayo de fase II estudia temozolomida y radioterapia en adultos con gliomas IDH wildtype, incluido el glioblastoma IDH wildtype. Los pacientes toman temozolomida por vía oral todos los días durante 6 semanas de radioterapia, administrada 5 días a la semana, y luego continúan con temozolomida por vía oral durante 12 meses si la enfermedad no progresa y la toxicidad es aceptable. El resultado principal no se indica en el registro; este es un ensayo de fase II.
who_for: Age 18 years or older
IDH wildtype glioma, per the listed historical grade II or III or molecular glioblastoma definitions
Karnofsky performance status of 70 or higher within 30 days before enrollment
Post-operative MRI with contrast is required for radiation planning
Blood counts, liver and kidney tests within set limits within 60 days before registration
not_for: Definite metastatic disease
Prior chemotherapy or radiotherapy for any brain tumor
Prior cranial or head and neck radiation with possible field overlap
Leptomeningeal disease or multicentric glioblastoma
Severe active comorbidity, such as recent heart problems, or HIV with CD4 count under 200 cells/microliter

NCT07625644.summary_en: This study tests BL-M14D1 given together with atezolizumab, compared with standard treatment, in people with extensive-stage small cell lung cancer who have not had prior treatment for it. BL-M14D1 and atezolizumab are given into a vein on day 1 of each 21-day cycle, and the length of treatment is not stated; the standard arm gets carboplatin, etoposide and atezolizumab for 4 cycles, followed by atezolizumab with or without lurbinectedin. The main outcome the study measures is not stated in the record; it is a Phase 3, randomized, open-label trial.
NCT07625644.summary_es: Este estudio prueba BL-M14D1 administrado junto con atezolizumab, comparado con el tratamiento estándar, en personas con cáncer de pulmón de células pequeñas en etapa extensa que no han recibido tratamiento previo para esta enfermedad. BL-M14D1 y atezolizumab se administran por vena el día 1 de cada ciclo de 21 días; la duración del tratamiento no se indica. El brazo estándar recibe carboplatino, etopósido y atezolizumab durante 4 ciclos, seguidos de atezolizumab con o sin lurbinectedina. El resultado principal que mide el estudio no se indica en el registro; es un estudio de fase 3, aleatorizado y abierto.
who_for: Previously untreated extensive-stage small cell lung cancer, confirmed by pathology or cytology
Eligible for platinum-based chemotherapy combined with an anti-PD-L1 inhibitor
At least one measurable lesion by RECIST v1.1 per investigator assessment
ECOG performance status of 0 to 1
Adequate organ function
not_for: Platinum or etoposide treatment for limited-stage small cell lung cancer within 6 months before enrollment
Prior topoisomerase inhibitor-based antibody-drug conjugate therapy
History of severe heart disease
Active autoimmune or inflammatory disease
Other cancers, except certain skin cancers or curatively treated cancer with at least 3 years disease-free

NCT07485647.summary_en: This Phase 2 trial tests a less frequent schedule of daratumumab with lenalidomide as maintenance therapy for multiple myeloma after a stem cell transplant. Daratumumab-hyaluronidase is given under the skin every 8 weeks in Year 1 and every 16 weeks in Years 2 through 4, and lenalidomide is taken by mouth once daily, starting at 10 mg and increasing to 15 mg if tolerated, until progression or unacceptable side effects. The main outcome is not stated; the study is a Phase 2 trial.
NCT07485647.summary_es: Este ensayo de fase 2 evalúa un esquema de daratumumab con menor frecuencia junto con lenalidomida como terapia de mantenimiento para el mieloma múltiple después de un trasplante de células madre. El daratumumab con hialuronidasa se aplica debajo de la piel cada 8 semanas durante el primer año y cada 16 semanas en los años 2 a 4, y la lenalidomida se toma por vía oral una vez al día, comenzando con 10 mg y aumentando a 15 mg si se tolera, hasta la progresión de la enfermedad o efectos secundarios inaceptables. El resultado principal no se indica en el registro; el estudio es un ensayo de fase 2.
who_for: Newly diagnosed multiple myeloma, age 18 to 70, after stem cell transplant with partial response or better.
Induction treatment included a proteasome inhibitor, an immunomodulatory drug, and an anti-CD38 antibody.
ECOG performance status of 0 to 2.
Blood counts, liver and kidney function within the study's stated limits.
Those who could become pregnant must use birth control and have pregnancy testing.
not_for: Concomitant amyloidosis or plasma cell leukemia.
Pregnant or breastfeeding, or a live vaccine within 30 days before the first dose.
Participation in another investigational study within 4 weeks before the first dose.
Immunodeficiency, or steroid use above 10 mg daily prednisone equivalent.
Another cancer progressing or treated within 3 years, brain or meningeal spread, or recent severe heart disease or stroke.

NCT05558124.summary_en: This Phase 1/1b study tests CPX-351 (Vyxeos) combined with gemtuzumab ozogamicin in newly diagnosed acute myeloid leukemia. Vyxeos is given as a fixed dose of 44 mg/m2 daunorubicin and 100 mg/m2 cytarabine on days 1, 3 and 5, and gemtuzumab ozogamicin is given at 3 mg/m2 on a schedule that depends on dose level: day 1 only, days 1 and 4, or days 1, 4 and 7. The study measures safety and aims to find the maximum tolerated dose and recommended Phase 2 dose.
NCT05558124.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1/1b prueba CPX-351 (Vyxeos) combinado con gemtuzumab ozogamicina en leucemia mieloide aguda de diagnóstico reciente. Vyxeos se administra en dosis fija de 44 mg/m2 de daunorrubicina y 100 mg/m2 de citarabina los días 1, 3 y 5, y gemtuzumab ozogamicina se administra a 3 mg/m2 con un esquema que depende del nivel de dosis: solo el día 1, los días 1 y 4, o los días 1, 4 y 7. El estudio mide la seguridad y busca la dosis máxima tolerada y la dosis recomendada para fase 2.
who_for: Adults aged 18 to 70 years with newly diagnosed acute myeloid leukemia, any risk by ELN 2017 criteria.
Myeloblasts that express CD33, shown by flow cytometry or immunohistochemistry.
ECOG performance status of 2 or less and eligible for intensive chemotherapy as judged by the treating physician.
Adequate heart function, with ejection fraction of at least 50%.
Hydroxyurea allowed for cell reduction until day 1 of study treatment.
not_for: Acute promyelocytic leukemia.
Known current, clinically active leukemia in the central nervous system.
Known FLT3 ITD or FLT3 TKD mutation.
Active hepatitis B or hepatitis C infection, or severe liver disease.
Prior AML treatment other than hydroxyurea or leukapheresis.

NCT05665738.summary_en: This study tests two-fraction high dose rate (HDR) brachytherapy given alone as monotherapy, in men with localized prostate cancer. The radiation is given as 13.5 Gy in 2 fractions during a single implant procedure, with the fractions 3 hours apart; the total duration and any other schedule details are not stated. This single-center pilot study investigates safety, and the record lists the phase as NA.
NCT05665738.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa la braquiterapia de alta tasa de dosis (HDR) en dos fracciones, administrada como monoterapia, en hombres con cáncer de próstata localizado. La radiación se administra como 13.5 Gy en 2 fracciones durante un solo procedimiento de implante, con las fracciones separadas por 3 horas; la duración total y otros detalles del esquema no se indican. Este estudio piloto de un solo centro investiga la seguridad, y el registro indica la fase como NA.
who_for: Confirmed prostate adenocarcinoma diagnosis
Favorable intermediate risk prostate cancer by NCCN criteria
Age 18 years or older
ECOG performance status below 2
Eligible for HDR monotherapy as judged by the treating radiation oncologist
not_for: Any prior treatment for prostate cancer or any prior androgen deprivation therapy
Prior pelvic malignancy or prior pelvic radiotherapy
Lymph node or distant metastases
Prostate volume over 60 cubic centimeters
IPSS score of 15 or higher before treatment

NCT06725758.summary_en: This study tests ODM-212 in people with selected advanced solid tumours. ODM-212 is given as 5 mg and/or 40 mg tablets, and how long or how often it is taken is not stated. The main outcome is not stated; this is a Phase 1/2 first-in-human study with a dose escalation part and a dose expansion part.
NCT06725758.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa ODM-212 en personas con tumores sólidos avanzados seleccionados. ODM-212 se administra en tabletas de 5 mg y/o 40 mg, y no se indica cuánto tiempo ni con qué frecuencia se toma. El resultado principal no se indica; se trata de un estudio de Fase 1/2 en seres humanos por primera vez, con una parte de escalado de dosis y una parte de expansión de dosis.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older with locally advanced or metastatic solid tumour not amenable to curative treatment
Needs systemic cancer treatment and is refractory, progressed, intolerant, or not a candidate for established therapies
ECOG performance status 0 to 1
Life expectancy greater than 12 weeks
Part 2: measurable disease by RECIST v1.1 (modified RECIST for mesothelioma) and an available tumour tissue sample
not_for: Brain or subdural metastases, unless asymptomatic and not needing treatment or adequately treated
Other malignancy active within the previous 2 years, with listed exceptions
Kidney impairment, end-stage renal disease, or urine albumin/creatinine ratio of 3 mg/mmol or higher
Significant heart disease, including heart failure, recent arrhythmia needing treatment, or LVEF below 50%
Pregnant or breastfeeding, or prior treatment with other TEAD inhibitors

NCT03866382.summary_en: This phase II study tests cabozantinib together with nivolumab and ipilimumab in rare genitourinary tumors that have spread from where they started. Cabozantinib is taken by mouth, and nivolumab and ipilimumab are given through an IV; cycles repeat every 21 days for cycles 1-4 and every 28 days after that, for up to 2 years if the disease does not progress and side effects are not unacceptable. The main outcome measure is not stated; this is a phase II study.
NCT03866382.summary_es: Este estudio de fase II evalúa cabozantinib junto con nivolumab e ipilimumab en tumores genitourinarios raros que se han diseminado desde su sitio de origen. El cabozantinib se toma por vía oral, y el nivolumab y el ipilimumab se administran por vena (IV); los ciclos se repiten cada 21 días en los ciclos 1 a 4 y cada 28 días después, durante hasta 2 años si la enfermedad no progresa y los efectos secundarios no son inaceptables. La medida de resultado principal no se indica; se trata de un estudio de fase II.
who_for: Metastatic rare genitourinary cancer shown on imaging or bone scan, with at least one measurable site of disease.
Histology that matches one of the listed cohorts, such as bladder, penile, kidney, urethral or prostate small cell tumors.
Age 18 years or older.
Karnofsky performance status of 80% or higher.
Up to 2 prior systemic anti-cancer treatments, or no prior treatment.
not_for: Prior treatment with cabozantinib.
Prior treatment with both a MET or VEGF inhibitor and a PD-1, PD-L1 or CTLA-4 therapy.
Prior PD-1, PD-L1 or CTLA-4 therapy, except in urothelial carcinoma cohorts.
Active or acute diverticulitis, intra-abdominal abscess or GI obstruction within 12 months.
Pregnancy or breastfeeding.

NCT06048484.summary_en: This Phase 2 study tests zimberelimab with stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT), with or without quemliclustat and etrumadenant, given before surgery in people with localized pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma who can have surgery. Zimberelimab is given intravenously every 2 weeks for 7 weeks (4 doses), quemliclustat is given intravenously on the same schedule in some groups, etrumadenant is taken by mouth daily for 7 weeks in one group, and SBRT is 40 Gy in 5 fractions. The study's stated goals are to check whether the treatment is safe and whether it further increases the immune response against the tumor.
NCT06048484.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 evalúa zimberelimab con radioterapia corporal estereotáxica (SBRT), con o sin quemliclustat y etrumadenant, administrados antes de la cirugía en personas con adenocarcinoma ductal de páncreas localizado que pueden someterse a cirugía. Zimberelimab se administra por vía intravenosa cada 2 semanas durante 7 semanas (4 dosis), quemliclustat se administra por vía intravenosa con el mismo esquema en algunos grupos, etrumadenant se toma por vía oral a diario durante 7 semanas en un grupo, y la SBRT es de 40 Gy en 5 fracciones. Los objetivos indicados por el estudio son verificar si el tratamiento es seguro y si aumenta aún más la respuesta inmunitaria contra el tumor.
who_for: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma confirmed by pathology
Completed 8 cycles of neoadjuvant modified FOLFIRINOX
Surgically resectable disease and considered appropriate for the operation
ECOG performance status of 0 or 1
Age 18 years or older
not_for: Prior treatment with immune checkpoint blockers such as anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1 or anti-CTLA-4 antibodies
Receiving other investigational agents or other anticancer drugs at the same time (hormone therapy allowed)
Active or past autoimmune disease or immune deficiency
Past or current idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis
Positive HIV test, active hepatitis B or C, or clinically significant liver disease

NCT06730347.summary_en: This Phase 2 study tests lorigerlimab, a bispecific protein that binds PD-1 and CTLA-4, in people with platinum-resistant ovarian cancer or clear cell gynecologic cancers. Lorigerlimab is given by intravenous infusion on Day 1 of each 21-day cycle, and treatment continues until cancer progresses, side effects become unacceptable, consent is withdrawn, or the study ends. The main outcome is not stated; the study is Phase 2 and will assess efficacy and safety.
NCT06730347.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 evalúa lorigerlimab, una proteína biespecífica que se une a PD-1 y CTLA-4, en personas con cáncer de ovario resistente a platino o cánceres ginecológicos de células claras. Se administra por infusión intravenosa el día 1 de cada ciclo de 21 días, y el tratamiento continúa hasta que el cáncer progrese, haya efectos secundarios inaceptables, la persona retire su consentimiento o termine el estudio. El resultado principal no se indica en el registro; el estudio es de fase 2 y evaluará la eficacia y la seguridad.
who_for: High-grade serous ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer resistant to platinum chemotherapy, with 1 to 3 prior lines.
Clear cell carcinoma of the ovary, endometrium, vagina, vulva, or cervix, with at least 1 prior line of therapy.
Persistent or recurrent disease with documented progression.
At least one measurable lesion by RECIST v1.1.
Available tumor tissue, or willingness to undergo a biopsy.
not_for: Primary platinum-refractory disease, meaning no response or progression within 3 months of first-line platinum.
Prior checkpoint inhibitor treatment, except allowed for clear cell endometrial and cervical cancer.
Active brain or leptomeningeal metastases.
Prior stem cell, tissue, or solid organ transplant.
Paracentesis within 4 weeks before starting study treatment.

NCT03878849.summary_en: This Phase 2 study tests 2X-121 as a single medicine for recurrent, advanced ovarian cancer that is platinum-resistant or in patients who are not eligible for platinum. 2X-121 is taken by mouth as capsules once daily in 28-day cycles, with 600 mg daily compared to 800 mg daily; total study length is not stated. The main outcome measure is not stated in the record; the study aims to select the best dose using PK/PD, safety, and efficacy data.
NCT03878849.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 evalúa 2X-121 como medicamento único para el cáncer de ovario recurrente y avanzado que es resistente al platino o en pacientes que no son elegibles para platino. 2X-121 se toma por vía oral en cápsulas una vez al día en ciclos de 28 días, comparando 600 mg diarios con 800 mg diarios; la duración total del estudio no se indica. La medida de resultado principal no se indica en el registro; el estudio busca elegir la mejor dosis con base en datos de farmacocinética/farmacodinámica, seguridad y eficacia.
who_for: Adults 18 or older with recurrent, advanced epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer.
High-grade serous or endometrioid, or predominantly serous or endometrioid tumor histology.
Platinum-resistant disease (progression within 6 months after last platinum dose), or platinum ineligible.
No more than one prior line of therapy in the platinum-resistant or platinum-ineligible setting.
Measurable disease on CT or MRI, and ECOG performance status of 1 or less.
not_for: Platinum-refractory disease, meaning progression during the last platinum-based chemotherapy.
Concurrent chemotherapy, radiotherapy, hormonal therapy, or other investigational drug during the study.
Another malignancy, except stage I or II cancer judged cured by the investigator.
Active hepatitis B or C, known HIV positivity, or active infection needing antibiotics.
Stroke, TIA, or heart attack within 12 months, or clinically significant heart disease.

NCT07109726.summary_en: This Phase 1/2 study tests TER-2013 in people with advanced solid tumors that have changes in the AKT/PI3K/PTEN pathway. The conditions listed include breast, endometrial, ovarian, cervical, lung, head and neck, and esophageal cancers. TER-2013 is taken by mouth as capsules or tablets, and some arms also receive fulvestrant as an intramuscular injection; how long or how often is not stated. The study measures safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and anti-tumor activity.
NCT07109726.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1/2 evalúa TER-2013 en personas con tumores sólidos avanzados que presentan cambios en la vía AKT/PI3K/PTEN. Las condiciones incluyen cáncer de mama, endometrio, ovario, cuello uterino, pulmón, cabeza y cuello, y esófago. TER-2013 se toma por vía oral en cápsulas o tabletas, y algunos grupos también reciben fulvestrant por inyección intramuscular; la duración o la frecuencia no se indican. El estudio mide la seguridad, la tolerabilidad, la farmacocinética, la farmacodinamia y la actividad antitumoral.
