who_for: Metastatic or locally advanced, unresectable solid tumor with an AKT/PI3K/PTEN pathway alteration found by a sponsor-approved test.
No available treatment with curative intent.
Measurable or evaluable disease per RECIST v1.1 (measurable disease for expansion cohorts).
ECOG performance status of 0 or 1.
Adequate organ function.
not_for: Known EGFR, KRAS, NRAS, HRAS, or BRAF co-mutation with a PI3K/AKT/PTEN alteration.
Clinically significant abnormalities of glucose metabolism.
Active brain metastases or carcinomatous meningitis.
Significant hemoptysis or hemorrhage within 4 weeks before first dose.
Malabsorption, uncontrolled nausea and vomiting, or GI disease likely to affect drug absorption.
cancer_types: head and neck squamous cell carcinoma

NCT06858735.summary_en: This Phase 2 study compares systemic therapy with and without liver-directed radiation therapy in patients with advanced intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma. Durvalumab, gemcitabine and cisplatin are given by IV, and patients must receive at least 4 cycles of systemic therapy; the dosing schedule and total duration are not stated. The main outcome is not stated; the study is a Phase 2 trial.
NCT06858735.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 compara la terapia sistémica con y sin radioterapia dirigida al hígado en pacientes con colangiocarcinoma intrahepático avanzado. Durvalumab, gemcitabina y cisplatino se administran por vía intravenosa, y los pacientes deben recibir al menos 4 ciclos de terapia sistémica; el esquema de dosis y la duración total no se indican. El resultado principal no se indica; el estudio es un ensayo de fase 2.
who_for: Adults aged 18 or older at study entry.
Body weight greater than 30 kg.
Pathology-confirmed intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma with at least one tumor 3 cm or larger.
Unresectable liver-confined disease, or spread to non-regional lymph nodes, lung, or bone.
Received at least 4 cycles of gemcitabine, cisplatin and durvalumab.
not_for: Participation in another investigational study within the last month.
Brain metastases or history of leptomeningeal carcinomatosis.
Active or prior autoimmune or inflammatory disorders, with listed exceptions.
Active hepatitis, or HIV not well controlled.
Live attenuated vaccine within 30 days before first dose, or pregnancy or breastfeeding.

NCT07667335.summary_en: This Phase 1/Phase 2 study tests quemliclustat added to enfortumab vedotin and pembrolizumab for unresectable, locally advanced, or metastatic urothelial cancer of the bladder, renal pelvis, or ureter. All study drugs are given by IV infusion: quemliclustat on day 1, enfortumab vedotin on days 1 and 8, and pembrolizumab on day 1 of each 21-day cycle, for up to 2 years if the disease does not progress and side effects are acceptable. The study measures safety, side effects, and the best dose, and how well the combination works, but the primary outcome is not stated.
NCT07667335.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1/fase 2 evalúa quemliclustat añadido a enfortumab vedotina y pembrolizumab para el cáncer urotelial de vejiga, pelvis renal o uréter que no puede extirparse con cirugía, que está localmente avanzado o que es metastásico. Todos los medicamentos del estudio se administran por infusión intravenosa: quemliclustat el día 1, enfortumab vedotina los días 1 y 8, y pembrolizumab el día 1 de cada ciclo de 21 días, por hasta 2 años si la enfermedad no progresa y los efectos secundarios son aceptables. El estudio mide la seguridad, los efectos secundarios y la dosis más adecuada, y qué tan bien funciona la combinación, pero el resultado principal no está indicado.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older who give written informed consent
Previously untreated locally advanced or metastatic bladder, renal pelvis, or ureter urothelial cancer
Measurable disease by RECIST v1.1 criteria
ECOG performance status of 0 to 2
Estimated life expectancy of at least 3 months, with blood, kidney, and liver lab values within required limits
not_for: Tumors with neuroendocrine, small cell, or other listed non-eligible histologies
Receiving other investigational agents or anticancer treatment, or without the required washout after surgery, radiation, or adjuvant immunotherapy
Systemic steroids within 10 days of enrollment (physiologic replacement allowed), or disease progression within 12 months after neoadjuvant or adjuvant therapy
Active autoimmune disease, active hepatitis B or C, HIV with CD4 below 350, QTcF above 480 ms, or leptomeningeal disease
Pregnancy, breastfeeding, or other conditions the investigator judges unsafe for participation

NCT07630168.summary_en: This study tests whether the time of day that PD-1 or PD-L1 immunotherapy is given affects outcomes in non-small cell lung cancer and in locally advanced, resectable head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. Patients are randomly assigned to receive their infusion before 12:00 PM or after 3 PM, for 4 cycles or 2 cycles depending on the listed intervention, with follow-up for up to 2 years; the length of each cycle is not stated. The record does not name a primary outcome, but it says survival and treatment response will be collected from medical records (Phase 2).
NCT07630168.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa si la hora del día en que se administra la inmunoterapia con PD-1 o PD-L1 afecta los resultados en el cáncer de pulmón de células no pequeñas y en el carcinoma de células escamosas de cabeza y cuello localmente avanzado y resecable. Los pacientes se asignan al azar a recibir la infusión antes de las 12:00 p. m. o después de las 3 p. m., durante 4 ciclos o 2 ciclos según la intervención indicada; la duración de cada ciclo no se indica, y el seguimiento es de hasta 2 años. El registro no nombra un resultado principal, pero indica que se recopilarán la supervivencia y la respuesta al tratamiento de los expedientes médicos (fase 2).
who_for: Adults 18 or older with metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (cohort 1).
Adults 18 or older with resectable head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (cohort 2).
Able to give written informed consent and to follow study procedures, in the investigator's judgment.
not_for: Currently using steroids (prednisone 10 mg or more, or equivalent) that cannot be stopped at least 7 days before standard treatment.
Prior PD-1, PD-L1 or CTLA4 immune checkpoint inhibitor treatment received less than 6 months before screening.
Currently taking part in another treatment clinical trial.
cancer_types: head and neck squamous cell carcinoma

NCT07100080.summary_en: This Phase 2/3 study compares izalontamab brengitecan (BMS-986507) with platinum-based chemotherapy, with or without amivantamab, in people with EGFR-mutated non-small cell lung cancer whose disease got worse during EGFR TKI therapy. The study drugs are given at a specified dose on specified days, and the exact schedule and treatment length are not stated. The main outcome measure is not stated; the record describes this as a randomized, open-label Phase 2/3 study.
NCT07100080.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2/3 compara izalontamab brengitecan (BMS-986507) con quimioterapia basada en platino, con o sin amivantamab, en personas con cáncer de pulmón de células no pequeñas con mutación de EGFR cuya enfermedad empeoró durante el tratamiento con inhibidores de la tirosina quinasa de EGFR. Los medicamentos del estudio se administran en una dosis específica en días específicos, y el esquema exacto y la duración del tratamiento no se indican. El resultado principal no se indica; el registro describe el estudio como aleatorizado, abierto y de fase 2/3.
who_for: Non-squamous lung cancer that cannot be treated with curative intent
EGFR mutation: exon 19 deletion or L858R
Disease progression on a 3rd-generation EGFR TKI as the most recent line of therapy
Eligible to receive cisplatin or carboplatin with pemetrexed, with or without amivantamab
not_for: Inadequate organ function or bone marrow reserve
Leptomeningeal metastases or spinal cord compression
Poorly controlled systemic medical conditions
Other protocol-defined inclusion or exclusion criteria apply

NCT05503797.summary_en: This Phase 2 study tests plixorafenib, a drug taken by mouth, in people with solid tumors or primary brain and spinal cord (CNS) tumors that have BRAF changes, including rare cancers such as anaplastic thyroid, ovarian, and cholangiocarcinoma. Plixorafenib is given as oral tablets continuously in 3-week cycles until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, or another reason for withdrawal. The main outcome is not stated in the record; the study is Phase 2.
NCT05503797.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 evalúa plixorafenib, un medicamento que se toma por vía oral, en personas con tumores sólidos o tumores primarios del sistema nervioso central (SNC) que tienen alteraciones en BRAF, incluidos cánceres raros como el carcinoma anaplásico de tiroides, el cáncer de ovario y el colangiocarcinoma. Plixorafenib se administra en tabletas por vía oral de forma continua en ciclos de 3 semanas, hasta la progresión de la enfermedad, toxicidad inaceptable u otra razón para retirarse. El resultado principal no se indica en el registro; el estudio es de fase 2.
who_for: Age 8 years or older and weight 25 kg or more.
Tumor with a BRAF fusion or BRAF V600E mutation, as defined by the subprotocol.
Unresectable, locally advanced, or metastatic disease, or recurrent or progressive CNS tumor.
Prior standard therapy received, not tolerated, or judged not appropriate by the investigator.
Archival tumor tissue available, or a new biopsy where required, and consent to provide scans.
not_for: Prior treatment with BRAF, ERK, or MEK inhibitors (depends on subprotocol).
Known or suspected NF-1 or RAS-related gene alterations.
Malignancy with co-occurring activating RAS mutation (Subprotocol A).
Active infection requiring systemic therapy.
Uncontrolled illness that would limit compliance, or HIV infection with exceptions.

NCT07107126.summary_en: This study tests RPT1G, a selective hyperbolic NAMPT inhibitor, in adults with relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and high-risk myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS). RPT1G is taken by mouth, and how long or how often it is given is not stated. The main goals are to learn whether RPT1G is safe and tolerable and to find the best dose and schedule; this is a Phase 1 study.
NCT07107126.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa RPT1G, un inhibidor selectivo hiperbólico de NAMPT, en adultos con leucemia mieloide aguda (LMA) recidivante o refractaria y síndromes mielodisplásicos (SMD) de alto riesgo. RPT1G se administra por vía oral; la duración y la frecuencia del tratamiento no se indican. Los objetivos principales son saber si RPT1G es seguro y tolerable y determinar la mejor dosis y esquema; es un estudio de fase 1.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older
ECOG performance status 2 or better
AML or high-risk MDS that has relapsed or is refractory, after standard therapy or declined standard therapy
Adequate liver function based on lab limits
Creatinine clearance above 50 mL/min
not_for: No evidence of blood or bone marrow involvement
Acute promyelocytic leukemia
Symptomatic central nervous system involvement by AML
Active infections
Prior or concurrent malignancy

NCT06057935.summary_en: This phase 2 study compares two ways of giving chemotherapy after surgery and HIPEC for malignant peritoneal mesothelioma: directly into the abdomen (intraperitoneal) or into a vein (intravenous). The drugs are pemetrexed plus cisplatin or carboplatin; the intravenous arm gives 4 cycles, with up to 6 at clinician discretion, and the number of intraperitoneal cycles is not stated. The main outcome measure is not stated in the record; the study is a randomized phase 2 trial.
NCT06057935.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 compara dos formas de administrar quimioterapia después de la cirugía y la HIPEC para el mesotelioma peritoneal maligno: directamente en el abdomen (intraperitoneal) o en una vena (intravenosa). Los medicamentos son pemetrexed más cisplatino o carboplatino; el brazo intravenoso recibe 4 ciclos, con hasta 6 a criterio del médico, y el número de ciclos intraperitoneales no se indica. El resultado principal que se mide no se indica en el registro; el estudio es un ensayo aleatorizado de fase 2.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older with a clinical diagnosis of malignant peritoneal mesothelioma
Epithelioid histology confirmed by pathology before randomization
Complete or near-complete cytoreductive surgery achieved or planned
ECOG performance status of 1 or less
Adequate blood counts, kidney function and liver function, and agreement to use contraception
not_for: Prior intraperitoneal or systemic chemotherapy or immunotherapy for peritoneal mesothelioma
Prior platinum-containing chemotherapy
Biopsy showing sarcomatoid, well-differentiated papillary or benign multicystic mesothelioma
Other prior cancers, with some exceptions, unless no activity for more than three years
Known allergy to cisplatin, carboplatin, pemetrexed or mitomycin

NCT03314974.summary_en: This Phase 2 study tests a myeloablative allogeneic stem cell transplant from a related or unrelated donor for blood and bone marrow diseases, including leukemia, lymphoma, myelodysplasia and multiple myeloma. Before transplant, patients receive total body irradiation, or busulfan and fludarabine, from Day -5 to Day -2, with the transplant on Day 0; cyclophosphamide is given on Days +3 and +4, tacrolimus starts on Day +5 and is tapered until Day +100, and mycophenolate mofetil is given through Day +35 or 7 days after engraftment, whichever is later. The record does not state a main outcome measure, and the study is listed as Phase 2.
NCT03314974.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 evalúa un trasplante alogénico de células madre mieloablativo de un donante relacionado o no relacionado, para enfermedades de la sangre y la médula ósea, incluidas leucemia, linfoma, mielodisplasia y mieloma múltiple. Antes del trasplante, los pacientes reciben irradiación corporal total, o busulfán y fludarabina, del Día -5 al Día -2, con el trasplante en el Día 0; la ciclofosfamida se administra los Días +3 y +4, el tacrolimus comienza el Día +5 y se reduce gradualmente hasta el Día +100, y el micofenolato de mofetilo se administra hasta el Día +35 o 7 días después del injerto, lo que ocurra más tarde. El registro no indica una medida de resultado principal, y el estudio figura como de fase 2.
who_for: Age 60 years or younger
Karnofsky score of at least 70% or Lansky play score of at least 70
Adequate kidney, liver, lung and heart function as defined in the record
Disease in a remission or stage listed in the disease-specific criteria
Voluntary written consent from the patient or legal representative
not_for: Pregnant or breastfeeding
Active HIV infection or known HIV positive serology
Active central nervous system malignancy
Chronic myelogenous leukemia in blast crisis
Evidence of progressive disease on imaging or biopsy

NCT06111313.summary_en: This Phase 2 study tests a single high-dose radiation session aimed at the MRI-visible tumor inside the prostate, in men with prostate cancer, with or without ultra-short-term hormone therapy using relugolix. Radiation is given once on the first day of treatment, and relugolix is taken as a daily oral tablet for 28 days, starting 2 weeks before radiation and continuing 2 weeks after. The record does not state a main outcome measure; it describes the study as Phase 2.
NCT06111313.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 prueba una sesión única de radiación de dosis alta dirigida al tumor visible en la resonancia magnética dentro de la próstata, en hombres con cáncer de próstata, con o sin terapia hormonal de duración muy corta con relugolix. La radiación se administra una vez el primer día del tratamiento, y el relugolix se toma como tableta oral diaria durante 28 días, comenzando 2 semanas antes de la radiación y continuando 2 semanas después. El registro no indica una medida de resultado principal; describe el estudio como de fase 2.
who_for: Biopsy-confirmed prostate adenocarcinoma with Gleason score 6 to 10
No spread to lymph nodes or distant sites by clinical or imaging tests
PSA 100 ng/mL or lower within 3 months of consent
Suspicious lesion on prostate MRI
Age 35 to 85 years at consent
not_for: Prior pelvic radiotherapy or prior androgen ablation therapy
Prior or planned radical prostatectomy
Pelvic lymph nodes or distant metastasis, per imaging or pathology criteria
Other active cancer, except nonmetastatic skin cancer or early-stage CLL
Zubrod status above 2 or inability to tolerate diagnostic MRI

NCT05779423.summary_en: This Phase 2 study tests ipilimumab and nivolumab together with cryoablation, a procedure that freezes part of a tumor, in adults with advanced melanoma that is growing or resistant after prior immunotherapy. Ipilimumab and nivolumab are given by intravenous infusion for cycles 1 to 4 at pre-determined doses under the oncologist's direction, and a core needle biopsy followed by cryoablation is done between cycles 1 and 2. The record does not state a main outcome measure, but it says the study aims to assess safety and effectiveness, and Stage 1 moves to Stage 2 if 6 or more of 15 participants have clinical benefit.
NCT05779423.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 evalúa ipilimumab y nivolumab junto con crioablación, un procedimiento que congela parte de un tumor, en adultos con melanoma avanzado que crece o es resistente después de una inmunoterapia previa. El ipilimumab y el nivolumab se administran por infusión intravenosa en los ciclos 1 a 4, con dosis predeterminadas y bajo la dirección del oncólogo, y se realiza una biopsia con aguja gruesa seguida de crioablación entre los ciclos 1 y 2. El registro no indica una medida principal de resultado, pero señala que el estudio busca evaluar la seguridad y la eficacia, y que la Etapa 1 pasa a la Etapa 2 si 6 o más de 15 participantes presentan beneficio clínico.
who_for: Adults 18 or older with unresectable melanoma that progressed on prior immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy.
Treating physician plans to start ipilimumab and nivolumab together.
Tumor suitable for percutaneous image-guided cryoablation under routine interventional radiology criteria.
Measurable disease by RECIST, apart from the lesion to be ablated.
ECOG performance status 2 or less, with adequate blood counts and organ function.
not_for: Progressing on ipilimumab and nivolumab as the last line of therapy.
Unresolved side effects above grade 1 from prior cancer treatment, or ongoing immune-related adverse events.
Symptomatic brain metastases or leptomeningeal disease.
Prednisone above 10 mg daily or equivalent, or uncontrolled illness.
Pregnant or breastfeeding, or currently receiving an investigational agent.

NCT07300150.summary_en: This Phase 1 study is testing PT0511, given alone or with cetuximab, in adults with advanced solid tumors that have a KRAS mutation or amplified wild-type KRAS. The listed conditions include colorectal cancer, pancreatic cancer, and non-small cell lung cancer. PT0511 is given by intravenous infusion until the disease gets worse or the participant cannot tolerate it, and how often and how long each dose is given is not stated. The main goal is to check safety and tolerability and to find the maximally tolerated dose and/or recommended Phase 2 dose.
NCT07300150.summary_es: Este estudio de Fase 1 evalúa PT0511, administrado solo o con cetuximab, en adultos con tumores sólidos avanzados que tienen una mutación de KRAS o amplificación de KRAS de tipo silvestre. Las enfermedades listadas incluyen cáncer colorrectal, cáncer de páncreas y cáncer de pulmón de células no pequeñas. PT0511 se administra por infusión intravenosa hasta que la enfermedad empeore o el participante no pueda tolerarlo, y la frecuencia y la duración de cada dosis no se indican. El objetivo principal es evaluar la seguridad y la tolerabilidad, y determinar la dosis máxima tolerada y/o la dosis recomendada para Fase 2.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older
Advanced or metastatic solid cancer confirmed by tissue or cell testing
KRAS mutation or amplified wild-type KRAS found by molecular testing
1 to 4 prior systemic therapies, or intolerant or ineligible for available therapies
Measurable disease by RECIST 1.1 and ECOG performance status 0 or 1
not_for: Active brain metastasis or carcinomatous meningitis, with some exceptions
Other cancer within the past 2 years, with some exceptions
Prior treatment with a KRAS/RAS degrader
Significant cardiovascular disease within 6 months of starting study therapy
Known hypersensitivity to any product given during dosing

NCT03425526.summary_en: This phase 1 trial tests allogeneic adenovirus-specific cytotoxic T lymphocytes, a donor T cell therapy, in patients with a weakened immune system and adenovirus-related disease. The listed conditions include hematopoietic and lymphoid cell neoplasm. The therapy is given as an intravenous infusion over 30 minutes within two weeks of enrollment, and more infusions may be given at the investigator's discretion if there is no disease progression or unacceptable toxicity; the total number of infusions is not stated. The record does not state a primary outcome measure; the brief summary says the study looks at side effects and how well the therapy works.
NCT03425526.summary_es: Este ensayo de fase 1 evalúa los linfocitos T citotóxicos específicos contra adenovirus de donante alogénico, una terapia con células T de donante, en pacientes con un sistema inmunitario debilitado y enfermedad relacionada con adenovirus. Las condiciones listadas incluyen neoplasia de células hematopoyéticas y linfoides. La terapia se administra como infusión intravenosa durante 30 minutos dentro de las dos semanas posteriores a la inscripción, y se pueden administrar más infusiones a criterio del investigador si no hay progresión de la enfermedad ni toxicidad inaceptable; el número total de infusiones no está indicado. El registro no indica una medida de resultado principal; el resumen breve señala que el estudio analiza los efectos secundarios y qué tan bien funciona la terapia.
who_for: Immunocompromised patients.
Patients age 1 year or older with asymptomatic adenovirus viremia, based on repeated or high-level quantifiable test results.
Patients age 1 year or older with probable or definitive adenoviral disease, as defined in the protocol appendix.
Written informed consent, or signed assent from patient, parent or guardian.
Willing to follow the study protocol requirements.
not_for: Taking prednisone above 0.1 mg/kg/day or equivalent at enrollment.
Received anti-thymocyte globulin within 14 days, or donor lymphocyte infusion or Campath within 28 days of enrollment.
Other uncontrolled infections, as defined in the criteria.
Active acute graft versus host disease, grade 2 or higher.

NCT05892718.summary_en: The study tests HCB101, an Fc-fusion protein that targets the SIRPα-CD47 pathway, in adults with advanced solid tumors or relapsed and refractory non-Hodgkin lymphoma. HCB101 is given as an intravenous (IV) infusion, and the dosing schedule and how often it is given are not stated. This Phase 1 study looks at safety, tolerability, how the body processes the drug, and anti-tumor activity, as listed in the official title.
NCT05892718.summary_es: El estudio evalúa HCB101, una proteína de fusión Fc que actúa sobre la vía SIRPα-CD47, en adultos con tumores sólidos avanzados o linfoma no Hodgkin recidivante y refractario. HCB101 se administra como infusión intravenosa (IV), y el esquema de dosis y la frecuencia no se indican. Este estudio de Fase 1 analiza la seguridad, la tolerabilidad, cómo el organismo procesa el fármaco y la actividad antitumoral, según se indica en el título oficial.
who_for: Adults aged 18 years or older.
Advanced solid tumor that is refractory to standard therapy or for which no standard treatment exists.
Non-Hodgkin lymphoma relapsed or refractory to at least 2 prior lines of therapy.
Measurable disease per RECIST v1.1 (solid tumors) or assessable disease per Lugano Classification (lymphoma).
ECOG performance status 0 to 2 and life expectancy of 12 weeks or more.
not_for: Known hypersensitivity to any component of HCB101.
Known active or untreated brain metastases or carcinomatous meningitis.
Prior treatment targeting the CD47 or SIRPα pathway.
Positive for hepatitis B, active hepatitis C, HIV, or active or latent tuberculosis.
Known inherited or acquired bleeding disorder, or previously documented hemolytic anemia or Evans Syndrome in the last 3 months.

NCT07293247.summary_en: This Phase 2 study compares targeted post-surgery radiation therapy (I²-PORT) followed by standard chemotherapy or immunotherapy with standard chemotherapy or immunotherapy alone. It is for non-small cell lung cancer that still has cancer in the lymph nodes after surgery. I²-PORT is given once a day, Monday through Friday, for 15 to 25 treatments over 5 to 6 weeks, and standard treatment starts 1 to 42 days after radiation ends and continues unless the disease gets worse or side effects are unacceptable. The main outcome is not stated; the study is listed as Phase 2.
NCT07293247.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 compara la radioterapia dirigida después de la cirugía (I²-PORT) seguida de quimioterapia o inmunoterapia estándar, con quimioterapia o inmunoterapia estándar sola. Es para el cáncer de pulmón de células no pequeñas que aún tiene cáncer en los ganglios linfáticos después de la cirugía. La I²-PORT se administra una vez al día, de lunes a viernes, en 15 a 25 sesiones durante 5 a 6 semanas, y el tratamiento estándar comienza entre 1 y 42 días después de terminar la radiación y continúa mientras la enfermedad no empeore ni haya toxicidad inaceptable. No se indica el resultado principal; el estudio figura como fase 2.
who_for: Diagnosis of non-small cell lung cancer, with no small cell component
Lobectomy or larger surgery within 8 weeks, with complete removal and residual cancer in lymph nodes
Prior 2 to 4 cycles of neoadjuvant systemic therapy
No metastatic disease on recent imaging
Age 18 or older with ECOG performance status 2 or better
not_for: Known EGFR mutation or ALK rearrangement
Prior radiation to the lungs or mediastinum
VEGF inhibitor within 90 days, or planned adjuvant VEGF inhibitor
Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis or interstitial lung disease needing anti-fibrotic medication
Pregnancy, or heart function below New York Heart Association class 2B

NCT05776979.summary_en: This study tests isatuximab given with lenalidomide as maintenance therapy after stem cell transplant in adults with high-risk multiple myeloma. Isatuximab is given into a vein over about 75 minutes, and lenalidomide is taken by mouth; study drugs start about 60 to 180 days after transplant and may be given for about 3 years. The main outcome is not stated; this is a Phase 2 study.
NCT05776979.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa isatuximab administrado junto con lenalidomida como terapia de mantenimiento después de un trasplante de células madre en adultos con mieloma múltiple de alto riesgo. Isatuximab se administra en una vena durante unos 75 minutos, y la lenalidomida se toma por vía oral; los medicamentos del estudio comienzan entre 60 y 180 días después del trasplante y pueden administrarse durante unos 3 años. El resultado principal no está indicado; este es un estudio de Fase 2.
who_for: Adults aged 18 to 72 with newly diagnosed symptomatic multiple myeloma and measurable disease
High-risk myeloma by R-ISS or ISS stage, or by specified genetic abnormalities
Partial response or better before starting maintenance therapy
Karnofsky score of at least 70% and/or ECOG performance status 2 or less
Autologous stem cell transplant with melphalan-based conditioning and adequate blood count recovery
not_for: Myeloma progression before starting maintenance therapy
Other investigational agents within 14 days or 5 half-lives before study treatment
Known allergy to study drugs or similar compounds, or to other listed components
Active infection requiring treatment or uncontrolled serious illness
HIV, or active hepatitis A, B or C; or major surgery within 4 weeks before treatment

NCT07661459.summary_en: This study tests whether optimizing ancillary therapies can improve the effect of immune checkpoint inhibitor treatment in people with solid tumors. The optimized regimen includes aspirin and loratadine, plus avoiding acetaminophen and THC-containing products, and participants receive it alongside standard immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy. The main outcome is not stated; the stated goal is to compare efficacy with a matched historical control group, and the study is Phase 2.
NCT07661459.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa si optimizar las terapias auxiliares puede mejorar el efecto del tratamiento con inhibidores de puntos de control inmunitario en personas con tumores sólidos. El esquema optimizado incluye aspirina y loratadina, además de evitar el acetaminofén y los productos que contienen THC, y los participantes lo reciben junto con el tratamiento estándar con inhibidores de puntos de control inmunitario. El resultado principal no se indica; el objetivo declarado es comparar la eficacia con un grupo de control histórico pareado, y el estudio es de Fase 2.
who_for: Adults aged 18 to 99 years with solid tumors and measurable disease, early or advanced stage.
Planned standard-of-care treatment with a PD-1 or PD-L1 immune checkpoint inhibitor.
ECOG performance status 0 to 3 and life expectancy of at least 3 months.
Willing to stop or not start daily acetaminophen and THC-containing products during the study.
Willing to take loratadine and aspirin, or continue a similar antihistamine or NSAID already being taken.
not_for: Contraindication to immunotherapy, aspirin, or loratadine, or high bleeding risk from blood thinners or antiplatelet agents.
True allergic reaction to loratadine or aspirin (intolerance does not count).
Immunocompromised, including solid organ transplant, active HIV, or autoimmune disease on immune-modulating drugs.
Early-stage disease with definitive therapy planned in less than 126 days from treatment start, or prior checkpoint inhibitors for advanced disease with excepti
Currently enrolled in an interventional cancer study, or other significant condition the investigator judges a safety risk.

NCT03604315.summary_en: This Phase 1 study tests how well a radioactive imaging tracer called fluorine F 18 fluorthanatrace works with PET/CT scans in people with solid tumors, including breast, ovarian, fallopian tube, and primary peritoneal cancers. Patients get FDG through an IV and a FDG PET/CT scan over 20 to 30 minutes if they have not had one as standard care, then at least 20 to 24 hours later get fluorine F 18 fluorthanatrace through an IV and a PET/CT scan over 1 hour. The record does not state a main outcome measure; the study is Phase 1.
NCT03604315.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1 evalúa qué tan bien funciona un trazador radiactivo de imagen llamado fluorine F 18 fluorthanatrace con estudios PET/TC en personas con tumores sólidos, como cáncer de mama, de ovario, de trompa de Falopio y peritoneal primario. Los pacientes reciben FDG por vía intravenosa y se les hace una PET/TC con FDG de 20 a 30 minutos, si no la han tenido como parte de su atención estándar; al menos 20 a 24 horas después reciben fluorine F 18 fluorthanatrace por vía intravenosa y una PET/TC de 1 hora. El registro no indica una medida de resultado principal; el estudio es de fase 1.
who_for: Has a known or suspected solid tumor.
Has at least one lesion 1.0 cm or larger seen on standard imaging such as CT, MRI, ultrasound, or FDG PET/CT.
not_for: Is pregnant or breastfeeding at screening.
Cannot tolerate imaging procedures, in the opinion of an investigator or treating physician.
Has a medical condition that a physician investigator considers could compromise safety or successful participation.

NCT07609225.summary_en: This study compares two imaging methods, FLT PET and chemical shift-encoded MRI (CSE-MRI), to look at bone marrow in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who are scheduled to receive 177Lu-PSMA therapy. FLT is given as an intravenous injection of up to 10 mCi (370 MBq), with PET imaging about one hour later, and each imaging session lasts 2 to 3 hours. The study's main goal is to see whether CSE-MRI is as accurate as FLT PET at telling active bone marrow from inactive bone marrow; it is an early phase 1 study.
NCT07609225.summary_es: Este estudio compara dos métodos de imagen, la PET con FLT y la resonancia magnética con codificación por desplazamiento químico (CSE-MRI), para observar la médula ósea en hombres con cáncer de próstata metastásico resistente a la castración que están programados para recibir terapia con 177Lu-PSMA. El FLT se administra como inyección intravenosa de hasta 10 mCi (370 MBq), con imágenes PET aproximadamente una hora después, y cada sesión de imagen dura de 2 a 3 horas. El objetivo principal es ver si la CSE-MRI es tan precisa como la PET con FLT para distinguir la médula ósea activa de la inactiva; es un estudio de fase 1 temprana.
who_for: Men aged 18 years or older.
Prostate cancer confirmed by tissue or cell testing.
Metastatic PSMA-positive castration-resistant prostate cancer, scheduled for 177Lu-PSMA therapy.
Clinically appropriate for standard Lu-177 PSMA therapy, with ECOG performance status 0 to 2.
Able to lie flat for at least 30 minutes during imaging.
not_for: Receiving any ongoing therapy that affects bone marrow, such as G-CSF.
Chemotherapy or radium-223 within 4 weeks.
Side effects from prior treatment not yet resolved to grade 2 or lower (CTCAE v5).
Uncontrolled illness, such as active infection, symptomatic heart failure, unstable angina, or arrhythmia.
Psychiatric or social situations that would limit compliance with study requirements, per the treating physician.

NCT04921917.summary_en: This study tests a brief exercise program given before radiation therapy and surgery in people with soft tissue sarcoma in an arm or leg. The exercise is done right before radiation, during the usual 10-week radiation course, using rubber bands for leg tumors or a hand-held dynamometer for arm tumors; how often it is done is not stated. The record does not state a main outcome measure; its stated purpose is to evaluate effects on limb function and wound healing after surgery, and the phase is listed as NA.
NCT04921917.summary_es: Este estudio prueba un programa breve de ejercicio que se realiza antes de la radioterapia y la cirugía en personas con sarcoma de tejido blando en un brazo o una pierna. El ejercicio se hace justo antes de la radioterapia, durante el tratamiento habitual de 10 semanas, usando bandas elásticas para tumores en la pierna o un dinamómetro manual para tumores en el brazo; la frecuencia no está indicada. El registro no indica una medida de resultado principal; su propósito declarado es evaluar los efectos en la función de la extremidad y la cicatrización de la herida después de la cirugía, y la fase aparece como NA.
who_for: Adults aged 18 to 85 years
Soft tissue sarcoma confirmed by pathology in an upper or lower extremity
Planned radiation therapy before surgical removal of the tumor
Expected primary wound closure at surgery
Able to attend follow-up visits and give own consent
not_for: Prior radiation to the tumor or surgical area
Prior surgery at the disease site other than biopsy
Planned radiation therapy after surgery
Chemotherapy within the last 30 days or high-dose steroids
Tumor ulcerating or fungating through the skin, or severe cardiopulmonary disease

NCT07193511.summary_en: This Phase 1/2 study tests AVZO-103, a Nectin4/Trop2 ADC (antibody-drug conjugate), alone and in combination, in adults with locally advanced or metastatic urothelial cancer or other solid tumors. AVZO-103 is given intravenously, and combination agents are given per their label, with dose and schedule set by the protocol; duration is not stated. The study measures safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, maximum tolerated dose, and antitumor activity.
NCT07193511.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1/2 evalúa AVZO-103, un ADC (conjugado anticuerpo-fármaco) dirigido a Nectin4/Trop2, solo y en combinación, en adultos con cáncer urotelial localmente avanzado o metastásico u otros tumores sólidos. AVZO-103 se administra por vía intravenosa, y los agentes de combinación se administran según su prospecto, con dosis y esquema definidos por el protocolo; la duración no se indica. El estudio mide la seguridad, la tolerancia, la farmacocinética, la farmacodinamia, la dosis máxima tolerada y la actividad antitumoral.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older with ECOG performance status of 1 or less
Life expectancy greater than 3 months
Confirmed locally advanced or metastatic urothelial cancer or other specified solid tumors
Measurable disease by RECIST v1.1
Agrees to provide molecular test results and tumor samples
not_for: Active brain metastases, unless treated, radiologically stable 4+ weeks, and not on steroids
Suspected or confirmed leptomeningeal disease, even if treated
Prior Stevens-Johnson syndrome or toxic epidermal necrolysis
History of drug-induced interstitial lung disease
History of any serious cardiovascular condition, or infection needing IV antibiotics, antivirals or antifungals within 2 weeks before first dose

NCT07032714.summary_en: This Phase 1 study tests mezigdomide and talquetamab, with dexamethasone, in adults with relapsed and refractory multiple myeloma. Talquetamab is injected under the skin, and mezigdomide is taken by mouth once a day on days 1 to 21 of 28-day cycles until disease progression or withdrawal, while dexamethasone is taken by mouth on a study schedule. The study aims to find the recommended dose and schedule of these drugs, and a main outcome measure is not stated.
NCT07032714.summary_es: Este estudio de Fase 1 evalúa mezigdomida y talquetamab, junto con dexametasona, en adultos con mieloma múltiple recidivante y refractario. El talquetamab se inyecta debajo de la piel, y la mezigdomida se toma por vía oral una vez al día en los días 1 a 21 de ciclos de 28 días, hasta la progresión de la enfermedad o el retiro del tratamiento; la dexametasona también se toma por vía oral según un calendario del estudio. El objetivo es encontrar la dosis y el esquema recomendados de estos medicamentos, y no se indica una medida de resultado principal.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma.
ECOG performance status of 2 or better.
Measurable myeloma disease by blood, urine, or free light chain tests.
At least three prior lines of therapy, including an immunomodulatory drug, a proteasome inhibitor, and an anti-CD38 antibody.
Disease progression on, or within 60 days after finishing, the last therapy.
not_for: Prior therapy with mezigdomide or iberdomide.
Prior anti-GPRC5D therapy, such as talquetamab.
Bispecific antibody therapy or gene-modified cell therapy within three months.
Primary refractory disease.
High-dose corticosteroids, or receiving any investigational agent.

NCT06065449.summary_en: This Phase III study compares stereotactic body radiation therapy (SBRT) at higher doses and different schedules with standard palliative radiation therapy for painful bone metastases. Participants are randomized to radiation given as one treatment, or as 3 or 5 daily treatments, with the record listing 8 Gy in one treatment or 20 Gy in 5 treatments as the standard arm and 16 Gy in one treatment or 27 Gy in 3 treatments in the other arm. The record does not state the main outcome measured; the study is listed as Phase III.
NCT06065449.summary_es: Este estudio de Fase III compara la radioterapia corporal estereotáctica (SBRT) con dosis más altas y diferentes esquemas frente a la radioterapia paliativa estándar para metástasis óseas dolorosas. Los participantes son asignados al azar a radiación en una sola sesión, o en 3 o 5 sesiones diarias, y el registro indica 8 Gy en una sesión o 20 Gy en 5 sesiones como brazo estándar, y 16 Gy en una sesión o 27 Gy en 3 sesiones en el otro brazo. El registro no indica el resultado principal que se mide; el estudio aparece registrado como Fase III.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older with a solid tumor and bone metastases on imaging (multiple myeloma is also eligible).
Pain or discomfort at the proposed treatment site.
Life expectancy of 3 months or more.
Able to complete pain assessment and quality of life surveys.
Able to understand and sign a written informed consent document.
not_for: Prior radiation therapy to the proposed treatment site.
Untreated spinal cord compression at the treatment site.
Unstable radiographic or pathologic fracture at the treatment site that is not mechanically stabilized.
Metastases along the cervical, thoracic, or lumbar spine (unless the primary site invades the paraspinal or spine region).
Pregnancy.

NCT06592599.summary_en: This Phase 2 study tests gemcitabine, docetaxel, and toripalimab given before chemoradiation for locoregionally advanced EBV-positive nasopharyngeal carcinoma. Toripalimab is given by IV every 3 weeks with 3 induction cycles of gemcitabine and docetaxel, then radiation (70 Gy) with weekly cisplatin, then capecitabine by mouth twice daily for 12 months, with toripalimab for up to 9 adjuvant doses. The record does not state a main outcome measure; it describes the study as a safety, feasibility and efficacy study.
NCT06592599.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 evalúa gemcitabina, docetaxel y toripalimab administrados antes de la quimiorradioterapia para el carcinoma nasofaríngeo localmente avanzado asociado al EBV. El toripalimab se administra por vía intravenosa cada 3 semanas junto con 3 ciclos de inducción de gemcitabina y docetaxel, luego radiación (70 Gy) con cisplatino semanal, y después capecitabina por vía oral dos veces al día durante 12 meses, con hasta 9 dosis adyuvantes de toripalimab. El registro no indica una medida de resultado principal; describe el estudio como un estudio de seguridad, factibilidad y eficacia.
who_for: Locoregionally advanced EBV-positive nasopharyngeal carcinoma (T3-4 with any N, or any T with N1-3, and no distant spread)
No prior treatment for nasopharyngeal carcinoma is allowed
ECOG performance status of 0, 1 or 2
Adequate blood counts, liver function and kidney function
Age 18 years or older
not_for: Prior systemic anticancer treatment for nasopharyngeal carcinoma
Prior radiation to the head and neck region that requires overlapping fields
Concurrent use of other anticancer treatment
Autoimmune disease or organ transplant that the investigator judges would raise risk from immune checkpoint inhibition
Pregnant or breastfeeding, or severe active comorbidity or AIDS

NCT05482893.summary_en: This Phase 1/2 study tests spevatamig (PT886), a bispecific antibody that targets CLDN18.2 and CD47, alone or with chemotherapy, targeted therapy, or an immune checkpoint inhibitor, in advanced gastric, gastroesophageal junction, pancreatic, biliary tract, and colorectal cancers. The route of administration and dosing schedule are not stated in the record. The study measures safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and preliminary efficacy.
NCT05482893.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1/2 evalúa spevatamig (PT886), un anticuerpo biespecífico que se dirige a CLDN18.2 y CD47, solo o combinado con quimioterapia, terapia dirigida o un inhibidor de punto de control inmunitario, en cáncer gástrico avanzado, de la unión gastroesofágica, pancreático, de vías biliares y colorrectal. La vía de administración y el esquema de dosis no se indican en el registro. El estudio mide la seguridad, la tolerabilidad, la farmacocinética, la farmacodinamia y la eficacia preliminar.
who_for: Age 18 or older, able to sign consent and follow the protocol.
Measurable disease by RECIST v1.1 criteria.
Unresectable or metastatic gastric, gastroesophageal junction, pancreatic, or biliary tract cancer, or colorectal cancer in some parts, depending on the part an
Able to provide a tumor tissue sample for CLDN18.2 and other biomarker testing.
ECOG performance status of 0 or 1 and adequate organ function.
not_for: Pregnant or breastfeeding women.
Women who could become pregnant and do not use adequate birth control.
Active autoimmune disease that needed systemic treatment in the past 2 years.
Prior CLDN18.2 or CD47 targeting therapy, or SIRPα targeting agents.

NCT06668493.summary_en: Nadofaragene firadenovec is being tested in adults with low-grade upper tract urothelial carcinoma (LG-UTUC), a cancer of the upper urinary tract. It is instilled into the renal pelvis; the record describes repeat dosing, but the number, schedule and length of dosing are not stated. The study measures safety and tolerability, plus complete response at 3 or 6 months, defined as no UTUC in the renal pelvis.
NCT06668493.summary_es: Se está probando nadofaragene firadenovec en adultos con carcinoma urotelial de tracto superior de bajo grado (LG-UTUC), un cáncer de las vías urinarias superiores. Se administra por instilación en la pelvis renal; el registro describe dosis repetidas, pero el número, el calendario y la duración de las dosis no se indican. El estudio mide la seguridad y la tolerabilidad, además de la respuesta completa a los 3 o 6 meses, definida como ausencia de UTUC en la pelvis renal.
who_for: Adults aged 18 or older who can give written informed consent.
Biopsy-proven low-grade upper tract urothelial cancer confirmed by pathology report within 2 months before enrollment.
At least one measurable papillary low-grade tumor of 5 to 15 mm above the ureteropelvic junction.
Willing to be available for at least 18 months after first dosing.
ECOG status of 2 or less and life expectancy over 2 years.
not_for: High-grade cytology or histology, or multifocal UTUC (some low-grade exceptions listed).
Current or past carcinoma in situ or muscle-invasive urothelial cancer in the urogenital tract.
Current or prior mitomycin gel or investigational drug for UTUC.
Known hypersensitivity to nadofaragene firadenovec, interferon alpha-2b, or adenovector medications.
Urinary tract infection or bacterial cystitis at screening (allowed once successfully treated).

NCT06025747.summary_en: This Phase 1 study tests abemaciclib given with radiation therapy before surgery for high-risk adipocytic retroperitoneal sarcoma. Abemaciclib is taken by mouth twice a day on days 1 to 28 of each 28-day cycle, for up to 3 cycles, and radiation therapy is given in 28 fractions starting on cycle 1 day 15, with surgery possible afterward. The study measures safety, side effects, and the best dose of abemaciclib; it is a Phase 1 trial.
NCT06025747.summary_es: Este estudio de Fase 1 evalúa abemaciclib administrado junto con radioterapia antes de la cirugía para el sarcoma retroperitoneal adipocítico de alto riesgo. El abemaciclib se toma por vía oral dos veces al día, los días 1 a 28 de cada ciclo de 28 días, durante hasta 3 ciclos, y la radioterapia se administra en 28 fracciones a partir del día 15 del ciclo 1, con la posibilidad de cirugía después. El estudio mide la seguridad, los efectos secundarios y la mejor dosis de abemaciclib; es un ensayo de Fase 1.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older
Newly diagnosed or locally recurrent MDM2 or CDK4-amplified adipocytic sarcoma with a dedifferentiated component
At least one measurable tumor on CT or MRI
Tumor judged surgically resectable, with plans for radiation therapy followed by surgery
ECOG performance status 0 or 1
not_for: Prior anticancer therapy for this diagnosis, or prior radiation to the affected area
Known brain or central nervous system metastases, or distant metastatic disease
Thromboembolic event within 1 year of treatment start
History of interstitial lung disease
Pregnant or breastfeeding

NCT04999384.summary_en: This study tests a drug called AN4005 in adults with advanced solid tumors or relapsed or refractory lymphoma. AN4005 is taken by mouth twice a day (BID) at dose levels from 50 mg to 600 mg, and the length of treatment is not stated. The study measures safety, tolerability and PK (how the body handles the drug), with the goal of finding the maximum tolerated dose and/or recommended phase 2 dose.
NCT04999384.summary_es: Este estudio prueba un medicamento llamado AN4005 en adultos con tumores sólidos avanzados o linfoma recidivante o refractario. AN4005 se toma por vía oral dos veces al día (BID), en dosis de 50 mg a 600 mg, y la duración del tratamiento no se indica. El estudio mide la seguridad, la tolerancia y la farmacocinética (PK, cómo el cuerpo maneja el medicamento), con el objetivo de encontrar la dosis máxima tolerada y/o la dosis recomendada para fase 2.
who_for: Age 18 or older, and able to give signed consent.
ECOG performance status of 0 or 1.
Life expectancy of at least 3 months.
Advanced solid tumor that is metastatic or unresectable, or relapsed or refractory lymphoma.
No standard life-prolonging treatment available, or standard treatment unsuitable according to the investigator.
not_for: Grade 3 or higher immune-related side effect from prior anti-PD-1, PD-L1 or other T-cell checkpoint therapy.
Systemic anticancer or investigational therapy within 4 weeks or 5 half-lives.
Live vaccine within 30 days before the first dose.
Another primary malignancy within the past 2 years, with listed exceptions.
Significant heart problems, such as heart failure above NYHA Class II or recent heart attack or stroke.

NCT05983276.summary_en: This Phase 2 study tests decitabine and selinexor added to carboplatin and paclitaxel in people with relapsed or treatment-resistant epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer. Treatment uses 28-day cycles: decitabine by IV on days 1 to 5, carboplatin and paclitaxel on day 6, and paclitaxel again on days 13, 20 and 27, with selinexor 60 mg by mouth weekly from day 7 in cycles 2 to 6 (cycle 1 is given once). The study measures side effects, tumor response, immune cell changes, disease progression and overall survival; the primary outcome is not stated.
NCT05983276.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 evalúa decitabina y selinexor añadidos a carboplatino y paclitaxel en personas con cáncer epitelial de ovario, de trompa de Falopio o peritoneal primario recurrente o resistente al tratamiento. El tratamiento se administra en ciclos de 28 días: decitabina por vía intravenosa los días 1 a 5, carboplatino y paclitaxel el día 6, y paclitaxel nuevamente los días 13, 20 y 27, con selinexor 60 mg por vía oral una vez por semana desde el día 7 en los ciclos 2 a 6 (el ciclo 1 se administra una sola vez). El estudio mide los efectos secundarios, la respuesta del tumor, los cambios en las células inmunitarias, la progresión de la enfermedad y la supervivencia global; el resultado principal no se indica.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older with good performance status (ECOG 2 or better)
Epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer that relapsed or progressed after platinum and taxane treatment
Measurable disease by GCIG CA125 criteria
Adequate liver and kidney function, and able to swallow and keep down oral medicines
Stable CNS metastases treated with radiotherapy are allowed
not_for: Previous treatment with selinexor or another XPO1 inhibitor
Known intolerance, hypersensitivity or contraindication to platinum or taxane therapy
Untreated central nervous system metastases
Myocardial infarction within 3 months before starting, or unstable cardiovascular disease
Blood clot related to metastatic disease that needs ongoing anticoagulation

NCT04434040.summary_en: This Phase 2 single-arm trial tests atezolizumab combined with sacituzumab govitecan in triple negative breast cancer that remains after neoadjuvant chemotherapy, in the breast or lymph nodes, with circulating tumor DNA in the blood. Both drugs are given by intravenous (IV) infusion: atezolizumab on day 1 and sacituzumab govitecan on days 1 and 8 of each 21-day cycle, for 6 cycles (18 weeks total). The main outcome measure is not stated; the study is Phase 2.
NCT04434040.summary_es: Este ensayo de Fase 2 de un solo grupo prueba atezolizumab combinado con sacituzumab govitecan en cáncer de mama triple negativo que permanece después de la quimioterapia neoadyuvante, en la mama o los ganglios linfáticos, con ADN tumoral circulante en la sangre. Ambos medicamentos se administran por infusión intravenosa (IV): atezolizumab el día 1 y sacituzumab govitecan los días 1 y 8 de cada ciclo de 21 días, durante 6 ciclos (18 semanas en total). La medida de resultado principal no está indicada; el estudio es de Fase 2.
who_for: Residual invasive breast cancer in the breast and/or lymph nodes after neoadjuvant chemotherapy.
HER2 negative primary tumor by local testing.
ER and PR negative primary tumor (under 10% of cells expressing hormone receptors).
Evidence of ctDNA in a blood sample collected after all neoadjuvant therapy.
ECOG performance status of 0 or 1, and age 18 or older.
not_for: Prior sacituzumab govitecan, irinotecan, or topoisomerase I antibody-drug conjugates for early stage disease.
Receipt of adjuvant chemotherapy after surgery.
Clinical or radiographic evidence of metastatic disease.
Active autoimmune disease, HIV, or hepatitis B or C.
Pregnant or breastfeeding women.

NCT05379595.summary_en: This study tests amivantamab alone and with standard chemotherapy in adults with advanced or metastatic colorectal cancer. Amivantamab is given as an intravenous infusion, with the dose based on body weight; when given alone, it is given on Days 1 and 15 of Cycle 2 of 28-day cycles, and when combined, it is given with mFOLFOX6 or FOLFIRI chemotherapy in 28-day cycles. The study measures anti-tumor activity, the recommended phase 2 combination dose, and safety.
NCT05379595.summary_es: Este estudio prueba amivantamab solo y junto con quimioterapia estándar en adultos con cáncer colorrectal avanzado o metastásico. Amivantamab se administra por infusión intravenosa, con una dosis según el peso corporal; cuando se usa solo, se da los días 1 y 15 del ciclo 2 de ciclos de 28 días, y cuando se combina, se da con quimioterapia mFOLFOX6 o FOLFIRI en ciclos de 28 días. El estudio mide la actividad antitumoral, la dosis recomendada de combinación para fase 2 y la seguridad.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older.
Unresectable or metastatic colon or rectal adenocarcinoma.
Tumor previously found to be wild-type for KRAS, NRAS, and BRAF, without HER2 amplification.
ECOG performance status 0 or 1.
Measurable disease (phase 2) or evaluable disease (phase 1b dose confirmation); tumor amenable to biopsy.
not_for: Identified KRAS, NRAS, BRAF, or EGFR mutation, or HER2 amplification, on central ctDNA testing (cohort-specific).
Symptomatic or untreated brain metastasis.
History or known presence of leptomeningeal disease.
Pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning pregnancy (childbearing potential).
Investigator judges participation not in the participant's best interest.

NCT06723457.summary_en: This phase 2 study tests the combination of epcoritamab and lenalidomide in patients with refractory or relapsed immunodeficiency-related large B-cell lymphoma. Epcoritamab is given under the skin (subcutaneous) weekly during cycle 1, then on days 1, 8, 15 and 22 of cycles 2-3, and on day 1 of cycles 4-12. Lenalidomide is taken by mouth on days 1-21 of each 28-day cycle, for up to 12 months if the disease does not progress and side effects are manageable. The main outcome measure is not stated in the record; the study is a phase 2 trial.
NCT06723457.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 evalúa la combinación de epcoritamab y lenalidomida en pacientes con linfoma de células B grandes relacionado con inmunodeficiencia, refractario o recidivante. El epcoritamab se administra por vía subcutánea una vez por semana durante el ciclo 1, luego los días 1, 8, 15 y 22 de los ciclos 2-3, y el día 1 de los ciclos 4-12. La lenalidomida se toma por vía oral los días 1-21 de cada ciclo de 28 días, durante hasta 12 meses si la enfermedad no progresa y los efectos secundarios son manejables. El registro no indica el resultado principal que se mide; el estudio es de fase 2.
who_for: Confirmed immunodeficiency-related large B-cell lymphoma, including monomorphic post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder or certain polymorphic B-cell disor
Disease that did not respond well to first-line chemo-immunotherapy or rituximab, or that came back after a complete response.
Judged ineligible for CAR-T cell therapy.
At least one measurable lesion on CT or MRI under Lugano criteria.
Age 18 or older with ECOG performance status 0-2.
not_for: Prior therapy with a bispecific T-cell engager targeting CD3 and CD20.
Chemotherapy or other antineoplastic therapy within about 1 week, or autologous stem cell transplant within 100 days.
Active disease in the central nervous system or uncontrolled seizures.
Myocardial infarction or stroke within 6 months, or left ventricular ejection fraction below 45%.
Pregnancy or breastfeeding, or live vaccine within 30 days before the first dose.

NCT05190471.summary_en: This phase 1 study tests BP1002, a liposomal Bcl-2 antisense oligodeoxynucleotide, in adults with refractory or relapsed acute myeloid leukemia (AML). BP1002 is first given alone at escalating doses and later with decitabine; the route, how often, and how long it is given are not stated. The main outcome is safety and tolerability, and the study also looks at dose-limiting toxicities, biologically effective doses, pharmacokinetics, and anti-leukemic effects.
NCT05190471.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1 evalúa BP1002, un oligodesoxinucleótido antisentido liposomal dirigido a Bcl-2, en adultos con leucemia mieloide aguda (LMA) refractaria o en recaída. BP1002 se administra primero solo en dosis crecientes y después en combinación con decitabina; la vía, la frecuencia y la duración del tratamiento no se indican. El resultado principal es la seguridad y la tolerabilidad, y el estudio también analiza las toxicidades limitantes de dosis, las dosis biológicamente efectivas, la farmacocinética y los efectos antileucémicos.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older with refractory or relapsed AML that did not respond to available active therapies
ECOG performance status of 0, 1, or 2
For the expansion phase, eligible to receive decitabine
Adequate liver and kidney function, including creatinine clearance of at least 60 mL/min
Agree to use contraception and able to give written informed consent
not_for: Active non-blood cancer, or other cancer treated within the past 12 months
Leptomeningeal leukemia needing intrathecal therapy
Acute promyelocytic leukemia with PML-RARA, or chronic myeloid leukemia
Anti-cancer therapy within 14 days before the first dose, or other investigational agents
Pregnant or breastfeeding, or uncontrolled heart, seizure, or other conditions that may interfere with study participation

NCT07069699.summary_en: This Phase 1b/2 trial tests pidnarulex (CX-5461) in adults with aggressive B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma that has MYC gene changes. Pidnarulex is given by IV over 60 minutes on days 1 and 8 of each 21-day cycle, and cycles repeat without disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. The trial is listed as Phase 1/Phase 2 and aims to assess safety, side effects, best dose and how well the treatment works.
NCT07069699.summary_es: Este ensayo de fase 1b/2 evalúa pidnarulex (CX-5461) en adultos con linfoma no Hodgkin de células B agresivo que presenta cambios en el gen MYC. El pidnarulex se administra por vía intravenosa durante 60 minutos los días 1 y 8 de cada ciclo de 21 días, y los ciclos se repiten sin progresión de la enfermedad ni toxicidad inaceptable. El ensayo está registrado como fase 1/fase 2 y busca evaluar la seguridad, los efectos secundarios, la dosis óptima y qué tan bien funciona el tratamiento.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older.
Aggressive B-cell lymphoma of double-expressor, high-grade with MYC and BCL2 and/or BCL6 rearrangement, or Burkitt type.
At least two prior lines for DLBCL, or at least one prior line for Burkitt lymphoma, with no effective standard options left.
Performance status ECOG 2 or better; ECOG 3 allowed if related to the lymphoma.
Adequate blood counts, liver and kidney function, and heart function (NYHA class II or better).
not_for: Taking strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or strong CYP3A4 inducers.
Baseline QTc interval above 480 msec.
Currently receiving other investigational agents.
Prior allergic reaction to compounds similar to CX-5461.
Pregnant or breastfeeding.

NCT07785609.summary_en: This study tests MK-2010 given together with sacituzumab tirumotecan (sac-TMT) in people with advanced solid tumors. Both drugs are given as an intravenous (IV) infusion, and how long or how often they are given is not stated. The study measures safety and tolerability, and how many participants have their cancer respond to treatment; it is a Phase 2 study.
NCT07785609.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa MK-2010 administrado junto con sacituzumab tirumotecan (sac-TMT) en personas con tumores sólidos avanzados. Ambos medicamentos se administran por infusión intravenosa (IV); la duración y la frecuencia no se indican en el registro. El estudio mide la seguridad y la tolerabilidad, y cuántos participantes tienen una respuesta del cáncer al tratamiento; es un estudio de fase 2.
who_for: Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 0 or 1
Has adequate organ function
If HIV-infected, HIV is well controlled on antiretroviral therapy
If hepatitis B surface antigen positive, undetectable HBV viral load and at least 4 weeks of HBV antiviral therapy
If history of hepatitis C infection, undetectable HCV viral load
not_for: Prior systemic anticancer therapy within 4 weeks or 5 half-lives before allocation
Active or known central nervous system metastases or carcinomatous meningitis
Noninfectious pneumonitis or interstitial lung disease requiring steroids, current pneumonitis, or suspected ILD
Active or ongoing stomatitis or mucositis of any grade
Currently receiving any anticoagulants

NCT06500884.summary_en: This Phase 2 study tests preventive treatments (Prophylaxis A, B, C and D) for taste changes (dysgeusia) caused by talquetamab in relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma. Talquetamab is given under the skin, and Prophylaxis A, B and C are taken by mouth starting 7 days before talquetamab, while Prophylaxis D is applied topically starting 1 day before. Prophylaxis may continue for up to 12 months, and longer at the physician's discretion, and the study also describes taste changes with ramantamig, given under the skin as one step-up dose followed by a treatment dose. The record states the aim is to see whether these preventive treatments reduce the occurrence, severity and duration of taste changes, but no formal main outcome measure is listed.
NCT06500884.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 evalúa tratamientos preventivos (profilaxis A, B, C y D) para los cambios en el gusto (disgeusia) causados por talquetamab en mieloma múltiple recidivante o refractario. Talquetamab se administra debajo de la piel, y las profilaxis A, B y C se toman por vía oral comenzando 7 días antes de talquetamab, mientras que la profilaxis D se aplica por vía tópica comenzando 1 día antes. La profilaxis puede continuar hasta 12 meses, y más tiempo a criterio del médico, y el estudio también describe los cambios en el gusto con ramantamig, que se administra debajo de la piel como una dosis inicial escalonada seguida de la dosis de tratamiento. El registro indica que el objetivo es ver si estos tratamientos preventivos reducen la aparición, la gravedad y la duración de los cambios en el gusto, pero no se incluye una medida de resultado principal formal.
who_for: Multiple myeloma that has come back or stopped responding
Previously treated with a proteasome inhibitor, an immunomodulatory drug, and an anti-CD38 antibody
Documented disease progression after the last treatment regimen
ECOG performance status 0 or 1; 2 or 3 only if due to stable limits not related to myeloma
Age 18 years or older and willing to follow protocol lifestyle restrictions
not_for: Life-threatening allergy or intolerance to study drugs or their excipients
Stroke, transient ischemic attack, or seizure within 6 months before screening
Serious heart events or NYHA class III or IV heart failure within 6 months before first dose
Major surgery or significant trauma within 2 weeks, or planned major surgery
Severe dysgeusia at screening, or oral conditions such as active infections or prior mouth cancer

NCT07231952.summary_en: This Phase 2 study tests a combination of pirtobrutinib, venetoclax, and rituximab in people with treatment-naive Waldenström's macroglobulinemia (WM) or lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma (LPL). Pirtobrutinib and venetoclax are taken by mouth once daily, and rituximab is given by intravenous (IV) or subcutaneous (SC) route; how long treatment lasts is not stated. The study aims to find out whether the combination is effective, but the main outcome measure is not stated.
NCT07231952.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 evalúa una combinación de pirtobrutinib, venetoclax y rituximab en personas con macroglobulinemia de Waldenström (WM) o linfoma linfoplasmocítico (LPL) que no han recibido tratamiento previo. El pirtobrutinib y el venetoclax se toman por vía oral una vez al día, y el rituximab se administra por vía intravenosa (IV) o subcutánea (SC); la duración del tratamiento no se indica. El estudio busca saber si la combinación es eficaz, pero el resultado principal a medir no se indica.
who_for: Adults aged 18 years or older.
Treatment-naive WM or IgM-type LPL with measurable disease.
Has at least one standard criterion requiring treatment, such as anemia, low platelets, or bulky disease.
ECOG performance status of 2 or less, with adequate blood counts and organ function.
Able to swallow pills and sign informed consent.
not_for: Prior systemic therapy for this disease.
Major bleeding or grade 3 or higher arrhythmia on a prior BTK inhibitor.
Significant heart disease, or QTcF above 470 msec.
Positive HIV test, or active hepatitis B or C infection.
Pregnancy or breastfeeding, or recent stem cell transplant or CAR-T therapy.

NCT07140315.summary_en: This Phase 1 study tests a new imaging tracer, [18F]DK222, in people with non-small cell lung cancer or urothelial cancer. The tracer is injected into a vein, and participants then get a PET/CT scan; how often or for how long is not stated. The study is designed to evaluate the safety and diagnostic performance of the tracer.
NCT07140315.summary_es: Este estudio de Fase 1 prueba un nuevo trazador de imagen, [18F]DK222, en personas con cáncer de pulmón de células no pequeñas o cáncer urotelial. El trazador se inyecta en una vena y luego los participantes se someten a una tomografía por emisión de positrones con tomografía computarizada (PET/CT); la frecuencia o la duración no se indican. El estudio está diseñado para evaluar la seguridad y el rendimiento diagnóstico del trazador.
who_for: Adults 18 or older who can give informed consent.
Confirmed non-small cell lung cancer or urothelial cancer, and eligible for anti-PD(L)-1 therapy.
ECOG performance status of 0 to 2.
Blood counts, kidney, and liver tests within acceptable limits, checked within 28 days before registration.
Women who could become pregnant need a negative pregnancy test and must use contraception.
not_for: Prior treatment with an anti-PD-L1 or anti-PD-L2 antibody, unless at least a 4-month washout has passed.
Side effects from earlier cancer treatment not recovered to grade 1 or better.
Increasing corticosteroid dose in the 7 days before the first anti-PD1 dose.
Severe allergic reaction to a prior monoclonal antibody or to study drug components.
Serious uncontrolled medical condition or active infection, pregnancy or breastfeeding.

NCT05430035.summary_en: This early phase study tests prophylactic heated intraperitoneal chemotherapy (HIPEC) with mitomycin C to lower the risk of peritoneal recurrence in people with gallbladder adenocarcinoma who are at high risk of that recurrence. The drug is delivered into the abdomen during surgery: 30 mg of mitomycin C over the first 60 minutes, then 10 mg over an additional 30 minutes, with the fluid heated to a tissue temperature of 42°. The study measures feasibility, including intra-operative complications, technical challenges, 90-day morbidity and mortality, length of stay, and readmission.
NCT05430035.summary_es: Este estudio en fase temprana evalúa la quimioterapia intraperitoneal calentada (HIPEC) preventiva con mitomicina C para reducir el riesgo de recurrencia peritoneal en personas con adenocarcinoma de vesícula biliar que tienen alto riesgo de esa recurrencia. El medicamento se administra dentro del abdomen durante la cirugía: 30 mg de mitomicina C durante los primeros 60 minutos, seguidos de 10 mg durante 30 minutos adicionales, con el líquido calentado a una temperatura tisular de 42°. El estudio mide la factibilidad, incluidas las complicaciones intraoperatorias, los desafíos técnicos, la morbilidad y mortalidad a 90 días, la duración de la estancia hospitalaria y los reingresos.
who_for: Confirmed gallbladder adenocarcinoma with bile spillage or intentional decompression during cholecystectomy, tumor through the gallbladder wall (T3/T4), or poor
ECOG performance status of 2 or less
Blood counts, liver tests, and creatinine within the required limits
Eligible for standard central liver resection and portal lymphadenectomy
Able to understand and sign written informed consent
not_for: Prior systemic therapy for gallbladder adenocarcinoma
Receiving other investigational agents, or known or suspected metastatic disease
Allergic reactions to mitomycin C or similar compounds
Uncontrolled illness, or pregnancy or breastfeeding
History of hepatitis B or C, or cancer-related biliary obstruction including need for a biliary stent

NCT05365035.summary_en: This study tests whether cladribine, low dose cytarabine, venetoclax, and azacitidine together can help control higher-risk myelodysplastic syndrome with excess blasts and/or higher-risk chronic myelomonocytic leukemia. Participants receive cladribine, cytarabine, and venetoclax for 2 cycles, then azacitidine and venetoclax for 2 cycles, repeating this pattern for up to a total of 18 (the unit is not fully stated in the record). The main outcome is not stated; this is a Phase 2 study.
NCT05365035.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa si la combinación de cladribina, citarabina a dosis bajas, venetoclax y azacitidina puede ayudar a controlar el síndrome mielodisplásico de mayor riesgo con exceso de blastos y/o la leucemia mielomonocítica crónica de mayor riesgo. Los participantes reciben cladribina, citarabina y venetoclax durante 2 ciclos, y luego azacitidina y venetoclax durante 2 ciclos, repitiendo este patrón hasta un total de 18 (la unidad no está completamente indicada en el registro). El resultado principal no se indica; este es un estudio de Fase 2.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older with higher-risk MDS or CMML.
Patients who did not respond to, or relapsed after, certain azacitidine-type drugs, or who have not received these drugs before (cohorts vary).
Daily activity level (performance status) of 2 or lower.
Adequate kidney and liver function.
Able to sign an informed consent document.
not_for: Uncontrolled infection that does not respond to antibiotics.
Heart failure of NYHA class III or IV, or ejection fraction below 50%.
Heart attack within the last 6 months, or unstable or uncontrolled angina.
Pregnant or breastfeeding women, or those with reproductive potential unwilling to use required contraception.
Receiving another investigational drug, chemotherapy, radiotherapy, or immunotherapy.

NCT03093116.summary_en: The study tests repotrectinib (TPX-0005) in people with advanced solid tumors that have an ALK, ROS1, or NTRK1-3 gene rearrangement. Repotrectinib is given by mouth as oral capsules, and how long or how often it is taken is not stated. The Phase 2 part measures the confirmed overall response rate, as assessed by blinded independent central review.
NCT03093116.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa repotrectinib (TPX-0005) en personas con tumores sólidos avanzados que tienen una reordenación de los genes ALK, ROS1 o NTRK1-3. Repotrectinib se administra por vía oral en forma de cápsulas, y la duración o la frecuencia del tratamiento no se indican. La parte de fase 2 mide la tasa de respuesta global confirmada, evaluada por una revisión central independiente y ciega.
who_for: Advanced or metastatic solid tumor with a documented ROS1 or NTRK1-3 gene fusion
ECOG performance status 0 to 1
Age 12 or older; ages 12 to 17 need parent or guardian assent
At least one measurable lesion by RECIST 1.1, confirmed before enrollment
Life expectancy of at least 3 months
not_for: Taking part in another therapeutic clinical trial at the same time
Symptomatic brain metastases or leptomeningeal involvement
Clinically significant heart disease within 6 months, or abnormal QTc
Active infection, including HIV positivity
Peripheral neuropathy of grade 2 or higher, or grade 3 to 4 interstitial lung disease

NCT07750158.summary_en: This study tests zanzalintinib, alone or with pembrolizumab plus berahyaluronidase alfa, compared with placebo, in people with stage II or III colorectal cancer that has molecular residual disease after definitive therapy. Zanzalintinib is taken as an oral tablet once daily, and pembrolizumab with berahyaluronidase alfa is given as a subcutaneous injection every 3 weeks, for up to 2 years. The study measures effectiveness compared with placebo as its primary objective; the specific outcome measure is not stated, and this is a Phase 3 study.
NCT07750158.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa zanzalintinib, solo o junto con pembrolizumab más berahyaluronidase alfa, comparado con placebo, en personas con cáncer colorrectal en etapa II o III con enfermedad residual molecular después del tratamiento definitivo. Zanzalintinib se toma como tableta oral una vez al día, y pembrolizumab con berahyaluronidase alfa se aplica como inyección subcutánea cada 3 semanas, durante hasta 2 años. El estudio mide la efectividad comparada con placebo como objetivo principal; la medida específica del resultado no se indica, y es un estudio de fase 3.
who_for: Stage II or III colon or rectal adenocarcinoma with completed definitive therapy.
Local test shows MSS, MSI-low, or pMMR status.
Positive for circulating tumor DNA on local Natera Signatera MRD test.
No radiographic evidence of disease on baseline CT or MRI scans.
Age 18 years or older.
not_for: Prior treatment with immune checkpoint inhibitors or VEGFR inhibitors.
History of solid organ or allogeneic stem cell transplant.
Another cancer that is progressing or needed active treatment within 2 years.
Colorectal cancer that needed systemic therapy before definitive therapy.
Systemic anticancer or radiation therapy after completing definitive therapy.

NCT04205968.summary_en: This Phase 2 study compares ramucirumab with paclitaxel against the FOLFIRI chemotherapy regimen in adults with advanced or refractory small intestinal adenocarcinoma. Ramucirumab and paclitaxel are given by vein (IV): ramucirumab on days 1 and 15 of each 28-day cycle, and paclitaxel on days 1, 8 and 15. FOLFIRI is also given by IV in 28-day cycles, and cycles repeat without disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. The record does not state the main outcome measured; it is a Phase 2 study.
NCT04205968.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 compara ramucirumab con paclitaxel contra el régimen de quimioterapia FOLFIRI en adultos con adenocarcinoma de intestino delgado avanzado o refractario. Ramucirumab y paclitaxel se administran por vena (IV): ramucirumab los días 1 y 15 de cada ciclo de 28 días, y paclitaxel los días 1, 8 y 15. FOLFIRI también se administra por IV en ciclos de 28 días, y los ciclos se repiten mientras no haya progresión de la enfermedad ni toxicidad inaceptable. El registro no indica el resultado principal que se mide; es un estudio de fase 2.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older
Small bowel adenocarcinoma confirmed by tissue or cell testing
Metastatic or locally advanced disease that cannot be removed by surgery
Disease that progressed on prior fluoropyrimidine and/or oxaliplatin therapy
Zubrod performance status of 0 or 1
not_for: Prior irinotecan, taxane, or ramucirumab for small bowel adenocarcinoma
Tumors with deficient mismatch repair (dMMR) or microsatellite instability high (MSI-H)
Recent arterial or venous blood clot, or recent grade 3-4 GI bleeding
History of GI perforation or fistula within 120 days
Chronic antiplatelet therapy or uncontrolled high blood pressure

NCT07129993.summary_en: This Phase 2/3 study compares datopotamab deruxtecan plus carboplatin or cisplatin with gemcitabine plus carboplatin or cisplatin in urothelial carcinoma that has progressed during or after enfortumab vedotin and pembrolizumab. Datopotamab deruxtecan is given by IV infusion every three weeks at 4 mg/kg or 6 mg/kg, and the comparison arm gets gemcitabine on Days 1 and 8 of each three-week cycle; how long treatment continues is not stated. The record does not state a primary outcome, but Part A (Phase 2) assesses preliminary efficacy and safety, and the Phase 3 part starts depending on Phase 2 results.
NCT07129993.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2/3 compara datopotamab deruxtecan más carboplatino o cisplatino con gemcitabina más carboplatino o cisplatino en carcinoma urotelial que progresó durante o después de enfortumab vedotina y pembrolizumab. El datopotamab deruxtecan se administra por infusión intravenosa cada tres semanas a 4 mg/kg o 6 mg/kg, y el brazo de comparación recibe gemcitabina los días 1 y 8 de cada ciclo de tres semanas; el registro no indica cuánto tiempo continúa el tratamiento. El registro no indica un desenlace principal, pero la Parte A (fase 2) evalúa la eficacia preliminar y la seguridad, y la parte de fase 3 comienza según los resultados de la fase 2.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older.
Unresectable, locally advanced, or metastatic urothelial carcinoma, confirmed by tissue or cell testing.
Radiographic progression during or after first-line enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab (or similar agents).
Considered eligible for cisplatin- or carboplatin-containing chemotherapy by the investigator.
Must provide a tumor tissue sample for biomarker testing.
not_for: Prior systemic therapy for advanced disease other than enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab, with some exceptions needing sponsor approval.
Prior TROP2-directed antibody-drug conjugate therapy.
History of allogeneic bone marrow or solid organ transplant.
Uncontrolled or significant cardiovascular disease, including QTcF above 470 ms.
History of non-infectious interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis requiring steroids, or current or suspected ILD/pneumonitis.

NCT02861898.summary_en: This study tests repeated intra-arterial infusions of cetuximab (CTX) after blood brain barrier disruption, given with standard chemotherapy and radiation, in newly diagnosed glioblastoma. Patients receive mannitol to disrupt the blood brain barrier, then three intra-arterial doses of cetuximab at 250 mg/m2, given at about days 30, 120 and 210 after surgery. The record does not state a main outcome measure; it is a Phase I/II trial.
