NCT02861898.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa infusiones intraarteriales repetidas de cetuximab (CTX) después de alterar la barrera hematoencefálica, administradas junto con quimioterapia y radioterapia estándar, en glioblastoma de diagnóstico reciente. Los pacientes reciben manitol para alterar la barrera hematoencefálica y luego tres dosis intraarteriales de cetuximab de 250 mg/m2, aproximadamente a los días 30, 120 y 210 después de la cirugía. El registro no indica una medida de resultado principal; es un ensayo de Fase I/II.
who_for: Adults 18 or older with newly diagnosed glioblastoma.
Tumor shows EGFR overexpression confirmed by pathology.
At least one biopsy-proven, evaluable tumor site.
Karnofsky performance status 70% or higher, or ECOG 0-2.
Expected survival of at least three months.
not_for: Pregnant or breastfeeding women.
Radiological evidence of leptomeningeal disease.
Prior allergic reaction to cetuximab.
Chemotherapy or radiation already started or completed before enrollment.
Significant medical or psychiatric conditions that raise risk or affect treatment or monitoring.

NCT07612215.summary_en:
The study tests elacestrant, a pill that targets the estrogen receptor, together with trastuzumab and pertuzumab, in advanced triple-positive breast cancer. It includes patients with and without an ESR1 mutation. The study is Phase 1/Phase 2.
Elacestrant is taken by mouth once daily at 345 mg. Trastuzumab and pertuzumab are given by IV infusion every 3 weeks. All drugs continue until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, or as the study doctor decides.
The main outcome measure is not stated. The study aims to assess safety and efficacy.
NCT07612215.summary_es:
El estudio evalúa elacestrant, una pastilla que actúa sobre el receptor de estrógeno, junto con trastuzumab y pertuzumab, en cáncer de mama triple positivo avanzado. Incluye a pacientes con y sin mutación en ESR1. El estudio es de Fase 1/Fase 2.
Elacestrant se toma por vía oral una vez al día, a una dosis de 345 mg. Trastuzumab y pertuzumab se administran por infusión intravenosa cada 3 semanas. Todos los medicamentos continúan hasta la progresión de la enfermedad, toxicidad inaceptable o según decida el médico del estudio.
El resultado principal del estudio no está indicado. El estudio busca evaluar la seguridad y la eficacia.
who_for: Women aged 18 or older who can give informed consent.
Histologically confirmed triple-positive breast cancer (ER, PR and HER2 positive).
Disease progression after at least one line of prior recommended therapy.
ECOG performance status of 2 or less.
Adequate blood counts and heart function (LVEF at least 50% or institutional lower limit of normal).
not_for: Prior treatment with a SERD.
More than two lines of chemotherapy for metastatic disease, including antibody drug conjugates.
Untreated or active brain (CNS) metastases.
Other malignancy within the past 5 years, with listed exceptions.
Male participants.

NCT06234098.summary_en: The study tests AT-1965 liposome injection in adults with advanced, refractory or recurrent solid tumors, including metastatic triple-negative breast cancer. AT-1965 is given into a vein once a week on days 1, 8 and 15 of each 4-week cycle, and the total length of treatment is not stated. The Phase 1/2 study measures the maximum tolerated dose or recommended Phase 2 dose and dose-limiting toxicities, along with safety and early signs of antitumor activity.
NCT06234098.summary_es: El estudio evalúa el liposoma inyectable AT-1965 en adultos con tumores sólidos avanzados, refractarios o recurrentes, incluido el cáncer de mama triple negativo metastásico. AT-1965 se administra por vena una vez por semana los días 1, 8 y 15 de cada ciclo de 4 semanas, y la duración total del tratamiento no se indica. Es un estudio de fase 1/2 que mide la dosis máxima tolerada o la dosis recomendada para fase 2, las toxicidades limitantes de dosis, la seguridad y las primeras señales de actividad antitumoral.
who_for: Unresectable or metastatic solid tumor that is refractory to standard therapy, or for which no standard therapy is suitable in the investigator's opinion.
At least one measurable lesion per RECIST version 1.1; Part A may allow non-measurable disease after sponsor discussion.
Age 18 or older with ECOG performance status 0 to 2.
Adequate blood counts, kidney function and liver function, as defined in the criteria.
Part B: metastatic triple-negative breast cancer after at least two prior treatments, including a taxane and sacituzumab govitecan-hziy; some subgroups need pri
not_for: Uncontrolled or unstable serious medical conditions, or uncontrolled diabetes.
History of interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis, or active pneumonitis within the last 6 months.
Clinically significant heart disease, including recent heart attack or stroke, LVEF below 50%, or QTcF of 470 msec or higher.
Anticancer therapy within 21 days, radiation within 2 weeks, or major surgery within 4 weeks.
Known HIV, unresolved hepatitis B or C, history of hemolysis, or adrenal gland disorders.

NCT06784726.summary_en: This phase 2 trial tests odronextamab given before CAR-T cell therapy as bridging therapy in adults with relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma. Odronextamab is given by intravenous infusion, with step-up dosing in cycle 1, then 160 mg weekly in cycles 2 to 4, then 320 mg every other week for the remaining cycles. The main outcome measure is not stated; the record describes the trial as phase 2.
NCT06784726.summary_es: Este ensayo de fase 2 evalúa odronextamab administrado antes de la terapia con células CAR-T como terapia puente en adultos con linfoma de células B grandes recidivante o refractario. Odronextamab se administra por infusión intravenosa, con dosis escalonadas en el ciclo 1, luego 160 mg semanales en los ciclos 2 a 4 y después 320 mg cada dos semanas en los ciclos restantes. La medida de resultado principal no se indica en el registro; el registro describe el estudio como de fase 2.
who_for: Histologically confirmed large B-cell lymphoma of the listed types, such as DLBCL, primary mediastinal, or high grade B-cell lymphoma.
At least one measurable lesion of 15 mm or more on PET, CT, or MRI.
Lymphoma failed prior frontline therapy and the patient meets criteria for a commercial CAR-T therapy.
Prior treatment with an anti-CD20 antibody therapy.
ECOG performance status 0 to 1; status 2 may be allowed if caused by lymphoma, at physician discretion.
not_for: Malignant cells in cerebrospinal fluid, or brain metastases (history of secondary CNS lymphoma may be allowed under conditions).
Prior anti-CD20 x anti-CD3 bispecific therapy, unless specific response and CD20 conditions are met.
Prior allogeneic stem cell transplant or any prior CAR-T cell therapy.
Known active, uncontrolled infection; HIV or chronic hepatitis B or C, with some exceptions.
Pregnant or breast-feeding women.

NCT05274048.summary_en: This Phase 1 trial tests neratinib together with fam-trastuzumab deruxtecan-nxki (TDxD) in advanced or unresectable gastric and esophageal cancer that overexpresses HER2, and in other gastrointestinal cancers with HER2 IHC 3+. Neratinib is taken as a daily pill on days 1 through 21 at doses of 120 mg, 160 mg, or 200 mg, and TDxD is given intravenously on day 1 of each 21-day cycle at a standard dose of 5.4 mg/m2. The study measures safety, toxicity, the recommended phase 2 dose, and the maximum tolerated dose.
NCT05274048.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1 prueba neratinib junto con fam-trastuzumab deruxtecan-nxki (TDxD) en cáncer gástrico y esofágico avanzado o no resecable que sobreexpresa HER2, y en otros cánceres gastrointestinales con HER2 IHC 3+. El neratinib se toma como pastilla diaria los días 1 al 21, en dosis de 120 mg, 160 mg o 200 mg, y el TDxD se administra por vía intravenosa el día 1 de cada ciclo de 21 días, a una dosis estándar de 5.4 mg/m2. El estudio mide la seguridad, la toxicidad, la dosis recomendada para fase 2 y la dosis máxima tolerada.
who_for: Unresectable or metastatic gastrointestinal cancer, such as esophagus, stomach, colon, biliary, pancreas, or unknown primary likely GI.
HER2 overexpression: IHC 3+ or IHC2+/ISH+ for gastroesophageal cancer; IHC 3+ for other GI cancers.
Progressed or intolerant after at least one prior HER2-directed therapy for metastatic disease (gastroesophageal cancers).
Measurable or evaluable disease by RECIST 1.1.
ECOG performance status 0-2 with blood counts and organ function within the stated limits.
not_for: Chemotherapy or radiotherapy within 2 weeks before the first dose, or prior treatment with TDxD.
Known untreated brain metastases.
Interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis, or lung disease needing oxygen support.
Use of strong inhibitors or inducers of neratinib or TDxD.
Pregnant or breastfeeding.

NCT06520098.summary_en: This study compares continuing a Bruton tyrosine kinase inhibitor (BTKi) alone with adding venetoclax to the BTKi in veterans with chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) or small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL). Both drugs are taken by mouth as pills; the comparison arm keeps the BTKi alone as long as it is working, while the other arm adds venetoclax to the BTKi for 12 cycles (one year), then stops both pills and monitors participants closely. The main outcome measure is not stated; this is a Phase 2 study.
NCT06520098.summary_es: Este estudio compara continuar solo con un inhibidor de la tirosina quinasa de Bruton (BTKi) frente a añadir venetoclax al BTKi en veteranos con leucemia linfocítica crónica (LLC) o linfoma linfocítico de pequeñas células (LLPC). Ambos medicamentos se toman por vía oral en forma de pastillas; el grupo de comparación mantiene solo el BTKi mientras le funcione, y el otro grupo añade venetoclax al BTKi durante 12 ciclos (un año), luego suspende ambas pastillas y los participantes son vigilados de cerca. El resultado principal no está indicado en el registro; este es un estudio de Fase 2.
who_for: Diagnosed with CLL or SLL, with the blood cell or lymph node criteria stated in the record
Currently receiving a BTK inhibitor (ibrutinib, acalabrutinib, or zanubrutinib) for at least six months
BTK inhibitor dose stable for at least the past three months
Performance status 0 to 2 on the standard ECOG scale
Detectable or measurable disease, with low tumor lysis syndrome risk (lymph nodes under 5 cm, lymphocyte count under 25 x 10^9/L)
not_for: Disease that progressed on BTK inhibitor therapy before starting study treatment
Previous treatment with the combination of a BTK inhibitor and venetoclax
History of Richter's transformation or prolymphocytic leukemia
Heart failure (NYHA class III or IV), unstable angina, or uncontrolled arrhythmia
Taking active anticoagulation with heparin or warfarin, or needing more than 20 mg daily of prednisone or equivalent

NCT07016399.summary_en: This phase II trial tests adding darolutamide to standard chemotherapy and immunotherapy before surgery, compared with standard therapy alone, in stage II-IIIA androgen receptor positive triple-negative breast cancer. Darolutamide is taken by mouth twice a day for 14 days in the experimental arm, and the standard drugs are given by vein (IV) in 21-day cycles, up to 8 cycles in total, before surgery. The record does not state the main outcome measure; the study is a phase II trial.
NCT07016399.summary_es: Este ensayo de fase II evalúa agregar darolutamida a la quimioterapia y la inmunoterapia estándar antes de la cirugía, en comparación con el tratamiento estándar solo, en cáncer de mama triple negativo con receptor de andrógenos positivo en etapa II-IIIA. En el grupo experimental, la darolutamida se toma por vía oral dos veces al día durante 14 días, y los medicamentos estándar se administran por vena (IV) en ciclos de 21 días, hasta 8 ciclos en total, antes de la cirugía. El registro no indica la medida de resultado principal; el estudio es de fase II.
who_for: Adults 18 or older with newly diagnosed breast cancer, stage II-IIIA.
Estrogen receptor and progesterone receptor staining under 10%.
HER2 negative by FISH.
Androgen receptor staining of at least 80% by IHC.
ECOG performance status of 0 or 1.
not_for: Breast cancer that cannot be removed by surgery, or that has spread to other sites.
Other cancers (not triple-negative breast cancer) within 5 years, except low-risk or adequately treated cases.
Pregnant or breastfeeding.
Moderate or severe liver impairment (Child-Pugh Class B or higher).
Heart disease that is clinically significant, myocarditis or pericarditis, or stroke or TIA within 6 months.

NCT07857616.summary_en: This study is testing SI-B036 in adults with advanced or metastatic solid tumors that have not responded to standard treatments. It is a Phase 1/1b, first-in-human, open-label study. SI-B036 is given by intravenous (IV) infusion on Day 1 of each 3-week cycle; the total duration is not stated. The main outcome is safety and tolerability.
NCT07857616.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa SI-B036 en adultos con tumores sólidos avanzados o metastásicos que no han respondido a los tratamientos estándar. Es un estudio de Fase 1/1b, de primera administración en humanos, sin enmascaramiento. SI-B036 se administra por infusión intravenosa (IV) el día 1 de cada ciclo de 3 semanas; la duración total no se indica. El resultado principal es la seguridad y la tolerabilidad.
who_for: Adults 18 or older with a locally advanced or metastatic solid tumor not treatable with curative surgery or radiation.
Received at least one line of standard therapy, or cancer is refractory to standard care, or no standard treatment exists.
Side effects from prior anticancer treatment have improved to grade 1 or lower.
Left ventricular ejection fraction of at least 50% and no serious heart dysfunction.
Dose expansion only: specific groups for non-small cell lung cancer, melanoma, or ovarian cancer with defined prior treatment rules.
not_for: Anticancer, immunotherapy, or targeted therapy within 4 weeks or 5 half-lives before the first dose, whichever is shorter.
Severe heart disease within 6 months, or prolonged QT interval or other QT-related risk factors.
Current or past noninfectious lung inflammation (ILD or pneumonitis) that needed steroids, or current ILD.
Active or untreated brain metastases, CNS tumors, or carcinomatous meningitis.
Pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning pregnancy during the study.

NCT06697184.summary_en: This Phase 1/2 study tests new dose ramp-up schedules for the drug sonrotoclax, given with zanubrutinib, in adults with chronic lymphocytic leukemia or mantle cell lymphoma. Participants first take zanubrutinib alone, then add oral sonrotoclax using a ramp-up schedule, for 15 cycles of 28 days in one arm or 27 cycles of 28 days in the other, with the second arm then continuing zanubrutinib alone until progression or other stopping criteria. The main goal stated is to establish the safety of these novel dosing and ramp-up schedules.
NCT06697184.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1/2 evalúa nuevos esquemas de aumento gradual de dosis del medicamento sonrotoclax, administrado junto con zanubrutinib, en adultos con leucemia linfocítica crónica o linfoma de células del manto. Los participantes primero toman zanubrutinib solo y luego agregan sonrotoclax oral con un esquema de aumento gradual, durante 15 ciclos de 28 días en un grupo o 27 ciclos de 28 días en el otro, y en este último grupo continúan con zanubrutinib solo hasta la progresión u otros criterios de suspensión. El objetivo principal indicado es establecer la seguridad de estos nuevos esquemas de dosis y de aumento gradual.
who_for: Stable ECOG performance status of 2 or better.
Adequate organ function and no very recent transfusion or blood growth factor.
CLL: confirmed diagnosis needing treatment, with at least one measurable lesion on CT or MRI.
MCL: confirmed diagnosis, relapsed or refractory after at least one prior line of systemic therapy, with measurable disease.
Participants who can have children must use a highly effective birth control method.
not_for: Unable to comply with the protocol requirements.
Active hepatitis B or hepatitis C infection.
Positive HIV serology, unless certain conditions are met.
Major surgical procedure within 28 days before the first dose.
Prior systemic treatment for CLL, or prior exposure to a BCL-2 inhibitor.

NCT06800963.summary_en: This study tests intravesical recombinant Mycobacterium BCG (rMBCG), a drug placed into the bladder, in adults with non-muscle invasive bladder cancer who have not had BCG before. It is given as one vial (19.2e8 colony-forming units) through a urinary catheter into the bladder as an induction course; the number of doses and how often are not stated. The main outcome measure is not stated; the study is a Phase 1/2 trial.
NCT06800963.summary_es: Este estudio prueba el Mycobacterium BCG recombinante intravesical (rMBCG), un medicamento que se coloca en la vejiga, en adultos con cáncer de vejiga no músculo invasivo que nunca han recibido BCG. Se administra como un vial (19.2e8 unidades formadoras de colonias) por una sonda urinaria dentro de la vejiga, como curso de inducción; el número de dosis y la frecuencia no se indican. La medida principal de resultado no se indica; el estudio es de Fase 1/2.
who_for: Adults aged 18 years or older.
Bladder cancer that has never been treated with BCG.
Carcinoma in situ, or stage Ta and/or T1 papillary tumors after transurethral resection.
No resectable disease left after TURBT surgery; residual carcinoma in situ is allowed.
ECOG performance status of 0, 1, or 2.
not_for: Muscle-invasive, locally advanced, metastatic, or extravesical bladder cancer.
Other cancer in the past 5 years that is progressing or needs active treatment, with listed exceptions.
Heart failure NYHA class III or IV, unstable angina, or heart attack within 6 months.
Active systemic infection needing IV antibiotics, active urinary tract infection, or active tuberculosis.
Pregnancy or breastfeeding, or lab values outside the study limits (low neutrophils or platelets, high liver enzymes or creatinine).

NCT06635785.summary_en: This Phase 1/2 study is testing AI-081, a bispecific antibody that targets PD-1 and VEGF, in people with advanced solid tumors. AI-081 is given by IV infusion at a designated dose every 3 weeks (q3w). The study measures the safety, pharmacokinetics (how the drug moves through the body), and efficacy of AI-081.
NCT06635785.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1/2 evalúa AI-081, un anticuerpo biespecífico que actúa contra PD-1 y VEGF, en personas con tumores sólidos avanzados. AI-081 se administra por infusión intravenosa en una dosis designada cada 3 semanas (q3w). El estudio mide la seguridad, la farmacocinética (cómo se distribuye el medicamento en el cuerpo) y la eficacia de AI-081.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older at the time of consent.
ECOG performance status of 1 or better.
Solid tumor that is metastatic or locally advanced.
Measurable disease according to RECIST 1.1.
Adequate organ function and written informed consent.
not_for: Not recovered to grade 1 or lower from side effects of prior cancer treatment (some exceptions listed).
Brain or leptomeningeal metastases.
Currently in another investigational trial or receiving other anticancer, immune, or cytokine therapy.
Uncontrolled high blood pressure, recent heart attack or stroke, or LVEF below 40%.
History of interstitial lung disease or non-infectious pneumonitis.

NCT06811116.summary_en: This phase I/II study tests sapanisertib added to cabozantinib in hepatocellular carcinoma (liver cancer) that has spread and has a change in the β-catenin gene. Both drugs are taken by mouth: sapanisertib is taken 3 days on and 4 days off per week, 5 days on and 2 days off per week, or on days 1-28 of each 28-day cycle, and cabozantinib is taken daily on days 1-28 of each cycle, repeated while the disease does not progress and side effects are acceptable. The primary outcome is not stated; the study is Phase I/II and looks at side effects, the best dose, and how well the treatment works.
NCT06811116.summary_es: Este estudio de fase I/II prueba sapanisertib añadido a cabozantinib en carcinoma hepatocelular (cáncer de hígado) que se ha diseminado y tiene un cambio en el gen de la β-catenina. Ambos medicamentos se toman por vía oral: sapanisertib se toma 3 días con tratamiento y 4 sin tratamiento por semana, 5 días con tratamiento y 2 sin tratamiento por semana, o los días 1 al 28 de cada ciclo de 28 días, y cabozantinib se toma a diario los días 1 al 28 de cada ciclo, repitiéndose mientras la enfermedad no progrese y los efectos secundarios sean aceptables. El resultado principal no está indicado; el estudio es de fase I/II y observa los efectos secundarios, la dosis más adecuada y qué tan bien funciona el tratamiento.
who_for: Liver cancer confirmed by lab testing that cannot be treated with a cure-intended approach
Measurable disease (Phase 2 portion)
β-catenin mutation found by next generation sequencing (Phase 2 portion)
Prior systemic therapy for metastatic disease, including a prior immune checkpoint inhibitor unless not eligible
Age 18 or older, ECOG performance status 2 or better, and Child-Pugh score A
not_for: Side effects from prior cancer treatment that are above grade 1, except hair loss
Currently receiving other investigational agents
Prior exposure to cabozantinib
Use of strong CYP3A4-inhibiting medicines, or inability to swallow oral medicines
Pregnancy or breastfeeding

NCT07216443.summary_en: This Phase 2 study is testing Orca-T, an allogeneic stem cell and T-cell immunotherapy biologic, after reduced intensity or non-myeloablative conditioning. It is being studied in people with acute myeloid leukemia, mixed phenotype acute leukemia, or myelodysplastic syndromes who are undergoing allogeneic transplant. How Orca-T is given and how long or how often are not stated. The study will evaluate safety, tolerability, and efficacy, but the main outcome is not stated.
NCT07216443.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 evalúa Orca-T, un biológico de inmunoterapia con células madre y linfocitos T de donante alogénico, después de un acondicionamiento de intensidad reducida o no mieloablativo. Se estudia en personas con leucemia mieloide aguda, leucemia aguda de fenotipo mixto o síndromes mielodisplásicos que se someterán a un trasplante alogénico. No se indica cómo se administra Orca-T ni la duración o frecuencia. El estudio evaluará la seguridad, la tolerabilidad y la eficacia, pero el resultado principal no se indica.
who_for: Age 18 or older.
Acute myeloid or mixed phenotype leukemia in complete remission or CR with incomplete hematologic recovery.
Myelodysplastic syndrome indicated for transplant, with 10% or less blasts in the bone marrow.
Planned reduced intensity or non-myeloablative transplant, with an 8/8 HLA-matched related or unrelated donor.
Meets stated organ function limits and is judged not eligible for a fully myeloablative transplant by the principal investigator.
not_for: Prior allogeneic stem cell transplant.
Current immunosuppressive therapy, or corticosteroids above 10 mg/day (topical and low-dose oral exceptions).
Planned donor lymphocyte infusion or planned T-cell depletion.
Karnofsky performance score below 60%.
Uncontrolled infection, or positive HIV, HTLV, hepatitis B, or hepatitis C test, with exceptions.

NCT06228326.summary_en: The study tests KB707, a genetically modified herpes simplex type 1 virus given by inhalation, in adults with advanced solid tumors affecting the lungs, including non-small cell lung cancer. KB707 is given by nebulization, weekly for three weeks and then every three weeks when used alone, or every 2 weeks with Keytruda (given every 6 weeks) or every 3 weeks with docetaxel in the combination groups, and treatment continues until progression, death, unacceptable toxicity, or another listed reason. The study is designed to measure safety, tolerability, preliminary efficacy, and immunologic effect, and it is a Phase 1/2 study.
NCT06228326.summary_es: El estudio evalúa KB707, un virus del herpes simple tipo 1 modificado genéticamente que se administra por inhalación, en adultos con tumores sólidos avanzados que afectan los pulmones, incluido el cáncer de pulmón de células no pequeñas. KB707 se administra por nebulización, una vez por semana durante tres semanas y luego cada tres semanas cuando se usa solo, o cada 2 semanas con Keytruda (administrado cada 6 semanas) o cada 3 semanas con docetaxel en los grupos de combinación, y el tratamiento continúa hasta la progresión, la muerte, toxicidad inaceptable u otra razón indicada. El estudio está diseñado para medir la seguridad, la tolerabilidad, la eficacia preliminar y el efecto inmunológico, y es un estudio de Fase 1/2.
who_for: Adults aged 18 or older at consent
Life expectancy longer than 12 weeks
ECOG performance status of 0 or 1
At least one measurable lung lesion per RECIST v1.1
NSCLC combination cohorts: stage 3 or 4 NSCLC with limited prior lines of therapy
not_for: Pregnant, nursing, or planning pregnancy during treatment or through three months after last dose
Known positive HIV 1/2 test
Not fully recovered from prior surgery or radiotherapy
NSCLC combination cohorts: active brain or leptomeningeal metastases, or another active cancer
NSCLC combination cohorts: active autoimmune disease needing systemic treatment, known hepatitis, or prior checkpoint inhibitor pneumonitis needing steroids

NCT01638676.summary_en: This study tests vemurafenib given together with metformin in people with unresectable stage IIIC or stage IV melanoma that has the BRAF V600E change. Vemurafenib is taken by mouth at 960 mg once daily, and metformin is taken by mouth at 500 mg twice daily for 2 weeks, then 850 mg twice daily; how long treatment lasts is not stated. The main outcome is safety, and the phase II part also looks at clinical activity; the study is phase 1/2.
NCT01638676.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa vemurafenib combinado con metformina en personas con melanoma en estadio IIIC o IV no resecable que tiene el cambio BRAF V600E. El vemurafenib se toma por vía oral a 960 mg una vez al día, y la metformina se toma por vía oral a 500 mg dos veces al día durante 2 semanas, luego 850 mg dos veces al día; la duración del tratamiento no se indica. El resultado principal es la seguridad, y la parte de fase II también evalúa la actividad clínica; el estudio es de fase 1/2.
who_for: Age 18 or older with histologically confirmed BRAF V600E melanoma, stage IIIC or IV.
ECOG performance status 0 to 2 and life expectancy of at least 3 months.
At least one site of measurable disease by RECIST 1.1.
Adequate blood, kidney and liver test results within 42 days before dosing.
Agrees to required contraception and gives written informed consent.
not_for: Prior treatment with vemurafenib.
Known allergy to metformin or any of its components.
Melanoma that progressed while on metformin.
Radiotherapy for non-CNS disease within 2 weeks before study treatment, or unrecovered radiation side effects above grade 1 (except hair loss).
Pregnant, breastfeeding, or not using required birth control; or uncontrolled infection or condition that could interfere.

NCT07731789.summary_en: This phase 2 study tests tafasitamab and rituximab as a treatment for newly diagnosed follicular lymphoma. Both drugs are given through an IV, with rituximab on day 1 of each 28-day cycle and tafasitamab on days 1, 8, 15 and 22 in cycles 1 to 3, then on days 1 and 15 in later cycles, for up to 12 cycles unless the disease progresses or toxicity is unacceptable. The main outcome is not stated in the record; the study is a phase 2 trial.
NCT07731789.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 evalúa tafasitamab y rituximab como tratamiento para el linfoma folicular de diagnóstico reciente. Ambos medicamentos se administran por vena: rituximab el día 1 de cada ciclo de 28 días, y tafasitamab los días 1, 8, 15 y 22 en los ciclos 1 a 3, y después los días 1 y 15, por hasta 12 ciclos, salvo que la enfermedad progrese o la toxicidad sea inaceptable. El resultado principal no se indica en el registro; el estudio es de fase 2.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older with histologically confirmed follicular lymphoma, grade 1, 2, 3A or classic.
Newly diagnosed and meeting at least one listed criterion for starting therapy, such as large nodes, B symptoms or low blood counts.
Measurable disease on CT or FDG-PET scan.
ECOG performance status of 2 or less.
Blood counts, liver and kidney function within stated limits; willing to use highly effective contraception if able to have children.
not_for: Grade 3B or transformed follicular lymphoma.
Known central nervous system involvement by lymphoma.
Receiving any other investigational agents.
Prior monoclonal antibody use within 4 weeks before the first dose.
Pregnant or breastfeeding.

NCT07023289.summary_en: This study compares telisotuzumab adizutecan, given alone, with standard of care in adults with colorectal cancer that is circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) positive after adjuvant treatment and has no radiographic evidence of disease. Telisotuzumab adizutecan is given by intravenous (IV) infusion, and the number and timing of doses are not stated; standard of care is chosen by the investigator and is described as active surveillance. The study runs for approximately 51 months, and its purpose is to assess change in disease activity; it is a Phase 2 study.
NCT07023289.summary_es: Este estudio compara telisotuzumab adizutecan, administrado solo, con el tratamiento estándar en adultos con cáncer colorrectal que tiene ADN tumoral circulante (ctDNA) positivo después del tratamiento adyuvante y no presenta evidencia radiográfica de enfermedad. El telisotuzumab adizutecan se administra por infusión intravenosa (IV), y el número y la frecuencia de las dosis no se indican; el tratamiento estándar lo elige el investigador y se describe como vigilancia activa. El estudio dura aproximadamente 51 meses y su propósito es evaluar el cambio en la actividad de la enfermedad; es un estudio de Fase 2.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older.
Histologically or cytologically confirmed adenocarcinoma of the colon or rectum.
At least 3 months of platinum-based doublet chemotherapy, given before or after surgery.
No radiographic evidence of disease on chest, abdominal and pelvic CT within 6 weeks before first dose.
ctDNA positive within 1 year after adjuvant therapy or tumor resection, with treatment starting within 6 weeks of positivity.
not_for: No available surgical tumor tissue sample.
History of interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis that needed systemic steroids.
Active interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis on screening chest CT.
Topoisomerase inhibitors used as part of adjuvant therapy.

NCT05733689.summary_en: This phase 1b study tests a response-guided approach to neoadjuvant (pre-surgery) chemotherapy in people with stage IB, II or III adenocarcinoma of the stomach or gastroesophageal junction. Patients receive one of the standard neoadjuvant regimens, FLOT or FOLFOX, given by intravenous infusion every 14 days for up to 6 months, and treatment may change based on response. The study aims to determine the efficacy and feasibility of this approach, but a specific main outcome measure is not stated.
NCT05733689.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1b evalúa un enfoque de quimioterapia neoadyuvante (antes de la cirugía) guiado por la respuesta, en personas con adenocarcinoma de estómago o de la unión gastroesofágica en estadio IB, II o III. Los pacientes reciben uno de los esquemas neoadyuvantes estándar, FLOT o FOLFOX, administrados por infusión intravenosa cada 14 días durante hasta 6 meses, y el tratamiento puede cambiar según la respuesta. El estudio busca determinar la eficacia y la factibilidad de este enfoque, pero no se indica una medida de resultado principal específica.
who_for: Adenocarcinoma of the stomach or gastroesophageal junction, confirmed by biopsy or cytology.
Stage IB, II or Stage III disease eligible for neoadjuvant doublet or triplet chemotherapy for up to 6 months.
Age 18 years or older.
ECOG performance status of 2 or less.
Life expectancy over 6 months, with adequate blood, liver and kidney function.
not_for: Known distant metastases from the gastroesophageal cancer.
Currently receiving other investigational agents.
Uncontrolled intercurrent illness, such as active infection or unstable heart conditions.
Another primary cancer needing active treatment or expected to need it within 12 months.
Pregnant or nursing.

NCT07182279.summary_en: This Phase 1/2 study tests adding a single dose of high dose rate brachytherapy (a type of radiation) before robotic prostate surgery in men with newly diagnosed, high-risk, non-metastatic prostate cancer. The radiation is given as one 15 Gy dose 4 to 8 weeks before robotic-assisted laparoscopic prostatectomy (RALP), and some patients also receive androgen blockade for 12 weeks starting 8 weeks after surgery. The main outcome is not stated in the record; the trial is Phase 1/2.
NCT07182279.summary_es: Este estudio de Fase 1/2 evalúa agregar una sola dosis de braquiterapia de alta tasa de dosis (un tipo de radiación) antes de la cirugía robótica de próstata en hombres con cáncer de próstata de alto riesgo, recién diagnosticado y sin metástasis. La radiación se administra en una dosis única de 15 Gy entre 4 y 8 semanas antes de la prostatectomía laparoscópica asistida por robot (RALP), y algunos pacientes también reciben bloqueo androgénico durante 12 semanas, comenzando 8 semanas después de la cirugía. El resultado principal no se indica en el registro; el estudio es de Fase 1/2.
who_for: Newly diagnosed prostate adenocarcinoma confirmed by biopsy, without metastatic disease.
Negative bone scan and CT scan or PSMA-PET for spread of disease.
Has a high-risk feature, such as PSA 20 or higher, Gleason score 8 or higher, or stage T3a or higher.
Age 40 or older with ECOG performance status 0 to 1.
Medically fit for surgery and brachytherapy, as judged by the principal investigator.
not_for: Metastatic disease shown on bone scan, CT, pelvic MRI, or PSMA-PET.
Declared high risk for anesthesia by a physician.
Prior pelvic radiation therapy.
Prostate gland larger than 70 cc.
Androgen deprivation therapy within the past 6 months.

NCT07006688.summary_en: This study tests ivosidenib, a tablet taken by mouth, in adults with IDH1-mutated cancers who also have liver or kidney impairment. Participants take 500 mg once a day in 28-day cycles, continuing until the end of the study. The study looks at safety, tolerability, how the body processes the drug (pharmacokinetics), and drug effects (pharmacodynamics); it is a Phase 1 study.
NCT07006688.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa ivosidenib, una tableta que se toma por vía oral, en adultos con cánceres con mutación IDH1 que también tienen insuficiencia hepática o renal. Los participantes toman 500 mg una vez al día en ciclos de 28 días, y continúan hasta el final del estudio. El estudio analiza la seguridad, la tolerabilidad, cómo el cuerpo procesa el medicamento (farmacocinética) y los efectos del medicamento (farmacodinamia); es un estudio de Fase 1.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older
Hematologic malignancy or solid tumor (not glioma) with a locally confirmed IDH1 R132 mutation
Moderate or severe liver impairment with adequate kidney function, or severe kidney impairment with adequate liver function
Control groups with adequate liver or kidney function
Women of childbearing potential who agree to use two effective birth control methods during the study and for 90 days after the last dose
not_for: Hematopoietic stem cell transplant within 60 days, or active graft-versus-host disease needing systemic therapy
Systemic anticancer, investigational, or radiation therapy within 14 days, or surgery within 4 weeks, before first dose
Calcineurin inhibitors within 4 weeks before enrollment
Significant heart disease within 6 months, including heart failure NYHA class III or IV, heart attack, unstable angina, or stroke
Known active inflammatory gastrointestinal disease, chronic diarrhea, or other conditions that limit oral drug absorption

NCT05020860.summary_en: This study tests chemotherapy given before surgery for early breast cancer, with some arms adding pembrolizumab, trastuzumab and pertuzumab. It is for people with triple negative, HER2-positive, or high-risk estrogen receptor-positive invasive breast cancer. Treatment is given in 21-day or 14-day cycles, with 4 cycles of each of two drug stages (paclitaxel-based, then doxorubicin plus cyclophosphamide), and the study measures whether early tumor shrinkage predicts how much tumor remains at surgery; the record is a Phase II trial and does not state a separate formal outcome measure.
NCT05020860.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa quimioterapia administrada antes de la cirugía para el cáncer de mama temprano, y algunos grupos añaden pembrolizumab, trastuzumab y pertuzumab. Está dirigido a personas con cáncer de mama invasivo triple negativo, HER2 positivo o con receptor de estrógeno positivo de alto riesgo. El tratamiento se administra en ciclos de 21 o 14 días, con 4 ciclos en cada una de dos etapas (una basada en paclitaxel, y luego doxorrubicina más ciclofosfamida); el estudio busca saber si la reducción temprana del tumor predice cuánto tumor queda en la cirugía, y el registro indica que es un ensayo de fase II sin una medida formal de resultado indicada por separado.
who_for: At least 18 years old and able to give informed consent
Invasive breast cancer that is triple negative, HER2-positive, or high-risk estrogen receptor-positive
Tumor at least 2 cm by exam or ultrasound
ECOG performance status of 0 or 1
Adequate heart pumping function and blood, liver and kidney test values
not_for: Definite evidence of Stage IV disease
Inflammatory breast cancer
Pregnant or breastfeeding
Prior anthracycline treatment or prior treatment for current breast cancer
Certain heart conditions that would prevent use of the study drugs

NCT06090266.summary_en: This Phase 1/2 study is testing OR502, an antibody that targets the LILRB2 protein, alone or with cemiplimab, in people with advanced solid tumors, including cutaneous melanoma and non-small cell lung cancer. OR502 is given by vein once every 3 weeks, and cemiplimab is given by vein at 350 mg; the total duration of treatment is not stated. The study measures safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and preliminary anti-tumor activity.
NCT06090266.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1/2 evalúa OR502, un anticuerpo que actúa sobre la proteína LILRB2, solo o junto con cemiplimab, en personas con tumores sólidos avanzados, incluidos melanoma cutáneo y cáncer de pulmón de células no pequeñas. OR502 se administra por vena una vez cada 3 semanas, y cemiplimab se administra por vena a una dosis de 350 mg; la duración total del tratamiento no está indicada. El estudio mide la seguridad, la tolerabilidad, la farmacocinética, la farmacodinamia y la actividad antitumoral preliminar.
who_for: Adults 18 or older with advanced or metastatic carcinoma, sarcoma, or melanoma that has progressed.
Disease that can be measured under RECIST v1.1.
Progression on standard therapy, intolerance to it, or no proven curative or life-prolonging options left (dose-escalation and monotherapy cohorts).
Cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma after a PD-(L)1 inhibitor, or platinum-resistant ovarian cancer that progressed on or within 6 months of platinum therapy (exp
Willing to use highly effective birth control if able to become pregnant.
not_for: ECOG performance status greater than 2.
Life expectancy under 12 weeks.
Known active CNS tumor or metastases, or carcinomatous meningitis, unless specific conditions are met.
Uncontrolled serious infection, or active hepatitis B, hepatitis C, or tuberculosis.
Systemic corticosteroids within 15 days or other immunosuppressive drugs within 30 days before study start.

NCT02343042.summary_en: This study tests selinexor taken with other myeloma medicines, including dexamethasone and partner drugs, in adults with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma and newly diagnosed multiple myeloma. Selinexor is taken by mouth, and the partner drugs are given by mouth, IV infusion, or injection depending on the arm. Cycles last 21, 28, or 35 days, and dosing schedules vary by arm. The record states that the study will assess efficacy and safety, and it is a Phase 1/2 study.
NCT02343042.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa selinexor combinado con otros medicamentos para el mieloma, como dexametasona y otros fármacos asociados, en adultos con mieloma múltiple recidivante o refractario y mieloma múltiple de diagnóstico reciente. El selinexor se toma por vía oral, y los otros fármacos se administran por vía oral, por infusión intravenosa o por inyección, según el grupo. Los ciclos duran 21, 28 o 35 días, y los esquemas de dosis varían según el grupo. El registro indica que el estudio evaluará la eficacia y la seguridad, y que es un estudio de fase 1/2.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older who sign written consent.
Relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma with measurable disease.
Symptomatic myeloma, based on IMWG guidelines.
Performance status (ECOG) of 2 or lower.
Adequate liver, kidney, and blood counts within 28 days before treatment starts; limits vary by arm.

NCT06005324.summary_en: This Phase 1 study tests a personalized treatment approach for locally advanced, HPV-negative head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. All participants first receive three cycles (9 weeks) of paclitaxel, carboplatin, and cetuximab, then chemoradiation chosen by imaging response: low dose radiation once daily for 5 days for 6.5 weeks, or standard dose radiation once daily for 5 days for 7 weeks, with the chemotherapy backbone chosen by the investigator. The record does not state a main outcome; it says the study will assess whether blood-based biomarker testing can be used to personalize cancer treatment.
NCT06005324.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1 evalúa un enfoque de tratamiento personalizado para el carcinoma de células escamosas de cabeza y cuello localmente avanzado, negativo para VPH. Todos los participantes reciben primero tres ciclos (9 semanas) de paclitaxel, carboplatino y cetuximab, y luego quimiorradiación según la respuesta en imágenes: radiación de dosis baja una vez al día durante 5 días por 6.5 semanas, o radiación de dosis estándar una vez al día durante 5 días por 7 semanas, con el esquema de quimioterapia elegido por el investigador. El registro no indica un resultado principal; señala que el estudio evaluará si las pruebas de biomarcadores en sangre pueden usarse para personalizar el tratamiento del cáncer.
who_for: Adults 18 or older with locally advanced, non-metastatic HPV-negative head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
Stage III or IV disease by AJCC 8th edition staging.
Measurable disease by RECIST 1.1 criteria.
No prior radiation or chemotherapy for head and neck cancer.
Performance status 0 to 1 and normal organ function as defined.
not_for: Unequivocal distant metastatic disease (M1).
Unidentifiable primary site.
Systemic anti-cancer treatment within the last 8 weeks.
Known active hepatitis B or hepatitis C, or history of HIV.
Known active tuberculosis or hypersensitivity to cetuximab or other protocol drugs.
cancer_types: head and neck squamous cell carcinoma

NCT06733350.summary_en: This phase 4 study tests testosterone replacement therapy in men with low testosterone and localized prostate cancer who are on active surveillance. Testosterone is given by injection, gel, lotion, or transdermal patch, at the treating physician's discretion, with active surveillance for up to 5 years; dosing frequency is not stated. The main outcome measure is not stated; this is a phase 4 study.
NCT06733350.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 4 evalúa la terapia de reemplazo de testosterona en hombres con niveles bajos de testosterona y cáncer de próstata localizado que están en vigilancia activa. La testosterona se administra en inyección, gel, loción o parche transdérmico, a criterio del médico tratante, con vigilancia activa durante hasta 5 años; la frecuencia de dosis no se indica. El resultado principal no se indica; es un estudio de fase IV.
who_for: Men aged 18 years or older.
Localized prostate cancer eligible for active surveillance (NCCN very low, low, or intermediate favorable risk).
Able to understand the study and sign the written informed consent form.
not_for: NCCN intermediate unfavorable, high, or very high risk localized prostate cancer.
For the testosterone group: locally advanced or metastatic prostate cancer, or male breast cancer.
For the testosterone group: an active desire to have children.
For the testosterone group: hematocrit above 54%, or baseline hematocrit of 48-50%.
For the testosterone group: uncontrolled or poorly controlled congestive heart failure.

NCT04941274.summary_en: This study tests abemaciclib, a drug currently used to treat a type of breast cancer, in people with Kaposi sarcoma, with or without HIV. Participants take abemaciclib tablets by mouth every day in 28-day cycles, and treatment continues until the cancer gets worse or side effects are unacceptable. The study aims to find a safe dose and see whether abemaciclib can shrink lesions or tumors; it is a Phase 1/2 study.
NCT04941274.summary_es: Este estudio prueba abemaciclib, un medicamento que actualmente se usa para tratar un tipo de cáncer de mama, en personas con sarcoma de Kaposi, con o sin VIH. Los participantes toman tabletas de abemaciclib por vía oral todos los días, en ciclos de 28 días, y el tratamiento continúa hasta que el cáncer empeore o los efectos secundarios sean inaceptables. El estudio busca encontrar una dosis segura y ver si abemaciclib puede reducir las lesiones o los tumores; es un estudio de Fase 1/2.
who_for: Kaposi sarcoma confirmed by the NCI pathology laboratory.
At least five measurable skin lesions, or evaluable disease per RECIST criteria.
Age 18 or older; HIV-positive or HIV-negative participants may enroll.
Adequate blood counts, liver, kidney and heart function as defined in the record.
Able to swallow oral medicine; ECOG performance status 2 or better.
not_for: Chemotherapy or immunotherapy within 3 weeks before study entry.
Radiotherapy without completing recovery and a washout of at least 14 days.
Currently receiving other investigational agents.
Pregnancy, or nursing while treated with abemaciclib.
Severe allergy to similar CDK inhibitor compounds, or interstitial lung disease.

NCT07853690.summary_en: This pilot study tests histotripsy, a non-invasive procedure that uses focused ultrasound waves to break down targeted tumor tissue, added to chemoimmunotherapy in biliary tract cancer. Histotripsy is given under general anesthesia, and the chemoimmunotherapy (gemcitabine, cisplatin, and durvalumab or pembrolizumab) is given by IV infusion every 3 weeks until disease progression or intolerable toxicity. The study's stated focus is safety and feasibility, and it also measures objective response rate, duration of response, disease control rate, progression-free survival, and overall survival, with bilirubin changes in cohort 2.
NCT07853690.summary_es: Este estudio piloto evalúa la histotripsia, un procedimiento no invasivo que usa ondas de ultrasonido enfocadas para destruir el tejido tumoral seleccionado, añadida a la quimioinmunoterapia en el cáncer de vías biliares. La histotripsia se administra bajo anestesia general, y la quimioinmunoterapia (gemcitabina, cisplatino y durvalumab o pembrolizumab) se administra por infusión intravenosa cada 3 semanas hasta la progresión de la enfermedad o toxicidad intolerable. El enfoque declarado del estudio es la seguridad y la factibilidad, y también mide la tasa de respuesta objetiva, la duración de la respuesta, la tasa de control de la enfermedad, la supervivencia libre de progresión y la supervivencia global, con cambios en la bilirrubina en la cohorte 2.
who_for: Age 18 or older and able to give informed consent
Confirmed biliary tract cancer that is locally advanced or metastatic and not eligible for resection or transplant
Disease measurable by RECIST v1.1
No prior systemic therapy for advanced disease (recurrence after surgery must be at least 6 months after adjuvant therapy)
ECOG performance status 0 to 2 and adequate blood, liver and kidney function
not_for: Prior immune-mediated therapy such as anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1 or anti-CTLA-4 antibodies
Active or prior autoimmune disorder, with listed exceptions
Uncontrolled infection, including hepatitis B, hepatitis C or uncontrolled HIV
Pregnant, planning pregnancy, or breastfeeding
Enrolled in another investigational trial or treated with an investigational device within 30 days of the planned procedure

NCT05797168.summary_en: This Phase 1/Phase 2 study tests AZD5335 (torvutatug samrotecan), an antibody-drug conjugate, alone or with other anti-cancer drugs, in people with solid tumors, including ovarian cancer, lung adenocarcinoma, endometrial cancer, and lung squamous cell carcinoma. Torvutatug samrotecan is given by IV infusion, saruparib and palacaparib are taken by mouth, and the dosing schedule and how often each drug is given are not stated. The study aims to assess safety, tolerability, and anti-cancer activity, and a specific primary outcome measure is not stated.
NCT05797168.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1/fase 2 evalúa AZD5335 (torvutatug samrotecan), un conjugado anticuerpo-fármaco, solo o combinado con otros medicamentos contra el cáncer, en personas con tumores sólidos, incluidos cáncer de ovario, adenocarcinoma de pulmón, cáncer endometrial y carcinoma escamoso de pulmón. El torvutatug samrotecan se administra por infusión intravenosa, el saruparib y el palacaparib se toman por vía oral, y el esquema de dosis y la frecuencia de cada medicamento no se indican. El estudio busca evaluar la seguridad, la tolerabilidad y la actividad contra el cáncer, y no se indica una medida de resultado principal específica.
who_for: Adults aged 18 years or older who can give informed consent
ECOG performance status of 0 or 1
Advanced solid tumor with measurable disease per RECIST v1.1
Life expectancy of at least 12 weeks
Prior adequate therapy, or investigator judges a trial to be the best next option
not_for: Spinal cord compression or history of leptomeningeal carcinomatosis
Brain metastases that are symptomatic, unstable, or need high-dose steroids
Active infection, or hepatitis or HIV not controlled as described in the criteria
History of non-infectious lung inflammation (ILD/pneumonitis) needing steroids or oxygen
Uncontrolled hypertension, recent heart attack or stroke, or QTcF above 470 msec

NCT06563388.summary_en: This Phase 3 study compares stereotactic ablative radiotherapy (SABR) given right away with SABR given after a 3-month delay, in patients with metastatic lung, colorectal, or prostate cancer that has spread to 1 to 10 sites. Patients receive SABR immediately or after 3 months of standard of care, and the number of treatments is not stated. The study measures the impact of timing on survival.
NCT06563388.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 3 compara la radioterapia ablativa estereotáctica (SABR) administrada de inmediato con la SABR administrada después de un retraso de 3 meses, en pacientes con cáncer de pulmón, colorrectal o de próstata metastásico que se ha diseminado a 1 a 10 sitios. Los pacientes reciben la SABR de inmediato o después de 3 meses de tratamiento estándar, y el número de tratamientos no se indica. El estudio mide el efecto del momento del tratamiento en la supervivencia.
who_for: Age 1 year or older and willing to give informed consent
ECOG performance status 3 or better
Life expectancy longer than 6 months
Histologically confirmed lung, prostate, or colorectal cancer with metastases seen on imaging
Newly diagnosed metastatic disease at 1 to 10 sites
not_for: No option for standard systemic therapy, or refuses systemic therapy
Chemotherapy or radiotherapy within 3 weeks before entry
Serious comorbidities that preclude radiotherapy, such as certain lung, bowel, or connective tissue conditions
Malignant pleural effusion or known brain metastases
Pregnant or nursing participants

NCT07793942.summary_en: This Phase 2 study tests the medicine MK-2010, given alone or with other treatments, in people with advanced solid tumors. MK-2010 is given as an intravenous infusion, and the dosing schedule is not stated, while some study arms also receive pembrolizumab, chemotherapy, or oral belzutifan. The study measures safety and tolerability, and how many participants have their cancer shrink or go away (response).
NCT07793942.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 evalúa el medicamento MK-2010, administrado solo o con otros tratamientos, en personas con tumores sólidos avanzados. MK-2010 se administra por infusión intravenosa, y el calendario de dosis no se indica; algunos grupos también reciben pembrolizumab, quimioterapia o belzutifan oral. El estudio mide la seguridad y la tolerancia, y cuántos participantes tienen una reducción o desaparición del cáncer (respuesta).
who_for: Has radiographically measurable disease per protocol.
Has well-controlled HIV on antiretroviral therapy, if diagnosed with HIV.
Has adequate organ function per protocol.
If receiving oral treatment, can swallow and keep down oral medication without absorption-altering gastrointestinal problems.
Age 18 years or older.
not_for: History of Kaposi's sarcoma or multicentric Castleman's disease, if diagnosed with HIV.
History of PRES or a seizure disorder.
Hepatic encephalopathy, hepatorenal syndrome, or Child-Pugh class B or worse cirrhosis.
Known active brain metastases or carcinomatous meningitis.
Current anticoagulant use, severe heart or blood vessel disease, myocarditis, cardiomyopathy, or inflammatory bowel disease.

NCT07089641.summary_en: This Phase Ib trial tests ERAS-801, an EGFR inhibitor, in adults with IDH wildtype, EGFR-altered grade IV glioblastoma or gliosarcoma that is progressive, recurrent, resectable, or newly diagnosed in people aged 70 or older. ERAS-801 is taken by mouth once or twice daily on days 1-28 of repeating 28-day cycles, with one arm starting 8-14 days before scheduled surgery, and cycles continue while there is no disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. The main outcome stated is safety and side effects.
NCT07089641.summary_es: Este ensayo de fase Ib evalúa ERAS-801, un inhibidor de EGFR, en adultos con glioblastoma o gliosarcoma de grado IV, con IDH de tipo silvestre y alteración de EGFR, que está progresando, recurrió, es resecable o fue diagnosticado recientemente en personas de 70 años o más. ERAS-801 se toma por vía oral una o dos veces al día durante los días 1 a 28 de ciclos repetidos de 28 días; en un grupo se inicia de 8 a 14 días antes de la cirugía programada, y los ciclos continúan mientras no haya progresión de la enfermedad ni toxicidad inaceptable. El resultado principal indicado es la seguridad y los efectos secundarios.
who_for: Adults 18 or older with progressive or recurrent grade IV glioblastoma or gliosarcoma after radiation, with or without chemotherapy
Tumor is IDH wildtype with EGFR amplification or mutation on a CLIA-certified test
Newly diagnosed grade 4 glioblastoma or gliosarcoma in patients 70 or older with life expectancy over 8 weeks
Tumor is surgically accessible and surgery is clinically indicated
Karnofsky performance status of 60% or higher
not_for: EGFR mutations in T790M or exon 20
Prior EGFR-targeted therapy that could deplete EGFR-altered tumor cells and confound results
Allergic reaction to compounds similar to ERAS-801
Receiving other investigational agents (progressive or recurrent group)
Concurrent malignancy, other than specified low-risk cancers, or prior malignancy not disease-free for more than three years

NCT03223610.summary_en: This study tests a combination of venetoclax, ibrutinib, prednisone, obinutuzumab, and lenalidomide (Revlimid), called ViPOR, in B-cell lymphoma that has returned or did not respond to treatment. The cancers listed include diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, Burkitt lymphoma, and non-Hodgkin lymphoma. Obinutuzumab is given into a vein on days 1 and 2, and the other four drugs are taken by mouth on set days. Each 21-day cycle is repeated for up to 6 cycles, or until the disease progresses or side effects are not acceptable. The main goal is to study the safety of ViPOR (Phase 1/Phase 2 study).
NCT03223610.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa una combinación de venetoclax, ibrutinib, prednisona, obinutuzumab y lenalidomida (Revlimid), llamada ViPOR, en linfoma de células B que volvió o no respondió al tratamiento. Los cánceres incluidos son linfoma difuso de células B grandes, linfoma de Burkitt y linfoma no Hodgkin. El obinutuzumab se administra por vena los días 1 y 2, y los otros cuatro medicamentos se toman por vía oral en días establecidos. Cada ciclo de 21 días se repite hasta 6 ciclos, o hasta que la enfermedad progrese o los efectos secundarios sean inaceptables. El objetivo principal es estudiar la seguridad de ViPOR (estudio de Fase 1/Fase 2).
who_for: Age 18 years or older
Confirmed B-cell lymphoma, such as DLBCL, transformed lymphoma, Burkitt lymphoma, follicular lymphoma, or mantle cell lymphoma
Relapsed or refractory disease after at least one prior treatment, as defined for each lymphoma type
ECOG performance status 2 or less
Blood counts, liver, kidney, and clotting values within the stated limits, unless caused by the lymphoma
not_for: Children under 18 years of age
Active CNS lymphoma
CLL or SLL (for the Phase 1b part)
Receiving another investigational agent, or chemotherapy, radiation, or anti-cancer antibodies within 2 weeks before the first dose
Prior treatment with more than one of venetoclax, ibrutinib, or lenalidomide, or allogeneic transplant within 6 months or active graft-versus-host disease

NCT07226986.summary_en: This Phase Ib/II study is testing AMO959 together with lutetium (177Lu) vipivotide tetraxetan (AAA617) and an androgen receptor pathway inhibitor (ARPI) in adults with PSMA-positive metastatic castration resistant prostate cancer. Dosing differs by arm, but most arms give AAA617 on day 1 of each 6-week cycle, with AMO959 twice daily on days 2 to 15, for a maximum of 6 cycles. The primary outcome is not stated; Phase Ib assesses safety, tolerability and pharmacokinetics, and Phase II assesses preliminary efficacy.
NCT07226986.summary_es: Este estudio de fase Ib/II evalúa AMO959 junto con lutecio (177Lu) vipivotida tetraxetán (AAA617) y un inhibidor de la vía del receptor de andrógenos (ARPI) en adultos con cáncer de próstata metastásico resistente a la castración con PSMA positivo. Los esquemas de dosis varían según el brazo, pero la mayoría de los brazos administra AAA617 el día 1 de cada ciclo de 6 semanas, con AMO959 dos veces al día los días 2 a 15, por un máximo de 6 ciclos. El resultado principal no se indica en el registro; la fase Ib evalúa seguridad, tolerabilidad y farmacocinética, y la fase II evalúa la eficacia preliminar.
who_for: Adults 18 or older with ECOG performance status 0 to 2.
Histologically confirmed prostate adenocarcinoma.
PSMA-positive disease on PSMA-PET imaging.
Castrate testosterone level and/or use of androgen deprivation therapy.
Progression on one prior ARPI in an earlier setting, by PSA, soft-tissue or bone criteria.
not_for: Prostate cancer histology other than adenocarcinoma, such as neuroendocrine or intraductal subtype.
Prior radioligand therapy or prior PSMA-targeted agents.
Prostate radiation with curative intent or other systemic anticancer treatment within 28 days of enrollment or randomization.
Other investigational agents within 28 days before first study dose.
Serious medical conditions that may interfere with study procedures or follow-up, or CNS metastases without required treatment or neurologic stability.

NCT06871410.summary_en: This phase 1 trial tests CD83 CAR T cells, which are genetically engineered immune cells, in adults with relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia (AML). Patients get leukapheresis to collect cells, then fludarabine and cyclophosphamide IV on days -5 to -3, then CD83 CAR T cells IV over 15 minutes on day 0. The study looks at safety, side effects, and the best dose, and the record does not list a separate primary outcome measure.
NCT06871410.summary_es: Este ensayo de fase 1 evalúa células CAR T con CD83, que son células inmunitarias modificadas genéticamente, en adultos con leucemia mieloide aguda (LMA) recidivante o refractaria. Los pacientes se someten primero a leucaféresis para obtener las células, luego reciben fludarabina y ciclofosfamida por vía intravenosa en los días -5 a -3, y después células CAR T con CD83 por vía intravenosa durante 15 minutos el día 0. El estudio analiza la seguridad, los efectos secundarios y la mejor dosis, y el registro no enumera una medida de resultado principal por separado.
who_for: Age 18 years or older.
Karnofsky performance status of 70% or higher.
Relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia as defined in the record.
At least 15% of AML blasts express CD83 by flow cytometry.
Meets stated kidney, liver, heart, lung and blood count limits.
not_for: Acute promyelocytic leukemia.
Active leukemia in the central nervous system.
Other active cancer within 2 years, with listed exceptions.
Ongoing uncontrolled serious infection, HIV, or active hepatitis B or C.
Pregnant or nursing.

NCT06827860.summary_en: This study tests subcutaneous talquetamab, alone and later with daratumumab, in older adults with multiple myeloma that returned early after treatment. Talquetamab is given under the skin, starting with three step-up doses, then 800 μg/kg every other week in 28-day cycles, and daratumumab is added in part 2 for some patients. The record does not state the main outcome measure; it is a Phase 2 single-arm study.
NCT06827860.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa talquetamab subcutáneo, solo y después junto con daratumumab, en adultos mayores con mieloma múltiple que recayó poco tiempo después del tratamiento. El talquetamab se administra debajo de la piel, comenzando con tres dosis de aumento gradual y luego 800 μg/kg cada dos semanas, en ciclos de 28 días, y el daratumumab se agrega en la parte 2 para algunos pacientes. El registro no indica la medida principal de resultado; es un estudio de fase 2 de un solo brazo.
who_for: Adults aged 70 years or older (no upper age limit stated).
Multiple myeloma that is relapsed or refractory after at least 2 prior lines of therapy.
Prior treatment must have included a proteasome inhibitor and an immunomodulatory drug.
Measurable disease by M-protein or free light chain levels.
Part 2 is limited to patients who are not refractory to an anti-CD38 antibody.
not_for: Prior treatment with T-cell-engaging antibodies.
Prior GPRC5D-directed therapy.
Gene-modified cell therapy such as CAR T within 3 months.
Prior allogeneic transplant, or autologous transplant within 12 weeks.
Known active brain or meningeal myeloma, or plasma cell leukemia, Waldenström macroglobulinemia, POEMS syndrome, or primary amyloid light chain amyloidosis.

NCT05588388.summary_en: This Phase 2 study tests adding bevacizumab to atezolizumab and chemotherapy (carboplatin and etoposide) in extensive-stage small cell lung cancer that has spread to the liver. Study drugs are given by IV every 3 weeks: 4 induction cycles of atezolizumab, bevacizumab, carboplatin and etoposide, then maintenance with atezolizumab and bevacizumab for up to 12 months or until progression or unacceptable toxicity. The study measures how long the cancer does not get worse (progression-free survival) and whether the treatment is safe and tolerable.
NCT05588388.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 evalúa agregar bevacizumab a atezolizumab y quimioterapia (carboplatino y etopósido) en cáncer de pulmón de células pequeñas en estadio extensivo que se ha diseminado al hígado. Los medicamentos se administran por vía intravenosa cada 3 semanas: 4 ciclos de inducción con atezolizumab, bevacizumab, carboplatino y etopósido, seguidos de mantenimiento con atezolizumab y bevacizumab por hasta 12 meses o hasta progresión o toxicidad inaceptable. El estudio mide cuánto tiempo el cáncer no empeora (supervivencia libre de progresión) y si el tratamiento es seguro y tolerable.
who_for: Extensive-stage small cell lung cancer with radiographic liver metastases at diagnosis.
Small cell lung cancer confirmed by tissue or cell testing.
No prior treatment for extensive-stage small cell lung cancer.
Measurable disease according to RECIST v1.1.
ECOG performance status of 0 to 2.
not_for: History of leptomeningeal disease.
Deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism or other significant blood clot in the 3 months before first dose.
Blood pressure not controlled (systolic above 150 or diastolic above 100 mmHg).
Tumor invading or abutting major blood vessels.
Active or past autoimmune disease or immune deficiency, except the listed exceptions.

NCT06682442.summary_en: This trial tests de-escalated (lower-dose) intensity-modulated radiation therapy (IMRT), guided by response to induction chemotherapy, compared with standard IMRT, in patients with EBV-associated nasopharyngeal carcinoma. Both arms receive IMRT once daily, 5 days a week, for up to 7 weeks, as long as there is no disease progression or unacceptable toxicity, and participants also have imaging scans and blood samples. The record does not state a main outcome measure; the listed phase is NA.
NCT06682442.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa la radioterapia IMRT de dosis reducida (desescalada), guiada por la respuesta a la quimioterapia de inducción, comparada con la IMRT estándar, en pacientes con carcinoma nasofaríngeo asociado al virus de Epstein-Barr. Ambos grupos reciben IMRT una vez al día, 5 días por semana, durante hasta 7 semanas, siempre que no haya progresión de la enfermedad ni toxicidad inaceptable; los participantes también se realizan estudios de imagen y toman muestras de sangre. El registro no indica una medida de resultado principal; la fase aparece como NA.
who_for: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma confirmed by biopsy or cytology.
Detectable EBV DNA in blood plasma.
Stage III to IVA disease with no distant metastasis at diagnosis.
Planning platinum-based induction chemotherapy and platinum-based chemotherapy with IMRT.
Age 18 or older with ECOG performance status 2 or better.
not_for: Prior systemic chemotherapy for nasopharyngeal carcinoma, other than induction chemotherapy.
Prior radiation to the nasopharynx or nearby areas that would overlap the trial radiation fields.
Investigational drug or device use within 4 weeks before the first dose.
Severe active comorbidity, or active untreated infection needing IV antibiotics.
Child-bearing potential without a documented negative pregnancy test.

NCT07541573.summary_en: This Phase 1a/1b study tests GTB-5550, a B7-H3-targeted natural killer cell engager called a TriSpecific Killer Engager, in select advanced solid tumors that failed prior therapy. GTB-5550 is given as a subcutaneous injection in the abdomen at one of six assigned doses, once a day on Days 1-5 and Days 8-12 of each 28-day cycle, followed by 2 weeks without treatment, and from Cycle 2 on it is given three times per week in weeks 1 and 2 (not on 3 consecutive days). The main outcome is not stated in the record; this is a Phase 1 study.
NCT07541573.summary_es: Este estudio de Fase 1a/1b evalúa GTB-5550, un motor de células asesinas naturales dirigido a B7-H3 llamado TriSpecific Killer Engager, en tumores sólidos avanzados seleccionados que fracasaron con tratamientos previos. GTB-5550 se administra como inyección subcutánea en el abdomen, en una de seis dosis asignadas, una vez al día los días 1 al 5 y 8 al 12 de cada ciclo de 28 días, seguida de 2 semanas sin tratamiento; a partir del ciclo 2 se administra tres veces por semana en las semanas 1 y 2 (no en 3 días consecutivos). El resultado principal no se indica en el registro; este es un estudio de Fase 1.
who_for: Age 18 or older with advanced or metastatic cancer confirmed by tissue or cytology.
Measurable disease by RECIST 1.1; bone-only mCRPC is exempt.
ECOG performance status 0 to 2.
Adequate blood, kidney, liver, heart and lung function within study limits.
Phase 1a only: agrees to stay within a 60-minute drive of the study center through Cycle 1 Day 15.
not_for: Anticancer treatment, surgery or radiotherapy within 14 days before the first dose; radioligand therapy needs longer washout.
Prior organ or allogeneic transplant, with one stated exception.
Pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning pregnancy within 4 months after the last dose.
QTc above 480 msec at screening or a family history of long QT syndrome.
Active autoimmune disease needing systemic treatment within the past year.

NCT04929223.summary_en: This Phase I/Ib study evaluates the safety and efficacy of targeted therapies or immunotherapy, alone or in combination, in adults with metastatic colorectal cancer whose tumors are biomarker positive. Study drugs are given by mouth or by intravenous (IV) infusion, and dosing schedules are set for each arm, such as divarasib by mouth once daily on Days 1-28 of 28-day cycles. The main outcome is not stated in the record; the study is Phase I/Ib.
NCT04929223.summary_es: Este estudio de fase I/Ib evalúa la seguridad y la eficacia de terapias dirigidas o de inmunoterapia, solas o combinadas, en adultos con cáncer colorrectal metastásico cuyos tumores son positivos para un biomarcador. Los medicamentos del estudio se administran por vía oral o por infusión intravenosa (IV), y los esquemas de dosis se definen para cada brazo, como divarasib por vía oral una vez al día en los días 1 a 28 de ciclos de 28 días. El resultado principal no se indica en el registro; el estudio es de fase I/Ib.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older who signed the cohort-specific consent form.
Metastatic colon or rectal adenocarcinoma with at least one measurable tumor.
ECOG performance status of 1 or less.
Tumor biomarker result confirmed by a validated test, as defined for each arm.
Life expectancy of at least 3 months, per the investigator.
not_for: Currently enrolled in another interventional clinical trial (follow-up periods of other trials are allowed).
Systemic anti-cancer treatment within 2 weeks or 5 half-lives before study treatment, whichever is shorter.
Pregnant or breastfeeding, or planning pregnancy during the study.
Symptomatic, untreated, or actively growing brain metastases.
Cancer other than colorectal cancer within 2 years before screening, with some exceptions.

NCT07252479.summary_en: This Phase 1 study tests AN9025, a pan-RAS inhibitor taken as an oral capsule, in adults with advanced or metastatic solid tumors that have RAS mutations. Participants take AN9025 by mouth every day or once a week until the disease gets worse, side effects become severe, or they leave the study. The main goal is to find doses that are safe and tolerable and to learn what medical problems occur with the drug.
NCT07252479.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1 prueba AN9025, un inhibidor pan-RAS que se toma en cápsulas orales, en adultos con tumores sólidos avanzados o metastásicos que tienen mutaciones en RAS. Los participantes toman AN9025 por vía oral todos los días o una vez por semana hasta que la enfermedad empeore, aparezcan efectos secundarios graves o decidan retirarse del estudio. El objetivo principal es encontrar dosis seguras y bien toleradas y conocer los problemas médicos que aparecen con el medicamento.
who_for: Age 18 or older and able to give informed consent.
ECOG performance status of 0 or 1.
Estimated life expectancy of at least 12 weeks, per the investigator.
Advanced or metastatic cancer that kept growing after available standard treatment.
Documented KRAS, NRAS or HRAS mutation, and agreement to provide tumor tissue.
not_for: Prior treatment with a pan-RAS(ON) inhibitor, with a backfill-cohort exception.
Symptomatic brain or central nervous system cancer or metastasis.
Pregnancy, planned pregnancy, or plans to breastfeed.
Moderate or severe heart disease, or certain heart rhythm or QT risk factors.
Use of strong CYP3A4 or P-gp interacting drugs, or inability to stop proton pump inhibitors.

NCT07550088.summary_en: This study is testing the combination of balstilimab, botensilimab, and agenT-797 in adults with metastatic colorectal cancer that is microsatellite stable (pMMR) and has spread to the liver, who have had previous treatment. The study drugs are given by intravenous (IV) infusion in repeating 42-day cycles: balstilimab 240 mg on Days 1, 15, and 29 of each cycle for up to 9 cycles, botensilimab 75 mg on Day 1 of Cycles 1 through 4, and agenT-797 at 1.4 x 10^7 cells/kg on Day 1 of Cycle 1 and Day 15 of Cycle 2. The study is measuring the objective response rate (the share of participants whose tumor shrinks on imaging) and side effects, and it is a Phase 2 single-arm study.
NCT07550088.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa la combinación de balstilimab, botensilimab y agenT-797 en adultos con cáncer colorrectal metastásico con inestabilidad de microsatélites estable (pMMR) que se ha extendido al hígado y que ya recibieron tratamiento previo. Los medicamentos del estudio se administran por infusión intravenosa (IV) en ciclos repetidos de 42 días: balstilimab 240 mg los días 1, 15 y 29 de cada ciclo, hasta 9 ciclos; botensilimab 75 mg el día 1 de los ciclos 1 a 4; y agenT-797 a 1.4 x 10^7 células/kg el día 1 del ciclo 1 y el día 15 del ciclo 2. El estudio mide la tasa de respuesta objetiva (el porcentaje de participantes cuyo tumor se reduce en las imágenes) y los efectos secundarios, y es un estudio de Fase 2 de un solo grupo.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older with metastatic colorectal cancer that has spread to the liver
At least one measurable lesion, including a target lesion in the liver, per RECIST v1.1
Tumor confirmed as MSS/pMMR by an FDA-approved test
Received at least one prior line of systemic therapy with fluorouracil, oxaliplatin, and irinotecan
ECOG performance status 0-1 and life expectancy of at least 12 weeks
not_for: Tumor is dMMR/MSI-high
Prior treatment with PD-1, PD-L1, CTLA-4, or other immunotherapy
Bowel obstruction or recent obstruction within 3 months
Active or untreated brain metastases or leptomeningeal disease
Active or recent autoimmune disease requiring systemic treatment

NCT07137494.summary_en: This Phase 1 study tests MB-CART19.1, a cell therapy made from modified T cells collected from the participant's blood, in adults with relapsed or refractory primary or secondary central nervous system lymphoma. It is given as a single infusion during an inpatient stay, 2 to 7 days after conditioning chemotherapy, following blood collection and cell manufacturing. The study tests different doses to find the highest dose that causes few or mild side effects; a formal main outcome measure is not stated.
NCT07137494.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1 evalúa MB-CART19.1, una terapia celular hecha con linfocitos T modificados obtenidos de la sangre del participante, en adultos con linfoma del sistema nervioso central primario o secundario recidivante o refractario. Se administra como una sola infusión durante una hospitalización, de 2 a 7 días después de la quimioterapia de acondicionamiento, tras la recolección de sangre y la fabricación de las células. El estudio prueba distintas dosis para encontrar la dosis más alta que cause pocos efectos secundarios o leves; no se indica una medida de resultado principal formal.
who_for: Adults aged 18 or older
Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) in the central nervous system, primary or secondary
Relapsed or refractory disease after at least one prior CNS-directed methotrexate-based therapy
Relapsed: brain or spine lesions progressing on imaging within 21 days of consent
Refractory: residual disease after the last line of therapy
not_for: Active lymphoma outside the central nervous system
Prior CD19-targeted CAR T cell therapy for systemic lymphoma
Most recent CSF or brain tissue shows no CD19 expression
ECOG performance status greater than 2
Pregnant or breastfeeding, or LVEF below 40%, or HIV, or active hepatitis B or C

NCT04329494.summary_en: This phase 1 trial studies the side effects of pressurized intraperitoneal aerosol chemotherapy (PIPAC) in patients with ovarian, uterine, appendiceal, gastric, or colorectal cancer that has spread to the lining of the abdomen. PIPAC is given during a laparoscopic procedure using chemotherapy such as cisplatin, doxorubicin, oxaliplatin, or mitomycin, with some drugs also given by IV, and treatment repeats every 4 to 6 weeks for up to 3 cycles, or every 28 days in one group. The record states that the study looks at side effects and safety and efficacy, but the main outcome measure is not stated.
NCT04329494.summary_es: Este ensayo de fase 1 estudia los efectos secundarios de la quimioterapia en aerosol intraperitoneal presurizado (PIPAC) en pacientes con cáncer de ovario, uterino, de apéndice, gástrico o colorrectal que se ha diseminado al revestimiento de la cavidad abdominal. La PIPAC se administra durante un procedimiento laparoscópico con quimioterapia como cisplatino, doxorrubicina, oxaliplatino o mitomicina, y algunos medicamentos también se dan por vía intravenosa; el tratamiento se repite cada 4 a 6 semanas hasta 3 ciclos, o cada 28 días en un grupo. El registro indica que el estudio analiza los efectos secundarios, la seguridad y la eficacia, pero no se indica la medida de resultado principal.
who_for: Confirmed ovarian, uterine, gastric, appendiceal, or colorectal cancer with peritoneal carcinomatosis
ECOG performance status of 2 or less
Blood counts, liver, and kidney tests within the stated limits
Peritoneal disease visible on imaging or laparoscopy, with progression on prior chemotherapy (varies by group)
Not a candidate for cytoreduction and HIPEC; ascites 5 liters or less
not_for: Cancer spread outside the peritoneum (gastric, colorectal, or appendiceal groups)
Prior maximum cumulative doses of anthracycline drugs (ovarian, uterine, gastric group)
Known DPD deficiency (colorectal or appendiceal groups)
Bowel obstruction needing a feeding tube or total parenteral nutrition
Prior intra-abdominal aerosol chemotherapy, or pregnancy

NCT07407920.summary_en: This phase 2 trial tests reduced after-surgery (adjuvant) therapy in patients with early HER2-positive or triple-negative breast cancer who had a complete pathologic response to pre-surgery treatment and no molecular residual disease in their blood. Patients receive 1 to 3 cycles of standard pembrolizumab, or trastuzumab with or without pertuzumab, after surgery, and a blood test (ctDNA) is done 4 to 6 weeks after surgery. Patients with a negative ctDNA test get no further study drug and have ctDNA tests every 3 months for 3 years, while patients with a positive test continue standard treatment as their doctor decides; the main outcome measure is not stated.
NCT07407920.summary_es: Este ensayo de fase 2 evalúa una terapia adyuvante (posterior a la cirugía) reducida en pacientes con cáncer de mama temprano HER2 positivo o triple negativo que tuvieron una respuesta patológica completa al tratamiento previo a la cirugía y no tienen enfermedad residual molecular en la sangre. Los pacientes reciben de 1 a 3 ciclos de pembrolizumab estándar, o trastuzumab con o sin pertuzumab, después de la cirugía, y se realiza una prueba de ctDNA en sangre de 4 a 6 semanas después de la cirugía.
