Es un estudio de fase 1 para encontrar la dosis, con partes de escalada y expansión de dosis; el resultado principal no está indicado, pero en cada nivel de dosis se revisa la toxicidad limitante de dosis (DLT) antes de pasar al siguiente.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older with acute myeloid leukemia (AML)
Relapsed or refractory AML, after at least one prior AML therapy
Not eligible for other therapies expected to give clinical benefit
ECOG performance status of 0, 1, or 2
Adequate liver, kidney, and heart function, based on the listed tests
not_for: Acute promyelocytic leukemia
Known allergy or hypersensitivity to the study drug or its ingredients
Significant heart disease, such as NYHA class above II, unstable angina, recent heart attack, or uncontrolled arrhythmia
Moderate or severe liver impairment (Child-Pugh class B or C)
Breastfeeding during the study or until 4 months after the last dose

NCT05859074.summary_en: This study tests MQ710, a virus-based treatment (virotherapy) that is injected into tumors, alone or together with pembrolizumab, in people with advanced solid tumors, including skin cancers, melanoma, and head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. MQ710 is injected directly into the tumor in multiple doses, and pembrolizumab 200 mg is given intravenously every 3 weeks in the combination group; how often MQ710 is given is not stated. This is a Phase 1 study, and its stated purpose is to find the highest dose of MQ710 that causes few or mild side effects.
NCT05859074.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa MQ710, un tratamiento basado en virus (viroterapia) que se inyecta en los tumores, solo o junto con pembrolizumab, en personas con tumores sólidos avanzados, incluidos cánceres de piel, melanoma y carcinoma de células escamosas de cabeza y cuello. MQ710 se inyecta directamente en el tumor en varias dosis, y en el grupo de combinación se administra pembrolizumab de 200 mg por vía intravenosa cada 3 semanas; la frecuencia de MQ710 no está indicada. Es un estudio de Fase 1, y su objetivo indicado es encontrar la dosis más alta de MQ710 que cause efectos secundarios leves o pocos.
who_for: Age 18 years or older.
Advanced or metastatic solid tumor that returned or worsened after prior treatment, or with no standard treatment available.
At least 2 tumors suitable for direct or ultrasound-guided injection, with at least one lesion 0.5 cm or larger.
ECOG performance status of 0 or 1.
Predicted life expectancy of 3 months or more.
not_for: Active infection needing antibiotics or physician monitoring.
Positive test for hepatitis B or hepatitis C, or HIV with CD4 count below 100.
Known active brain metastases or carcinomatous meningitis.
Pregnant, breastfeeding, or expecting to conceive or father a child during the trial.
Need for anticoagulation therapy, such as warfarin, or known allergy to MQ710 transgene products or formulation.
cancer_types: head and neck squamous cell carcinoma

NCT06311578.summary_en: This Phase 1 study tests JNJ-87704916, an oncolytic virus, alone and with cetrelimab, in advanced solid tumors, including non-small cell lung cancer. JNJ-87704916 is given as an intratumoral injection into tumors, and how long or how often it is given is not stated. The study aims to determine safety, feasibility, and the recommended doses and regimens.
NCT06311578.summary_es: Este estudio de Fase 1 evalúa JNJ-87704916, un virus oncolítico, solo y con cetrelimab, en tumores sólidos avanzados, incluido el cáncer de pulmón de células no pequeñas. JNJ-87704916 se administra como inyección intratumoral, y no se indica cuánto tiempo ni con qué frecuencia se administra. El estudio busca determinar la seguridad, la viabilidad y las dosis y regímenes recomendados.
who_for: Part 1: advanced or metastatic solid tumor after all available standard of care
Part 2: metastatic or locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer confirmed by tissue or cell testing
Has at least one tumor that can be injected
ECOG performance status of 0 or 1
Adults 18 years or older; people who can have children need a negative pregnancy test
not_for: Active disease involving the central nervous system, with some exceptions
Past or active serious herpes infection, or active herpes needing ongoing antiviral therapy
Active infection needing antibiotics, antifungals or antivirals within 7 days before the first dose, or long-term use of these drugs
Past solid organ or blood stem cell transplant
Positive HIV test or other immunodeficiency; or allergy to protein-based therapies or a significant drug allergy

NCT06974110.summary_en: This Phase 1 study tests MOMA-341, a drug taken by mouth, alone or with irinotecan or immunotherapy, in adults with advanced or metastatic solid tumors that have MSI-H or dMMR changes, including endometrial, colorectal and gastric cancers. MOMA-341 is given orally in 21-day cycles alone or with immunotherapy, and in 28-day cycles with irinotecan, which is given by IV infusion; total treatment duration is not stated. The study is designed to assess safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics and early clinical activity, and it is a Phase 1 study.
NCT06974110.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1 evalúa MOMA-341, un medicamento que se toma por vía oral, solo o con irinotecán o inmunoterapia, en adultos con tumores sólidos avanzados o metastásicos que presentan alteraciones MSI-H o dMMR, incluidos los cánceres de endometrio, colorrectal y gástrico. MOMA-341 se administra por vía oral en ciclos de 21 días solo o con inmunoterapia, y en ciclos de 28 días con irinotecán, que se administra por infusión intravenosa; la duración total del tratamiento no está indicada. El estudio está diseñado para evaluar la seguridad, la tolerabilidad, la farmacocinética, la farmacodinamia y la actividad clínica preliminar, y es un estudio de fase 1.
who_for: Adults aged 18 years or older.
Unresectable advanced or metastatic solid tumor with MSI-H or dMMR, histologically confirmed.
Progressed on a prior anti-PD-(L)1 regimen, unless ineligible or without access to these therapies.
At least one lesion at baseline suitable for imaging; ECOG performance status 2 or less.
Recovered from prior therapy, radiotherapy or surgery; agrees to contraception and written consent.
not_for: Known Werner Syndrome.
Active advanced-stage malignancy, with some early-stage cancer exceptions.
Clinically relevant cardiovascular disease or CNS metastases with progressive neurological symptoms.
Known uncontrolled infection, allergy to MOMA-341, or GI impairment affecting absorption.
Pregnant or breastfeeding; HIV, active liver disease, or other factors the investigator judges disqualifying.

NCT07188090.summary_en: This Phase 2 trial tests a stem cell collection approach that uses G-CSF, with plerixafor added only when needed, before autologous stem cell transplant in people with multiple myeloma, Hodgkin lymphoma, or non-Hodgkin lymphoma. G-CSF (peg-filgrastim or filgrastim) starts on day -4, before stem cell collection on day 0, and plerixafor is given if the collection is below the target after the first day or the target is not reached after two days, with extra collection days added until the goal is met. The record does not state a specific primary outcome measure, but it aims to see whether adequate stem cell collection can be reached and whether the risk of engraftment syndrome may be reduced.
NCT07188090.summary_es: Este ensayo de fase 2 evalúa un enfoque para recolectar células madre que usa G-CSF, con plerixafor añadido solo cuando se necesita, antes de un trasplante autólogo de células madre en personas con mieloma múltiple, linfoma de Hodgkin o linfoma no Hodgkin. El G-CSF (pegfilgrastim o filgrastim) comienza el día -4, antes de la recolección de células madre el día 0, y se administra plerixafor si la recolección queda por debajo de la meta después del primer día o si no se alcanza la meta después de dos días; se añaden días adicionales de recolección hasta cumplir el objetivo. El registro no indica una medida de resultado principal específica, pero el estudio busca determinar si se puede lograr una recolección adecuada de células madre y si el riesgo de síndrome de injerto podría reducirse.
who_for: Age 18 years or older.
Undergoing autologous stem cell transplant for multiple myeloma, Hodgkin lymphoma, or non-Hodgkin lymphoma.
Karnofsky performance status of at least 60%.
Adequate heart, lung, liver and kidney function, per the listed measures.
Life expectancy over 12 months, not counting the disease being transplanted for.
not_for: Uncontrolled HIV.
Uncontrolled bacterial infection.
Active central nervous system disease.
Pregnancy or breastfeeding.
Another cancer, except skin cancer that needs only local treatment.

NCT06176690.summary_en: This Phase 1 study tests banked allogeneic C7R-modified CD30 CAR Epstein-Barr virus-specific T cells (C7R.CD30.CAR-EBVST) in people with relapsed or refractory CD30-positive lymphomas. The cells are given by IV infusion on Day 0 over about 1 to 10 minutes, at one of four dose levels, and how often they are repeated is not stated. The study aims to assess safety and effectiveness, but no specific primary outcome measure is stated; the study is Phase 1.
NCT06176690.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1 evalúa linfocitos T específicos para el virus de Epstein-Barr, de donante y almacenados en banco, modificados con C7R y con el receptor CD30 CAR (C7R.CD30.CAR-EBVST), en personas con linfomas CD30 positivos recidivantes o refractarios. Las células se administran por infusión intravenosa el Día 0, durante aproximadamente 1 a 10 minutos, en uno de cuatro niveles de dosis; no se indica con qué frecuencia se repiten. El estudio busca evaluar la seguridad y la eficacia, pero no se indica una medida principal de resultado específica; el estudio es de fase 1.
who_for: Hodgkin lymphoma, or listed CD30-positive lymphomas (CD30+ aggressive B-cell, ALK-positive or ALK-negative anaplastic T-cell, or other peripheral T-cell lymphom
Tumor tests CD30-positive in a CLIA-certified pathology laboratory.
Age 12 to 75 years.
Adequate liver, kidney and oxygen levels, and Karnofsky or Lansky score above 60%.
Recovered from acute side effects of prior chemotherapy, and signed informed consent.
not_for: Investigational cell therapy or vaccine within the past 6 weeks.
Investigational small molecule drug within the past 2 weeks, or anti-CD30 antibody therapy within 4 weeks.
Allergy to murine (mouse) protein-containing products.
Pregnant or breastfeeding.
Tumor location where enlargement could block the airway, high-dose steroids, active uncontrolled infection, or NYHA class III or IV heart disease.

NCT05698524.summary_en: This Phase 1 study tests abexinostat (PCI-24781) together with metronomic temozolomide in adults with recurrent high grade glioma. Abexinostat is taken by mouth on days 1-4, 8-11 and 15-18 of each 28-day cycle, and temozolomide is taken by mouth until disease progression or intolerance, with the record listing its dose as both once and twice daily. The study will determine the recommended dose and the side effects of this combination.
NCT05698524.summary_es: Este estudio de Fase 1 evalúa abexinostat (PCI-24781) junto con temozolomida metronómica en adultos con glioma recurrente de alto grado. El abexinostat se toma por vía oral los días 1-4, 8-11 y 15-18 de cada ciclo de 28 días, y la temozolomida se toma por vía oral hasta la progresión de la enfermedad o la intolerancia, aunque el registro indica su dosis tanto una vez como dos veces al día. El estudio determinará la dosis recomendada y los efectos secundarios de esta combinación.
who_for: Adults 19 years or older with high grade glioma (grade III or IV)
Prior radiation and standard temozolomide; further treatment for earlier progression is allowed
At least 3 months after the end of chemoradiotherapy, or biopsy or imaging showing progression
ECOG performance status of 0 to 2
Adequate blood counts, kidney function and liver function
not_for: Another active cancer, except nonmelanoma skin cancer or controlled prostate cancer
Significant heart disease, certain heart rhythm problems, or prolonged QTc on ECG
Malabsorption or bowel conditions that affect drug absorption, or recent chemotherapy, radiation, immunotherapy or corticosteroids
Known HIV, active hepatitis B or C, or uncontrolled systemic infection
Pregnant or breast-feeding, or use of valproic acid or another HDAC inhibitor

NCT05187182.summary_en: This Phase 1 study tests CA-4948 with FOLFOX chemotherapy and a PD-1 inhibitor (nivolumab or pembrolizumab), with or without trastuzumab, in people with unresectable or metastatic gastric, gastroesophageal junction, or esophageal cancer. CA-4948 is taken by mouth twice daily, and mFOLFOX7 and nivolumab are given every 14 days in 14-day cycles; pembrolizumab is given on day 1 of every third cycle for a maximum of 2 years, and trastuzumab is given every 14 days in some arms. The main outcome is not stated in the record; this is a Phase 1 study.
NCT05187182.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1 evalúa CA-4948 junto con quimioterapia FOLFOX y un inhibidor de PD-1 (nivolumab o pembrolizumab), con o sin trastuzumab, en personas con cáncer gástrico, de la unión gastroesofágica o esofágico irresecable o metastásico. CA-4948 se toma por vía oral dos veces al día, y mFOLFOX7 y nivolumab se administran cada 14 días en ciclos de 14 días; el pembrolizumab se administra el día 1 de cada tercer ciclo durante un máximo de 2 años, y el trastuzumab se administra cada 14 días en algunos brazos. El resultado principal no se indica en el registro; se trata de un estudio de fase 1.
who_for: Advanced unresectable or metastatic adenocarcinoma or squamous cell carcinoma of the stomach, gastroesophageal junction, or esophagus.
Measurable or evaluable disease by RECIST 1.1.
Known HER2 status if the tumor is adenocarcinoma.
No prior systemic treatment for advanced disease; up to two prior cycles of FOLFOX allowed.
Age 18 or older, ECOG 0 or 1, with adequate blood, liver, and kidney function.
not_for: Current or planned alternative, naturopathic, or botanical cancer treatment (medical marijuana is permitted).
Currently receiving another investigational therapeutic agent.
History of clinically relevant tumor bleeding, or untreated ulcerating tumor.
Interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis grade 2 or higher.
Pregnant or breastfeeding.

NCT05629546.summary_en: This Phase 1 study tests memory-like natural killer (ML NK) cells given with nivolumab and relatlimab in advanced or metastatic melanoma that has progressed after treatment with checkpoint inhibitors. ML NK cells are given on Day 0, and nivolumab and relatlimab start at Day 29 and continue every 28 days for up to 11 cycles, or until unacceptable toxicity or progression. The study looks at safety, tolerability, and preliminary anti-tumor activity, and it is a Phase 1 study.
NCT05629546.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1 prueba células asesinas naturales de memoria (ML NK) junto con nivolumab y relatlimab en melanoma avanzado o metastásico que progresó después de tratamiento con inhibidores de puntos de control. Las células ML NK se administran el día 0, y nivolumab y relatlimab comienzan el día 29 y continúan cada 28 días por hasta 11 ciclos, o hasta toxicidad inaceptable o progresión. El estudio evalúa la seguridad, la tolerabilidad y la actividad temprana contra el tumor, y es un estudio de fase 1.
who_for: Advanced or metastatic melanoma that progressed after at least 12 weeks or at least 2 doses of a PD-1 or PD-L1 treatment.
Age 18 years or older.
ECOG performance status of 2 or better at screening.
Adequate liver, kidney, oxygen, and heart pumping function, as defined in the record.
Life expectancy longer than 12 weeks.
not_for: Active autoimmune disease that requires immunosuppression.
Prior grade 3 or 4 immune-related side effect from cancer immunotherapy that led to stopping that treatment.
Symptomatic brain metastases or leptomeningeal disease.
Prior tumor infiltrating lymphocyte therapy or organ allograft.
Pregnant or breastfeeding, or uncontrolled infection such as HIV or hepatitis B or C.

NCT06517017.summary_en: This phase 2 study tests isatuximab, dexamethasone and lenalidomide given with a slow, gentle approach in people with very frail, newly diagnosed multiple myeloma or plasma cell leukemia. Subcutaneous isatuximab is given weekly during the first two 28-day cycles and then every two weeks, with dexamethasone given on isatuximab days and lenalidomide added after two cycles. The record does not state a primary outcome measure; its stated goal is to learn whether this approach improves treatment adherence and quality of life.
NCT06517017.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 evalúa isatuximab, dexametasona y lenalidomida administrados con un enfoque lento y suave en personas con mieloma múltiple o leucemia de células plasmáticas de nuevo diagnóstico y muy frágiles. El isatuximab subcutáneo se administra semanalmente durante los primeros dos ciclos de 28 días y después cada dos semanas, la dexametasona se administra los días de isatuximab, y la lenalidomida se añade después de dos ciclos. El registro no indica una medida de resultado principal; su objetivo declarado es saber si este enfoque mejora la adherencia al tratamiento y la calidad de vida.
who_for: Adults aged 18 or older.
Newly diagnosed multiple myeloma and/or plasma cell leukemia, having completed one or fewer prior cycles of myeloma treatment.
IMWG frailty score of 3 or higher.
Recovered to baseline or grade 1 or less from toxicities of any prior treatment, unless clinically nonsignificant or stable.
Able to give informed consent and agree to the protocol contraception requirements.
not_for: Currently receiving other investigational agents.
Any condition that the investigator judges would compromise understanding, consent, or safe participation.
Known prior severe (grade 3 or higher) hypersensitivity to the study drug or its components.
Currently taking medications prohibited by the protocol.

NCT04683679.summary_en: This Phase 2 study tests pembrolizumab with radiation therapy, with or without olaparib, in women with metastatic triple-negative or hormone-receptor positive, HER2-negative breast cancer. Pembrolizumab is given as a 30-minute IV infusion every 3 weeks for 3 doses, olaparib is taken as tablets twice daily for 2 cycles of 21 days each, and radiation is given as 8-9 Gy in 3 fractions (or 30 Gy in 6 Gy fractions for large tumors). The main outcome measure is not stated in the record.
NCT04683679.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 evalúa pembrolizumab con radioterapia, con o sin olaparib, en mujeres con cáncer de mama metastásico triple negativo o con receptores hormonales positivos y HER2 negativo. El pembrolizumab se administra como infusión intravenosa de 30 minutos cada 3 semanas, durante 3 dosis; el olaparib se toma en tabletas dos veces al día durante 2 ciclos de 21 días cada uno; y la radiación se administra en 8-9 Gy en 3 fracciones (o 30 Gy en fracciones de 6 Gy para tumores grandes). La medida de resultado principal no está indicada en el registro.
who_for: Women at least 18 years old with triple-negative or ER-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer.
Metastatic or recurrent disease in the stated breast cancer subtypes.
ECOG performance status of 0 to 1.
Measurable disease per RECIST 1.1, including a lesion that will not receive radiation.
For metastatic triple-negative disease, prior immunotherapy with progression and/or PD-L1-negative status.
not_for: More than 3 prior lines of systemic therapy for metastatic triple-negative breast cancer.
Prior grade 3 or higher immune-mediated side effects from immunotherapy.
Live vaccine within 30 days before the first study drug dose.
Recent systemic anticancer therapy or radiotherapy within the stated washout periods.
Pregnancy or breastfeeding, or another malignancy that is progressing or treated within 2 years.

NCT07283679.summary_en: This study tests ONC-PluReceptor NK cell therapy, combined with epcoritamab and tafasitamab, in people with recurrent or refractory B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma. The NK cells are given by injection, and the dose and schedule are not stated. The study aims to learn whether the treatment can help control the lymphoma and to study its safety; it is a Phase 1/2 study.
NCT07283679.summary_es: Este estudio prueba la terapia con células NK ONC-PluReceptor, combinada con epcoritamab y tafasitamab, en personas con linfoma no Hodgkin de células B recurrente o refractario. Las células NK se administran por inyección; la dosis y el calendario no se indican. El estudio busca saber si el tratamiento puede ayudar a controlar el linfoma y estudiar su seguridad; es un estudio de Fase 1/2.
who_for: Adults aged 18 to 80 years with relapsed or refractory DLBCL or follicular lymphoma.
Failed at least 2 prior lines of therapy, or had an autologous or allogeneic stem cell transplant.
Prior CAR-T failure, or not eligible for CAR-T cells.
Tumor biopsy positive for CD19 or CD20 at 1% or more by immunohistochemistry or flow cytometry.
Karnofsky performance status of 60% or higher.
not_for: Lymphoma in complete remission with no measurable disease sites.
Active hepatitis B or C, or HIV infection.
Active central nervous system involvement.
Systemic steroid therapy or immunosuppressive therapy at enrollment.
Anti-cancer treatment within the prior 2 weeks.

NCT07524218.summary_en: This study tests time-restricted eating, a meal-timing plan, in adults with a solid tumor that was removed by surgery and who are starting adjuvant treatment. Participants in the time-restricted eating group eat within an 8-hour daily window that starts 1 to 3 hours after waking, on 6 or more days a week; the control group has no time limit and eats within a window of 12 or more hours per day, and the study duration is not stated. The record does not state a main outcome; the phase is listed as NA (not applicable).
NCT07524218.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa la alimentación con restricción horaria, un plan de horarios de comidas, en adultos con un tumor sólido que fue extirpado mediante cirugía y que van a iniciar tratamiento adyuvante. Los participantes del grupo de alimentación con restricción horaria comen dentro de una ventana diaria de 8 horas que empieza entre 1 y 3 horas después de despertar, 6 o más días por semana; el grupo control no tiene límite de tiempo y come dentro de una ventana de 12 horas o más al día, y la duración del estudio no se indica. El registro no indica un resultado principal; la fase aparece como NA (no aplicable).
who_for: Age 18 or older, any sex
Solid tumor treated with curative-intent surgical resection and planned adjuvant therapy
BMI of at least 18.5 kg/m2
Willing and able to follow assessments, visit schedules, and restrictions
not_for: No planned systemic adjuvant therapy after surgery
Strictly keeping an eating window under 10 hours on most days
Regular overnight shift work (at least 1 night per week)
Dependent on parenteral or enteral nutrition
Pregnant or breastfeeding

NCT05683418.summary_en: The study tests TOS-358, a covalent PI3K-alpha inhibitor, in women with HR-positive, HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer. TOS-358 is taken by mouth once or twice a day in the dose-finding part, and in the combination part it is given with fulvestrant (injection into the muscle) and a CDK4/6 inhibitor at standard doses; treatment duration is not stated. The main outcomes are the maximum tolerated dose and recommended phase 2 dose, along with safety and tolerability (Phase 1).
NCT05683418.summary_es: El estudio prueba TOS-358, un inhibidor covalente de PI3K-alfa, en mujeres con cáncer de mama metastásico HR positivo y HER2 negativo. TOS-358 se toma por vía oral una o dos veces al día en la parte de búsqueda de dosis, y en la parte combinada se administra con fulvestrant (inyección intramuscular) y un inhibidor de CDK4/6 a dosis estándar; la duración del tratamiento no se indica. Los resultados principales son la dosis máxima tolerada y la dosis recomendada para la fase 2, además de la seguridad y la tolerancia (Fase 1).
who_for: Adults 18 years or older
Locally advanced, recurrent, or metastatic HR-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer
Up to 3 prior lines of therapy for metastatic disease
Known PIK3CA mutation or amplification confirmed by a validated test
ECOG performance status of 0 or 1
not_for: Type 1 diabetes or uncontrolled type 2 diabetes
Known active brain or central nervous system metastases
PTEN mutations
Fasting plasma glucose above 140 mg/dL or HbA1c above 7.0%

NCT06006013.summary_en: This phase II study tests cabozantinib together with pembrolizumab in adults with adrenocortical carcinoma that is locally advanced, metastatic, or cannot be removed by surgery. Cabozantinib is taken by mouth once daily on days 1 to 21 of each 21-day cycle, and pembrolizumab is given through a vein on day 1 of each cycle; cycles repeat without disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. The main outcome is not stated; this is a phase II study.
NCT06006013.summary_es: Este estudio de fase II evalúa cabozantinib combinado con pembrolizumab en adultos con carcinoma adrenocortical localmente avanzado, metastásico o que no puede extirparse con cirugía. Cabozantinib se toma por vía oral una vez al día durante los días 1 a 21 de cada ciclo de 21 días, y pembrolizumab se administra por vía intravenosa el día 1 de cada ciclo; los ciclos se repiten mientras no haya progresión de la enfermedad ni toxicidad inaceptable. El resultado principal no está indicado en el registro; se trata de un estudio de fase II.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older.
ECOG performance status 2 or lower, or Karnofsky 50% or higher.
Metastatic or unresectable locally advanced adrenal cortical carcinoma, confirmed by tissue.
Measurable disease by RECIST version 1.1.
Life expectancy of at least 12 weeks and blood, liver and kidney test values within set limits.
not_for: Prior immune checkpoint blockade, such as anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1 or anti-CTLA-4 antibodies, or CD137 agonists.
Small molecule kinase inhibitor use within 2 weeks before first dose.
Current use of mitotane, with stopping rules stated.
Known brain metastases or cranial epidural disease that is not adequately treated and stable.
Certain blood thinners, such as warfarin, dabigatran or clopidogrel, with some exceptions stated.

NCT06401603.summary_en: This Phase 1 study tests decitabine with lisaftoclax and olverembatinib in adults with advanced chronic myeloid leukemia or Philadelphia chromosome-positive acute myeloid leukemia. Decitabine is given by IV, and lisaftoclax and olverembatinib are given by mouth; how often and for how long is not stated. The stated goal is to find the recommended doses of lisaftoclax and olverembatinib to use with decitabine, and this is a Phase 1 study.
NCT06401603.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1 evalúa decitabina junto con lisaftoclax y olverembatinib en adultos con leucemia mieloide crónica avanzada o leucemia mieloide aguda Filadelfia positiva. La decitabina se administra por vía intravenosa, y el lisaftoclax y el olverembatinib se administran por vía oral; la frecuencia y la duración no están indicadas. El objetivo indicado es encontrar las dosis recomendadas de lisaftoclax y olverembatinib para usarlas con decitabina, y este es un estudio de fase 1.
who_for: Adults 18 or older with chronic myeloid leukemia in accelerated or myeloid blast phase, or Philadelphia chromosome-positive acute myeloid leukemia.
Has been intolerant or resistant to at least one prior BCR::ABL1 TKI.
Performance status of 3 or better on the ECOG scale.
Liver, heart, kidney and pancreas function within the listed limits.
Able to give written informed consent and agree to use contraception.
not_for: Previously received lisaftoclax or olverembatinib.
Acute or chronic pancreatitis, or pancreatitis within the past year.
Serious heart problems, recent heart attack, stroke, or long QT syndrome.
Serious infection not controlled with antibiotics, or active leukemia in the central nervous system.
Pregnant or breastfeeding, or uncontrolled HIV, hepatitis B or hepatitis C.

NCT01954992.summary_en: This Phase 3 study compares glufosfamide with fluorouracil (5-FU) in people with metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma whose disease got worse during or after gemcitabine treatment. Glufosfamide is given by IV infusion over 6 hours on Day 1 of each 21-day cycle, and 5-FU is given by IV over 30 minutes on Day 1 of each week. The study aims to assess whether glufosfamide provides additional survival benefit compared with 5-FU.
NCT01954992.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 3 compara glufosfamida con fluorouracilo (5-FU) en personas con adenocarcinoma pancreático metastásico cuya enfermedad empeoró durante o después del tratamiento con gemcitabina. La glufosfamida se administra por infusión intravenosa durante 6 horas el Día 1 de cada ciclo de 21 días, y el 5-FU se administra por vía intravenosa durante 30 minutos el Día 1 de cada semana. El estudio busca evaluar si la glufosfamida ofrece un beneficio adicional en la supervivencia en comparación con el 5-FU.
who_for: At least 18 years old
Pancreatic adenocarcinoma confirmed by biopsy or cytology
Metastatic pancreatic cancer
Disease progression during or after gemcitabine-based treatment
ECOG performance status 0 to 1
not_for: More than one prior systemic therapy regimen for metastatic pancreatic cancer
Insulin-dependent diabetes
Symptomatic brain metastases
Cardiovascular disease within the past year (NYHA Class 2 to 4)
Hemoglobin below 9 g/dL, or creatinine clearance below 60 mL/min

NCT07226609.summary_en: This study tests a dietary intervention for people with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma who are receiving induction chemotherapy with daratumumab (or isatuximab), lenalidomide, bortezomib, and dexamethasone (DRVd). The intervention group receives high-fiber plant-based meals for 12 weeks and dietitian phone or video calls every 2 weeks for 12 weeks, while the usual care group has study team calls every 4 weeks and one dietitian call at the end of induction chemotherapy. The study measures quality of life using questionnaires, and it also looks at treatment response and other disease, microbiome, and immune markers.
NCT07226609.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa una intervención dietética para personas con mieloma múltiple recién diagnosticado que reciben quimioterapia de inducción con daratumumab (o isatuximab), lenalidomida, bortezomib y dexametasona (DRVd). El grupo de intervención recibe comidas basadas en plantas y ricas en fibra durante 12 semanas, y llamadas o videollamadas con un dietista cada 2 semanas durante 12 semanas; el grupo de atención habitual tiene llamadas con el equipo del estudio cada 4 semanas y una llamada con un dietista al final de la quimioterapia de inducción. El estudio mide la calidad de vida mediante cuestionarios, y también analiza la respuesta al tratamiento y otros marcadores de la enfermedad, del microbioma e inmunológicos.
who_for: Newly diagnosed multiple myeloma with bone marrow involvement, age 18 or older.
Planned four 28-day cycles of DRVd induction chemotherapy.
Baseline dietary fiber intake under 30 grams per day on a 24-hour recall.
Not following a minimally processed whole-food plant-based diet in the last 3 months.
Able to complete study surveys, procedures and visits.
not_for: Leptomeningeal or central nervous system involvement.
Body mass index of 19 or lower.
Severe allergy to legumes, peanuts or tree nuts.
Prior combination infusion chemotherapy such as VDPACE or DCEP.
Concurrent weight loss or dietary program that requires a specific diet or weight loss supplements.

NCT07221032.summary_en: This phase 1 study tests FT836 CAR T-cell therapy combined with daratumumab in adults with relapsed and/or refractory multiple myeloma. FT836 is given by IV injection at dose levels of 1 x 10^8, 3 x 10^8, or up to 9 x 10^8 cells per dose, and daratumumab is given intravenously at 16 mg/kg; how long or how often is not stated. The study measures safety and preliminary efficacy, but specific outcome measures are not stated in the record.
NCT07221032.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1 evalúa la terapia con células CAR T FT836 combinada con daratumumab en adultos con mieloma múltiple recidivante y/o refractario. FT836 se administra por inyección intravenosa en niveles de dosis de 1 x 10^8, 3 x 10^8 o hasta 9 x 10^8 células por dosis, y daratumumab se administra por vía intravenosa a 16 mg/kg; la duración o la frecuencia no están indicadas. El estudio mide la seguridad y la eficacia preliminar, pero las medidas de resultado específicas no están indicadas en el registro.
who_for: Age 18 to under 80 years.
At least 3 prior lines of therapy, including a proteasome inhibitor, an immunomodulator, and a CD38 monoclonal antibody.
Measurable disease by serum M-protein, urine M-protein, or light chain criteria.
Karnofsky performance score of 70 or higher.
Adequate liver, kidney, heart, and lung function as defined in the study criteria.
not_for: Positive pregnancy test in a person of childbearing potential.
Confirmed active HIV, hepatitis B, or hepatitis C infection.
Significant autoimmune disease, or active autoimmune condition needing more than 20 mg prednisone daily.
Active central nervous system involvement by malignancy.
Prior gene therapy or any gene-modified cellular therapy.

NCT04899908.summary_en: This study tests whether AGuIX gadolinium-based nanoparticles make stereotactic radiation work better for brain metastases that are harder to control with radiation alone. It includes several cancer types that have spread to the brain, such as melanoma, lung, breast, and gastrointestinal cancers. The nanoparticles or a placebo are given by intravenous injection 3-5 days before radiation and up to two times during radiation, depending on the radiation schedule. The main outcome is not stated in the record; this is a Phase II, double-blind, randomized study.
NCT04899908.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa si las nanopartículas basadas en gadolinio AGuIX hacen que la radiación estereotáctica funcione mejor en metástasis cerebrales que son más difíciles de controlar solo con radiación. Incluye varios tipos de cáncer que se han extendido al cerebro, como melanoma y cánceres de pulmón, mama y gastrointestinales. Las nanopartículas o un placebo se administran por inyección intravenosa 3 a 5 días antes de la radiación y hasta dos veces durante la radiación, según el esquema de radiación. El desenlace principal no se indica en el registro; se trata de un estudio de Fase II, doble ciego y aleatorizado.
who_for: Biopsy-proven solid cancer with at least one brain lesion 5 mm or larger.
Melanoma growing despite immunotherapy, a gastrointestinal primary, or HER2-positive breast cancer.
Cystic brain metastases, or metastases 2 cm or larger.
Local recurrence after prior stereotactic or whole brain radiation.
Age 18 or older, kidney filtration of 60 or higher, Karnofsky score of 70 or higher, and expected survival of at least 3 months.
not_for: Cannot have a brain MRI or cannot receive gadolinium.
Widespread, definitive leptomeningeal disease.
Need for radiation to more than 10 targets (or more than 20 after prior whole brain radiation).
Pregnant or breastfeeding.
Prior brain radiation with active metastases near the brainstem, eyes, optic nerves, or optic chiasm that exceed the stated dose limits.

NCT06021626.summary_en: This Phase 1 study tests CRD3874-SI, a STING agonist, in people with advanced or metastatic solid tumors, including sarcoma and Merkel cell carcinoma. CRD3874-SI is given as a weekly IV infusion in 28-day cycles, starting at 0.1 mg/kg, with four weekly doses in cycles 1 and 2 and three weekly doses from cycle 3 on. The study measures safety and side effects to find the highest dose with few or mild side effects; it is a Phase 1 study.
NCT06021626.summary_es: Este estudio de Fase 1 prueba CRD3874-SI, un agonista de STING, en personas con tumores sólidos avanzados o metastásicos, incluidos sarcoma y carcinoma de células de Merkel. CRD3874-SI se administra como infusión intravenosa semanal en ciclos de 28 días, comenzando con 0.1 mg/kg, con cuatro dosis semanales en los ciclos 1 y 2 y tres dosis semanales desde el ciclo 3. El estudio mide la seguridad y los efectos secundarios para encontrar la dosis más alta con pocos efectos secundarios o leves; es un estudio de Fase 1.
who_for: Age 18 or older and able to give written informed consent.
Locally advanced or metastatic solid tumor that progressed on at least one systemic therapy, or has no standard treatment, or the person is intolerant or declin
Cancer type and prior treatment lines must fit a listed group, such as head and neck squamous cell, adenoid cystic, Merkel cell, sarcoma, melanoma, or non-small
ECOG 0 or 1, or KPS 70% to 100%.
Measurable disease per RECIST v1.1 and adequate blood, liver, kidney, and heart function.
not_for: Known prior severe hypersensitivity to the study drug or its components, including polyethylene glycol.
Clinically significant immunosuppression, or systemic immunosuppressive therapy or steroid doses above the stated limits.
Prior organ transplant or allogeneic stem-cell transplant; autologous transplant considered only if at least 5 years ago.
Symptomatic or systemically treated autoimmune disease within 2 years, or uncontrolled medical conditions, active infection needing systemic therapy, or symptom
Resting QTc of 470 ms or more, or currently receiving study therapy in another investigational study.

NCT05800574.summary_en: This study tests lymphoscintigraphy-directed elective neck radiation with primary chemoradiation for p16-positive, favorable risk oropharynx cancer. Radiation therapy is given Monday to Friday in 35 fractions over 6 or 7 weeks, with cisplatin 40mg/m2 given weekly for 7 weeks. The record does not state the main outcome measure; it is a Phase 2 study.
NCT05800574.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa la radiación electiva del cuello guiada por linfocentellografía, junto con quimiorradioterapia primaria, para el cáncer de orofaringe p16 positivo de riesgo favorable. La radioterapia se administra de lunes a viernes en 35 fracciones durante 6 o 7 semanas, con cisplatino de 40 mg/m2 semanal durante 7 semanas. El registro no indica el resultado principal que se mide; es un estudio de Fase 2.
who_for: Squamous cell cancer of the oropharynx confirmed by pathology
Tumor shows moderate to severe p16 staining in at least 70% of cells
Node-negative with tumor within 1 cm of midline, or N1 with more than one node on the cancer's side
Disease that can be measured under RECIST 1.1
ECOG performance status 0-1 and age 18 or older
not_for: Tumor crosses the midline
Bilateral neck lymph node involvement (N2)
p16-negative squamous cell carcinoma
Prior systemic therapy for this cancer, or prior head and neck surgery involving the neck
Pregnant or breastfeeding, or allergy to technetium-99m tilmanocept

NCT06452160.summary_en: This Phase 1 study is testing BGC515 capsules in people with advanced solid tumors, including mesothelioma and epithelioid hemangioendothelioma. BGC515 is taken by mouth once a day in 21-day cycles, and in the first part of the study the dose is raised in steps. The study measures safety, tolerability, how the body processes the drug (pharmacokinetics), and preliminary efficacy.
NCT06452160.summary_es: Este estudio de Fase 1 prueba las cápsulas de BGC515 en personas con tumores sólidos avanzados, incluidos el mesotelioma y el hemangioendotelioma epitelioide. BGC515 se toma por vía oral una vez al día en ciclos de 21 días, y en la primera parte del estudio la dosis se aumenta por etapas. El estudio mide la seguridad, la tolerabilidad, cómo el organismo procesa el medicamento (farmacocinética) y los primeros signos de eficacia.
who_for: Adults 18 or older with advanced solid tumors, including mesothelioma or epithelioid hemangioendothelioma.
Disease got worse on standard treatment, standard treatment was not tolerated, or standard treatment is declined or not accessible.
Expansion part: other advanced solid tumors with Hippo signaling pathway abnormalities.
ECOG performance score of 0 or 1 and life expectancy of at least 12 weeks.
At least one measurable lesion and a signed informed consent form.
not_for: Previous or current use of TEAD inhibitors.
Inadequate washout from prior therapies, as described in the protocol.
Severe or unstable systemic disease, or unstable or symptomatic brain (CNS) metastases.
Clinically significant cardiovascular disease, as defined in the protocol.
Pregnant or breastfeeding women, or known allergy to BGC515 or its ingredients or excipients.

NCT06910124.summary_en: This study tests linvoseltamab added to lenalidomide maintenance therapy in people with multiple myeloma. Linvoseltamab is given by intravenous (IV) infusion on a set schedule, and lenalidomide is taken by mouth at 10 mg daily on days 1 through 21 of each 28-day cycle, for up to 24 cycles. The record does not state a primary outcome measure; it describes goals of reaching or keeping MRD negativity, controlling disease longer, and extending response, and the study is Phase 2.
NCT06910124.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa linvoseltamab añadido al tratamiento de mantenimiento con lenalidomida en personas con mieloma múltiple. Linvoseltamab se administra por infusión intravenosa (IV) según un calendario establecido, y la lenalidomida se toma por vía oral a 10 mg diarios en los días 1 al 21 de cada ciclo de 28 días, por hasta 24 ciclos. El registro no indica una medida de resultado principal; describe como objetivos alcanzar o mantener la negatividad de enfermedad residual mínima (MRD), controlar la enfermedad por más tiempo y prolongar la respuesta, y el estudio es de Fase 2.
who_for: Newly diagnosed multiple myeloma treated with a triplet or quadruplet initial combination therapy.
Currently on lenalidomide maintenance for 12 months or less, with PR, VGPR or CR but MRD-positive (cohort 1).
Relapse from complete response without meeting IMWG progression criteria (cohort 2).
ECOG performance status of 3 or less, with adequate blood counts and organ function.
Able to give written informed consent and follow contraception rules.
not_for: Prior myeloma therapy beyond the initial IMiD, proteasome inhibitor, anti-CD38 or transplant-based combination.
Receiving other investigational agents, unless the PI decides they do not interfere.
Hepatitis B or C infection, or HIV meeting the listed criteria.
NYHA stage III or IV heart failure, or heart attack or bypass within 3 months.
Active cancer other than myeloma needing treatment in the past 6 months, or neurodegenerative condition or seizure within 12 months.

NCT07223125.summary_en: This Phase 1 study tests JNJ-89862175, an antibody drug conjugate that targets ENPP3, in people with advanced solid tumors. The record does not state how the drug is given or how often. The study aims to find the recommended phase 2 doses in Part 1 and to further evaluate safety at those doses in Part 2.
NCT07223125.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1 evalúa JNJ-89862175, un conjugado anticuerpo-fármaco dirigido a ENPP3, en personas con tumores sólidos avanzados. El registro no indica cómo se administra el medicamento ni con qué frecuencia. El estudio busca determinar las dosis recomendadas para fase 2 en la Parte 1 y evaluar con más detalle la seguridad a esas dosis en la Parte 2.
who_for: Confirmed metastatic or unresectable solid tumor: lung adenocarcinoma, clear cell or papillary renal cell carcinoma, endometrioid ovarian, or endometrioid uteri
ECOG performance status of 0 to 1 at screening.
Age 18 years or older.
Not pregnant or breastfeeding, and agree to avoid pregnancy and egg or sperm donation during the study and for 4 months after the last dose.
not_for: Active central nervous system involvement, unless clinically stable.
Clinically significant cardiovascular disease within 6 months before informed consent.
History of solid organ or hematologic stem cell transplant.
Known allergy, hypersensitivity, or intolerance to excipients of JNJ-89862175.
Prior or current second malignancy likely to interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.

NCT05565118.summary_en: This study tests recording of brain electrical activity within and around high-grade glioma tumors during surgery, in people with high-grade glioma, including glioblastoma. Participants undergo intraoperative electrocorticography through a subdural grid and depth electrode during their surgery, and a small tissue biopsy is taken at the recording sites; how long or how often is not stated. The stated purpose is to test safety and feasibility, the main outcome measure is not stated, and the record lists the study as Phase 1.
NCT05565118.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa el registro de la actividad eléctrica cerebral dentro y alrededor de tumores de glioma de alto grado, durante la cirugía, en personas con glioma de alto grado, incluido el glioblastoma. Los participantes se someten a electrocorticografía intraoperatoria mediante una rejilla subdural y un electrodo de profundidad durante la cirugía, y se toma una pequeña biopsia de tejido en los sitios de registro; la duración o frecuencia no está indicada. El propósito declarado es evaluar la seguridad y la factibilidad, la medida de resultado principal no está indicada, y el registro clasifica el estudio como Fase 1.
who_for: Adults 18 or older with high-grade glioma suspected on MRI, confirmed on frozen tissue check.
Adults with a past confirmed high-grade glioma having surgery for a likely recurrent or progressive tumor.
Karnofsky performance status of 60 or higher.
Considered appropriate for neurosurgery, with blood counts and clotting tests in range within 1 month before surgery.
Able to give written informed consent.
not_for: Severe health problems that the treating physician judges raise surgical risk too much.
Other major medical illness or psychiatric condition that would prevent completing the protocol.
Pregnancy.
Clotting or platelet problems that raise the risk of bleeding.
Tumor located in an eloquent or critical brain area, as judged by the neurosurgeon.

NCT05672524.summary_en: This Phase II study tests tucatinib and trastuzumab, given with standard chemotherapy, in people with HER2-positive locally advanced rectal adenocarcinoma. Tucatinib is taken by mouth at 300 mg twice a day, and trastuzumab is given every three weeks, for an initial 6-week lead-in, then standard induction chemotherapy continues with both drugs for five more cycles (15 extra weeks). The record does not state the main outcome measure; the study is Phase II.
NCT05672524.summary_es: Este estudio de fase II evalúa tucatinib y trastuzumab, administrados junto con quimioterapia estándar, en personas con adenocarcinoma rectal localmente avanzado HER2 positivo. El tucatinib se toma por vía oral a 300 mg dos veces al día, y el trastuzumab se administra cada tres semanas, durante un periodo inicial de 6 semanas; después, la quimioterapia de inducción estándar continúa con ambos medicamentos por cinco ciclos adicionales (15 semanas). El registro no indica la medida principal de resultado; el estudio es de fase II.
who_for: Be 18 years of age or older
Rectal adenocarcinoma confirmed as HER2-positive by lab testing
Locally advanced disease within 15 cm of the anal verge, with no distant spread
ECOG performance status of 0 or 1
Tumor tests RAS wild-type and has intact mismatch repair or microsatellite stability
not_for: Recurrent rectal cancer
Prior pelvic radiation, chemotherapy, or surgery for rectal cancer
Tumor causing symptomatic bowel obstruction
HIV, active hepatitis B or C, or chronic liver disease
Pregnancy or breastfeeding

NCT07908979.summary_en: This phase II study tests neoadjuvant enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab, followed by assessments that guide later treatment, in people with muscle-invasive bladder cancer (clinical stage T2-T3, N0, M0). Enfortumab vedotin is given into a vein at 1.25 mg/kg (maximum 125 mg) on Days 1 and 8 of each 21-day cycle for 3 cycles, and pembrolizumab is given into a vein at 200 mg on Day 1 of each 21-day cycle, or as a subcutaneous form per protocol. The record does not state the main outcome measure; the study is a phase II trial.
NCT07908979.summary_es: Este estudio de fase II evalúa enfortumab vedotina más pembrolizumab administrados antes de la cirugía (neoadyuvancia), seguidos de evaluaciones que orientan los tratamientos posteriores, en personas con cáncer de vejiga que invade el músculo (estadio clínico T2-T3, N0, M0). La enfortumab vedotina se administra por vena a 1,25 mg/kg (máximo 125 mg) los días 1 y 8 de cada ciclo de 21 días, durante 3 ciclos, y el pembrolizumab se administra por vena a 200 mg el día 1 de cada ciclo de 21 días, o en su forma subcutánea según el protocolo. El registro no indica la medida de resultado principal; el estudio es de fase II.
who_for: Bladder urothelial carcinoma confirmed by pathology report, including mixed variant histology
Muscle invasion shown on tissue examination
Clinical stage T2-T3, N0, M0 disease
ECOG performance status 0 or 1
Age 18 years or older
not_for: Small cell histology in any part of the tumor
Prior systemic chemotherapy for muscle-invasive bladder cancer
Prior enfortumab vedotin-based treatment
Prior PD-1, PD-L1 or CD137 agonist therapy
Uncontrolled diabetes, HbA1c above 8.5%, or a history of listed autoimmune disease

NCT05861050.summary_en: This phase 1/2 trial tests glofitamab (with obinutuzumab pretreatment), venetoclax, and lenalidomide in people with newly diagnosed, high-risk mantle cell lymphoma. Glofitamab and obinutuzumab are given by vein (IV), and venetoclax and lenalidomide are taken by mouth; how long or how often treatment is given is not stated. The main outcome measure is not stated, but the trial is described as testing safety and effectiveness.
NCT05861050.summary_es: Este ensayo de fase 1/2 evalúa glofitamab (con una dosis previa de obinutuzumab), venetoclax y lenalidomida en personas con linfoma de células del manto de alto riesgo recién diagnosticado. Glofitamab y obinutuzumab se administran por vena (IV), y venetoclax y lenalidomida se toman por vía oral; no se indica cuánto dura ni con qué frecuencia se administra el tratamiento. El resultado principal del estudio no se indica, pero el ensayo se describe como una prueba de la seguridad y la eficacia.
who_for: Newly diagnosed mantle cell lymphoma that needs treatment, with no prior systemic anticancer therapy
Age 18 to 80 years
ECOG performance status of 2 or lower
High-risk features, such as blastoid or pleomorphic variant, Ki67 of 50% or higher, or TP53 mutation
Agreement to allow use of archival tumor tissue from diagnostic biopsy
not_for: Current use of warfarin
Treatment with strong or moderate CYP3A inhibitors or strong CYP3A inducers within the set time before study drug
Positive hepatitis B surface antigen test at screening
Significant cardiovascular disease, such as NYHA class III or IV heart disease or recent heart attack
Pregnancy, breastfeeding, or plans to become pregnant during the study

NCT07513389.summary_en: This single-arm Phase II trial tests whether leaving out radiation after surgery is possible and safe for selected people with HPV-associated oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma. Participants have transoral robotic surgery and no postoperative radiation, with routine clinical follow-up and serial ctHPVDNA testing (NavDx); how long and how often are not stated. The record says the study measures feasibility and oncologic safety of omitting radiation.
NCT07513389.summary_es: Este ensayo de fase II con un solo grupo evalúa si es posible y seguro omitir la radioterapia después de la cirugía en personas seleccionadas con carcinoma de células escamosas de orofaringe asociado al VPH. Los participantes se someten a cirugía robótica transoral y no reciben radioterapia posoperatoria, con seguimiento clínico de rutina y pruebas seriadas de ADN tumoral del VPH en sangre (NavDx); la duración y la frecuencia no se indican. El registro indica que el estudio mide la viabilidad y la seguridad oncológica de omitir la radioterapia.
who_for: Biopsy-proven squamous cell carcinoma, p16 positive, and NavDx positive for HPV16 TTMV only.
Staged cT0-2 N1 M0 (AJCC 8th edition) with limited lymph node size and number.
Well lateralized tonsil, base of tongue, or glossotonsillar sulcus primary tumor.
10 or fewer pack-years of smoking, or no smoking for at least 5 years.
Suitable for transoral robotic surgery and platinum chemotherapy, with ECOG 0-1 and adequate blood, kidney and liver function.
not_for: Prior head and neck surgery or radiation that could change the meaning of pathology results.
Current smoker or tobacco user.
Current immunosuppressive or disease-modifying rheumatoid drugs, or active lupus, scleroderma, or psoriatic arthritis.
Known HIV positivity.
Other cancer within 5 years (with listed exceptions), severe recent comorbidity, pregnancy or breastfeeding, or involuntary incarceration.

NCT06353997.summary_en: The study tests INBRX-106 given together with pembrolizumab, before the main treatment, in people with stage II or III triple negative breast cancer. Both drugs are given by IV infusion: pembrolizumab at 200 mg and INBRX-106 at 0.1 mg/kg, every 3 weeks; the total length of treatment is not stated. The record says the study is a Phase II trial to assess efficacy and feasibility, but a specific main outcome measure is not stated.
NCT06353997.summary_es: El estudio evalúa INBRX-106 administrado junto con pembrolizumab, antes del tratamiento principal, en personas con cáncer de mama triple negativo en estadio II o III. Ambos medicamentos se administran por infusión intravenosa: pembrolizumab a 200 mg e INBRX-106 a 0.1 mg/kg, cada 3 semanas; la duración total del tratamiento no se indica. El registro dice que el estudio es de Fase II para evaluar la eficacia y la factibilidad, pero no se indica una medida de resultado principal específica.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older.
ECOG performance status of 0 or 2.
Histologically confirmed HER2-negative triple negative breast cancer; ER/PR up to 10% allowed.
Primary breast tumor measurable by ultrasound and at least 1 cm.
Clinically appropriate for neoadjuvant pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy with curative intent; no prior TNBC therapy; sTIL score at least 1%.
not_for: Bilateral breast cancer.
Suspected or confirmed metastatic disease.
Prior anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1, anti-PD-L2, or other T-cell stimulatory agent such as OX40, CTLA-4 or CD137 (some exceptions for other cancers).
Pregnant or breastfeeding.
Known HIV, active hepatitis B or C, or active tuberculosis.

NCT05327023.summary_en: This study tests giving donor lymphocytes (white blood cells from the transplant donor) early after an allogeneic blood or bone marrow transplant in people with high-risk hematologic malignancies. Donor lymphocyte infusion is given on day +7 after transplant (or day +21 for one dose level), at escalating doses, after chemotherapy drugs given IV and sirolimus and mycophenolate given by mouth or IV. The record lists the study as Phase 1/Phase 2 and does not state a main outcome measure, but its stated objective is to learn whether early donor lymphocytes help reduce the risk of relapse.
NCT05327023.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa la infusión de linfocitos del donante (glóbulos blancos del donante del trasplante) poco después de un trasplante alogénico de células madre sanguíneas o de médula ósea en personas con neoplasias hematológicas de alto riesgo. La infusión se administra en el día +7 después del trasplante (o en el día +21 para un nivel de dosis), en dosis crecientes, junto con medicamentos de quimioterapia por vía intravenosa y sirolimus y micofenolato por vía oral o intravenosa. El registro indica que el estudio es de Fase 1/Fase 2 y no señala una medida de resultado principal, pero su objetivo declarado es saber si los linfocitos del donante administrados temprano ayudan a reducir el riesgo de recaída.
who_for: Adults aged 18 to 65 with a listed high-risk blood cancer, such as AML, ALL, MDS, lymphoma, or multiple myeloma.
Disease that has not responded well to standard treatment or has a high risk of relapse, per the listed criteria.
Karnofsky performance score above 60%.
At least one potentially suitable HLA-matched or HLA-haploidentical donor.
Related donor aged 12 or older who is suitable and willing to donate blood, bone marrow, and stool for research.
not_for: Prior myeloablative conditioning for an autologous or allogeneic transplant.
Currently receiving other investigational agents, or prior experimental therapy not finished at least 3 weeks before conditioning.
Active non-hematopoietic cancer that is metastatic, relapsed or refractory, or locally advanced and not curable (non-melanoma skin cancer excluded).
Uncontrolled intercurrent illness that the investigator judges unsafe for transplant.
Active breastfeeding.

NCT07190469.summary_en: PQ203, a peptide drug-conjugate, is being tested in people with advanced solid tumors, including triple negative breast cancer. It is given by intravenous infusion once weekly; how long treatment continues is not stated. The study measures safety and tolerability, and it is a Phase 1 study.
NCT07190469.summary_es: PQ203, un conjugado peptídico de fármaco, se está probando en personas con tumores sólidos avanzados, incluido el cáncer de mama triple negativo. Se administra por infusión intravenosa una vez por semana; no se indica por cuánto tiempo continúa el tratamiento. El estudio mide la seguridad y la tolerabilidad, y es un estudio de fase 1.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older.
Metastatic or locally advanced solid tumor that has progressed on standard therapy or is otherwise ineligible for it.
ECOG performance status of 0 to 1.
Measurable disease according to RECIST v1.1.
Adequate blood, liver, kidney and heart function based on lab tests within 14 days of the first dose.
not_for: Primary central nervous system malignancies.
Prior receipt of an MMAE-containing drug or a SORT1-targeting medication.
History of non-infectious interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis, or current or suspected lung inflammation that cannot be ruled out.
Active peripheral neuropathy above grade 1.
Known or suspected pregnancy or lactation, or weight above 115 kg.

NCT06833073.summary_en: This Phase 2 study tests intismeran autogene (V940) given with BCG, compared with BCG alone, in people with high-risk non-muscle invasive bladder cancer. In the combination group, intismeran autogene is given as a 1 mg intramuscular injection every 3 weeks for 9 doses, and TICE BCG 50 mg is put into the bladder once weekly for 6 weeks, then once weekly in weeks 13-15, 25-27, 49-51, and 73-75. The study aims to learn whether people live longer and without the cancer growing, spreading, or coming back.
NCT06833073.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 prueba intismeran autogene (V940) administrado junto con BCG, en comparación con BCG solo, en personas con cáncer de vejiga no músculo-invasivo de alto riesgo. En el grupo de combinación, intismeran autogene se administra como inyección intramuscular de 1 mg cada 3 semanas por 9 dosis, y BCG TICE de 50 mg se instila en la vejiga una vez por semana durante 6 semanas, y luego una vez por semana en las semanas 13-15, 25-27, 49-51 y 73-75. El estudio busca saber si las personas viven más tiempo y sin que el cáncer crezca, se extienda o regrese.
who_for: Has high-risk bladder cancer confined to the inner lining, including Ta, T1, and/or carcinoma in situ (Cohort A)
Has carcinoma in situ with or without papillary tumors and is ineligible for or refuses IVESIC therapy (Cohort B)
Has not had BCG, or had BCG more than 2 years before high-risk recurrence (Cohort A)
Most recent TURBT was within 12 weeks before randomization, with confirmed high-risk histology
not_for: Has locally advanced (T2-T4) or metastatic urothelial cancer
Received systemic anticancer therapy, including investigational agents, within 4 weeks before randomization
Received prior cancer vaccine treatment
Had a heart attack within 6 months of randomization, or has immunodeficiency or chronic systemic steroid use
Has current active tuberculosis or known HIV infection (Cohort A)

NCT06083883.summary_en: This Phase 1/1b study tests NY-ESO-1 TCR/IL-15 NK cells, which are donated natural killer cells that express a T-cell receptor against NY-ESO-1, given with chemotherapy in advanced synovial sarcoma and myxoid/round cell liposarcoma. The drugs are given by IV (vein), with fludarabine and cyclophosphamide given with the NK cells, in dose groups of up to 6 participants and up to 4 NK cell dose levels. How often and for how long doses are given is not stated. The study measures the recommended dose of NK cells, and the record also says safety and effects will be studied.
NCT06083883.summary_es: Este estudio de Fase 1/1b evalúa células NK de donante que expresan un receptor de células T contra NY-ESO-1, administradas junto con quimioterapia en sarcoma sinovial avanzado y liposarcoma mixoide/de células redondas. Los medicamentos se administran por IV (vena): fludarabina y ciclofosfamida junto con las células NK, en grupos de hasta 6 participantes y hasta 4 niveles de dosis de células NK. La frecuencia y la duración de las dosis no se indican en el registro. El estudio mide la dosis recomendada de células NK, y el registro también indica que se estudiarán la seguridad y los efectos.
who_for: Advanced synovial sarcoma or myxoid/round cell liposarcoma with NY-ESO-1 positive tumor
HLA-A*02:01, HLA-A*02:05 or HLA-A*02:06 positive
Relapsed or refractory after at least one prior line of systemic therapy with doxorubicin and/or ifosfamide (or trabectedin for liposarcoma)
Measurable disease by RECIST v1.1
ECOG performance status 0-1, age 16-80 years, weight 40 kg or more
not_for: Any prior anti-NY-ESO-1 therapy
Active hepatitis B or C, or HIV with detectable viral load
Active autoimmune disease within 12 months of enrollment
Other malignancy within the past 2 years, with listed exceptions
Pregnant or breastfeeding

NCT05603910.summary_en: This study tests lenvatinib and pembrolizumab with a short course of pelvic radiation therapy in people with recurrent or unresectable endometrial carcinoma that is mismatch repair proficient (pMMR). Lenvatinib is taken by mouth every day at dose levels of 4, 8, 12 or 16 mg, pembrolizumab 200 mg is given through a vein on Days 1, 22 and 43, and whole pelvic radiation is given in 16 daily-fraction doses of 2.5 Gy (40 Gy) followed by a boost, with about 7 weeks of radiation and about 10 to 12 weeks of total treatment. The study is a Phase 1 trial that aims to see whether this combination is feasible, and no main outcome measure is listed in the record.
NCT05603910.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa lenvatinib y pembrolizumab junto con un curso corto de radioterapia pélvica en personas con carcinoma endometrial recurrente o no operable que es pMMR (con reparación de desajustes competente). El lenvatinib se toma por vía oral todos los días en dosis de 4, 8, 12 o 16 mg, el pembrolizumab de 200 mg se aplica por vía intravenosa los días 1, 22 y 43, y la radioterapia pélvica total se administra en 16 fracciones de 2,5 Gy (40 Gy) seguidas de un refuerzo, con unas 7 semanas de radiación y unas 10 a 12 semanas de tratamiento total. Es un estudio de fase 1 que busca determinar si esta combinación es factible, y el registro no indica una medida de resultado principal.
who_for: Biopsy-proven recurrent or unresectable pMMR endometrial carcinoma, or uterine carcinosarcoma, for whom external beam radiation is considered appropriate.
Measurable disease of at least 1.0 cm, with at least one site in the pelvis or vagina and no disease outside the pelvis.
ECOG performance status 0 to 2 (Karnofsky score 50 or higher).
Adequate blood counts, kidney, liver and albumin levels as defined in the record.
Age 18 or older, able to sign consent, and using birth control if of childbearing potential.
not_for: Mismatch repair deficient (dMMR) endometrial carcinoma or dMMR uterine carcinosarcoma.
Known active brain metastases or carcinomatous meningitis.
Prior external beam radiation to the vagina, pelvis or abdomen.
Another malignancy that is progressing or needs active treatment (some skin cancers and in situ cervical cancer excepted).
Investigational agent within 4 weeks, or systemic steroids or immunosuppressive therapy within 21 days before the first dose.

NCT07226869.summary_en: The study tests computer guidance software used during microwave ablation, a procedure that heats and destroys liver tumors, in adults with localized hepatocellular carcinoma (liver cancer). The ablation is done with CT guidance while the software shows which part of the tumor has been treated, and follow-up is at one month and then every 3 months with blood tests and contrast-enhanced CT or MRI. The study measures how often a tumor is incompletely treated, local tumor recurrence at 2 years, and changes in medical problems after the procedure.
NCT07226869.summary_es: El estudio prueba un software de guía por computadora que se usa durante la ablación por microondas, un procedimiento que calienta y destruye tumores del hígado, en adultos con carcinoma hepatocelular (cáncer de hígado) localizado. La ablación se realiza con guía de tomografía computarizada mientras el software muestra qué parte del tumor ya fue tratada, y el seguimiento es al mes y luego cada 3 meses, con análisis de sangre y estudios de TC con contraste o resonancia magnética. El estudio mide con qué frecuencia un tumor queda tratado de forma incompleta, la recurrencia local del tumor a los 2 años y los cambios en problemas médicos después del procedimiento.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older with a life expectancy of at least 1 year
Hepatocellular carcinoma confirmed by imaging, biopsy, or cirrhosis with high AFP
Localized liver tumors: up to 5 lesions, at least one 2–5 cm, none over 5 cm, judged feasible for ablation
Performance status 0–2 (ECOG), adequate platelets and INR, and able to have contrast CT or MRI
Willing and able to give informed consent
not_for: Prior ablation, TACE, SBRT, or resection of the target lesion or a lesion within 1 cm of it
More than 5 liver lesions, or any lesion that cannot be completely ablated
Uncontrolled liver decompensation, such as persistent encephalopathy
Uncorrectable coagulopathy, contraindication to contrast imaging, active systemic infection, or pregnancy
Unable to follow the imaging schedule

NCT06763341.summary_en: This Phase 1 study tests the safety, side effects, and best dose of AOH1996, a PCNA inhibitor, given with azacitidine and venetoclax, in adults with relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia (AML). AOH1996 is taken by mouth twice a day on days 1 to 28 of each 28-day cycle, and patients receive up to 2 cycles, or up to 12 if they reach complete remission with transfusion independence and the disease does not progress. The schedule for azacitidine and venetoclax is not stated. No main outcome measure is stated in the record; the study is a Phase 1 trial.
NCT06763341.summary_es: Este estudio de Fase 1 evalúa la seguridad, los efectos secundarios y la dosis más adecuada de AOH1996, un inhibidor de PCNA, administrado junto con azacitidina y venetoclax, en adultos con leucemia mieloide aguda (LMA) recidivante o refractaria. AOH1996 se toma por vía oral dos veces al día los días 1 a 28 de cada ciclo de 28 días, y los pacientes reciben hasta 2 ciclos, o hasta 12 si logran una remisión completa con independencia de transfusiones y la enfermedad no progresa. El esquema de azacitidina y venetoclax no se indica. El registro no indica una medida de resultado principal; el estudio es de Fase 1.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older.
Relapsed or refractory AML that failed available effective treatment, or for which such treatment is not an option.
ECOG performance status of 2 or less and life expectancy over 3 months.
White blood cell count of 25 x 10^9/L or less before starting study therapy.
Adequate liver, kidney, and blood clotting test results within 14 days before day 1.
not_for: Acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL) or t(15;17) abnormality.
Hematopoietic stem cell transplant within 100 days before day 1.
Active central nervous system disease or active graft versus host disease.
Unstable heart disease, including heart attack within the past 6 months.
Pregnant or breastfeeding females.

NCT06858813.summary_en: This Phase 1 study is testing ABBV-324, an investigational drug, in adults with hepatocellular cancer or squamous-cell non-small cell lung cancer. ABBV-324 is given by intravenous (IV) infusion, and some participants receive oral lenvatinib; the study lasts about 6.5 years and how often doses are given is not stated. The study measures adverse events and change in disease activity, and it is a Phase 1 study.
NCT06858813.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1 evalúa ABBV-324, un medicamento en investigación, en adultos con cáncer hepatocelular o cáncer de pulmón de células no pequeñas de tipo escamoso. ABBV-324 se administra por infusión intravenosa (IV), algunos participantes reciben lenvatinib oral, el estudio dura unos 6.5 años y la frecuencia de las dosis no se indica. El estudio mide los eventos adversos y el cambio en la actividad de la enfermedad; es un estudio de fase 1.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older.
ECOG performance status of 0 or 1.
Measurable disease per RECIST version 1.1.
Locally advanced, metastatic or unresectable HCC confirmed by histology or cytology; Part 2 requires prior checkpoint inhibitor regimen and no prior lenvatinib.
Part 1 only: advanced LUSC not amenable to surgery, after failure of platinum chemotherapy with an immune checkpoint inhibitor and/or targeted therapy.
not_for: Fibrolamellar HCC, sarcomatoid HCC, or mixed cholangiocarcinoma/HCC.
Unresolved adverse events above Grade 1 from prior anticancer therapy, except alopecia.
Untreated brain or meningeal metastases, or metastases needing ongoing steroids for cerebral edema.
History of interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis needing systemic steroids, or active ILD or pneumonitis on screening CT.
Anticancer therapy stopped within 14 days or 5 half-lives (whichever is shorter) before the first ABBV-324 dose.

NCT05789303.summary_en: This Phase 2 study tests belantamab mafodotin combined with carfilzomib, pomalidomide, and dexamethasone (KPd) in adults with relapsed multiple myeloma. Belantamab mafodotin is given by IV on Day 1 of 28-day cycles, and the other drugs follow the schedules listed in the record; participation is about 6 to 24 months. The record does not state a main outcome measure; the study is Phase 2.
NCT05789303.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 evalúa belantamab mafodotina combinada con carfilzomib, pomalidomida y dexametasona (KPd) en adultos con mieloma múltiple recidivante. La belantamab mafodotina se administra por vía intravenosa el día 1 de ciclos de 28 días, y los otros medicamentos siguen los esquemas indicados en el registro; la participación dura aproximadamente de 6 a 24 meses. El registro no indica una medida de resultado principal; el estudio es de fase 2.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older
Relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma that has progressed after at least 2 prior lines of anti-myeloma treatment
Measurable disease by serum M-protein, urine M-protein, or involved free light chains
ECOG performance status of 2 or less and life expectancy over 3 months
Cohort 2 includes participants who had prior CAR T-cell therapy
not_for: Waldenström's macroglobulinemia, systemic amyloidosis, POEMS syndrome, or plasma cell leukemia at screening
Prior refractory status to belantamab mafodotin
Significant neuropathy (Grade 3-4, or Grade 2 with pain)
Active infection requiring treatment, or serious cardiovascular risk such as uncontrolled arrhythmia or uncontrolled hypertension
Pregnant or lactating

NCT05797805.summary_en: This Phase 1/2 study tests tegavivint (BC2059), a TBL1 inhibitor, alone and combined with lenvatinib or cabozantinib, in adults with advanced hepatocellular carcinoma. Tegavivint is given weekly on days 1, 8, 15, and 22 of a 28-day cycle, and lenvatinib and cabozantinib are given once daily on days 1 to 28 of each cycle. The record does not state the main outcome measure; the study is described as Phase 1/2.
NCT05797805.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1/2 evalúa tegavivint (BC2059), un inhibidor de TBL1, solo y combinado con lenvatinib o cabozantinib, en adultos con carcinoma hepatocelular avanzado. El tegavivint se administra semanalmente los días 1, 8, 15 y 22 de un ciclo de 28 días, y el lenvatinib y el cabozantinib se administran una vez al día los días 1 al 28 de cada ciclo. El registro no indica la medida principal de resultado; el estudio se describe como de fase 1/2.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older with advanced hepatocellular carcinoma.
Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer stage C, or stage B not suitable for locoregional or curative treatment.
Progression, intolerance, or contraindication to at least one prior line of systemic therapy.
Measurable disease by RECIST 1.1 on CT or MRI.
ECOG performance status 0 or 1, and Child-Pugh class A or B (score 7 or less) without hepatic encephalopathy.
not_for: Known fibrolamellar, sarcomatoid, or mixed cholangiocarcinoma and HCC.
Currently receiving other anticancer or experimental agents.
Known Gilbert's syndrome or other genetic conditions affecting UGT1A1 function.
Pregnant or breastfeeding women.
Clinically significant heart disease or baseline QTc (Fridericia) of 450 ms or more.

NCT04222062.summary_en: This Phase 2 study compares GLIADEL wafers placed at the surgical site with stereotactic radiosurgery in people with metastatic brain tumors that are removed surgically. After the tumor is removed, GLIADEL wafers are placed to cover the tumor bed, with the number based on cavity size, while the comparison group receives stereotactic radiosurgery within six weeks after surgery; the total length of treatment is not stated. The study aims to see whether adding GLIADEL works as well as surgery with radiosurgery in keeping the cancer from coming back, and a formal primary outcome measure is not stated.
NCT04222062.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 compara las obleas GLIADEL colocadas en el sitio de la cirugía con la radiocirugía estereotáctica en personas con tumores cerebrales metastásicos que se extirpan quirúrgicamente. Después de extirpar el tumor, se colocan obleas GLIADEL para cubrir el lecho tumoral, y la cantidad depende del tamaño de la cavidad; el grupo de comparación recibe radiocirugía estereotáctica dentro de las seis semanas posteriores a la cirugía, y la duración total del tratamiento no se indica. El estudio busca saber si agregar GLIADEL funciona igual que la cirugía con radiocirugía para evitar que el cáncer regrese, y no se indica una medida principal formal de resultado.
who_for: Age 18 or older (19 or older in Nebraska).
Metastatic brain tumor, up to four tumors, each up to 4 cm, with surgery planned at one site.
Karnofsky Performance Status of 60 or higher and RPA class I, II or III.
Estimated survival of at least 3 months, per the primary oncologist.
Labs adequate for surgery, INR 1.3 or lower, and able to consent and follow the protocol.
not_for: Prior treatment to the planned resection area, or prior whole brain radiation.
Lymphoma, germ cell cancer, small cell lung cancer, or anaplastic thyroid cancer.
Leptomeningeal disease or a neurodegenerative disorder such as dementia.
Tumor larger than 4 cm, or Karnofsky Performance Status below 60.
Bleeding disorder, or anticoagulants or antiplatelet agents that cannot be stopped for surgery.

NCT05327686.summary_en: This Phase II trial tests adding stereotactic ablative radiation therapy (SABR) to standard immunotherapy for people with unresectable or metastatic renal cell carcinoma. The radiation is given in 3 sessions over 1 to 3 weeks, and immunotherapy continues while the disease does not progress and side effects are acceptable. The main outcome is not stated in the record; this is a randomized Phase II study.
NCT05327686.summary_es: Este ensayo de fase II evalúa agregar radioterapia estereotáctica ablativa (SABR) a la inmunoterapia estándar para personas con carcinoma de células renales no resecable o metastásico. La radiación se administra en 3 sesiones durante 1 a 3 semanas, y la inmunoterapia continúa mientras la enfermedad no progrese y los efectos secundarios sean aceptables. El resultado principal no se indica en el registro; se trata de un estudio aleatorizado de fase II.
who_for: Kidney cancer (renal cell carcinoma) confirmed by tissue testing
Lymph node-positive unresectable or metastatic disease on recent scans
IMDC intermediate or poor risk disease
Measurable disease outside the primary kidney tumor
Not recommended for, or refused, immediate nephrectomy
not_for: Planned definitive treatment of all metastatic sites
Untreated or unstable brain metastases or cranial epidural disease
Systemic therapy for metastatic kidney cancer started more than 90 days before registration
Active autoimmune disease needing ongoing steroids or immunosuppressants
Pregnancy, or unwillingness to stop breastfeeding

NCT07504796.summary_en: This phase 2 study tests whether circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) results can guide adding ipilimumab to nivolumab and relatlimab as first-line treatment for advanced or metastatic melanoma. Patients receive nivolumab 480 mg and relatlimab 160 mg every 4 weeks, and patients with positive ctDNA at week 6 may be randomized to also receive ipilimumab 1 mg/kg intravenously every 8 weeks. The main outcome measured is progression-free survival, and secondary outcomes include objective response rate and immune-related adverse events.
NCT07504796.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 evalúa si los resultados del ADN tumoral circulante (ctDNA) pueden guiar la adición de ipilimumab a nivolumab y relatlimab como tratamiento de primera línea para melanoma avanzado o metastásico. Los pacientes reciben nivolumab 480 mg y relatlimab 160 mg cada 4 semanas, y los pacientes con ctDNA positivo en la semana 6 pueden ser asignados aleatoriamente para recibir también ipilimumab 1 mg/kg por vía intravenosa cada 8 semanas. El resultado principal que se mide es la supervivencia libre de progresión, y los resultados secundarios incluyen la tasa de respuesta objetiva y los eventos adversos relacionados con la inmunidad.
who_for: Adults 18 or older with unresectable stage IIIB-IV melanoma from skin, acral, mucosal, or unknown primary site.
At least one measurable lesion per RECIST 1.1.
Planned to start standard first-line treatment for metastatic disease.
Detectable ctDNA at baseline.
ECOG performance status of 0 to 1.
not_for: Carcinomatosis meningitis or current ocular/uveal melanoma.
History of myocarditis.
Autoimmune disease needing immunosuppression beyond prednisone 10 mg daily or equivalent.
Prior anticancer treatment for metastatic disease, with listed exceptions.
Known hypersensitivity to monoclonal antibodies, or pregnancy.

NCT06444269.summary_en: This Phase 2 study tests response adaptive ablative pre-operative SPBI (RAPS) radiation and a non-surgical sentinel lymph node check using microbubble contrast ultrasound in early-stage estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer. Radiation is given before surgery, and the number of doses and schedule are not stated. The main outcome measure is not stated; the record lists efficacy of pre-operative radiation and whether microbubble contrast ultrasound can replace operative sentinel lymph node biopsy as goals.
