NCT06444269.summary_es: Este estudio de Fase 2 evalúa la radiación preoperatoria SPBI adaptativa y ablativa (RAPS) y una revisión no quirúrgica del ganglio centinela con ultrasonido de contraste con microburbujas, en cáncer de mama temprano receptor de estrógeno positivo. La radiación se administra antes de la cirugía; el número de dosis y el esquema no se indican. La medida de resultado principal no se indica; el registro enumera como objetivos la eficacia de la radiación preoperatoria y si el ultrasonido de contraste con microburbujas puede reemplazar la biopsia quirúrgica del ganglio centinela.
who_for: Women 18 or older with invasive breast cancer 3 cm or less and node negative (T1-T2 cN0).
Estrogen or progesterone receptor positive and HER2 negative tumor.
Tumor does not involve the overlying skin.
No surgery, endocrine therapy, or chemotherapy for the current breast cancer.
Tumor visible on CT or MRI, or marked with a clip.
not_for: Multicentric (multifocal across the breast) disease.
Prior radiation to the involved breast or prior breast cancer on the same side.
Tumor larger than 3 cm.
Pregnant or lactating.
Active lupus or scleroderma.

NCT07746388.summary_en: This Phase 2 study tests cemiplimab, an immune checkpoint inhibitor, before surgery in adults with resectable stage II to IIIB non-small cell lung cancer. Cemiplimab is given by IV infusion every 3 weeks, for at least 3 doses before surgery, with a possible 4th dose depending on scans after cycle 2. The main outcome measure is not stated in the record; the study is Phase 2.
NCT07746388.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 evalúa cemiplimab, un inhibidor de puntos de control inmunitario, antes de la cirugía en adultos con cáncer de pulmón de células no pequeñas en estadio II a IIIB que puede resecarse. Cemiplimab se administra por infusión intravenosa cada 3 semanas, al menos 3 dosis antes de la cirugía, con una posible cuarta dosis según los estudios de imagen después del ciclo 2. La medida de resultado principal no se indica en el registro; el estudio es de fase 2.
who_for: Adults aged 18 or older
ECOG performance status of 0 or 1
Stage II to IIIB(N2) non-small cell lung cancer considered resectable before systemic therapy
PD-L1 tumor proportion score of 50% or higher
Tumor reviewed by a multidisciplinary thoracic tumor board before enrollment
not_for: Locally advanced unresectable or stage IV (metastatic) disease
Large-cell neuroendocrine or small cell carcinoma histology, including mixed histology
Known sensitizing EGFR mutations or ALK translocation
Brain metastases
Prior anti-PD-(L)1, anti-CTLA-4, or other T-cell co-regulatory antibody therapy

NCT06929286.summary_en: This Phase 3 study compares nadofaragene firadenovec with usual care treatments for high-grade non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) in people whose BCG treatment has failed. Usual care for randomized patients is intravesical gemcitabine plus docetaxel (GemDoce), and the record also lists other standard options such as mitomycin, BCG re-treatment, and pembrolizumab. Nadofaragene firadenovec is instilled into the bladder every 3 months for up to 12 months, and GemDoce is given weekly for 6 weeks for induction, then monthly for up to 24 months for those with a complete response. The record does not state the main outcome measure; the study is described as comparing effectiveness.
NCT06929286.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 3 compara nadofaragene firadenovec con tratamientos de atención habitual para el cáncer de vejiga no músculo invasivo (CVNMI) de alto grado, en personas cuyo tratamiento con BCG ha fallado. La atención habitual para los pacientes asignados es gemcitabina más docetaxel (GemDoce) por vía intravesical, y el registro también menciona otras opciones estándar, como mitomicina, nuevo tratamiento con BCG y pembrolizumab. Nadofaragene firadenovec se instila en la vejiga cada 3 meses durante hasta 12 meses, y GemDoce se administra semanalmente durante 6 semanas como inducción, y luego mensualmente durante hasta 24 meses en quienes tienen respuesta completa. El registro no indica la medida de resultado principal; el estudio se describe como una comparación de efectividad.
who_for: Age 21 years or older.
High-grade non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (Tis, Ta, or T1) under care of a participating urologist.
One or more BCG induction courses, and the treating urologist judges that BCG has failed.
Received at least one intravesical or systemic NMIBC treatment in the previous 12 months, with some timing allowances for TURBT.
Treating urologist sees no contraindication to nadofaragene firadenovec and is uncertain whether it is better than best usual care.
not_for: Choosing radical cystectomy.
Currently receiving an experimental therapy for NMIBC in a clinical trial.
Prior exposure to nadofaragene firadenovec.

NCT06079346.summary_en: This randomized study compares OT-101 added to mFOLFIRINOX with mFOLFIRINOX alone in advanced, unresectable or metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. OT-101 is an antisense drug given by IV on Days 4-7 of a 14-day cycle, and mFOLFIRINOX starts on Day 1 of each cycle; the total number of cycles is not stated. The study measures efficacy and safety, but the main outcome measure is not stated; the study is Phase 2/3.
NCT06079346.summary_es: Este estudio aleatorizado compara OT-101 añadido a mFOLFIRINOX con mFOLFIRINOX solo, en cáncer de páncreas avanzado, no resecable o metastásico (adenocarcinoma ductal). OT-101 es un fármaco antisentido que se administra por vía intravenosa los días 4 a 7 de un ciclo de 14 días, y mFOLFIRINOX comienza el día 1 de cada ciclo; el número total de ciclos no se indica. El estudio evalúa la eficacia y la seguridad, pero la medida de resultado principal no se indica; es un estudio de fase 2/3.
who_for: Advanced, unresectable or metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma confirmed by tissue biopsy or documented history
Measurable disease by RECIST v1.1
Age 18 years or older, with signed informed consent
ECOG performance status 0 to 1
Adequate blood, liver and kidney function, and life expectancy of at least 3 months
not_for: Pancreatic islet, acinar cell, lymphoma, sarcoma, biliary tree or cystadenocarcinoma tumors
Prior immune checkpoint inhibitor treatment
Known dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase (DPD) deficiency
Active central nervous system metastases
Active HIV or active hepatitis A, B or C infection

NCT06063486.summary_en: This phase 2 trial tests a curcumin supplement (C3 complex/Bioperine) against placebo in people with clonal cytopenia of undetermined significance, low-risk myelodysplastic syndrome, or myeloproliferative neoplasms (polycythemia vera, essential thrombocythemia, or myelofibrosis). Participants take the supplement or placebo by mouth twice a day for 12 months, unless the disease progresses or side effects are unacceptable. The study compares effects on inflammatory cytokines, symptoms and disease parameters; a specific primary outcome is not stated.
NCT06063486.summary_es: Este ensayo de fase 2 evalúa un suplemento de cúrcuma (complejo C3/Bioperine) comparado con placebo en personas con citopenia clonal de significado indeterminado, síndrome mielodisplásico de bajo riesgo o neoplasias mieloproliferativas (policitemia vera, trombocitemia esencial o mielofibrosis). Los participantes toman el suplemento o el placebo por vía oral dos veces al día durante 12 meses, salvo que la enfermedad progrese o aparezca toxicidad inaceptable. El estudio compara los efectos sobre las citocinas inflamatorias, los síntomas y los parámetros de la enfermedad; no se indica un resultado primario específico.
who_for: Age 18 or older with ECOG performance status 2 or less
Polycythemia vera, essential thrombocythemia, or myelofibrosis per WHO 2016 criteria, with at least one symptom scoring above 3
CCUS or low-risk MDS, with persistent cytopenia for more than 6 months
Baseline fatigue symptom score of at least 25
Able to understand and sign written informed consent
not_for: Taking curcumin supplements, including multivitamins, and unwilling to stop 24 hours before study start
Active treatment for another cancer, except hormonal therapy for a cancer in remission or certain growth factors
Intermediate or high-risk MDS
Pregnant or nursing
Taking oral or intravenous steroids or other anti-inflammatory medicines at the listed doses

NCT06153173.summary_en: The study tests mirdametinib, a MEK inhibitor, in people with Langerhans cell histiocytosis, juvenile xanthogranuloma, Rosai-Dorfman disease, or other histiocytic disorders. Mirdametinib is taken by mouth twice daily on a continuous schedule, with each cycle lasting 4 weeks; the total length of treatment is not stated. The main outcome is not stated; this is a Phase 2 trial.
NCT06153173.summary_es: El estudio evalúa mirdametinib, un inhibidor de MEK, en personas con histiocitosis de células de Langerhans, xantogranuloma juvenil, enfermedad de Rosai-Dorfman u otros trastornos histiocíticos. El mirdametinib se toma por vía oral dos veces al día, de forma continua, con ciclos de 4 semanas; la duración total del tratamiento no se indica. El resultado principal no se indica; este es un estudio de fase 2.
who_for: Age 2 years or older with a histiocytic disorder that needs systemic therapy.
Diagnosis confirmed by biopsy review or molecular testing, or by a positive blood test in cases where biopsy is not feasible.
Measurable disease on PET scan or brain MRI.
Adequate kidney, liver, blood count and albumin levels; abnormalities caused by the disease are allowed.
not_for: Cytotoxic myelosuppressive chemotherapy within 14 days, or a MEK inhibitor within 30 days or 5 half-lives, or disease progression on a MEK inhibitor.
Steroids within 14 days before the first dose, or long-term steroid use over 30 consecutive days (endocrine replacement is an exception); radiation within 14 da
Risk factors for retinal vein occlusion, such as high eye pressure, uncontrolled glaucoma, high cholesterol or triglycerides, high blood sugar, or uncontrolled
LVEF below 55% or significant cardiac disease not caused by the histiocytic disease.
Pregnant or breastfeeding, or at risk of pregnancy or fathering a baby without acceptable birth control.

NCT04939610.summary_en: This Phase 1/2 study is testing 177Lu-FAP-2286, a targeted radionuclide therapy that binds to fibroblast activation protein (FAP), in patients with advanced solid tumors. Phase 2 includes pancreatic, non-small cell lung, and breast cancers. Patients must first have a 68Ga-FAP-2286 PET scan showing FAP uptake, then receive 177Lu-FAP-2286 by IV every 6 weeks for up to 6 doses in Phase 1, or every 4 weeks in Phase 2 monotherapy, with doses of 3.7 to 9.25 GBq (100 to 250 mCi). The study measures safety and tolerability and establishes the recommended Phase 2 dose in Phase 1, and measures safety and efficacy in Phase 2.
NCT04939610.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1/2 evalúa 177Lu-FAP-2286, una terapia radionuclídica dirigida que se une a la proteína de activación de fibroblastos (FAP), en pacientes con tumores sólidos avanzados. La fase 2 incluye cáncer de páncreas, cáncer de pulmón de células no pequeñas y cáncer de mama. Los pacientes primero deben tener una tomografía PET con 68Ga-FAP-2286 que muestre captación de FAP, y luego reciben 177Lu-FAP-2286 por vía intravenosa cada 6 semanas, hasta 6 dosis en la fase 1, o cada 4 semanas en la monoterapia de la fase 2, con dosis de 3.7 a 9.25 GBq (100 a 250 mCi). El estudio mide la seguridad y la tolerabilidad y establece la dosis recomendada para fase 2 en la fase 1, y mide la seguridad y la eficacia en la fase 2.
who_for: Age 18 years or older.
ECOG performance status of 0 or 1.
Life expectancy of 6 months or more.
Measurable disease per RECIST v1.1.
Adequate blood, liver, and kidney function laboratory values; Phase 2 also requires specific prior treatment history by cancer group.
not_for: Active cancer other than the one under study, with limited exceptions stated in the record.
Symptomatic or untreated brain or CNS metastases, or leptomeningeal disease.
Pancreatic endocrine or neuroendocrine tumors (Phase 2 pancreatic groups).
Prior taxane therapy in the Phase 2 lung combination group.
Phase 1 requires tumor that is refractory or has progressed after prior treatment with no satisfactory alternatives.

NCT06639724.summary_en: This Phase 1b study tests fostamatinib, a Syk kinase inhibitor approved for chronic idiopathic thrombocytopenia purpura, added to gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel chemotherapy around surgery for resectable, non-metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. Participants take fostamatinib 100 mg by mouth twice a day for 7 days before chemotherapy and then during it, while gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel are given by vein on days 1, 8, and 15 of each 28-day cycle; the total number of cycles is not stated. The main outcome is not stated in the record; the study is a Phase 1b trial.
NCT06639724.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1b evalúa fostamatinib, un inhibidor de la quinasa Syk aprobado para la púrpura trombocitopénica idiopática crónica, añadido a la quimioterapia con gemcitabina y nab-paclitaxel alrededor de la cirugía para el adenocarcinoma ductal de páncreas resecable y no metastásico. Los participantes toman fostamatinib 100 mg por vía oral dos veces al día durante 7 días antes de la quimioterapia y luego durante esta, mientras que la gemcitabina y el nab-paclitaxel se administran por vena los días 1, 8 y 15 de cada ciclo de 28 días; el número total de ciclos no se indica. El resultado principal no se indica en el registro; el estudio es de fase 1b.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older who can give written informed consent
ECOG performance status of 1 or less
Resectable primary pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma on recent CT or MRI
Confirmed surgical candidate by surgical consult within 28 days before enrollment
Adequate blood counts, liver, kidney and bilirubin levels
not_for: Any prior treatment for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
Recurrent or metastatic pancreatic cancer
Peripheral neuropathy above grade 2
Investigational agent within 28 days before first study dose, or major surgery within 28 days
Pregnancy or lactation

NCT07197827.summary_en: This Phase 1/2 study tests YL242, given alone or with other drugs (pembrolizumab, or 5-FU and leucovorin), in people with advanced solid tumors. YL242 is given by intravenous (IV) infusion, with the first dose over about 90 minutes and later doses over about 60 minutes if no infusion reaction occurs; how often doses are given is not stated. The study's main stated aim is to evaluate safety and tolerability.
NCT07197827.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1/2 evalúa YL242, administrado solo o con otros medicamentos (pembrolizumab, o 5-FU y leucovorina), en personas con tumores sólidos avanzados. YL242 se administra por infusión intravenosa (IV); la primera dosis dura unos 90 minutos y las siguientes unos 60 minutos si no hay reacción a la infusión, y la frecuencia de las dosis no se indica. El objetivo principal indicado en el estudio es evaluar la seguridad y la tolerabilidad.
who_for: Age 18 years or older.
ECOG performance status of 0 or 1.
Adequate organ and bone marrow function.
Advanced or metastatic solid tumor; for most parts, at least one prior line of systemic therapy.
Specific tumor groups by study part, such as NSCLC without AGA or HCC with no prior systemic therapy, mCRC, or HER2-negative gastric/GEJ cancer.
not_for: Intolerance to prior topoisomerase I inhibitor or to an ADC containing one.
Uncontrolled or clinically significant cardiovascular or cerebrovascular disease.
Clinically significant concurrent lung disease.
History of leptomeningeal carcinomatosis or carcinomatous meningitis.
Any condition the investigator judges could interfere with consent, participation, or result interpretation.

NCT04722523.summary_en: This study tests cemiplimab, given with platinum chemotherapy (cisplatin or carboplatin), docetaxel (or paclitaxel if docetaxel cannot be used), and cetuximab, before surgery in people with resectable, locally advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. Chemotherapy and cemiplimab are given in cycles over several weeks, with cetuximab given weekly for about 10 weeks, and surgery follows about 28 days (plus or minus 7 days) after the third cycle. The record does not state a main outcome measure; the listed phase is Phase 1.
NCT04722523.summary_es: Este estudio prueba cemiplimab, administrado con quimioterapia a base de platino (cisplatino o carboplatino), docetaxel (o paclitaxel si no se puede usar docetaxel) y cetuximab, antes de la cirugía en personas con carcinoma de células escamosas de cabeza y cuello, localmente avanzado y resecable. La quimioterapia y el cemiplimab se administran en ciclos durante varias semanas, el cetuximab se administra cada semana durante unas 10 semanas, y la cirugía se realiza unos 28 días (más o menos 7 días) después del tercer ciclo. El registro no indica una medida de resultado principal; la fase indicada es la Fase 1.
who_for: Squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck, confirmed by tissue or cell testing
Locally advanced disease with no distant spread, where standard care would be surgery then radiation with or without chemotherapy
Disease must be removable by surgery, and the patient must be a surgical candidate
Age 18 or older with ECOG performance status below 1
Adequate blood counts, kidney function and liver function
not_for: Prior radiation or systemic therapy for head and neck cancer
Oral cavity cancer that cannot be removed by surgery
Autoimmune or inflammatory disorder treated with steroids or immunomodulators in the past 5 years, with listed exceptions
Immune-related pneumonitis in the past 5 years, or interstitial lung disease
Uncontrolled HIV, hepatitis B or hepatitis C, or immunodeficiency
cancer_types: head and neck squamous cell carcinoma

NCT03706027.summary_en: This study compares two radiation schedules for early-stage lung cancer that is in the outer (peripheral) parts of the lungs. Patients are randomly assigned to either 3 fractions given over 3 days, for a total of 54 Grays, or 5 fractions given over 5 days, for a total of 60 Grays, followed by follow-up with their radiation oncologist. The study looks at the kinds of side effects (toxicity) patients have with each schedule, and its official title describes it as a randomized phase II study.
NCT03706027.summary_es: Este estudio compara dos esquemas de radiación para el cáncer de pulmón en etapa temprana que se encuentra en las partes externas (periféricas) de los pulmones. Los pacientes son asignados al azar a 3 fracciones administradas en 3 días, para una dosis total de 54 Grays, o a 5 fracciones administradas en 5 días, para una dosis total de 60 Grays, seguidos de un control con su oncólogo radioterapeuta. El estudio analiza qué tipos de efectos secundarios (toxicidad) presentan los pacientes con cada esquema, y su título oficial lo describe como un estudio aleatorizado de fase II.
who_for: Lung cancer of a non-small cell type, such as squamous, adenocarcinoma, or large cell
Stage I or II disease with T1 N0 M0, or T2 up to 5 cm with N0 M0
Zubrod performance status 0 to 2 within 4 weeks of study entry
Women who could become pregnant and men must use effective contraception
not_for: Central tumors located near the main airways (within 2 cm of the proximal bronchial tree)
Evidence of regional or distant spread after staging
Prior malignancy in the past 2 years, with some exceptions
Previous lung or mediastinal radiation, or planned concomitant antineoplastic therapy
Pregnant or breastfeeding women

NCT07719361.summary_en: This Phase 1 study is testing FX-111, a drug taken by mouth, in adult men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. Participants take FX-111 once daily in continuous 28-day cycles; the total duration is not stated. The study measures side effects (safety and tolerability) and whether FX-111 reduces or prevents cancer progression.
NCT07719361.summary_es: Este estudio de Fase 1 evalúa FX-111, un medicamento que se toma por vía oral, en hombres adultos con cáncer de próstata metastásico resistente a la castración. Los participantes toman FX-111 una vez al día en ciclos continuos de 28 días; la duración total no se indica. El estudio mide los efectos secundarios (seguridad y tolerabilidad) y si FX-111 reduce o previene la progresión del cáncer.
who_for: Adult men with confirmed prostate adenocarcinoma.
PSA at least 2 ng/mL at screening, with two consecutive rises at least 1 week apart.
Cancer progressed on hormone therapy and at least one prior potent AR pathway inhibitor.
Continuing hormone therapy with a GnRH agonist or antagonist, unless both testicles were removed.
Agrees to highly effective contraception during the study and for 90 days after.
not_for: Predominant small cell or neuroendocrine prostate cancer on the most recent biopsy.
Brain metastases needing ongoing radiation or high-dose steroids.
Prior treatment with AR degraders or AR ligand molecules such as RIPTAC.
Blood clots within 4 weeks before starting treatment.
Concurrent malignancy needing treatment, or a prior malignancy active within 2 years (unless clinically stable or treated with curative intent).

NCT04150042.summary_en: This phase 1 study tests a combination of melphalan, BCNU, vitamin B12b, and vitamin C given with the patient's own stem cells, in metastatic pancreatic cancer and metastatic breast cancer. The drugs are given intravenously in 2 cycles, with an autologous stem cell infusion after each cycle, and the vitamin C dose is escalated over time. The study measures the safety of the treatment and is a phase 1 trial.
NCT04150042.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1 evalúa una combinación de melfalán, BCNU, vitamina B12b y vitamina C, administrada junto con las propias células madre del paciente, en cáncer de páncreas metastásico y cáncer de mama metastásico. Los medicamentos se administran por vía intravenosa en 2 ciclos, con una infusión de células madre hematopoyéticas autólogas después de cada ciclo, y la dosis de vitamina C aumenta de forma escalonada. El estudio mide la seguridad del tratamiento y es un ensayo de fase 1.
who_for: Age 18 years or older.
Stage IV pancreatic cancer or HER2-negative breast cancer.
Karnofsky score of 60% or higher.
Expected survival of at least 6 months, as judged by the investigator.
BRCA1, BRCA2, or PALB2 mutation, or at least 16 weeks of first-line platinum chemotherapy without treatment failure.
not_for: Rapid disease progression, as judged by the investigator.
Current cholangitis or biliary tract obstruction.
Known or suspected brain (central nervous system) metastases.
Left ventricular ejection fraction below 45%.
Hemoglobin below 9 g/dL.

NCT06207305.summary_en: This Phase I/II study tests intraperitoneal paclitaxel, a chemotherapy drug given directly into the abdominal cavity, in people with metastatic appendiceal adenocarcinoma. The intervention list also names dexamethasone, diphenhydramine and famotidine, each listed as given by mouth, and how often or how long any drug is given is not stated. The study aims to find the recommended paclitaxel dose, and the outcome measure is stated only as finding that dose; the study is Phase I/II.
NCT06207305.summary_es: Este estudio de fase I/II evalúa paclitaxel intraperitoneal, un medicamento de quimioterapia que se administra directamente en la cavidad abdominal, en personas con adenocarcinoma apendicular metastásico. La lista de intervenciones también incluye dexametasona, difenhidramina y famotidina, que aparecen como administrados por vía oral; la frecuencia o la duración de cualquier medicamento no se indica. El estudio busca encontrar la dosis recomendada de paclitaxel, y la medida de resultado solo se indica como encontrar esa dosis; el estudio es de fase I/II.
who_for: Age 18 years or older.
ECOG performance status 2 or lower.
Histologically confirmed unresectable metastatic appendiceal adenocarcinoma, with disease in the peritoneal cavity.
Not a candidate for cytoreductive surgery.
Adequate blood cell counts, liver and kidney function.
not_for: Metastases outside the peritoneal cavity.
Active infection that would preclude protocol therapy.
Unstable angina or New York Heart Association grade II or greater heart failure.
Unable to comply with study procedures, such as due to cognitive impairment.
Receiving any other investigational agents.

NCT05491512.summary_en: This study tests whether a lower radiation dose, given with standard chemotherapy, can reduce side effects in people with HPV-positive throat cancer (oropharyngeal cancer). Radiation is given as a total of 30 Gy in 2 Gy fractions over 3 weeks, with cisplatin given by IV at the start of radiation for 2 cycles, and carboplatin and 5-fluorouracil may replace cisplatin. The record does not state a main outcome measure; the study is listed as Phase 2.
NCT05491512.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa si una dosis más baja de radiación, junto con quimioterapia estándar, puede reducir los efectos secundarios en personas con cáncer de garganta asociado al VPH (cáncer de orofaringe). La radiación se administra en una dosis total de 30 Gy, en fracciones de 2 Gy durante 3 semanas, y se da cisplatino por vía intravenosa al inicio de la radiación (2 ciclos); el carboplatino y el 5-fluorouracilo pueden sustituir al cisplatino. El registro no indica una medida principal de resultado; el estudio figura como fase 2.
who_for: HPV-associated squamous cell carcinoma of the oropharynx, proven by biopsy or surgical tissue.
Measurable disease at the primary tumor site or in lymph nodes.
No distant metastasis on FDG PET/CT.
Age 18 or older, with ECOG 0-2 or KPS 50 or higher.
Hypoxia negative, as stated in the arm descriptions.
not_for: Prior head and neck radiation therapy.
Simultaneous cancers outside the oropharynx (exceptions may be approved).
Prior systemic chemotherapy for this cancer.
Prior invasive cancer, other than non-melanoma skin cancer, without disease-free periods listed.
Severe active conditions, such as recent heart failure, heart attack, serious infection, or COPD flare needing hospital care.

NCT07136181.summary_en: NBM-BMX, a drug that blocks an enzyme called HDAC8, is being tested in people with metastatic uveal melanoma, an eye cancer that has spread to other parts of the body. Participants take NBM-BMX as a capsule by mouth twice daily on an empty stomach, and treatment may continue as long as the cancer does not get worse and side effects remain manageable. This is a Phase 1/Phase 2 study that aims to find the best dose and to learn about side effects, how the body processes the drug, and whether it may slow or shrink tumors.
NCT07136181.summary_es: NBM-BMX, un medicamento que bloquea una enzima llamada HDAC8, se está probando en personas con melanoma uveal metastásico, un cáncer del ojo que se ha extendido a otras partes del cuerpo. Los participantes toman NBM-BMX en forma de cápsula por vía oral dos veces al día, con el estómago vacío, y el tratamiento puede continuar mientras el cáncer no empeore y los efectos secundarios se puedan manejar. Este es un estudio de Fase 1/Fase 2 que busca encontrar la mejor dosis y conocer los efectos secundarios, cómo el cuerpo procesa el medicamento y si puede frenar o reducir los tumores.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older with metastatic uveal melanoma.
ECOG performance status 2 or lower.
Measurable disease by RECIST 1.1.
Histologic or cytologic confirmation of metastatic uveal melanoma.
If HLA-A*02:01-positive, prior tebentafusp is required unless unavailable or clinically inappropriate.
not_for: Pregnant or nursing women.
Prior HDAC inhibitor treatment.
Difficulty swallowing oral medications.
Current use of moderate or strong CYP2C8 inhibitors or inducers, or P-gp or BCRP inhibitors.
Positive hepatitis B or C test, unless viral levels are below the limit of detection.

NCT06428019.summary_en: This study tests venetoclax given with obinutuzumab or with acalabrutinib for adults with previously untreated chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL), a cancer of blood cells. Venetoclax is taken as a tablet by mouth; obinutuzumab is given as an intravenous infusion; acalabrutinib is taken as a tablet by mouth. Some arms use a 5-week venetoclax ramp-up, and the total study duration is about 28 months. The study measures safety, including side effects, and change in disease activity; the record lists the phase as Phase 3.
NCT06428019.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa venetoclax combinado con obinutuzumab o con acalabrutinib para adultos con leucemia linfocítica crónica (LLC) no tratada previamente, un cáncer de las células sanguíneas. El venetoclax se toma en tableta por vía oral; el obinutuzumab se administra como infusión intravenosa; el acalabrutinib se toma en tableta por vía oral. Algunos grupos usan un periodo de ajuste gradual de venetoclax de 5 semanas, y la duración total del estudio es de unos 28 meses. El estudio mide la seguridad, incluidos los efectos secundarios, y el cambio en la actividad de la enfermedad; el registro indica que es un estudio de Fase 3.
who_for: Adults aged 18 years or older.
Previously untreated chronic lymphocytic leukemia that needs treatment by 2018 iwCLL criteria.
Life expectancy greater than 6 months.
ECOG performance status of 2 or lower.
Creatinine clearance of 30 mL/min or higher by Cockcroft-Gault formula.
not_for: Active or uncontrolled infection.
Richter's transformation.
Active immune thrombocytopenia.

NCT04734730.summary_en: This Phase 2 study tests talazoparib with androgen deprivation therapy and abiraterone in men with castration-sensitive prostate cancer. Talazoparib, abiraterone acetate, and prednisone are taken by mouth once daily on days 1-28 of each 28-day cycle, and androgen deprivation therapy is given as injections (degarelix, leuprolide acetate) or goserelin under the skin, with bicalutamide taken by mouth in some arms. Cycles repeat every 28 days while the disease does not progress and side effects are acceptable, and the total length of treatment is not stated. The main outcome measure is not stated in the record; the study is labeled Phase 2.
NCT04734730.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 evalúa talazoparib con terapia de privación androgénica y abiraterona en hombres con cáncer de próstata sensible a la castración. Talazoparib, acetato de abiraterona y prednisona se toman por vía oral una vez al día en los días 1 a 28 de cada ciclo de 28 días, y la terapia de privación androgénica se administra mediante inyecciones (degarelix, acetato de leuprolida) o acetato de goserelina bajo la piel, con bicalutamida por vía oral en algunos grupos. Los ciclos se repiten cada 28 días mientras la enfermedad no progrese y los efectos secundarios sean aceptables, y la duración total del tratamiento no se indica. La medida de resultado principal no se indica en el registro; el estudio está clasificado como fase 2.
who_for: Prostate adenocarcinoma confirmed by biopsy or cytology
Metastatic disease (soft tissue and/or bone) before androgen treatment started
Karnofsky performance status of 60 to 100
Hormone therapy for metastatic disease started no more than 60 days before registration, with other prior hormone therapy limits
Adequate liver, kidney, and blood counts within 28 days before registration
not_for: Prior or planned ketoconazole, aminoglutethimide, or enzalutamide
Prior cytotoxic chemotherapy for metastatic prostate cancer
Known brain metastases
New York Heart Association class III or IV heart failure, or certain heart events within 6 months
Known HIV, active hepatitis B or C, or primary or secondary adrenal insufficiency

NCT05800665.summary_en: This study tests an investigational drug called RO7656594 in people with advanced or metastatic prostate cancer. The drug is taken by mouth on specified days in 28-day cycles, and the dose is raised in successive groups of participants until a study-specific threshold is reached. The study measures safety, tolerability, how the body processes the drug (pharmacokinetics), and preliminary activity; it is a Phase 1 study.
NCT05800665.summary_es: Este estudio prueba un medicamento en investigación llamado RO7656594 en personas con cáncer de próstata avanzado o metastásico. El medicamento se toma por vía oral en días específicos de ciclos de 28 días, y la dosis se aumenta en grupos sucesivos hasta alcanzar un umbral definido por el estudio. El estudio mide la seguridad, la tolerabilidad, cómo el cuerpo procesa el medicamento (farmacocinética) y la actividad preliminar; es un estudio de fase 1.
who_for: ECOG performance status of 1 or lower
Metastatic prostate adenocarcinoma without small-cell carcinoma or neuroendocrine features
Prior treatment with a second-generation androgen receptor-targeted therapy
Prior taxane treatment, or considered ineligible for or refused a taxane
If BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation is known: prior PARP inhibitor, or considered ineligible for one
not_for: Approved systemic anti-cancer therapy within 14 days or 5 half-lives (whichever is longer, up to 28 days) before first study treatment
Investigational agent within 28 days before first study treatment
Previous androgen receptor protein degrader treatment
Untreated central nervous system metastases or leptomeningeal disease

NCT06885034.summary_en: This study tests risvutatug rezetecan (also called Ris-Rez or GSK5764227) in adults with advanced gastrointestinal cancers that cannot be surgically removed and that were previously treated, with colorectal and pancreatic cancer cohorts listed. How it is given is not stated, and the dose and schedule are not stated. The record does not name a main outcome measure; it says the study will check how well the medicine works, how safe it is, and how the body handles it, and the study is Phase 1b/2.
NCT06885034.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa risvutatug rezetecan (también llamado Ris-Rez o GSK5764227) en adultos con cánceres gastrointestinales avanzados que no se pueden extirpar con cirugía y que ya recibieron tratamiento, e incluye cohortes de cáncer colorrectal y de páncreas. No se indica cómo se administra, ni la dosis ni la frecuencia. El registro no nombra un resultado principal; indica que el estudio verificará qué tan bien funciona el medicamento, qué tan seguro es y cómo lo maneja el cuerpo, y el estudio es de Fase 1b/2.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older, or the legal age of consent where the study takes place.
Unresectable, locally advanced or metastatic colon or rectal adenocarcinoma (colorectal cohort).
Unresectable, locally advanced or metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma (pancreatic cohort).
ECOG performance status of 0 or 1.
Willing to use adequate contraception and able to give informed consent.
not_for: Prior treatment with an antibody-drug conjugate that has a TOPO1-inhibitor payload.
Untreated brain or CNS metastases, or brain/CNS metastases that have progressed.
Current or past interstitial lung disease or non-infectious pneumonitis, or suspected pneumonitis that imaging cannot rule out.
Prior allogeneic or autologous bone marrow transplant or other solid organ transplant.
Pregnant or breastfeeding.

NCT06799065.summary_en: This Phase 1/2 study tests ATX-295, an oral drug that blocks a protein called KIF18A, alone and with bevacizumab (or a biosimilar), in adults with advanced or metastatic solid tumors, including ovarian cancer. ATX-295 is taken as tablets by mouth, and in the combination it is given with bevacizumab (or a biosimilar) by intravenous infusion, at various doses and schedules, with duration and frequency not stated. The main stated goal is to find a safe and tolerated dose, and the study also looks at how the drug moves through the body, its effects on the body, and early antitumor activity.
NCT06799065.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1/2 evalúa ATX-295, un medicamento oral que bloquea una proteína llamada KIF18A, solo y con bevacizumab (o un biosimilar), en adultos con tumores sólidos avanzados o metastásicos, incluido el cáncer de ovario. ATX-295 se toma en tabletas por vía oral, y en la combinación se administra con bevacizumab (o un biosimilar) por infusión intravenosa, en distintas dosis y esquemas, con la duración y frecuencia no indicadas. El objetivo principal indicado es encontrar una dosis segura y bien tolerada, y el estudio también observa cómo el medicamento se distribuye en el cuerpo, sus efectos en el organismo y la actividad antitumoral temprana.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older with locally recurrent or metastatic solid tumors, including high-grade serous ovarian cancer.
Disease that has returned or worsened after standard therapies with proven benefit, or no standard treatment is suitable.
Monotherapy ovarian cohort: high-grade serous ovarian cancer that is platinum-resistant or platinum-intolerant.
Monotherapy lung cohort: squamous non-small-cell lung cancer previously treated with a platinum, a taxane, and a checkpoint inhibitor.
Measurable disease (evaluable disease allowed during dose escalation) and ECOG performance status of 0 to 1.
not_for: Clinically unstable brain tumors or brain metastasis.
Any other concurrent anticancer treatment, except hormonal blockade.
Major surgery within 3 weeks before starting study treatment, or medical problems that limit oral intake or absorption.
Need for proton pump inhibitors or H2-receptor antagonists during dose escalation, or inability to stop strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors or inducers.
Active or uncontrolled cardiovascular disease, pregnancy, intent to breastfeed or conceive during treatment.

NCT04762199.summary_en: This Phase 1b study tests MRX-2843 given together with osimertinib in patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer that has an EGFR gene mutation. Both drugs are taken by mouth once daily on days 1 to 28, and each 28-day cycle repeats while the disease does not progress and side effects are acceptable. The study measures side effects and the best dose, and it is a Phase 1b safety and pharmacodynamic study.
NCT04762199.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1b evalúa MRX-2843 combinado con osimertinib en pacientes con cáncer de pulmón de células no pequeñas avanzado que tiene una mutación del gen EGFR. Ambos medicamentos se toman por vía oral una vez al día durante los días 1 a 28, y cada ciclo de 28 días se repite mientras la enfermedad no progrese y los efectos secundarios sean aceptables. El estudio mide los efectos secundarios y la mejor dosis, y es un estudio de fase 1b de seguridad y farmacodinámica.
who_for: Metastatic (spread) non-small cell lung cancer with an activating EGFR mutation.
ECOG performance status of 0 to 2.
Blood counts, liver and kidney tests within the limits stated.
Cohort rules: treatment-naive for one expansion cohort; progression on certain EGFR TKIs for another.
Able to swallow oral medication and sign written consent.
not_for: Chemotherapy or radiotherapy within 4 weeks (6 weeks for nitrosoureas or mitomycin C).
Symptomatic untreated brain metastases.
Known interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis.
QTc over 500 msec, cardiomyopathy, or LVEF under 50%.
Pregnancy or breastfeeding.

NCT07795749.summary_en: This Phase 2 study tests paclitaxel given into the abdomen together with systemic therapy in people with gastrointestinal cancers that have spread to the lining of the abdomen, called peritoneal carcinomatosis. Paclitaxel is given into the abdomen and through a vein, either every 2 weeks or every 3 weeks, and the length of treatment is not stated. The record does not state a primary outcome measure; the stated aim is to assess feasibility, and the study is Phase 2.
NCT07795749.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 evalúa paclitaxel administrado en la cavidad abdominal junto con terapia sistémica, en personas con cánceres gastrointestinales que se han diseminado al revestimiento del abdomen, llamado carcinomatosis peritoneal. El paclitaxel se administra dentro del abdomen y por vena, cada 2 semanas o cada 3 semanas; la duración del tratamiento no se indica. El registro no indica una medida de resultado principal; el objetivo indicado es evaluar la factibilidad, y el estudio es de fase 2.
who_for: Adenocarcinoma (cancer that starts in gland cells) of the digestive tract, confirmed by tissue or cell testing
Peritoneal carcinomatosis, shown by positive abdominal fluid cytology or by imaging, laparoscopy, or laparotomy
Age 18 or older with ECOG performance status 2 or less
Life expectancy greater than 3 months
Blood counts, liver, kidney, and albumin levels within the study limits
not_for: Bowel obstruction, except gastric outlet obstruction from the primary cancer
Uncontrolled illness, such as active infection, heart failure, or stroke or heart attack within 3 months
Another primary cancer within the last 3 years, with some skin and early-stage cancers excepted
Prior repeated intraperitoneal therapy (HIPEC, PIPAC, or NIPEC); a single HIPEC at surgery is not excluded
Pregnant or nursing

NCT03184038.summary_en: This study looks at brain function in patients with multiple brain metastases from solid tumors who are treated with stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) or stereotactic body radiation therapy (SBRT). SRS is given as one treatment on day 1, and SBRT is given in 3 fractions over days 1 to 7. The study measures neurocognitive function (thinking and brain-related abilities) at baseline, 4 months, and 12 months after treatment.
NCT03184038.summary_es: Este estudio analiza la función cerebral en pacientes con múltiples metástasis cerebrales de tumores sólidos que reciben radiocirugía estereotáxica (SRS) o radioterapia corporal estereotáxica (SBRT). La SRS se administra como un solo tratamiento el día 1, y la SBRT se administra en 3 fracciones durante los días 1 a 7. El estudio mide la función neurocognitiva (capacidades de pensamiento y funcionamiento relacionadas con el cerebro) al inicio, a los 4 meses y a los 12 meses después del tratamiento.
who_for: Pathologically proven solid tumor (except small cell lung cancer and germ cell tumor)
Karnofsky performance status of 60 or higher
1 to 10 brain metastases, with size limits on the largest lesions
Serum creatinine and creatinine clearance within stated limits
Able to complete neurocognitive testing, give written consent, and speak English
not_for: Glioma or other WHO grade II to IV primary brain tumor
Brain surgery within 14 days before enrollment
Planned chemotherapy during radiosurgery
Leptomeningeal metastases
Intractable seizures despite anticonvulsant therapy

NCT06545955.summary_en: This Phase 3 study tests intravesical nadofaragene firadenovec alone or followed by intravesical gemcitabine and docetaxel in people with high-grade, BCG-unresponsive non-muscle invasive bladder cancer with carcinoma in situ. The record says the pembrolizumab arm has closed, so the study now has two arms with 1:1 randomization. The drugs are given into the bladder, and the dose schedule and how often they are given are not stated. The main outcome measure is not stated in this record, and the study is Phase 3.
NCT06545955.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 3 evalúa nadofaragene firadenovec intravesical solo o seguido de gemcitabina y docetaxel intravesicales en personas con cáncer de vejiga no músculo-invasivo de alto grado, resistente a BCG, con carcinoma in situ. El registro indica que el brazo de pembrolizumab se cerró, por lo que el estudio ahora tiene dos brazos con aleatorización 1:1. Los medicamentos se administran dentro de la vejiga, y el esquema de dosis y la frecuencia no están indicados. La medida de resultado principal no se indica en este registro, y el estudio es de fase 3.
who_for: Carcinoma in situ, with or without high-grade Ta/T1 bladder cancer.
Bladder cancer that did not respond to, or came back after, at least 2 courses of BCG within 12 months.
ECOG performance status of 2 or lower, and age 18 or older.
Life expectancy longer than 2 years, in the investigator's opinion.
Participants who choose not to have a cystectomy.
not_for: Muscle-invasive or metastatic disease shown at screening.
Upper tract urothelial carcinoma or urothelial carcinoma in the prostatic urethra.
Prior treatment with nadofaragene firadenovec at any time.
Prior systemic therapy for bladder cancer, or prior intravesical chemotherapy for BCG-unresponsive disease.
Pelvic external beam radiotherapy within 2 years, or investigational drug use within 1 month before screening.

NCT06411821.summary_en: This Phase 2 study tests ulixertinib in people with histiocytic neoplasms. Patients start ulixertinib at 300 mg twice daily, given in 28-day cycles; the total length of treatment is not stated. The main outcome measure is not stated, but the study aims to find out whether ulixertinib is effective and safe.
NCT06411821.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 evalúa ulixertinib en personas con neoplasias histiocíticas. Los pacientes comienzan con ulixertinib a 300 mg dos veces al día, en ciclos de 28 días; la duración total del tratamiento no se indica. La medida de resultado principal no se indica, pero el estudio busca saber si ulixertinib es eficaz y seguro.
who_for: Histiocytic neoplasm confirmed by pathology, with supporting radiologic or molecular findings
Mutation in a MAPK pathway gene for the primary group; not required for the exploratory group
Disease that can be measured on imaging, confirmed by a radiologist
Age 12 or older, with age limits that change after the interim analysis
Disease that is recurrent, refractory, or persistent after prior treatment, or multisystem disease, or single-system disease causing organ problems
not_for: Uncontrolled or severe other medical condition
Histiocytic neoplasm treatment within 28 days or 5 half-lives before the first dose
Disease that is meant for observation only or first-line local therapy
Pregnant or breastfeeding
Inability to swallow tablets, a feeding tube, or prior stomach or duodenal surgery that may affect absorption

NCT05528133.summary_en: This study tests genomically guided radiation therapy, which personalizes the radiation dose using a genomic score, in people with triple negative breast cancer who have had breast-conserving surgery. Radiation is given once daily, 5 days per week, with a total dose of 50 Gy in 25 fractions or 42.56 Gy in 16 fractions, with or without a 10 Gy boost in 5 fractions to the cavity. The study's purpose is to determine whether this approach is feasible, and it is a Phase II study.
NCT05528133.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa la radioterapia guiada por genómica, que personaliza la dosis de radiación usando una puntuación genómica, en personas con cáncer de mama triple negativo que se han sometido a cirugía conservadora de mama. La radiación se administra una vez al día, 5 días por semana, con una dosis total de 50 Gy en 25 fracciones o de 42.56 Gy en 16 fracciones, con o sin un refuerzo de 10 Gy en 5 fracciones en la cavidad. El objetivo del estudio es determinar si este enfoque es factible, y es un estudio de Fase II.
who_for: Had breast-conserving surgery (lumpectomy) with axillary evaluation by sentinel node biopsy or axillary dissection
Triple negative breast cancer confirmed by tissue biopsy
Enough tissue available to calculate the RSI score
Age 18 or older, life expectancy over 16 weeks, and KPS 70 or higher
not_for: Metastatic breast cancer
Pregnant or breastfeeding
Positive surgical margins
Allergy or hypersensitivity to any study drug or component
Major surgery or significant traumatic injury not recovered from within 14 days

NCT07214987.summary_en: This study tests toripalimab given with cisplatin and docetaxel (called PDT) as induction therapy for locally advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma in patients who are CPS-positive. The medicines are given by intravenous infusion once every 21 days, for up to 3 cycles. The study is a Phase 2 trial that measures safety and tolerability.
NCT07214987.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa toripalimab junto con cisplatino y docetaxel (llamado PDT) como terapia de inducción para el carcinoma de células escamosas de cabeza y cuello localmente avanzado en pacientes con CPS positivo. Los medicamentos se administran por infusión intravenosa una vez cada 21 días, hasta 3 ciclos. El estudio es de Fase 2 y mide la seguridad y la tolerabilidad.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older.
New diagnosis of confirmed squamous cell carcinoma of listed head and neck sites.
Stage III or non-metastatic stage IV disease (stage II or III for HPV-associated oropharynx).
Investigator judges the person a candidate for induction systemic therapy.
ECOG performance status of 1 or less and life expectancy over 12 weeks.
not_for: Proven distant metastases below the clavicle.
Diagnosis of EBV-associated nasopharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma.
Prior head or neck radiotherapy that prevents curative-intent radiation.
Pre-existing peripheral neuropathy grade 2 or higher.
Active second malignancy as defined by the investigator, or pregnancy or breastfeeding.
cancer_types: head and neck squamous cell carcinoma

NCT06907043.summary_en: This Phase 1/2 study tests EIK1004 (IMP1707), a PARP1 selective inhibitor, in people with advanced solid tumors, including breast, ovarian, prostate, and pancreatic cancer with certain changes in homologous recombination repair genes. The study drug is taken by mouth as tablets once daily, except for a single-dose period, with doses increasing until progressive disease or the participant stops; the total length of treatment is not stated beyond that. The study measures safety and tolerability and also evaluates preliminary activity, and the main outcome measure is not stated.
NCT06907043.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1/2 evalúa EIK1004 (IMP1707), un inhibidor selectivo de PARP1, en personas con tumores sólidos avanzados, incluidos cáncer de mama, de ovario, de próstata y de páncreas con ciertos cambios en genes de reparación por recombinación homóloga. El medicamento del estudio se toma por vía oral en forma de tabletas una vez al día, excepto durante un período de dosis única, y las dosis aumentan hasta que la enfermedad progrese o el participante deje el tratamiento; la duración total del tratamiento no se indica más allá de eso. El estudio mide la seguridad y la tolerabilidad y también evalúa la actividad preliminar, y la medida de resultado principal no se indica.
who_for: Adults aged 18 to 89 years with advanced solid tumors.
Breast cancer, HER2-negative, after prior chemotherapy; hormonal therapy first if hormone receptor-positive.
Ovarian, fallopian tube or peritoneal cancer after at least one prior platinum-based chemotherapy for advanced disease.
Metastatic castrate-resistant prostate cancer on ongoing hormone suppression therapy, with up to one prior taxane line.
ECOG performance status of 0 or 1, life expectancy of at least 12 weeks, and known deleterious or suspected deleterious HRR gene mutations.
not_for: Prior use of a PARP1 selective inhibitor.
Investigational or approved anti-cancer therapy within 28 days before the first dose.
Mean resting QTcF above 470 ms or below 340 ms.
Active hepatitis B or C infection.
Untreated brain lesions larger than 2.0 cm, symptomatic leptomeningeal disease, or poorly controlled seizures.

NCT07270978.summary_en: This study tests CD33 FPBMC, which are fresh immune cells armed with an anti-CD3 x anti-CD33 bispecific antibody, in adults with acute myeloid leukemia or myelodysplastic syndrome who still have measurable residual disease. Participants receive 4 weekly intravenous infusions, followed by 4-6 weeks of a hypomethylating agent with or without venetoclax, and one such cycle may be repeated up to 4 times. The record does not list a primary outcome measure; it describes the study as a Phase 1 study to understand safety and estimate efficacy.
NCT07270978.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa las CD33 FPBMC, que son células mononucleares de sangre periférica frescas armadas con un anticuerpo biespecífico anti-CD3 x anti-CD33, en adultos con leucemia mieloide aguda o síndrome mielodisplásico que aún tienen enfermedad residual medible. Los participantes reciben 4 infusiones intravenosas semanales, seguidas de 4 a 6 semanas de un agente hipometilante con o sin venetoclax, y este ciclo puede repetirse hasta 4 veces. El registro no indica una medida de resultado principal; describe el estudio como una fase 1 para conocer la seguridad y estimar la eficacia.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older.
Newly diagnosed or relapsed/refractory AML after intensive chemotherapy or at least 2 cycles of non-intensive treatment.
Relapsed/refractory MDS or MDS/MPN overlap after specified prior hypomethylating agent treatment.
Persistent or recurrent measurable residual disease with residual blasts that are CD33 positive.
LVEF at least 45% at rest and performance status of 2 or less.
not_for: Prior anti-CD33 therapy.
Pregnancy or breastfeeding.
Blasts of 25% or more.
Significant liver, kidney or immune dysfunction, or uncontrolled serious infection, as defined in the criteria.
Known HIV with detectable viral load, hepatitis B surface antigen positive, or known or suspected active hepatitis C.

NCT06176989.summary_en: The study tests enasidenib, a drug that targets the IDH2 gene mutation, in rare cancers of the nasal cavity or skull base that have an IDH2 mutation. Enasidenib is taken by mouth once a day, every day, in 28-day cycles with no rest between cycles. Participants may stay in the study as long as the drug is helping them. The main outcome is not stated in the record; this is a Phase 2 study.
NCT06176989.summary_es: El estudio prueba enasidenib, un medicamento dirigido a la mutación del gen IDH2, en cánceres raros de la cavidad nasal o de la base del cráneo que tienen una mutación de IDH2. El enasidenib se toma por vía oral una vez al día, todos los días, en ciclos de 28 días sin periodos de descanso entre ciclos. Los participantes pueden permanecer en el estudio mientras el medicamento les esté ayudando. El desenlace principal no se indica en el registro; este es un estudio de Fase 2.
who_for: Adults 18 years and older.
Locally advanced or metastatic chondrosarcoma, sinonasal adenocarcinoma, large-cell neuroendocrine carcinoma, olfactory neuroblastoma, or sinonasal undifferenti
Tumor has an IDH2 mutation, R140 or R172, with a primary tumor in the sinonasal cavity or skull base.
Measurable disease per RECIST 1.1 criteria.
ECOG performance status 0-2 and adequate blood, liver and kidney function.
not_for: Prior treatment with an IDH1 or IDH2 inhibitor.
Systemic anticancer treatment within 3 weeks before the first dose.
New or progressive brain metastases or leptomeningeal disease.
Clinically significant heart disease, or QTc above 450 msec.
Pregnancy.

NCT06930352.summary_en: This phase 2 trial tests ziftomenib in adults with NPM1-mutated or KMT2A-rearranged acute myeloid leukemia (AML) who are not eligible for standard frontline therapy. Ziftomenib is taken by mouth once daily on days 1 to 28 of each 28-day cycle, for up to 24 cycles if the disease does not progress and side effects are acceptable. The record does not state the main outcome measure; it is a phase 2 study.
NCT06930352.summary_es: Este ensayo de fase 2 evalúa ziftomenib en adultos con leucemia mieloide aguda (LMA) con mutación en NPM1 o reordenamiento de KMT2A que no son elegibles para la terapia estándar de primera línea. Ziftomenib se toma por vía oral una vez al día, en los días 1 a 28 de cada ciclo de 28 días, hasta 24 ciclos si la enfermedad no progresa y los efectos secundarios son aceptables. El registro no indica la medida de resultado principal; es un estudio de fase 2.
who_for: Newly diagnosed AML with a KMT2A rearrangement or NPM1 mutation, or other menin-sensitive mutations.
Not eligible for, or unwilling to receive, standard induction therapy.
Age 75 or older with adequate kidney and liver function, or age 18 to 74 with at least one listed comorbidity.
White blood cell count of 10,000/uL or lower; hydroxyurea, cytarabine, or leukapheresis may be used to control it.
Agrees to use effective contraception during the study.
not_for: Acute promyelocytic leukemia or chronic myelogenous leukemia in blast crisis.
Clinically active leukemia in the central nervous system.
Prior AML treatment, except hydroxyurea or cytarabine used to control white cell count.
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or inducers, with some exceptions; uncontrolled infection; QTcF over 480 ms.
Pregnant or breastfeeding; required dual antiplatelet therapy; condition that prevents informed consent.

NCT07006506.summary_en: This study tests belumosudil, an oral selective inhibitor of ROCK2, to help prevent graft-versus-host disease in people with blood cancer who have had a stem cell transplant. The drug is taken by mouth (oral), and the dose, how often it is taken, and how long it is given are not stated. This is a Phase II study; its main outcome is not stated, but it aims to find out whether adding belumosudil may be an effective prevention approach and to look at safety.
NCT07006506.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa belumosudil, un inhibidor selectivo de ROCK2 que se toma por vía oral, para ayudar a prevenir la enfermedad de injerto contra huésped en personas con cáncer de la sangre que recibieron un trasplante de células madre. El medicamento se toma por vía oral; la dosis, la frecuencia y la duración del tratamiento no se indican. Es un estudio de fase II; el resultado principal no se indica, pero busca saber si agregar belumosudil puede ser un enfoque eficaz para prevenir la enfermedad de injerto contra huésped y evaluar su seguridad.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older with a blood cancer in morphologic remission.
Received a stem cell transplant from a 7-8/8 matched related or unrelated donor, or a haploidentical donor.
Stem cell graft taken from peripheral blood.
Transplant timing limits apply at consent and before starting belumosudil.
Karnofsky score at least 70%, with adequate liver and kidney function tests.
not_for: Received a CD34+ selected or engineered stem cell graft.
Received in vivo T cell depletion, such as anti-thymocyte globulin.
Uncontrolled heart conditions, heart failure, or heart attack within the past 6 months.
Active secondary cancer, or prior cancer needing systemic therapy within 5 years (with listed exceptions).
Active GVHD needing systemic therapy, prior belumosudil use, or allergy to belumosudil or other ROCK2 inhibitors.

NCT06059391.summary_en: This Phase 2 study tests the CMV-MVA Triplex vaccine given to HLA-matched related stem cell donors, to help prevent cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection in patients receiving a stem cell transplant for blood cancers. Donors receive the vaccine or a placebo as an injection into the muscle on day 0, then G-CSF stem cell mobilization on days 5 to 9 and apheresis on days 10 to 14, and recipients are transplanted within 9 weeks of donor vaccination. The record does not state a primary outcome measure; the study is randomized and placebo-controlled, and its stated aim is to see whether it helps prevent CMV infection.
NCT06059391.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 evalúa la vacuna CMV-MVA Triplex administrada a donantes de células madre emparentados con HLA compatible, para ayudar a prevenir la infección por citomegalovirus (CMV) en pacientes que reciben un trasplante de células madre por cánceres de la sangre. Los donantes reciben la vacuna o un placebo como inyección en el músculo el día 0, luego movilización de células madre con G-CSF los días 5 a 9 y aféresis los días 10 a 14; los receptores son trasplantados dentro de las 9 semanas posteriores a la vacunación del donante. El registro no indica una medida de resultado principal; el estudio es aleatorizado y controlado con placebo, y su objetivo declarado es determinar si ayuda a prevenir la infección por CMV.
who_for: Adult donors aged 18 or older who can give informed consent.
Adult recipients aged 18 or older with a planned transplant from a related donor.
Recipients with a blood cancer such as leukemia, lymphoma, myelodysplastic syndrome, or myelofibrosis.
Recipients who are CMV seropositive.
Recipients with an 8/8 HLA-matched related donor and Karnofsky score of 70 or more or ECOG of 2 or less.
not_for: Donors with a prior transplant, or chemotherapy, radiation, or immunotherapy within 21 days before protocol therapy.
Donors who received another vaccine within 30 days before or after the study vaccine.
Donors who are HIV, hepatitis B or C, or HTLV positive.
Recipients with multiple myeloma or a prior allogeneic transplant.
Recipients with autoimmune disease, a prior investigational CMV vaccine, or recent anti-CMV antiviral treatment.

NCT06561048.summary_en: This study compares soquelitinib, an ITK inhibitor, with standard treatment chosen by the physician (pralatrexate or belinostat) in adults with relapsed or refractory peripheral T-cell lymphoma not otherwise specified, follicular helper T-cell lymphoma, or systemic anaplastic large-cell lymphoma. Soquelitinib 200 mg is taken by mouth twice a day, and standard treatment is given for up to 2 years. The main outcome is not stated; this is a Phase 3 study.
NCT06561048.summary_es: Este estudio compara soquelitinib, un inhibidor de ITK, con el tratamiento estándar elegido por el médico (pralatrexato o belinostat) en adultos con linfoma periférico de células T no especificado de otra manera, linfoma de células T folicular auxiliar o linfoma anaplásico sistémico de células grandes en recaída o refractario. Soquelitinib de 200 mg se toma por vía oral dos veces al día, y el tratamiento estándar se administra por hasta 2 años. El resultado principal no se indica; este es un estudio de Fase 3.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older.
ECOG performance status of 0 to 2.
Confirmed PTCL-NOS, follicular helper T-cell lymphoma, or systemic anaplastic large-cell lymphoma.
Progressed on, refractory to, relapsed on, or intolerant to prior therapy; 1 to 3 prior systemic therapies.
FDG-avid disease on PET and measurable disease of at least 1.5 cm on CT.
not_for: T-cell lymphoma with active central nervous system involvement.
Prior administration of an ITK inhibitor.
Known HIV, positive hepatitis B surface antigen, or positive hepatitis C antibody test.
History of allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation.
Pregnant or breastfeeding women, or those intending to become pregnant during the study.
cancer_types: peripheral t-cell lymphoma, not otherwise specified
nodal peripheral t-cell lymphoma with tfh phenotype

NCT07703878.summary_en: This phase 1 study tests the drug GS-1206 in adults with solid tumors. GS-1206 is taken by mouth once a day for up to 35 cycles, and one group receives escalating doses; cycle length is not stated. The study aims to learn about safety, tolerability, and antitumor activity, and the main outcome measure is not stated.
NCT07703878.summary_es: El estudio evalúa el medicamento GS-1206 en adultos con tumores sólidos. Se toma por vía oral una vez al día, hasta 35 ciclos, y un grupo recibe dosis crecientes; la duración de cada ciclo no se indica. El estudio de fase 1 busca conocer la seguridad, la tolerabilidad y la actividad antitumoral, y la medida de resultado principal no se indica.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older.
Tumor has a protocol-specified mutation confirmed by a locally approved test.
Part A: advanced or metastatic solid tumor that progressed after treatment known to confer clinical benefit, unless the person refused, could not tolerate, or i
Part B: enrollment in protocol-specified tumor types.
not_for: Investigational drugs within 28 days before Cycle 1 Day 1.
Anticancer biologic therapy or immunotherapy within 28 days before Cycle 1 Day 1.
Anticancer chemotherapy or targeted small molecule therapy within 21 days before Cycle 1 Day 1 (42 days for nitrosoureas or mitomycin).
Major surgery within 28 days before Cycle 1 Day 1.
Radiation therapy within 21 days before Cycle 1 Day 1, with limited palliation exceptions.

NCT06043817.summary_en: This study tests STX-721/PFL-721 in adults with non-small cell lung cancer that has an EGFR or HER2 exon 20 insertion mutation. The route of administration, and how often and how long it is given, are not stated; doses are escalated in some parts, and some parts give it with platinum-based chemotherapy. The study measures safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetic exposure, and preliminary antitumor activity, and it is a Phase 1/2 study.
NCT06043817.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa STX-721/PFL-721 en adultos con cáncer de pulmón de células no pequeñas que tiene una mutación de inserción en el exón 20 de EGFR o HER2. La vía de administración, y con qué frecuencia y durante cuánto tiempo se administra, no se indica; en algunas partes del estudio las dosis se aumentan y en otras se combina con quimioterapia basada en platino. El estudio mide la seguridad, la tolerabilidad, la exposición farmacocinética y la actividad antitumoral preliminar, y es un estudio de Fase 1/2.
who_for: Stage IIIB/C or IV non-small cell lung cancer not eligible for curative surgery or chemoradiation
Tumor has an EGFR or HER2 exon 20 insertion mutation confirmed by a qualified local lab
Prior treatment limits: Part 1 requires all approved therapies or ineligibility; Parts 2 and 3 require 1 to 2 prior lines, one platinum-based unless contraindic
Documented tumor progression on imaging with at least one measurable lesion
Age 18 or older with ECOG performance status 0 or 1
not_for: Tumor known to have the EGFR exon 20 insertion H773_V774insH variant
EGFR kinase activating mutation together with T790M and/or C797S resistance mutation
Another cancer, different from lung cancer, diagnosed within 2 years before screening
Symptomatic brain or spinal metastases
Unresolved toxicities from prior cancer therapy above grade 1, except alopecia and peripheral neuropathy

NCT06095089.summary_en: This Phase 1 study tests JNJ-87189401 combined with JNJ-78278343 in adults with advanced prostate cancer. The record does not state how the drugs are given or how often; doses are increased in steps across the study parts. The study measures the recommended regimen for later Phase 2 testing and the safety of the combination.
NCT06095089.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1 evalúa JNJ-87189401 combinado con JNJ-78278343 en adultos con cáncer de próstata avanzado. El registro no indica cómo se administran los medicamentos ni con qué frecuencia; las dosis aumentan por pasos en las distintas partes del estudio. El estudio mide el régimen recomendado para una fase 2 posterior y la seguridad de la combinación.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older.
Histologically confirmed adenocarcinoma of the prostate.
Measurable or evaluable disease per PCWG3 criteria.
Prior orchiectomy or ongoing GnRH analog therapy, for certain study parts.
ECOG performance status of 0 or 1.
not_for: Small cell, carcinoid, mixed, or large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma.
Autoimmune disease in the 12 months before consent.
Heart attack, severe or unstable angina, or serious ventricular arrhythmia within 6 months before consent.
Heart failure (NYHA class II to IV) within 6 months before consent.
Transient ischemic attack or stroke within 6 months before consent.

NCT07301268.summary_en: This Phase 2 study tests GI-102 alone or with pembrolizumab before surgery in adults with recurrent or progressive IDH wildtype glioblastoma or IDH mutated grade 4 astrocytoma. GI-102 is given by IV infusion over 30 to 120 minutes on day 1 of cycle 1, and surgery is done 14 days later. Pembrolizumab IV may be added in some arms, and cycles repeat every 21 days, with GI-102 given for up to 2 years. The main outcome measure is not stated in the record.
NCT07301268.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 evalúa GI-102 solo o con pembrolizumab antes de la cirugía en adultos con glioblastoma IDH silvestre o astrocitoma IDH mutado de grado 4, recurrente o progresivo. GI-102 se administra por infusión intravenosa durante 30 a 120 minutos el día 1 del ciclo 1, y la cirugía se realiza 14 días después. En algunos brazos se puede agregar pembrolizumab intravenoso, los ciclos se repiten cada 21 días y GI-102 se puede administrar hasta por 2 años. El registro no indica la medida de resultado principal.
who_for: Age 18 or older
Tissue-confirmed progressive or recurrent IDH wildtype grade IV glioblastoma (including gliosarcoma) or IDH mutated grade 4 astrocytoma
Candidate for surgical resection
ECOG performance status 0, 1, or 2 and KPS 60 or higher
Willing to give blood and tissue samples for research
not_for: Pregnant or nursing, or of childbearing potential and not using contraception
Life-threatening raised intracranial pressure needing immediate surgery
Bevacizumab or chemotherapy within 30 days before registration
Hypersensitivity to pembrolizumab, IL-2, GI-102, or its excipients
Active hepatitis B and hepatitis C together, active tuberculosis, or prior pneumonitis or interstitial lung disease needing steroids

NCT07732634.summary_en: This study tests RiMO-301 given with hypofractionated radiation and pembrolizumab before surgery, for resectable, locally advanced head and neck cancer. RiMO-301 is injected into the tumor once on Day 0, followed by radiation of 5 fractions of 4-5 Gray over 5-15 days. Pembrolizumab 200 mg is given every 3 weeks for 2 cycles before surgery. The main outcome is major pathologic response; this is a phase 2 study.
NCT07732634.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa RiMO-301 administrado con radioterapia hipofraccionada y pembrolizumab antes de la cirugía, para cáncer de cabeza y cuello resecable y localmente avanzado. RiMO-301 se inyecta en el tumor una vez el Día 0, seguido de radioterapia de 5 fracciones de 4-5 Gray durante 5-15 días. Pembrolizumab 200 mg se administra cada 3 semanas durante 2 ciclos antes de la cirugía. El resultado principal es la respuesta patológica mayor; es un estudio de fase 2.
who_for: Head and neck cancer that needs surgery to remove it.
At least one tumor that can be reached for injection and can receive radiation.
Tumor measurable on cross-sectional imaging.
Recovered from acute side effects of prior cancer treatment to grade 1 or less.
Adequate blood counts and liver function, ECOG 0-2, and life expectancy of at least 12 weeks.
not_for: HPV-associated head and neck cancer.
Nasopharyngeal head and neck cancer.
Symptomatic brain metastases or carcinomatous meningitis.
Anti-cancer treatment other than PD-1 inhibitors within 4 weeks before injection.
Active autoimmune disease needing systemic treatment in the past 2 years.

NCT05753748.summary_en: This trial compares endoscopic surveillance with endoscopic eradication therapy in people with Barrett's esophagus and low-grade dysplasia, a condition that can be linked to esophageal adenocarcinoma. Eradication therapy uses radiofrequency ablation through an endoscope every 2 to 3 months until intestinal metaplasia is gone or up to 5 treatments are given, followed by surveillance endoscopy every 6 months for the first year and then yearly. The record does not state the main outcome measure, and the study phase is listed as NA.
NCT05753748.summary_es: Este ensayo compara la vigilancia endoscópica con la terapia endoscópica de erradicación en personas con esófago de Barrett y displasia de bajo grado, una afección que puede estar relacionada con el adenocarcinoma de esófago. La terapia de erradicación usa ablación por radiofrecuencia a través de un endoscopio cada 2 a 3 meses, hasta que desaparezca la metaplasia intestinal o se completen hasta 5 tratamientos, seguida de endoscopias de vigilancia cada 6 meses durante el primer año y luego cada año. El registro no indica cuál es el resultado principal que se mide, y la fase del estudio aparece como NA.
who_for: Age 18 to 89 years
Barrett's esophagus with low-grade dysplasia confirmed by a central pathology panel within the previous 12 months
Able to tolerate proton pump inhibitor or potassium-competitive acid blocker therapy, by self-report
Able to stop antiplatelet and anticoagulant medicines as guidelines advise around procedures
not_for: Pregnancy
Prior endoscopic eradication therapy for Barrett's esophagus
History of high-grade dysplasia or esophageal adenocarcinoma, or prior esophagectomy
Active erosive esophagitis (Los Angeles Grade B or higher), until it resolves
Esophageal varices, known portal hypertension, or life expectancy under 2 years

NCT04174352.summary_en: This early-phase study tests different doses of tamoxifen in patients with metastatic ER-positive breast cancer that has an ESR1 gene mutation. Tamoxifen is taken by mouth once daily at one of four dose levels (20, 80, 160, or 200 mg), with three participants per level, and is started within 14 days of a FES PET/CT scan and continued until progression or drug intolerance. The study uses FES PET/CT imaging to measure estrogen receptor blockade and find the optimal tamoxifen dose; the record does not state a separate primary outcome measure.
NCT04174352.summary_es: Este estudio en fase temprana prueba diferentes dosis de tamoxifeno en pacientes con cáncer de mama metastásico positivo para receptores de estrógeno que tienen una mutación en el gen ESR1. El tamoxifeno se toma por vía oral una vez al día en uno de cuatro niveles de dosis (20, 80, 160 o 200 mg), con tres participantes por nivel, y se inicia dentro de los 14 días posteriores a una tomografía FES PET/CT y se continúa hasta la progresión o la intolerancia al medicamento. El estudio usa la imagen FES PET/CT para medir el bloqueo de los receptores de estrógeno y encontrar la dosis óptima de tamoxifeno; el registro no indica una medida de resultado principal por separado.
who_for: Metastatic or unresectable breast cancer that is ER-positive (10% or more) and HER2 negative.
ESR1 mutation found by a CLIA-certified test on tumor biopsy tissue or circulating free DNA.
Measurable disease per RECIST 1.1, or evaluable bone disease with a lesion of at least 10 mm.
Prior endocrine therapy in the metastatic setting, or progression within 12 months of adjuvant endocrine therapy.
ECOG performance status 0-1, life expectancy over 12 weeks, and ability to take oral medications.
not_for: Liver-only disease.
Tamoxifen, fulvestrant, or other ER-blocking therapy within 60 days before FES PET/CT.
Peripheral neuropathy above grade 1, or significant eye or retinal disorders above grade 1.
History of venous thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, or stroke.
QTcF of 470 msec or higher, or use of strong CYP2D6, CYP3A4, or CYP2C9 inhibitors or inducers.

NCT07637578.summary_en: This Phase II study tests elranatamab given in an outpatient setting, with a single dose of tocilizumab, in adults with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma. Elranatamab is given under the skin in step-up doses on Day 1 and Day 4, then 76 mg on Days 8, 15 and 22 of Cycle 1, every other week in Cycles 2 and 3, and once per cycle in Cycles 4 to 12, for up to 12 cycles of 28 days each. The main outcome is the overall incidence of cytokine release syndrome during Cycle 1.
NCT07637578.summary_es: Este estudio de fase II evalúa elranatamab administrado en un entorno ambulatorio, junto con una dosis única de tocilizumab, en adultos con mieloma múltiple recidivante o refractario. El elranatamab se aplica debajo de la piel en dosis de inicio gradual el Día 1 y el Día 4, luego 76 mg los Días 8, 15 y 22 del Ciclo 1, cada dos semanas en los Ciclos 2 y 3, y una vez por ciclo en los Ciclos 4 a 12, hasta 12 ciclos de 28 días cada uno. El resultado principal es la incidencia global de síndrome de liberación de citocinas durante el Ciclo 1.
who_for: Diagnosed with multiple myeloma that has come back or did not respond to treatment.
Has had at least one prior line of therapy that included lenalidomide and an anti-CD38 antibody.
Has measurable disease at screening.
Able to do most daily activities (performance status 0 or 1).
At least 18 years old and willing to take antiviral and pneumonia prevention medicines.
not_for: Past grade 3 or higher cytokine release syndrome or immune effector neurotoxicity (ICANS).
Active central nervous system myeloma involvement.
Fever or active infection at the time of enrollment.
Hepatitis B infection or active hepatitis C infection.
Certain heart problems, or heart attack, stroke or similar event within 6 months.

NCT05996185.summary_en: This single-arm Phase II study tests mogamulizumab added to standard chemotherapy (DA-EPOCH or CHOEP) in adults with aggressive T-cell lymphoma, including adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma (ATLL). Mogamulizumab is given as a 1.0 mg/kg IV infusion over at least 1 hour on Days 1, 8, and 15 of Cycle 1 and on Day 1 of later cycles, in 21-day cycles, with six cycles planned. The record does not state a main outcome measure; the study is Phase II.
NCT05996185.summary_es: Este estudio de fase II, de un solo grupo, evalúa mogamulizumab añadido a la quimioterapia estándar (DA-EPOCH o CHOEP) en adultos con linfoma de células T agresivo, incluida la leucemia/linfoma de células T del adulto (ATLL). El mogamulizumab se administra como infusión intravenosa de 1,0 mg/kg durante al menos 1 hora los días 1, 8 y 15 del ciclo 1, y el día 1 de los ciclos siguientes, en ciclos de 21 días, con seis ciclos planificados. El registro no indica una medida de resultado principal; el estudio es de fase II.
who_for: Adults 18 or older with histologically confirmed T-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma.
ECOG performance status 0-2, unless lymphoma compromises it and chemotherapy benefit is expected.
Prior treatment with one cycle of CHOP, CHOEP or EPOCH is allowed if needed to control disease.
For peripheral T-cell lymphoma, at least one measurable lesion of 1.5 cm or larger.
Adequate organ and bone marrow function within 10 days before the first dose.
not_for: Systemic anticancer or investigational therapy within 3 weeks before the first dose.
Radiotherapy or skin-directed treatment within 2 weeks before study treatment.
Pregnancy, breastfeeding, or a live vaccine within 30 days before the first dose.
Active uncontrolled infection, active myocarditis, or NYHA class III-IV heart failure.
Known active brain metastases or carcinomatous meningitis, or another untreated malignancy in the past 2 years (some exceptions listed).

NCT06563375.summary_en: This Phase 1 study tests NP-101 in adults with solid tumors. NP-101 is given by mouth, and how long or how often is not stated. The study measures safety and preliminary effectiveness.
NCT06563375.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1 evalúa NP-101 en adultos con tumores sólidos. NP-101 se administra por vía oral, y el registro no indica cuánto tiempo ni con qué frecuencia. El estudio mide la seguridad y la eficacia preliminar.
who_for: Adults 18 or older with advanced or metastatic solid tumor that returned or worsened after standard treatment, or with no standard treatment available.
Measurable disease per RECIST v1.1 for dose expansion; evaluable or measurable disease for dose escalation.
ECOG performance status of 0 or 1 and life expectancy of at least 3 months.
Adequate blood, liver, kidney, and heart function, and willing to give consent.
Willing to undergo required tumor biopsy and blood collections.
not_for: Allergic reaction to compounds similar to the study drug.
Unresolved toxicities from prior therapy above the stated grade limits.
Currently receiving other investigational agents.
Unable to swallow and keep down oral medication, or GI disease affecting absorption.
Brain or leptomeningeal metastases, or pregnancy or breastfeeding.

NCT03860883.summary_en: This study compares two safety margins of surgical removal, 1 cm and 2 cm, for stage II primary cutaneous melanoma.
