NCT04585750.summary_es: El estudio evalúa rezatapopt (PC14586), un medicamento oral que reactiva p53, solo o con pembrolizumab, en tumores sólidos avanzados con la mutación TP53 Y220C. El rezatapopt se toma por vía oral una vez al día, con dosis que aumentan por etapas en la Fase 1 y con 2000 mg diarios con alimentos en las cohortes de expansión, y el pembrolizumab 200 mg por vía intravenosa se administra cada 3 semanas en los brazos de combinación; la duración del tratamiento no se indica. El registro no indica una medida principal de resultado; describe la evaluación de seguridad, tolerabilidad, farmacocinética y eficacia, y el estudio es de Fase 1/2.
who_for: Locally advanced or metastatic solid tumor with a TP53 Y220C mutation
ECOG performance status of 0 or 1
Previously treated with one or more lines of anticancer therapy and progressive disease
Age 18 or older, or 12 to 17 with Safety Review Committee approval
Combination part: anti-PD-1/PD-L1 naive or progressed on that treatment, with measurable disease
not_for: Known KRAS single nucleotide variant (monotherapy phase; ovarian cancer exception)
Brain metastases unless neurologically stable and not needing steroids
Active, uncontrolled hepatitis B, hepatitis C, or HIV infection
Recent stroke, heart attack, or other heart conditions within stated time windows
Known active malignancy, other than treated cervical intraepithelial neoplasia or non-melanoma skin cancer

NCT07516925.summary_en: This Phase 2 study tests ivonescimab in people with advanced or unresectable leiomyosarcoma who have had previous treatment. Ivonescimab is given intravenously (IV) every 3 weeks on Day 1 of each cycle, for up to 24 months in total. The main outcome measure is not stated; the record says the study aims to learn whether the treatment is effective and safe, with few or mild side effects.
NCT07516925.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 evalúa ivonescimab en personas con leiomiosarcoma avanzado o no resecable que ya recibieron tratamiento previo. Ivonescimab se administra por vena (IV) cada 3 semanas, el día 1 de cada ciclo, durante un máximo de 24 meses en total. El resultado principal no está indicado en el registro; el registro señala que el estudio busca saber si el tratamiento es eficaz y seguro, con efectos secundarios leves o pocos.
who_for: Adults 18 or older with unresectable or metastatic leiomyosarcoma confirmed by biopsy.
ECOG performance status 0 to 2.
Between 1 and 3 prior lines of systemic therapy for leiomyosarcoma.
Measurable disease per RECIST v1.1.
Blood, kidney, liver and clotting test values within the stated limits.
not_for: Prior anti-PD1, PD-L1, or VEGF inhibitor therapy.
Symptomatic autoimmune disease, or autoimmune disease needing systemic treatment in the past 2 years.
Major surgery or serious trauma within 4 weeks before randomization.
Recent bleeding problems, or poorly controlled high blood pressure.
Symptomatic brain metastases or leptomeningeal disease.

NCT06066424.summary_en: This Phase 1 study tests TROP2 CAR-NK cells, which are natural killer immune cells made from cord blood and engineered to target TROP2, in adults with advanced solid tumors. The cells are given by vein (IV) at one of up to 5 dose levels, after lymphodepleting chemotherapy with fludarabine and cyclophosphamide, and how long or how often treatment lasts is not stated. The study's main goal is to find the recommended dose of TROP2-CAR-NK cells; other outcome measures are not stated.
NCT06066424.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1 prueba células NK con receptor CAR dirigido a TROP2, que son células inmunitarias naturales asesinas obtenidas de sangre de cordón y modificadas para atacar TROP2, en adultos con tumores sólidos avanzados. Las células se administran por vena (IV) en uno de hasta 5 niveles de dosis, después de quimioterapia de linfodepleción con fludarabina y ciclofosfamida; la duración o la frecuencia del tratamiento no se indican. El objetivo principal del estudio es encontrar la dosis recomendada de las células NK con CAR-TROP2; no se indican otras medidas de resultado.
who_for: Age 18 years or older.
Advanced or metastatic solid tumor that progressed after standard treatment, or with no standard treatment available (dose escalation).
Tumor TROP2 expression of 2+ or 3+ by IHC test.
ECOG performance status of 0 or 1.
Life expectancy of at least 3 months.
not_for: Pregnant or breastfeeding.
Known active brain metastases or carcinomatous meningitis.
Prior CAR T, NK, or other genetically modified T or NK cell therapy.
Known HIV infection or active or chronic hepatitis B or C.
Active autoimmune disease needing systemic treatment in the past 2 years.

NCT05623020.summary_en: This Phase 3 study compares elranatamab, daratumumab and lenalidomide with daratumumab, bortezomib, lenalidomide and dexamethasone in adults with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma who are not candidates for transplant. How each drug is given, and the dose and schedule, are not stated in the record. The study measures the rate of minimal residual disease (MRD) negative complete response and progression-free survival (PFS).
NCT05623020.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 3 compara elranatamab, daratumumab y lenalidomida con daratumumab, bortezomib, lenalidomida y dexametasona en adultos con mieloma múltiple recién diagnosticado que no son candidatos a trasplante. El registro no indica cómo se administra cada medicamento, ni la dosis ni con qué frecuencia. El estudio mide la tasa de respuesta completa negativa para enfermedad residual mínima (MRD) y la supervivencia libre de progresión (PFS).
who_for: Newly diagnosed multiple myeloma that is not a candidate for high-dose chemotherapy and stem cell transplant due to age or comorbidities.
Measurable disease by IMWG criteria, such as serum M-protein of at least 1 g/dL in Part 2.
ECOG performance status of 2 or lower.
Age 18 years or older; no upper age limit stated.
Not pregnant and willing to use contraception.
not_for: Smoldering multiple myeloma.
Monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance.
Waldenström macroglobulinemia or plasma cell leukemia.
Active, uncontrolled infection, including COVID-19, hepatitis B or C, or HIV.
Other active malignancy within 3 years before enrollment, with some exceptions.

NCT04585490.summary_en: This study tests whether adding tremelimumab and chemotherapy to durvalumab, with treatment guided by a blood test for circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA), can help in stage III or recurrent non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Patients with detectable ctDNA receive 4 cycles of chemotherapy with tremelimumab and durvalumab every 21 days, then durvalumab to complete 1 year, while patients with undetectable ctDNA receive durvalumab alone. The record does not state a main outcome measure; its stated goal is to see whether circulating cancer cells in the blood can be decreased, and the study is Phase 3.
NCT04585490.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa si agregar tremelimumab y quimioterapia a durvalumab, con un tratamiento guiado por un examen de sangre para el ADN tumoral circulante (ctDNA), puede ayudar en el cáncer de pulmón de células no pequeñas (CPCNP) en estadio III o recurrente. Los pacientes con ctDNA detectable reciben 4 ciclos de quimioterapia con tremelimumab y durvalumab cada 21 días, y luego durvalumab hasta completar 1 año, mientras que los pacientes con ctDNA no detectable reciben solo durvalumab. El registro no indica una medida de resultado principal; su objetivo declarado es ver si pueden disminuir las células cancerosas circulantes en la sangre, y el estudio es de Fase 3.
who_for: Stage III or recurrent NSCLC treated earlier with platinum chemotherapy and radiation, with no known progression.
Currently receiving consolidation durvalumab, with less than 32 weeks since the first dose.
Age 18 or older and weight over 30 kg.
ECOG performance status of 0 or 1.
Adequate blood counts, kidney and liver function, and a tumor sample believed to be available.
not_for: Mixed small cell and non-small cell lung cancer histology.
Prior grade 3 or higher immune-related adverse event on immunotherapy, or an unresolved one above grade 1.
Autoimmune or inflammatory disorder likely to limit continuing durvalumab.
Active uncontrolled infection, or active hepatitis B, hepatitis C, tuberculosis or HIV as defined.
Pregnant or breastfeeding, or not using effective birth control when required.

NCT04933903.summary_en: This phase 2 study tests ipilimumab and nivolumab given with low-dose stereotactic body radiation therapy before surgery in people with resectable non-small cell lung cancer. Ipilimumab is given as one intravenous dose on day 1, and nivolumab is given intravenously on days 1, 15 and 29, while stereotactic body radiation therapy is given in one or two treatments completed by day 3. The main outcome measured is pathologic response, including major and complete pathologic response, in patients who go on to surgery.
NCT04933903.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 prueba ipilimumab y nivolumab junto con radioterapia estereotáctica corporal de dosis baja antes de la cirugía, en personas con cáncer de pulmón de células no pequeñas resecable. El ipilimumab se administra en una dosis intravenosa el día 1, y el nivolumab se administra por vía intravenosa los días 1, 15 y 29, mientras que la radioterapia estereotáctica corporal se da en una o dos sesiones, completadas antes del día 3. El resultado principal que se mide es la respuesta patológica, incluida la respuesta patológica mayor y la respuesta patológica completa, en los pacientes que se someten a cirugía.
who_for: Pathologically confirmed non-small cell lung cancer, resectable stage IB to IIIB
Candidates for surgery with intent to remove the tumor completely (R0)
Age 18 or older with ECOG performance status 0-1
Lung function adequate to tolerate the planned lung resection
Blood counts, liver and kidney function within the stated limits
not_for: Prior thoracic radiation
Pregnant or nursing
Unable to give informed consent or have an acceptable surrogate consent
Not operable, as judged by a thoracic surgeon
Blood counts, liver or kidney function outside the stated limits

NCT04278118.summary_en: This phase 2 study tests hypofractionated proton or photon radiation therapy in people with benign brain or nerve sheath tumors, such as meningiomas, pituitary adenomas, and schwannomas. Patients receive radiation daily, Monday through Friday, over 17 fractions (or 20 fractions for grade 2-3 meningiomas) for 3.5 to 4 weeks. The main outcome is not stated in the record; this is a phase II study.
NCT04278118.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 evalúa la radioterapia hipofraccionada con protones o fotones en personas con tumores benignos del cerebro o de las vainas nerviosas, como meningiomas, adenomas de hipófisis y schwannomas. Los pacientes reciben radiación diariamente, de lunes a viernes, en 17 fracciones (o 20 fracciones para meningiomas de grado 2-3) durante 3.5 a 4 semanas. El resultado principal no se indica en el registro; es un estudio de fase II.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older
Benign intracranial or nerve sheath tumor, such as meningioma, pituitary adenoma, or schwannoma
WHO grade 2-3 meningiomas are also allowed
Recommended to receive proton or photon fractionated radiation therapy
Has signed informed consent
not_for: Pregnant women
Women who could become pregnant without a negative pregnancy test or adequate birth control
Prior radiation that overlaps with the current target area
Unable to undergo magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)

NCT05986240.summary_en: This Phase 1 study tests danvatirsen alone and then combined with venetoclax in adults with relapsed or refractory myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS) or acute myeloid leukemia (AML). Danvatirsen is given by infusion, with loading doses and then weekly doses over 28-day cycles at increasing dose levels, and venetoclax is taken by mouth at 400 mg daily for 28 days per cycle. The record does not state a main outcome measure; the study is described as evaluating safety and efficacy.
NCT05986240.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1 prueba danvatirsen solo y después combinado con venetoclax en adultos con síndromes mielodisplásicos (SMD) o leucemia mieloide aguda (LMA) recidivantes o refractarios. El danvatirsen se administra por infusión, con dosis de carga y luego dosis semanales en ciclos de 28 días, a niveles de dosis crecientes, y el venetoclax se toma por vía oral a 400 mg diarios durante 28 días por ciclo. El registro no indica una medida de resultado principal; el estudio se describe como una evaluación de seguridad y eficacia.
who_for: Age 18 years or older and able to sign informed consent.
Morphologically confirmed AML or MDS by WHO criteria.
Relapsed or refractory AML with no FDA-approved or standard therapy options.
Intermediate, high or very high IPSS-R MDS refractory or relapsed after at least 2 cycles of hypomethylating agent therapy, or rapid progression.
ECOG performance status of 0 to 2.
not_for: Acute promyelocytic leukemia.
Low or very low risk MDS after failure of first-line hypomethylating agents.
Active, uncontrolled infection.
Active central nervous system leukemia.
Previous exposure to danvatirsen.

NCT05123482.summary_en: This study is testing AZD8205, a new antibody drug conjugate, alone or combined with other anticancer agents in people with advanced or metastatic solid tumors, including breast, biliary tract, ovarian, endometrial, and squamous non-small cell lung cancer. The route, dose, and schedule are not stated in the record. The main outcomes are safety, tolerability, and the recommended Phase 2 dose or maximum tolerated dose in dose escalation, and anti-tumor activity in dose expansion.
NCT05123482.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa AZD8205, un nuevo conjugado anticuerpo-fármaco, solo o combinado con otros agentes anticancerosos, en personas con tumores sólidos avanzados o metastásicos, incluidos cáncer de mama, carcinoma de vías biliares, cáncer de ovario, cáncer de endometrio y cáncer de pulmón de células no pequeñas de tipo escamoso. La vía de administración, la dosis y el esquema no se indican en el registro. Los resultados principales son la seguridad, la tolerabilidad y la dosis recomendada de fase 2 o la dosis máxima tolerada en la fase de escalada de dosis, y la actividad antitumoral en la fase de expansión.
who_for: Age 18 or older.
Relapsed or metastatic solid tumor treated with prior standard therapy, or where the investigator judges a trial is the best next option.
Measurable disease per RECIST v1.1.
ECOG performance status 0 to 1 and life expectancy of 12 weeks or more.
Histologically or cytologically confirmed breast, ovarian, biliary tract, endometrial, or squamous non-small cell lung cancer (sub-study criteria vary).
not_for: Nitrosourea or mitomycin C within 6 weeks before first dose.
Spinal cord compression or history of leptomeningeal carcinomatosis.
Active infection, including tuberculosis, HBV, HCV, or HIV.
Current or past interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis that needed steroids.
Symptomatic heart failure (NYHA class 2 or higher) or history of MDS or AML.

NCT07020117.summary_en: This Phase 1 study tests [225Ac]Ac-AKY-1189, a Nectin-4 radiopharmaceutical, in people with previously treated locally advanced or metastatic solid tumors, including the listed cancer types. The drug is given as an injection, and how often and for how long it is given is not stated. The study measures safety and efficacy and aims to find the maximum tolerated or administered dose and the recommended Phase 2 dose.
NCT07020117.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1 evalúa [225Ac]Ac-AKY-1189, un radiofármaco dirigido a Nectina-4, en personas con tumores sólidos localmente avanzados o metastásicos que ya recibieron tratamiento previo, incluidos los tipos de cáncer enumerados. El medicamento se administra como inyección, y en el registro no se indica con qué frecuencia ni durante cuánto tiempo. El estudio mide la seguridad y la eficacia, y busca determinar la dosis máxima tolerada o administrada y la dosis recomendada para fase 2.
who_for: Histologic or cytologic confirmation of locally advanced or metastatic solid tumor
At least one measurable tumor lesion on CT per RECIST v1.1
ECOG performance status of 0 or 1
Documented progression on prior therapy for metastatic disease
Adequate end-organ function and ability to give informed consent; CNS metastases allowed if neurologically stable
not_for: Prior treatment with a therapeutic radiopharmaceutical
Prior Nectin-4 targeted therapy, except enfortumab vedotin
Investigational agent received within the previous 28 days
Chemotherapy, targeted therapy, biologic, immunotherapy or external-beam radiotherapy within 3 weeks before study treatment
Serious medical condition that would impair participation or affect toxicity assessment

NCT07278362.summary_en: This Phase 4 study tests testosterone replacement therapy in men with low testosterone and low-risk prostate cancer who are on active surveillance. Participants self-inject 100 mg of testosterone cypionate once a week for 12 months. The record does not list a specific outcome measure; the stated purpose is to evaluate the safety of the therapy.
NCT07278362.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 4 evalúa la terapia de reemplazo de testosterona en hombres con niveles bajos de testosterona y cáncer de próstata de bajo riesgo que están en vigilancia activa. Los participantes se inyectan por sí mismos 100 mg de cipionato de testosterona una vez por semana durante 12 meses. El registro no indica una medida de resultado específica; el propósito declarado es evaluar la seguridad de la terapia.
who_for: Males aged 18 or older.
Newly diagnosed low-risk prostate cancer, or low-risk prostate cancer on active surveillance.
Two testosterone levels below 350 ng/dL, taken before 10am, 24 hours to 90 days apart.
Symptoms of low testosterone (Aging Male's Symptoms score above 27).
Able to obtain the medication and give written informed consent.
not_for: Gleason score 7 (Grade Group 2) or higher on biopsy.
PSA above 10 ng/mL at baseline.
Current testosterone replacement therapy, or use within the past year.
Hematocrit above 51% at baseline.
T3 or T4 disease, history of breast cancer, or unstable angina.

NCT04918186.summary_en: This study tests several drugs, including durvalumab, toripalimab, BA3011, BA3021 and ENB003, in platinum resistant high grade serous ovarian cancer. The drugs are given by intravenous (IV) infusion, and durvalumab is given as 1500 mg over 60 minutes on day 1 every 4 weeks; the schedules for the other drugs are not stated. The record does not state the main outcome measured; the study is a Phase 2 trial.
NCT04918186.summary_es: Este estudio prueba varios medicamentos, entre ellos durvalumab, toripalimab, BA3011, BA3021 y ENB003, en el cáncer de ovario seroso de alto grado resistente al platino. Los medicamentos se administran por infusión intravenosa (IV), y durvalumab se administra como 1500 mg durante 60 minutos el día 1 cada 4 semanas; los esquemas de los otros medicamentos no se indican. El registro no indica el resultado principal que se mide; el estudio es un ensayo de Fase 2.
who_for: Women with platinum resistant high grade serous ovarian, fallopian tube or peritoneal cancer
Disease progressed within 6 months of last platinum-containing chemotherapy
Measurable disease as defined by RECIST 1.1
ECOG performance status 0 or 1 and life expectancy of at least 3 months
Age 18 years or older
not_for: Symptomatic uncontrolled brain metastases requiring corticosteroid treatment
Active or past autoimmune or inflammatory disorder within the past 3 years, with some exceptions
Pregnant or breastfeeding women
Significant cardiac disease within 6 months, or QTc above 470 msec (450 msec with added risk factors)
History of interstitial lung disease or non-infectious pneumonitis

NCT06385080.summary_en: This study tests amivantamab alone or with other drugs (pembrolizumab, paclitaxel, or pembrolizumab with carboplatin) in squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck, including recurrent or metastatic disease and resectable locally advanced disease before and after surgery. Amivantamab is given as a subcutaneous injection weekly in Cycle 1 and then every 3 weeks, and pembrolizumab, paclitaxel and carboplatin are given intravenously, with carboplatin for Cycles 1 to 6 in one arm; total treatment length is not stated. The study measures safety and early signs of effectiveness and confirms a recommended dose with paclitaxel, and the main outcome measure is not stated.
NCT06385080.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa amivantamab solo o combinado con otros medicamentos (pembrolizumab, paclitaxel o pembrolizumab con carboplatino) en el carcinoma de células escamosas de cabeza y cuello, incluida la enfermedad recurrente o metastásica y la enfermedad localmente avanzada resecable antes y después de la cirugía. Amivantamab se administra como inyección subcutánea semanalmente en el Ciclo 1 y luego cada 3 semanas, mientras que pembrolizumab, paclitaxel y carboplatino se administran por vena cada 3 semanas, y el carboplatino en los Ciclos 1 a 6 en un brazo; la duración total del tratamiento no se indica. El estudio mide la seguridad y las primeras señales de efectividad y confirma una dosis recomendada con paclitaxel, y la medida de resultado principal no se indica.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older with recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma considered incurable by local therapies
For the perioperative cohort: resectable locally advanced disease, stage III or IVa
Primary tumor in the oropharynx, oral cavity, hypopharynx, or larynx, with cohort-specific tumor marker rules
ECOG performance status of 0 to 1
Adequate blood counts and organ function (hemoglobin, neutrophils, platelets)
not_for: Interstitial lung disease, pneumonitis or pulmonary fibrosis, or suspected disease not ruled out by imaging
Untreated brain metastases, leptomeningeal disease, or spinal cord compression not definitively treated
Clinically significant cardiovascular disease history
Recent chemotherapy, targeted therapy, immunotherapy or investigational agent within 2 weeks or 4 half-lives, whichever is longer (maximum 28 days)
Palliative radiotherapy within 7 days of the first study dose
cancer_types: squamous cell carcinoma of head and neck

NCT07133997.summary_en: This Phase 1/1b study tests recombinant Erwinia asparaginase and venetoclax given together with blinatumomab in adults with relapsed or refractory CD19-positive B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia. Asparaginase Erwinia is given by injection into the muscle on days 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 and 13; venetoclax is taken by mouth daily on days 1 to 14 or every other day on those odd-numbered days; and blinatumomab is given as a continuous IV infusion on days 8 to 35 of cycle 1 and days 1 to 28 of cycle 2, for up to 2 cycles. The record does not state a primary outcome; it says the study looks at safety, side effects, and how well the combination works.
NCT07133997.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1/1b evalúa la asparaginasa Erwinia recombinante y venetoclax, administrados junto con blinatumomab, en adultos con leucemia linfoblástica aguda de células B positiva para CD19 que recidivó o es refractaria. La asparaginasa Erwinia se aplica por inyección intramuscular los días 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 y 13; el venetoclax se toma por vía oral a diario los días 1 a 14, o cada dos días en los días impares indicados; y el blinatumomab se administra como infusión intravenosa continua los días 8 a 35 del ciclo 1 y los días 1 a 28 del ciclo 2, hasta 2 ciclos. El registro no indica un resultado principal; dice que el estudio evalúa la seguridad, los efectos secundarios y qué tan bien funciona la combinación.
who_for: Age 12 to 55 years
Relapsed or refractory CD19-positive B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia
At least 5% blasts in the bone marrow
ECOG 2 or lower, or Karnofsky score 70 or higher
Heart pumping function (LVEF) of 50% or higher, with other lab values within stated limits
not_for: Allogeneic stem cell transplant within 8 weeks before starting study treatment
Active leukemia in the central nervous system
History of grade 3 or higher pancreatitis, or known allergy to study drugs
Other active cancer, with listed exceptions
Pregnant or breastfeeding

NCT05239546.summary_en: This study tests dostarlimab, a drug given by IV, in people with stage II or III colon cancer that has deficient mismatch repair (dMMR). It is a Phase II, single-arm study, so all participants receive the same treatment. Dostarlimab is given as 500 mg IV every 3 weeks for 6 cycles, then 1000 mg every 6 weeks for 8 cycles, until 1.5 years. The study measures the rate of major clinical response and non-operative management after 18 weeks (up to 6 cycles).
NCT05239546.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa dostarlimab, un medicamento que se administra por vía intravenosa, en personas con cáncer de colon en estadio II o III que tiene deficiencia en la reparación de errores de apareamiento (dMMR). Es un estudio de fase II de un solo brazo, por lo que todos los participantes reciben el mismo tratamiento. Dostarlimab se administra a 500 mg por vía IV cada 3 semanas durante 6 ciclos, y luego a 1000 mg cada 6 semanas durante 8 ciclos, hasta 1.5 años. El estudio mide la tasa de respuesta clínica mayor y de manejo no quirúrgico después de 18 semanas (hasta 6 ciclos).
who_for: Age 18 years or older.
Biopsy-proven dMMR colon cancer, stage II or III.
Potentially surgically resectable, and willing to forgo surgery if study endpoints are met.
ECOG performance status less than or equal to 1.
No metastatic disease on CT scan within 28 days of treatment start.
not_for: More than one primary tumor (synchronous primary tumor).
Obstruction or perforation needing a diverting ostomy or immediate resection.
Clinical T4b tumor.
Known hypersensitivity to dostarlimab or its components or excipients.
Grade 3 or higher immune-related adverse event with prior immunotherapy.

NCT05898646.summary_en: This phase II trial compares shorter-duration and longer-duration maintenance therapy with daratumumab in patients with light chain (AL) amyloidosis who received daratumumab as initial treatment. Daratumumab is given under the skin (subcutaneously) on day 1 of each 28-day cycle, for up to 6 cycles in one group or up to 18 cycles in the other, unless the disease gets worse or side effects are unacceptable. The trial aims to improve survival, but the specific primary outcome measure is not stated.
NCT05898646.summary_es: Este ensayo de fase II compara una terapia de mantenimiento con daratumumab de menor duración con una de mayor duración, en pacientes con amiloidosis de cadenas ligeras (AL) que recibieron daratumumab como tratamiento inicial. El daratumumab se administra debajo de la piel (subcutáneo) el día 1 de cada ciclo de 28 días, hasta 6 ciclos en un grupo o hasta 18 ciclos en el otro, a menos que la enfermedad empeore o los efectos secundarios sean inaceptables. El ensayo busca mejorar la supervivencia, pero la medida específica del resultado principal no se indica.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older.
AL amyloidosis confirmed by tissue testing with adequate typing.
Completed 6 cycles of daratumumab-CyBorD-based induction, or plans to before cycle 1.
Reached a hematologic response (complete, very good partial, or partial with a required level) after induction, as defined in the record.
ECOG performance status 0 to 3 and blood counts above listed minimums.
not_for: Pregnant or nursing, or able to have children and unwilling to use contraception.
More than one cycle of daratumumab maintenance before registration.
Multiple myeloma at diagnosis, as defined by listed criteria.
Positive hepatitis B surface antigen.
Immunocompromised, or HIV positive and on antiretroviral therapy; or uncontrolled illness or active infection.

NCT07763210.summary_en: This Phase 2 study tests early intrathecal cytarabine and hydrocortisone to treat ICANS, a nervous system side effect of CAR T-cell therapy, in adults with non-Hodgkin lymphoma. Intrathecal cytarabine (100 mg) and hydrocortisone (100 mg) are given when grade 1 or 2 ICANS starts after axicabtagene ciloleucel or brexucabtagene autoleucel, and dexamethasone IV 10 mg and methylprednisolone 1 g daily until adverse events resolve are also listed. The study measures the rate of grade 3 or higher ICANS and how long ICANS lasts, compared with historical experience.
NCT07763210.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 evalúa la administración temprana de citarabina y hidrocortisona intratecales para tratar la ICANS, un efecto secundario del sistema nervioso de la terapia con células CAR T, en adultos con linfoma no Hodgkin. La citarabina intratecal (100 mg) y la hidrocortisona (100 mg) se administran cuando aparece una ICANS de grado 1 o 2 después de axicabtagén ciloleucel o brexucabtagén autoleucel; también se mencionan dexametasona IV de 10 mg y metilprednisolona de 1 g al día hasta que se resuelvan los eventos adversos. El estudio mide la tasa de ICANS de grado 3 o superior y la duración de la ICANS, en comparación con la experiencia histórica.
who_for: Age 18 years or older
Histologically confirmed non-Hodgkin lymphoma of the listed types
Meets institutional criteria for standard CD19 CAR T therapy
Has provided documented informed consent
Meets the stated organ function limits for blood counts, kidney, liver and clotting
not_for: Active hepatitis B or hepatitis C infection
Uncontrolled systemic infection despite treatment
Needs anti-platelet or anticoagulant drugs that cannot be safely held
Active malignancy in the last 24 months, other than high-grade B-cell lymphoma, with listed exceptions
History of platelet transfusion refractoriness or declining transfusion support

NCT05401110.summary_en: This phase 1 study tests osimertinib combined with carotuximab in advanced non-small cell lung cancer that has an EGFR mutation. Osimertinib is taken by mouth once daily at 40 mg or 80 mg, and carotuximab is given into a vein weekly for 4 weeks, then every 2 weeks, at 10 mg/kg or 15 mg/kg, until disease progression, withdrawal, or intolerance. The main measure is the number of dose-limiting toxicities, used to find the maximum tolerated dose.
NCT05401110.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1 evalúa osimertinib combinado con carotuximab en cáncer de pulmón de células no pequeñas avanzado con mutación de EGFR. El osimertinib se toma por vía oral una vez al día, en dosis de 40 mg u 80 mg, y el carotuximab se administra en una vena cada semana durante 4 semanas y luego cada 2 semanas, en dosis de 10 mg/kg o 15 mg/kg, hasta progresión, retiro del estudio o intolerancia. La medida principal es el número de toxicidades limitantes de dosis, que se usa para encontrar la dosis máxima tolerada.
who_for: Stage IV or recurrent/metastatic non-squamous NSCLC with an EGFR activating mutation
Disease progression on a prior EGFR TKI, including osimertinib, depending on study part
Age 18 or older with ECOG performance status 0 to 2
Measurable disease by RECIST 1.1
Archival tumor tissue from after progression, or willingness to have a fresh biopsy
not_for: Past or current interstitial lung disease or clinically active lung inflammation
Small cell lung cancer histology
Prior exposure to carotuximab or any CD105-targeted antibody
Uncontrolled high blood pressure or an acute cardiovascular event in the past 6 months
Pregnancy or breastfeeding

NCT07140679.summary_en: This trial tests toripalimab, an immunotherapy drug, after surgery to reduce the risk of cancer recurrence in patients with mismatch repair deficient stage IIB, IIC, or III colon cancer. Toripalimab is given into a vein every 3 weeks for 6 months (8 doses), followed by surveillance with blood tests, CT scans, and colonoscopy until 5 years after surgery. The main outcome is not stated; this is a Phase 2 trial.
NCT07140679.summary_es: Este ensayo evalúa toripalimab, un medicamento de inmunoterapia, después de la cirugía para reducir el riesgo de recurrencia del cáncer en pacientes con cáncer de colon en estadio IIB, IIC o III con deficiencia de reparación de errores de apareamiento. El toripalimab se administra en una vena cada 3 semanas durante 6 meses (8 dosis), seguido de vigilancia con análisis de sangre, tomografías computarizadas y colonoscopias hasta 5 años después de la cirugía. El resultado principal no se indica; este es un ensayo de Fase 2.
who_for: Resected stage IIB, IIC, or III dMMR or MSI-H colon cancer (AJCC 8).
Complete (R0) resection 4 to 12 weeks before the first dose.
Tissue sample from the surgical specimen is available.
ECOG performance status 0, 1, or 2.
At least 18 years of age.
not_for: Neoadjuvant treatment for dMMR colon cancer.
Metastatic dMMR colon cancer.
Prior treatment with any immune checkpoint inhibitor.
History of pneumonitis needing steroids or interstitial lung disease.
Active hepatitis B or C, or autoimmune disease treated systemically in the past 2 years.

NCT07188896.summary_en: This Phase 2 trial tests fianlimab and cemiplimab, with or without ipilimumab, or ipilimumab plus nivolumab, as first-line treatment for advanced clear cell renal cell carcinoma. All drugs are given by IV, patients are randomized 2:2:1 to three arms, and the treatment schedule and length are not stated. The main outcome is not stated; the record describes this as a randomized Phase 2 trial.
NCT07188896.summary_es: Este ensayo de fase 2 evalúa fianlimab y cemiplimab, con o sin ipilimumab, o ipilimumab más nivolumab, como tratamiento de primera línea para el carcinoma de células renales avanzado de células claras. Todos los medicamentos se administran por vía intravenosa, los pacientes se asignan al azar en una proporción 2:2:1 a tres grupos, y el calendario y la duración del tratamiento no se indican. El resultado principal no se indica; el registro describe este estudio como un ensayo aleatorizado de fase 2.
who_for: Adults aged 18 or older with advanced clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
Karnofsky performance status of 70% or higher within 14 days before registration.
Kidney cancer that cannot be cured by surgery or radiation, or is metastatic (stage IV).
No prior systemic therapy for kidney cancer, including neoadjuvant or adjuvant therapy.
Measurable disease according to RECIST 1.1 within 28 days before registration.
not_for: Prior systemic treatment for kidney cancer in the neoadjuvant, adjuvant, or metastatic setting.
Any condition needing ongoing prednisone of 10 mg per day or more.
History of myocarditis.
Autoimmune disease needing immunosuppressive treatment within the past 2 years.
Central nervous system (brain) metastases, as described in the protocol.

NCT07545954.summary_en: This study tests DSP-0390 taken together with atezolizumab as maintenance treatment for extensive stage small cell lung cancer that has not progressed after first-line chemoimmunotherapy. DSP-0390 is taken by mouth once a day in 21-day cycles at 180 mg, 120 mg, or a determined safe dose, and atezolizumab is given per standard of care (FDA-approved dose 1200 mg IV every three weeks), until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity, for up to 2 years. The study evaluates safety and preliminary efficacy, and it is a Phase 1 study (a Phase Ib pilot with a safety lead-in).
NCT07545954.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa DSP-0390 administrado junto con atezolizumab como tratamiento de mantenimiento para el cáncer de pulmón de células pequeñas en etapa extensa que no ha progresado después de la quimioinmunoterapia de primera línea. DSP-0390 se toma por vía oral una vez al día en ciclos de 21 días, a 180 mg, 120 mg o una dosis segura determinada, y atezolizumab se administra según el estándar de atención (dosis aprobada por la FDA de 1200 mg por vía intravenosa cada tres semanas), hasta la progresión de la enfermedad o toxicidad inaceptable, por un máximo de 2 años. El estudio evalúa la seguridad y la eficacia preliminar, y es un estudio de Fase 1 (un piloto de Fase Ib con una fase inicial de seguridad).
who_for: Confirmed small cell lung cancer.
Extensive stage disease that has not progressed after 3-4 cycles of first-line platinum-based chemoimmunotherapy.
Measurable disease per RECIST 1.1.
At least 18 years old with ECOG performance status of 2 or less.
Adequate blood counts, liver function, and kidney function as defined in the criteria.
not_for: Prior or current cancer that could interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.
Investigational agents within 4 weeks before Day 1 (6 weeks for investigational immunotherapy).
Untreated symptomatic brain metastases or clinically evident CNS hemorrhage.
Pregnant or breastfeeding.
Conditions that significantly limit oral drug absorption, such as short-gut syndrome, or an abnormal ECG or history of Torsade de Pointes.
cancer_types: extensive stage small cell lung cancer

NCT07087860.summary_en: This Phase 2 study compares therapeutic plasma exchange (TPE) followed by enfortumab vedotin and pembrolizumab with standard next-line therapy. It is for people with bladder or upper urinary tract urothelial cancer that has spread and has not responded to previous treatment. TPE is given on days 1 to 3 of cycles 1 to 3, enfortumab vedotin and pembrolizumab are given by vein, and cycles repeat every 21 days in the absence of disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. The main outcome is not stated in the record; this is a Phase 2 study.
NCT07087860.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 compara el intercambio terapéutico de plasma (TPE) seguido de enfortumab vedotina y pembrolizumab con la terapia estándar de siguiente línea. Está dirigido a personas con cáncer urotelial de vejiga o de vías urinarias superiores que se ha diseminado y no ha respondido a tratamientos previos. El TPE se administra los días 1 a 3 de los ciclos 1 a 3, la enfortumab vedotina y el pembrolizumab se dan por vena, y los ciclos se repiten cada 21 días mientras no haya progresión de la enfermedad ni toxicidad inaceptable. El resultado principal no está indicado en el registro; este es un estudio de fase 2.
who_for: Age 18 years or older.
Urothelial carcinoma of the bladder or upper urinary tract that progressed despite enfortumab vedotin and pembrolizumab (Groups A and B).
Urothelial carcinoma that progressed despite an antibody-drug conjugate and is not a candidate for Groups A and B (Cohort C).
Measurable disease and ECOG performance status 0, 1, or 2.
Blood counts, liver and kidney tests within set limits, obtained within 30 days before registration.
not_for: Pregnant or nursing, or able to become pregnant or father a child and unwilling to use contraception.
Any neuroendocrine or signet ring cell features in the tumor.
Another active cancer that is progressing or needing treatment change within 24 months, with listed exceptions.
Uncontrolled heart disease or certain heart or brain events within 6 months.
Psychiatric illness or substance use that would limit study compliance, or investigator judges participation not in the participant's best interest.
cancer_types: renal pelvis and ureter urothelial carcinoma

NCT06136624.summary_en: This phase 3 study compares opevesostat (MK-5684) with abiraterone acetate or enzalutamide in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer that was previously treated with a next-generation hormonal agent and taxane-based chemotherapy. Opevesostat is taken by mouth as 5 mg tablets twice daily, with dexamethasone and fludrocortisone acetate once daily, until progression. The main outcome measured is overall survival (OS).
NCT06136624.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 3 compara opevesostat (MK-5684) con acetato de abiraterona o enzalutamida en cáncer de próstata metastásico resistente a la castración que fue tratado previamente con un agente hormonal de nueva generación y quimioterapia basada en taxanos. El opevesostat se toma por vía oral en tabletas de 5 mg dos veces al día, junto con dexametasona y acetato de fludrocortisona una vez al día, hasta la progresión. El resultado principal que se mide es la supervivencia global (OS).
who_for: Adenocarcinoma of the prostate confirmed by biopsy or cytology, without small cell histology
Prostate cancer progressed on androgen deprivation therapy within 6 months before screening, with distant metastatic disease
Disease progressed during or after one novel hormonal agent
Received 1 to 2 taxane-based chemotherapy regimens for mCRPC, with progression during or after treatment
ECOG performance status of 0 or 1
not_for: Gastrointestinal disorder that might affect drug absorption
History of pituitary dysfunction
Poorly controlled diabetes or clinically significant abnormal potassium or sodium levels
Active or unstable cardiovascular or cerebrovascular disease, or recent seizures
Known active central nervous system metastases or carcinomatous meningitis

NCT05419518.summary_en: This Phase 2 study tests dose-escalated palliative radiation for painful cancer that has spread to bones outside the spine, or to other non-bone sites. Radiation is given as 50 Gy in 10 fractions, or may be reduced to 40 Gy in 8 fractions for non-spine metastases; at least three daily treatments are given each week, and missed treatments are made up at the end of the schedule. The study measures the complete pain response rate at one month.
NCT05419518.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 evalúa radioterapia paliativa con dosis más altas para el dolor causado por cáncer que se ha extendido a huesos fuera de la columna, o a otros sitios que no son huesos. La radiación se administra como 50 Gy en 10 fracciones, o puede reducirse a 40 Gy en 8 fracciones para metástasis fuera de la columna; se dan al menos tres tratamientos diarios por semana, y los tratamientos perdidos se reponen al final del esquema. El estudio mide la tasa de respuesta completa del dolor al mes.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older who gave signed informed consent
Malignancy proven by tissue (histologic) testing
Bone or non-bone metastases shown by imaging or tissue testing
Pain score of 3 or higher
Life expectancy of six months or more
not_for: Metastases from highly radiosensitive tumors such as lymphoma, myeloma, or germ cell tumor
Spinal metastasis
Active compression of the spinal cord or cauda equina
Previous radiation or SBRT to the same site
More than 3 sites needing radiation treatment

NCT05318469.summary_en: This study tests ivermectin given together with an immune checkpoint inhibitor, balstilimab or pembrolizumab, in people with metastatic triple negative breast cancer or metastatic HR+/HER2- breast cancer. Ivermectin is taken by mouth on days 1-3, 8-10, and 15-17 of each 21-day cycle, and balstilimab or pembrolizumab is given intravenously on day 1 of each 21-day cycle. Treatment continues until disease progression, intolerable side effects, withdrawal of consent, or up to 35 treatments or 2 years of the immunotherapy, whichever comes first. The record does not state a primary outcome; it describes a Phase 1/2 study of side effects and best dose, with secondary measures that include objective response rate and progression-free survival.
NCT05318469.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa ivermectina administrada junto con un inhibidor de puntos de control inmunitario, balstilimab o pembrolizumab, en personas con cáncer de mama metastásico triple negativo o cáncer de mama metastásico HR+/HER2-. La ivermectina se toma por vía oral los días 1-3, 8-10 y 15-17 de cada ciclo de 21 días, y el balstilimab o el pembrolizumab se administra por vía intravenosa el día 1 de cada ciclo de 21 días. El tratamiento continúa hasta la progresión de la enfermedad, efectos secundarios intolerables, retiro del consentimiento, o hasta 35 tratamientos o 2 años de inmunoterapia, lo que ocurra primero. El registro no indica un resultado principal; describe un estudio de Fase 1/2 sobre efectos secundarios y la mejor dosis, con medidas secundarias que incluyen la tasa de respuesta objetiva y la supervivencia libre de progresión.
who_for: Age 18 years or older.
ECOG performance status of 1 or less.
Biopsy-proven metastatic triple negative breast cancer or HR+/HER2- breast cancer.
Progressed on 1 to 2 prior lines of systemic therapy in the metastatic setting.
Measurable or evaluable disease by RECIST 1.1.
not_for: Known active brain metastases or carcinomatous meningitis.
Pneumonitis that required steroids in the past, or current pneumonitis.
Immunodeficiency, or chronic steroid use above 10 mg prednisone daily, or other immunosuppressive therapy within 7 days before first dose.
Current use of warfarin.
Known HIV infection, or active hepatitis B or hepatitis C infection.

NCT06492759.summary_en: This Phase II study tests high dose radiation therapy given with pembrolizumab and chemotherapy in patients with PD-L1 positive metastatic triple negative breast cancer. Radiation is given once every other day for 3 doses, pembrolizumab is given by IV on day 1 of each 21-day cycle, and patients also receive one of three chemotherapy options: nab-paclitaxel or paclitaxel IV on days 1, 8, and 15 of each cycle, or carboplatin and gemcitabine IV on days 1 and 8 of each 21-day cycle. The main outcome measure is not stated in the record; the study is Phase II.
NCT06492759.summary_es: Este estudio de fase II evalúa la radioterapia de dosis alta administrada junto con pembrolizumab y quimioterapia en pacientes con cáncer de mama triple negativo metastásico con PD-L1 positivo. La radioterapia se administra una vez cada dos días en 3 dosis, el pembrolizumab se administra por vía IV el día 1 de cada ciclo de 21 días, y los pacientes también reciben una de tres opciones de quimioterapia: nab-paclitaxel o paclitaxel IV los días 1, 8 y 15 de cada ciclo, o carboplatino y gemcitabina IV los días 1 y 8 de cada ciclo de 21 días. El resultado principal del estudio no se indica en el registro; el estudio es de fase II.
who_for: Biopsy-proven metastatic PD-L1 positive triple negative breast cancer with at least 2 measurable metastatic sites on imaging.
PD-L1 combined positive score of 10 or higher by the Dako 22c3 assay.
At least 1 metastatic site that can be treated with high dose radiotherapy.
Age 18 years or older, with ECOG performance status 0-2 or Karnofsky 60% or higher.
ER and PR negative (10% or fewer cells) and HER2 negative by the stated tests.
not_for: Prior chemotherapy or targeted therapy for metastatic triple negative breast cancer before starting this combination.
Previous radiation to the metastases that would be treated on this study.
Untreated brain or central nervous system disease.
Uncontrolled pleural effusion, pericardial effusion, or ascites.
Autoimmune disease needing systemic treatment, or HIV with CD4 count below 200 cells/microliter.

NCT05701527.summary_en: EBC-129 is being tested alone and together with pembrolizumab in adults with advanced solid tumours. EBC-129 is given as an intravenous infusion over 30 to 120 minutes on Day 1 of each 21-day cycle, and pembrolizumab is given at 200 mg intravenously every 21 days. The study measures safety and tolerability; the phase is Phase 1.
NCT05701527.summary_es: EBC-129 se está probando solo y junto con pembrolizumab en adultos con tumores sólidos avanzados. EBC-129 se administra como infusión intravenosa de 30 a 120 minutos el día 1 de cada ciclo de 21 días, y pembrolizumab se administra a 200 mg por vía intravenosa cada 21 días. El estudio mide la seguridad y la tolerabilidad; la fase es la 1.
who_for: Adults aged 18 or older (21 or older in Singapore).
Progression of a locally advanced unresectable or metastatic solid tumour with no alternative standard therapy with proven benefit, or intolerance to such thera
ECOG performance status 2 or lower for Part A, and 0-1 for Parts B, C and D.
Adequate liver, kidney and bone marrow function per protocol standard.
Body weight 40 to 100 kg in Parts A and B, or up to 120 kg in other parts.
not_for: Unable or unwilling to provide a tumour tissue sample, unless biopsy poses significant risk.
Anti-cancer or investigational therapy within 28 days before study drug, or concurrent anti-cancer therapy.
Prior radiation therapy.
Clinically active brain metastases.
Pregnancy or breastfeeding, or active HIV, hepatitis B or hepatitis C infection.

NCT07043608.summary_en: This Phase II study tests zanzalintinib plus an investigator-chosen bone-strengthening agent in people with metastatic clear cell renal cell carcinoma that has spread to bone. Zanzalintinib is taken by mouth once a day in 28-day cycles and continued until study stop criteria are met, and the bone-strengthening agent is given intravenously. The record does not state the main outcome measure; this is a Phase II study.
NCT07043608.summary_es: Este estudio de fase II evalúa zanzalintinib junto con un agente fortalecedor de huesos elegido por el investigador, en personas con carcinoma de células renales de células claras metastásico que se ha diseminado a los huesos. El zanzalintinib se toma por vía oral una vez al día en ciclos de 28 días y se continúa hasta cumplir los criterios de suspensión del estudio, mientras que el agente fortalecedor de huesos se administra por vía intravenosa. El registro no indica la medida de resultado principal; se trata de un estudio de fase II.
who_for: Unresectable advanced or metastatic kidney cancer with a mainly clear cell type
At least three bone metastases seen on bone scan, with one not planned for radiation
1 to 3 prior lines of therapy, including immune-based therapy in the metastatic or adjuvant setting
ECOG performance status of 2 or less
Adequate blood, liver and kidney function within 14 days before first study treatment
not_for: Prior treatment with zanzalintinib for kidney cancer
Small molecule kinase inhibitor or VEGF-targeted therapy within 2 weeks before first dose
Known brain metastases or cranial epidural disease not adequately treated and stable
Need for whole brain radiotherapy
Certain anticoagulants or platelet inhibitors, or recent significant bleeding

NCT06572618.summary_en: This phase 2 study tests nemtabrutinib with rituximab in people with previously untreated mantle cell lymphoma. Nemtabrutinib is taken by mouth once a day on days 1-28 of each 28-day cycle, and rituximab is given into a vein. Induction lasts up to 6 cycles and maintenance up to 24 cycles, as long as there is no disease progression or unacceptable toxicity; the record does not state the main outcome measure.
NCT06572618.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 evalúa nemtabrutinib junto con rituximab en personas con linfoma de células del manto que no han recibido tratamiento previo. El nemtabrutinib se toma por vía oral una vez al día durante los días 1 a 28 de cada ciclo de 28 días, y el rituximab se administra por vena. La fase de inducción dura hasta 6 ciclos y la de mantenimiento hasta 24 ciclos, siempre que no haya progresión de la enfermedad ni toxicidad inaceptable; el registro no indica cuál es el resultado principal que se mide.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older
ECOG performance status of 2 or lower
Diagnosis of mantle cell lymphoma confirmed by biopsy testing
Needs treatment and has not received prior systemic cancer therapy
Measurable lymph node or extranodal lymphoma on imaging
not_for: Chronic systemic steroid use above 20 mg/day prednisone equivalent
Severe ongoing bleeding disorder
Unstable heart disease, including heart attack within the past 6 months
Corrected QT prolongation above 450 msec or other significant ECG abnormalities
Primary or secondary CNS lymphoma or history of CNS lymphoma

NCT06031688.summary_en: This Phase II study compares tepotinib with or without ramucirumab in adults with stage IV or recurrent non-small cell lung cancer that has a MET exon 14 skipping gene change. Tepotinib is taken by mouth once a day on days 1 to 21 of each 21-day cycle, and ramucirumab is given into a vein over 30 to 60 minutes on day 1 of each cycle. Cycles repeat every 21 days if the disease does not progress and side effects are not unacceptable, and the main outcome is not stated in the record.
NCT06031688.summary_es: Este estudio de fase II compara tepotinib con o sin ramucirumab en adultos con cáncer de pulmón de células no pequeñas en estadio IV o recurrente, que tiene un cambio en el gen MET llamado salto del exón 14. El tepotinib se toma por vía oral una vez al día en los días 1 a 21 de cada ciclo de 21 días, y el ramucirumab se administra por vena durante 30 a 60 minutos el día 1 de cada ciclo. Los ciclos se repiten cada 21 días si la enfermedad no progresa y los efectos secundarios no son inaceptables, y el resultado principal no se indica en el registro.
who_for: Stage IV or recurrent non-small cell lung cancer with a MET exon 14 skipping mutation
Measurable disease seen on CT or MRI scan
Brain scan within 42 days before randomization
Zubrod performance status of 0 to 1
Blood counts, liver and kidney tests within set limits
not_for: Other actionable changes such as EGFR, ALK, ROS1, KRAS, HER2 or BRAF V600E
Prior MET inhibitor or angiogenesis inhibitor therapy, including bevacizumab or ramucirumab
Untreated or active brain metastases or leptomeningeal disease
Interstitial lung disease that needed steroid treatment
Pregnancy or breastfeeding

NCT07372625.summary_en: This Phase 1 study tests how rezatapopt affects the way the body processes four other drugs: metformin, rosuvastatin, repaglinide, and midazolam. It is done in people with advanced solid tumors that have a TP53 Y220C mutation. The study drugs are taken by mouth, and rezatapopt is given as 2000 mg once daily in 21-day cycles through Cycle 33 (about 2 years) or until another stop criterion is met. The record does not state a primary outcome measure; it describes collecting serial PK samples to measure drug levels in the body.
NCT07372625.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1 evalúa cómo rezatapopt afecta la forma en que el cuerpo procesa cuatro otros medicamentos: metformina, rosuvastatina, repaglinida y midazolam. Se realiza en personas con tumores sólidos avanzados que tienen una mutación TP53 Y220C. Los medicamentos del estudio se toman por vía oral, y rezatapopt se administra en dosis de 2000 mg una vez al día en ciclos de 21 días hasta el Ciclo 33 (aproximadamente 2 años) o hasta que se cumpla otro criterio de suspensión. El registro no indica una medida de resultado principal; describe la toma de muestras PK seriadas para medir los niveles de los fármacos en el cuerpo.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older who have given written informed consent.
ECOG performance status of 0 or 1.
Confirmed locally advanced or metastatic solid tumor with a TP53 Y220C mutation found by an NGS test.
Patients with castration-resistant prostate cancer must be on ongoing androgen deprivation therapy or be surgically or medically castrated.
Life expectancy of at least 3 months as assessed by the investigator, with adequate organ function.
not_for: Ovarian, breast, lung, or endometrial tumor patients eligible for the PYNNACLE trial, unless that cohort is closed.
Anticancer therapy within 21 days or 5 half-lives, or radiotherapy within 14 days, before first dose.
Known significant allergy or hypersensitivity to rezatapopt, metformin, rosuvastatin, repaglinide, or midazolam.
Untreated brain or leptomeningeal metastases, spinal cord compression, or stroke or TIA within 6 months.
Uncontrolled heart disease, QTcF above 470 msec, uncontrolled hypertension, or a known KRAS SNV mutation.

NCT07154290.summary_en: This Phase 2 study tests ubamatamab with and without marlotamig (REGN7075) in adults with advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer. Both drugs are given as described in the protocol, and sarilumab is also given to help with immune-related side effects of ubamatamab; how often and for how long treatment lasts is not stated. The record does not state a primary outcome measure, but it says the study looks at how well the drugs work, their side effects, their levels in the blood, and antibodies against them.
NCT07154290.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 evalúa ubamatamab con y sin marlotamig (REGN7075) en adultos con cáncer de pulmón de células no pequeñas avanzado o metastásico. Ambos fármacos se administran según lo descrito en el protocolo, y también se administra sarilumab para ayudar con los efectos secundarios relacionados con el sistema inmunitario causados por ubamatamab; la frecuencia y la duración del tratamiento no se indican. El registro no indica una medida de resultado principal, pero señala que el estudio analiza qué tan bien actúan los fármacos, sus efectos secundarios, sus niveles en la sangre y los anticuerpos contra ellos.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older with advanced or metastatic NSCLC (stage IIIB not suitable for chemoradiotherapy, stage IIIC, or stage IV).
Received appropriate first-line standard treatment for advanced or metastatic NSCLC, as described in the protocol.
Has tumor tissue available for MUC16 testing by immunohistochemistry.
Has at least one radiographically measurable lesion by CT or MRI per RECIST v1.1.
ECOG performance status of 0 or 1.
not_for: Disease progressed fewer than 84 days after starting first anti-PD-(L)1 therapy.
Toxicity from prior treatment not resolved to grade 1 before starting study treatment (with listed exceptions).
Untreated or active primary brain tumor, CNS metastases, leptomeningeal disease, or spinal cord compression.
Investigational drug given within 4 weeks before the first study dose, or current participation in another investigational study.
Anti-EGFR antibody therapy within the drug-specific window before the first study dose.

NCT07253662.summary_en: This phase 1 trial tests pressurized intraperitoneal aerosolized chemotherapy (PIPAC) with nab-paclitaxel in patients with pancreatic adenocarcinoma that has spread to the peritoneum. Nab-paclitaxel is delivered into the abdomen during a laparoscopic procedure and stays in contact with the peritoneum for 30 minutes, with up to three procedures given every six weeks. The main stated aim is to confirm the safety of PIPAC with nab-paclitaxel.
NCT07253662.summary_es: Este ensayo de fase 1 evalúa la quimioterapia aerosolizada intraperitoneal presurizada (PIPAC) con nab-paclitaxel en pacientes con adenocarcinoma de páncreas que se ha diseminado al peritoneo. El nab-paclitaxel se administra en la cavidad abdominal durante un procedimiento laparoscópico y permanece en contacto con el peritoneo durante 30 minutos, con hasta tres procedimientos cada seis semanas. El objetivo principal indicado es confirmar la seguridad de PIPAC con nab-paclitaxel.
who_for: Adults 18 or older with pancreatic adenocarcinoma and suspected or confirmed peritoneal spread.
ECOG performance status of 2 or better.
Blood counts, liver tests and kidney function within the limits listed in the record.
Peritoneal disease visible on cross-sectional imaging or diagnostic laparoscopy.
Laparoscopy shows feasible access, room for aerosol, no impending bowel obstruction, under 5 L ascites, and not a candidate for cytoreduction and HIPEC.
not_for: Confirmed or suspected spread outside the peritoneum.
Bowel obstruction needing a feeding tube or total parenteral nutrition.
Life expectancy under 4 months, or prior intra-abdominal aerosol chemotherapy.
Prior anaphylactic reaction to nab-paclitaxel, or ascites over 5 L.
Uncontrolled illness, immune compromise, other investigational agents, or pregnancy.

NCT04511013.summary_en: This phase 2 study compares encorafenib, binimetinib and nivolumab with ipilimumab and nivolumab in BRAF V600 mutant melanoma that has spread to the brain. Encorafenib and binimetinib are taken by mouth, and nivolumab is given by IV on day 1 of each cycle. In the other arm, ipilimumab is given by IV on day 1 of cycles 1 to 4, with cycles repeating every 21 days for 4 cycles and then every 28 days, while disease does not progress or toxicity is not unacceptable.
NCT04511013.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 compara encorafenib, binimetinib y nivolumab con ipilimumab y nivolumab en melanoma con mutación BRAF V600 que se ha diseminado al cerebro. Encorafenib y binimetinib se toman por vía oral, y nivolumab se administra por vía intravenosa el día 1 de cada ciclo. En el otro brazo, ipilimumab se administra por vía intravenosa el día 1 de los ciclos 1 a 4, y los ciclos se repiten cada 21 días durante 4 ciclos y luego cada 28 días, mientras la enfermedad no progrese ni la toxicidad sea inaceptable. El estudio busca saber qué enfoque es más eficaz para reducir y controlar las metástasis cerebrales.
who_for: Melanoma with BRAF V600 mutation confirmed by a CLIA-certified laboratory.
Melanoma that has spread to the brain, with at least one brain lesion 0.5 cm or larger.
Brain lesion not irradiated, or progressed after prior radiation, per treating physician.
Zubrod performance status of 2 or less.
Age 18 years or older.
not_for: Uveal melanoma as the primary site.
Prior systemic therapy for metastatic disease; neoadjuvant or adjuvant therapy is allowed.
Radiation therapy within 7 days before randomization.
Pregnant or nursing, or not willing to use effective contraception; hormonal contraceptives are not allowed.
Serious active infection needing systemic therapy, or certain autoimmune disease treated with biologics in the past 6 months.

NCT05847569.summary_en: This phase 2 trial tests alternate doses and dosing schedules of belantamab mafodotin in adults with recurrent or refractory, triple-class refractory multiple myeloma. The drug is given intravenously (IV) on day 1 of each cycle, and cycles repeat every 6 weeks if the disease does not progress and side effects are acceptable; one arm repeats the next cycle at 3 weeks before moving to every 6 weeks. The main outcome measure is not stated in the record; this is a phase 2 trial.
NCT05847569.summary_es: Este ensayo de fase 2 evalúa dosis y esquemas de administración alternativos de belantamab mafodotina en adultos con mieloma múltiple recurrente o refractario, refractario a tres clases de tratamiento. El medicamento se administra por vena (IV) el día 1 de cada ciclo, y los ciclos se repiten cada 6 semanas si la enfermedad no progresa y los efectos secundarios son aceptables; en un brazo, el siguiente ciclo se repite a las 3 semanas y luego cada 6 semanas. El resultado principal no se indica en el registro; es un ensayo de fase 2.
who_for: Age 18 years or older.
ECOG performance status 0, 1 or 2.
Multiple myeloma that progressed after at least 3 prior lines, including a proteasome inhibitor, an immunomodulatory agent, and an anti-CD38 antibody.
Measurable disease by serum or urine M-protein, or by free light chain levels.
Blood counts, liver tests and kidney function within the required limits, checked within 28 days before registration.
not_for: Prior belantamab mafodotin therapy.
Active plasma cell leukemia, symptomatic amyloidosis, active POEMS syndrome, or Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia.
Unresolved toxicity grade 2 or higher from previous treatment, except alopecia or neuropathy up to grade 2.
Other cancer, unless considered medically stable for more than 2 years or curatively treated nonmelanoma skin cancer.
Current corneal epithelial disease, except mild punctuate keratopathy.

NCT05064280.summary_en: This Phase II study tests pembrolizumab given with lenvatinib in patients with solid tumors that have spread to the brain, including triple negative breast cancer, non-small cell lung cancer, and other solid tumor types. Pembrolizumab is given by IV at 200 mg on day 1 every 3 weeks, and lenvatinib is taken by mouth at 20 mg once daily; the total duration is not stated. The main outcome measured is intracranial objective response rate, assessed by modified RECIST v1.1.
NCT05064280.summary_es: Este estudio de fase II evalúa pembrolizumab combinado con lenvatinib en pacientes con tumores sólidos que se han diseminado al cerebro, incluidos cáncer de mama triple negativo, cáncer de pulmón de células no pequeñas y otros tipos de tumores sólidos. El pembrolizumab se administra por vía intravenosa a 200 mg el día 1 cada 3 semanas, y el lenvatinib se toma por vía oral a 20 mg una vez al día; la duración total no se indica. El resultado principal que se mide es la tasa de respuesta objetiva intracraneal, evaluada con RECIST v1.1 modificado.
who_for: Age 18 years or older with confirmed triple negative breast cancer, non-small cell lung cancer, or another solid tumor
Brain metastases, with or without active disease outside the brain
At least one measurable brain metastasis of 0.5 to 3 cm on MRI
ECOG performance status of 0 or 1
Life expectancy of at least 12 weeks
not_for: Non-small cell lung cancer with certain oncogenic driver mutations or fusions (such as EGFR, ALK, or MET amplification)
Hepatocellular carcinoma
Prior lenvatinib or other antiangiogenic tyrosine kinase inhibitor, alone or with a PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor
Leptomeningeal metastases or symptomatic spinal cord compression
Known HIV, or active tuberculosis

NCT06678659.summary_en: The study tests REC-1245, a drug taken by mouth, in people with unresectable, locally advanced, or metastatic cancer, including certain relapsed or refractory lymphomas. REC-1245 is taken by mouth once a day, and the length of treatment is not stated. The study measures safety, tolerability, how the body processes the drug, its effects on the body, and early activity against cancer; it is a Phase 1/2 study.
NCT06678659.summary_es: El estudio evalúa REC-1245, un medicamento por vía oral, en personas con cáncer no resecable, localmente avanzado o metastásico, incluidos ciertos linfomas recidivantes o refractarios. REC-1245 se toma por vía oral una vez al día, y la duración del tratamiento no se indica. El estudio mide la seguridad, la tolerancia, cómo el cuerpo procesa el medicamento, sus efectos en el organismo y la actividad temprana contra el cáncer; es un estudio de fase 1/2.
who_for: Has histologically confirmed unresectable, locally advanced, or metastatic select solid tumor or select relapsed or refractory lymphoma
Has progressed, relapsed, or was intolerant to at least one standard systemic cancer treatment, or was considered ineligible for standard therapy
ECOG performance status of 1 or lower; adolescents need a Lansky or Karnofsky score of 70 or higher
Has measurable disease at baseline on CT and/or MRI per RECIST 1.1 or Lugano criteria
not_for: Received treatment with another RBM39 degrader
Has clinically significant gastrointestinal disease or gastrointestinal malabsorption

NCT07015242.summary_en: This Phase 2 study tests lisocabtagene maraleucel (liso-cel, also called Breyanzi) as first-line treatment for adults with primary central nervous system lymphoma who are not eligible for a transplant. The record lists study drugs given at specified doses on specified days, but the route, length of treatment and frequency are not stated. The main outcome measure is not stated in the record.
NCT07015242.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 evalúa lisocabtagene maraleucel (liso-cel, también llamado Breyanzi) como tratamiento de primera línea para adultos con linfoma primario del sistema nervioso central que no son elegibles para un trasplante. El registro indica medicamentos del estudio en dosis específicas en días específicos, pero la vía, la duración del tratamiento y la frecuencia no se indican. El registro no indica la medida de resultado principal.
who_for: Adults 18 or older with histologically confirmed primary CNS lymphoma.
Not eligible for transplant per physician assessment, with age 65 or older or HCT-CI score of 3 or more.
Suitable, per investigator, for high-dose methotrexate-based treatment.
Disease responded to prior high-dose methotrexate, with complete or partial response.
ECOG performance status of 0, 1, or 2, with no prior experimental treatment for PCNSL.
not_for: Secondary CNS lymphoma caused by systemic disease.
Primary intraocular or vitreoretinal lymphoma, isolated CSF disease, or relapsed or refractory PCNSL.
Another cancer not in remission for at least 2 years, with listed exceptions.
Prior CAR T-cell or other genome-editing gene therapy, HIV, or active hepatitis B or C.
Active autoimmune disease needing immunosuppression, or prior allogeneic or solid organ transplant needing immunosuppression.

NCT07210086.summary_en: This phase II study looks at PSMA-PET scans and circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) to monitor prostate cancer that has spread to a few sites, after radiation aimed at those sites. Patients receive ablative-intent radiation therapy to all sites of metastatic disease, and some also receive androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) and an androgen receptor signaling inhibitor (ARSI); how often and how long are not stated. The study measures PSMA-PET responses at 6 and 12 months, how they relate to PSA changes and later progression, and ctDNA changes; the primary outcome is not stated.
NCT07210086.summary_es: Este estudio de fase II analiza las imágenes PSMA-PET y el ADN tumoral circulante (ctDNA) para vigilar el cáncer de próstata que se ha extendido a pocos sitios, después de radioterapia dirigida a esos sitios. Los pacientes reciben radioterapia con intención ablativa en todos los sitios de enfermedad metastásica, y algunos también reciben terapia de privación androgénica (ADT) y un inhibidor de la vía de señalización del receptor de andrógenos (ARSI); la frecuencia y la duración no se indican. El estudio mide las respuestas en PSMA-PET a los 6 y 12 meses, su relación con los cambios de PSA y la progresión posterior, y los cambios en el ctDNA; el resultado principal no se indica.
who_for: Adults 18 or older with KPS 70 or higher, or ECOG 0-1.
Biopsy-confirmed castration-sensitive prostate adenocarcinoma with rising PSA.
De novo or hormone-sensitive oligometastatic or oligoprogressive disease with up to five sites outside the pelvis.
Measurable disease and eligible for ablative-intent radiation to all metastatic sites.
Agreement to use effective birth control if of childbearing potential.
not_for: Planning lifelong continuous or intermittent ADT.
More than 3 months of neoadjuvant ADT before consent for the current course.
Polymetastatic or polyprogressive disease, or metastases in brain or liver.
Active HIV, chronic hepatitis B, or hepatitis C infection, unless the listed treatment or viral control conditions are met.
Contraindication to flotufolastat F 18 or PSMA-PET, or other active malignancy that could interfere with study assessments.

NCT03886662.summary_en: The study tests LB-100, a drug given by vein, in adults with low or intermediate-1 risk myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS). LB-100 is given through an intravenous infusion over 120 minutes on days 1, 3 and 5 of each 21-day cycle. The record does not state the main outcome; it is a Phase 1 and Phase 2 study that looks at safety and effectiveness.
NCT03886662.summary_es: El estudio prueba LB-100, un medicamento que se administra por vena, en adultos con síndromes mielodisplásicos (SMD) de riesgo bajo o intermedio-1. LB-100 se administra como infusión intravenosa durante 120 minutos los días 1, 3 y 5 de cada ciclo de 21 días. El registro no indica el resultado principal; es un estudio de Fase 1 y Fase 2 que evalúa la seguridad y la eficacia.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older who sign the informed consent form.
Diagnosed with MDS or MDS/MPN that needs treatment for low blood counts, low or intermediate-1 risk by IPSS.
Disease progressed or not tolerated after at least 2 cycles of azacitidine, decitabine, or lenalidomide (lenalidomide only for del(5q) patients).
ECOG performance status of 0, 1, or 2.
Adequate kidney function (creatinine clearance 60 mL/min or higher) and liver lab values as defined in the record.
not_for: Known HIV infection.
Symptomatic heart failure, heart attack within 6 months, unstable angina, serious uncontrolled arrhythmia, or QTcF 450 msec or higher.
Other cancer diagnosed within the past year, with limited exceptions for resected skin cancers or carcinoma in situ.
Chemotherapy or experimental agents for MDS within 14 days before the first study dose, or ongoing growth factors such as ESAs, G-CSF, or GM-CSF.
Pregnant or breastfeeding.

NCT07228442.summary_en: This phase 2 study tests L19IL2/L19TNF, given into tumors, in people with locally advanced cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (a skin cancer) who have progressed on or cannot tolerate immune checkpoint inhibitor treatment. The drug is injected into all injectable skin and subcutaneous lesions once weekly for up to 4 weeks, and a second 4-week course may be given if the best response is partial response or stable disease, per the treating physician. The main stated objective is to evaluate the activity of the treatment; the specific outcome measure is not stated, and patients are followed for up to 160 weeks.
NCT07228442.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 evalúa L19IL2/L19TNF, administrado dentro de los tumores, en personas con carcinoma cutáneo de células escamosas localmente avanzado (un cáncer de piel) que progresaron con un inhibidor de puntos de control inmunitario o que no lo toleran. El medicamento se inyecta en todas las lesiones cutáneas y subcutáneas inyectables una vez por semana, durante hasta 4 semanas, y se puede administrar un segundo ciclo de 4 semanas si la mejor respuesta es respuesta parcial o enfermedad estable, según el criterio del médico tratante. El objetivo principal indicado es evaluar la actividad del tratamiento; la medida específica de resultado no se indica, y los pacientes son seguidos hasta 160 semanas.
who_for: Locally advanced skin squamous cell carcinoma that progressed on or cannot be tolerated with immune checkpoint inhibitor treatment
At least one injectable, measurable skin or subcutaneous lesion
Age 18 or older with ECOG/WHO performance status of 2 or less
Willing to provide tumor biopsy tissue at screening and for response confirmation
not_for: Radiation therapy to tumor sites within 4 weeks before study drug
Current topical or systemic chemotherapy or immunotherapy
Visceral metastasis
Known allergy to IL2, TNF, or other human proteins, peptides, or antibodies
Pregnancy or breast-feeding

NCT06730542.summary_en: This Phase 1 study is testing zanubrutinib added to Pola-R-CHP and high-dose methotrexate in adults with secondary central nervous system lymphoma. Zanubrutinib is taken by mouth as capsules, starting at 160 mg twice a day or 320 mg once a day at the beginning of Cycle 2 of Pola-R-CHP, and participants are in the study for up to 2 years. The record does not state a main outcome measure; it lists the study as Phase 1.
NCT06730542.summary_es: Este estudio de Fase 1 evalúa zanubrutinib añadido a Pola-R-CHP y metotrexato en dosis altas en adultos con linfoma secundario del sistema nervioso central. El zanubrutinib se toma por vía oral en cápsulas, comenzando con 160 mg dos veces al día o 320 mg una vez al día al inicio del Ciclo 2 de Pola-R-CHP, y los participantes permanecen en el estudio hasta 2 años. El registro no indica una medida de resultado principal; figura como estudio de Fase 1.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older.
Large B-cell lymphoma confirmed by histology under WHO classification.
Lymphoma involving both systemic sites and the central nervous system at presentation.
ECOG performance status of 2 or less, except when caused by lymphoma.
Life expectancy greater than 3 months.
not_for: Primary CNS lymphoma without evidence of systemic lymphoma.
Prior systemic lymphoma therapy, including anthracycline-based regimens, with exceptions listed in the record.
Uncontrolled or clinically significant heart disease, including recent heart attack or QTcF above 450 msec.
Active HIV or hepatitis B or C infection, with exceptions listed in the record.
Pregnancy, breastfeeding, or current treatment with strong CYP3A inducers.

NCT06868277.summary_en: This Phase III study compares rilvegostomig with pembrolizumab, each given alone as first-line treatment, in people with PD-L1-high metastatic non-small cell lung cancer. Both drugs are given by intravenous infusion on Day 1 of each 21-day cycle, and the total duration is not stated. The study's stated purpose is to assess efficacy and safety; a specific primary outcome is not stated.
NCT06868277.summary_es: Este estudio de fase III compara rilvegostomig con pembrolizumab, administrados cada uno por separado como tratamiento de primera línea, en personas con cáncer de pulmón de células no pequeñas metastásico con PD-L1 alto. Ambos medicamentos se administran por infusión intravenosa el día 1 de cada ciclo de 21 días, y la duración total no se indica. El objetivo declarado del estudio es evaluar la eficacia y la seguridad; no se indica un resultado principal específico.
who_for: Stage IV non-small cell lung cancer not amenable to curative treatment.
No sensitizing EGFR mutations and no ALK or ROS1 rearrangements.
WHO/ECOG performance status of 0 or 1 without recent decline.
Life expectancy of at least 12 weeks.
At least one measurable lesion not previously irradiated.
not_for: Small cell or neuroendocrine histology components.
Any prior systemic therapy for advanced or metastatic lung cancer.
Any prior anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1, or anti-TIGIT therapy.
Brain metastases unless asymptomatic and stable without steroids or anticonvulsants for 4 weeks.
Autoimmune or inflammatory disorder needing chronic steroids or immunosuppressive treatment, or a history of organ transplant.

NCT06495125.summary_en: This study tests defactinib and avutometinib given with nivolumab in patients with advanced lung adenocarcinoma that has an LKB1 mutation and did not respond to anti-PD1 treatment. Defactinib is taken by mouth twice a day on days 1 to 21, avutometinib is taken by mouth twice a week for 21 days, and nivolumab is given through a vein on day 1 of each 28-day cycle, repeated while the disease does not progress and side effects are acceptable. The main outcome is not stated in the record; this is a Phase 2 study.
NCT06495125.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa defactinib y avutometinib administrados junto con nivolumab en pacientes con adenocarcinoma de pulmón avanzado que tiene una mutación de LKB1 y no respondió al tratamiento anti-PD1. El defactinib se toma por vía oral dos veces al día los días 1 al 21, el avutometinib se toma por vía oral dos veces por semana durante 21 días, y el nivolumab se administra por vena el día 1 de cada ciclo de 28 días, que se repite mientras la enfermedad no progrese y los efectos secundarios sean aceptables. El resultado principal no se indica en el registro; este es un estudio de Fase 2.
who_for: Advanced lung adenocarcinoma that is not suitable for surgery or combined modality treatment.
Known LKB1 mutation confirmed in the tumor.
Disease that progressed after immune checkpoint inhibitor and first-line chemotherapy.
Measurable disease, age 18 or older, and ECOG performance status 0 or 1.
Adequate blood counts, liver function, kidney function, and recovery from prior treatment side effects.
not_for: Known treatable driver mutation with an FDA-approved targeted therapy, such as EGFR, ALK, or ROS1 (KRAS excepted).
Unstable or symptomatic brain metastasis, or known leptomeningeal disease.
Pre-existing autoimmune condition with higher risk from nivolumab, or serious autoimmune toxicity with prior checkpoint inhibitor.
Active hepatitis B, hepatitis C, or HIV infection that is active or needs therapy.
Pregnant or breastfeeding, current warfarin use, or history of rhabdomyolysis.

NCT06073067.summary_en: The study tests GRID radiation therapy given before standard radiation and surgery in adults with resectable extremity soft tissue sarcoma. A single priming dose of GRID is given before conventional radiotherapy (XRT) and tumor resection; the duration of XRT is not stated.
