Immunosuppression, including HIV, active hepatitis B or C, or steroids above 10 mg/day prednisone equivalent
Prior IMLYGIC or GM-CSF treatment, or MEK inhibitor use within 6 months
Open herpetic skin lesions or ongoing anti-herpetic treatment
QTc interval above 470 msec or other conditions the investigator judges unsafe

NCT05832086.summary_en: This Phase 2 study compares a fasting mimicking diet with a usual diet in men with metastatic castrate sensitive prostate adenocarcinoma. Participants eat the fasting mimicking diet for 5 days each month for 6 monthly cycles, and all participants receive standard prostate cancer treatment. The study aims to examine effects on response to cancer treatment and metabolic outcomes, and the main outcome measure is not stated.
NCT05832086.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 compara una dieta que imita el ayuno con una dieta habitual en hombres con adenocarcinoma de próstata metastásico sensible a la castración. Los participantes consumen la dieta que imita el ayuno durante 5 días cada mes, en 6 ciclos mensuales, y todos reciben el tratamiento estándar para el cáncer de próstata. El estudio busca examinar los efectos en la respuesta al tratamiento del cáncer y en los resultados metabólicos, y la medida principal de resultado no está indicada en el registro.
who_for: Prostate adenocarcinoma that is metastatic and castrate sensitive, confirmed by biopsy, with metastatic disease confirmed by biopsy or MRI.
Starting or receiving first-line intensified hormone therapy with abiraterone, apalutamide, enzalutamide, or darolutamide, with or without chemotherapy.
Reads, writes, and understands English or Spanish, and has telephone access for contact with the study dietitian.
Able to give written informed consent and comply with study requirements.
not_for: Allergy to any ingredient on the Xentigen ingredient list.
Diabetes without stable diabetes medicine for 6 months, and without physician consent to hold it during fasting days.
Significant heart, lung, or liver disease, or ongoing alcohol or drug abuse, per the study physician.
BMI under 20, actively trying to lose weight, on weight loss medicine, or planning weight loss surgery in the next 6 months.
Self-reported weight loss of 10% or more in the last 6 months.

NCT07446322.summary_en: This study tests adding pelareorep to FOLFIRI and bevacizumab as second-line treatment for metastatic, RAS-mutated, microsatellite-stable colorectal cancer. Pelareorep, FOLFIRI and bevacizumab are given by intravenous infusion, and how long or how often is not stated. The main outcome is not stated; this is a Phase 2 study that assesses efficacy and safety.
NCT07446322.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa el efecto de agregar pelareorep a FOLFIRI y bevacizumab como tratamiento de segunda línea para cáncer colorrectal metastásico con mutación RAS y sin inestabilidad de microsatélites. Pelareorep, FOLFIRI y bevacizumab se administran por infusión intravenosa, y la duración o la frecuencia no se indican en el registro. El resultado principal no se indica; es un estudio de fase 2 que evalúa la eficacia y la seguridad.
who_for: Metastatic colon or rectal cancer with measurable disease
Not candidates for curative surgery or curative radiation
Progressed on or intolerant to first-line oxaliplatin-based chemotherapy, or relapsed within 6 months of adjuvant oxaliplatin
Tumor has a RAS mutation and is not MSI-H or dMMR
Age 18 or older, ECOG performance status 0 or 1
not_for: Prior treatment with irinotecan
Symptomatic brain metastases
Ongoing side effects of grade 2 or higher from recent cancer treatment
Active autoimmune disease or use of immunosuppressive medicines
Another primary cancer in the last 3 years, with stated exceptions

NCT03099356.summary_en: This trial tests cyclophosphamide and sirolimus together in adults with metastatic, radioactive iodine (RAI)-refractory differentiated thyroid cancer. Both drugs are taken by mouth: sirolimus 4 mg on days 1 to 28, and cyclophosphamide 100 mg on days 1 to 5 and 15 to 19 of each 28-day cycle, with imaging once every 2 cycles. Patients are monitored for side effects and imaging is used to evaluate efficacy, but the main outcome measure is not stated; this is a Phase 2 pilot trial.
NCT03099356.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa cyclophosphamide y sirolimus juntos en adultos con cáncer de tiroides diferenciado metastásico y refractario al yodo radiactivo (RAI). Ambos medicamentos se toman por vía oral: sirolimus 4 mg los días 1 a 28, y cyclophosphamide 100 mg los días 1 a 5 y 15 a 19 de cada ciclo de 28 días, con imágenes una vez cada 2 ciclos. Los pacientes son vigilados por efectos secundarios y se usan imágenes para evaluar la eficacia, pero la medida principal de resultado no se indica en el registro; es un estudio piloto de fase 2.
who_for: Differentiated thyroid cancer that has spread or cannot be cured with standard treatment, or patient declines curative treatment.
Measurable disease larger than 10 mm that has grown based on RECIST criteria.
Prior radioactive iodine (131I) treatment failure, or not a candidate for it as judged by the treating doctor.
Age 18 or older with ECOG performance status 0 to 2.
Life expectancy of at least 12 weeks.
not_for: Previous treatment with an mTOR inhibitor.
Chemotherapy, tyrosine kinase inhibitor, or radiation therapy within 4 weeks.
Radioactive iodine (131I) therapy within 24 weeks before entry.
No prior next generation sequencing, and unable to get FoundationOne testing on archival tissue.
Pregnant or breast-feeding women.

NCT05552222.summary_en: This Phase 3 study compares teclistamab with daratumumab and lenalidomide, and talquetamab with daratumumab and lenalidomide, against daratumumab, lenalidomide and dexamethasone. It is for people with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma who are not candidates for high-dose chemotherapy with stem cell transplant as first treatment. Teclistamab, talquetamab and daratumumab are given as subcutaneous injections, lenalidomide is taken by mouth, and dexamethasone is given by mouth or intravenously; how long or how often is not stated. The record does not name a main outcome measure; its stated purpose is to compare efficacy.
NCT05552222.summary_es: Este estudio de Fase 3 compara teclistamab con daratumumab y lenalidomida, y talquetamab con daratumumab y lenalidomida, frente a daratumumab, lenalidomida y dexametasona. Está dirigido a personas con mieloma múltiple recién diagnosticado que no son candidatas a quimioterapia de altas dosis con trasplante de células madre como tratamiento inicial. Teclistamab, talquetamab y daratumumab se administran como inyecciones subcutáneas, la lenalidomida se toma por vía oral y la dexametasona se administra por vía oral o intravenosa; la duración o frecuencia no se indica. El registro no menciona una medida de resultado principal; su objetivo declarado es comparar la eficacia.
who_for: Newly diagnosed multiple myeloma, per IMWG criteria
Not a candidate for high-dose chemotherapy with stem cell transplant due to older age, other health conditions, or a planned deferral
ECOG performance status 0 to 2
Age 18 years or older
Agrees not to become pregnant, breastfeed, or father a child during the study and for a set period after the last dose
not_for: Prior therapy for multiple myeloma or smoldering myeloma, other than a short corticosteroid course within set limits
Myeloma Frailty Index of 2 or more (a score of 2 from age alone is allowed)
Stroke, transient ischemic attack, or seizure within 6 months before randomization
Known allergy or intolerance to teclistamab or talquetamab ingredients
Known contraindication to daratumumab or lenalidomide

NCT06795022.summary_en: This Phase 1/2 study is testing AZD9793, a T cell-engaging antibody that targets GPC3, in adults with GPC3-positive advanced or metastatic solid tumours; the registered condition is hepatocellular carcinoma. It is given as an intravenous (IV) infusion or as a subcutaneous (SC) injection, and how long or how often is not stated. The study aims to determine whether the treatment is safe, tolerable and has anti-cancer activity.
NCT06795022.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1/2 evalúa AZD9793, un anticuerpo que activa las células T y se dirige a GPC3, en adultos con tumores sólidos avanzados o metastásicos que son positivos para GPC3; el tipo de cáncer registrado es carcinoma hepatocelular. Se administra por vía intravenosa (IV) en infusión o por vía subcutánea (SC) en inyección; la duración o la frecuencia no se indica en el registro. El estudio busca determinar si el tratamiento es seguro, tolerable y tiene actividad contra el cáncer.
who_for: Adults aged 18 years or older.
Confirmed advanced, metastatic or unresectable liver cancer (HCC), proven by pathology.
Tumour tests GPC3 positive by central laboratory testing.
BCLC stage B (not eligible for locoregional therapy) or stage C, with Child-Pugh class A.
ECOG 0-1 and predicted life expectancy of 12 weeks or more.
not_for: Unresolved toxicity from prior cancer therapy at grade 2 or higher, with listed exceptions.
CAR-T cell therapy within the last 6 months.
Requires chronic immunosuppressive therapy, including prednisone above 10 mg daily.
Radiation within 14 days or major surgery within 14 days before first dose.
History of HLH or MAS, or a thromboembolic event within the past 3 months.

NCT07740941.summary_en: This Phase 2 study tests two PD-1-based immunotherapy regimens given before surgery (neoadjuvant) in patients with resectable stage IIIB to stage IV (M1a) melanoma, either cutaneous or of unknown primary. Patients are randomized to pembrolizumab 200 mg IV every 3 weeks for two infusions, or to one infusion of ipilimumab (3 mg/kg) plus nivolumab (1 mg/kg), followed by one infusion of nivolumab 240 mg IV 3 weeks later; both arms then have lymph node dissection and no adjuvant treatment. The study measures overall survival at 24 months, and event-free survival at 12 months.
NCT07740941.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 evalúa dos regímenes de inmunoterapia basados en PD-1 administrados antes de la cirugía (neoadyuvantes) en pacientes con melanoma resecable en estadio IIIB a estadio IV (M1a), de origen cutáneo o de origen primario desconocido. Los pacientes se asignan al azar a pembrolizumab 200 mg por vía IV cada 3 semanas, en dos infusiones, o a una infusión de ipilimumab (3 mg/kg) más nivolumab (1 mg/kg), seguida de una infusión de nivolumab 240 mg por vía IV 3 semanas después; en ambos brazos se realiza luego la disección de ganglios linfáticos y no se da tratamiento adyuvante. El estudio mide la supervivencia global a 24 meses y la supervivencia libre de eventos a 12 meses.
who_for: Age 18 years or older.
ECOG performance status of 0 to 2.
Confirmed cutaneous melanoma or melanoma of unknown primary.
AJCC stage IIIB or IVa disease that is resectable and measurable by iRECIST criteria.
Adequate blood, kidney, liver, and heart function.
not_for: Prior treatment with PD-1 and CTLA-4 inhibitors.
Active autoimmune disease needing systemic disease-modifying or immunosuppressive drugs.
Any condition the investigator judges to place the patient at unacceptable risk, including conditions that would interfere with participation.

NCT06529523.summary_en: This Phase 2 study tests tislelizumab, a PD-1 blocking drug, in people with mismatch repair deficient (dMMR) colorectal cancer who live in Nigeria. Tislelizumab is given as an IV infusion of 200 mg every 3 weeks, with the first infusion over 60 minutes and later ones over 30 minutes, until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, withdrawal, death, or completion of 104 weeks (35 doses). The record does not state a primary outcome measure, but says the study will look at whether the drug is effective and at its safety.
NCT06529523.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 evalúa tislelizumab, un fármaco que bloquea PD-1, en personas con cáncer colorrectal con deficiencia en la reparación de errores de apareamiento (dMMR) que viven en Nigeria. El tislelizumab se administra por vía intravenosa a 200 mg cada 3 semanas; la primera infusión dura 60 minutos y las siguientes 30 minutos, hasta progresión de la enfermedad, toxicidad inaceptable, retiro del estudio, muerte o completar 104 semanas (35 dosis). El registro no indica una medida de resultado principal, pero señala que el estudio analizará si el fármaco es eficaz y su seguridad.
who_for: Age 18 years or older
ECOG performance status of 0 or 1
No prior treatment for the cancer, with dMMR colorectal cancer confirmed by immunohistochemistry
Metastatic disease not eligible for curative surgery, or stage II or III rectal cancer without distant spread
Adequate blood, kidney, liver and clotting test results within 14 days of start
not_for: Other active malignancy
Prior immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy, or prior grade 3 or higher immune-related side effects
Active autoimmune disease needing systemic therapy within the past 2 years
History of interstitial lung disease, noninfectious pneumonitis, or uncontrolled lung disease
Recent heart or blood vessel events (such as heart attack or stroke within 6 months), or pregnancy or breastfeeding

NCT06662786.summary_en: This Phase 3 study compares amivantamab plus mFOLFOX6 or FOLFIRI with cetuximab plus mFOLFOX6 or FOLFIRI as first-line treatment for unresectable or metastatic left-sided colorectal cancer in adults whose tumors are KRAS/NRAS and BRAF wild-type. Participants receive treatment in 28-day cycles and continue until radiographic disease progression or other discontinuation criteria are met; the route of administration is not stated. The study measures progression-free survival, meaning how long participants remain disease-free.
NCT06662786.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 3 compara amivantamab más mFOLFOX6 o FOLFIRI con cetuximab más mFOLFOX6 o FOLFIRI como tratamiento de primera línea para el cáncer colorrectal del lado izquierdo, no resecable o metastásico, en adultos con tumores de tipo silvestre para KRAS/NRAS y BRAF. Los participantes reciben el tratamiento en ciclos de 28 días y continúan hasta la progresión radiográfica de la enfermedad u otros criterios de suspensión; la vía de administración no se indica. El estudio mide la supervivencia libre de progresión, es decir, cuánto tiempo los participantes permanecen sin que la enfermedad avance.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older.
Adenocarcinoma of left-sided colorectal cancer that is unresectable or metastatic.
KRAS, NRAS, and BRAF wild-type tumor, by local and/or central testing.
Measurable disease per RECIST v1.1 and ECOG performance status 0 or 1.
No prior systemic therapy for unresectable or metastatic colorectal cancer; adjuvant or neoadjuvant therapy allowed if completed over 12 months before recurrenc
not_for: History or current interstitial lung disease, pneumonitis, or pulmonary fibrosis.
Known allergy or intolerance to amivantamab, cetuximab, or components of the chemotherapy regimens.
Prior or current second malignancy that could interfere with study endpoints or treatment.
Known dMMR/MSI-H status or HER2-positive/amplified tumor.
Prior exposure to agents targeting EGFR, MET, or VEGF.

NCT06040970.summary_en: This Phase 1/2 study tests sacituzumab govitecan given together with cisplatin in people with platinum-sensitive recurrent ovarian or endometrial cancer. Cisplatin is given by IV at 70 mg/m2, and sacituzumab govitecan is given at 7.5 mg/kg or 5 mg/kg; how often and for how long are not stated. The record does not state a primary outcome measure; its stated goal is to find the optimal dose of sacituzumab govitecan to use with cisplatin.
NCT06040970.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1/2 evalúa sacituzumab govitecan combinado con cisplatino en personas con cáncer de ovario o endometrio recurrente sensible al platino. El cisplatino se administra por vía intravenosa a 70 mg/m2, y el sacituzumab govitecan se administra a 7.5 mg/kg o 5 mg/kg; la frecuencia y la duración no se indican. El registro no indica una medida de resultado principal; su objetivo declarado es encontrar la dosis óptima de sacituzumab govitecan para usar con cisplatino.
who_for: Confirmed epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, peritoneal, or endometrial cancer that has recurred
Cancer progressed more than 6 months after the last platinum-based chemotherapy
Female, aged 18 or older
WHO performance status 0-1 and life expectancy of at least 12 weeks
Measurable disease on CT or PET/CT scan
not_for: Prior sacituzumab govitecan, irinotecan, or Trop-2 antibody drug conjugate treatment
Peripheral neuropathy grade 2 or greater
Known active brain metastases or carcinomatous meningitis
Pregnant or nursing
Active hepatitis B, hepatitis C, HIV, or other uncontrolled serious conditions

NCT06533579.summary_en: The study tests VNX-101, a gene therapy that carries instructions for a CD3/CD19 bi-specific T-cell engager, in adults and teens with relapsed or refractory CD19-positive leukemia or lymphoma. It is given as a single intravenous (IV) infusion at one of four dose levels, which are tested in escalating order. This Phase 1/2 study looks at safety, dose-finding, pharmacokinetics, and efficacy; a specific main outcome measure is not stated.
NCT06533579.summary_es: El estudio prueba VNX-101, una terapia génica que lleva instrucciones para un engager biespecífico de células T CD3/CD19, en adultos y adolescentes con leucemia o linfoma positivos para CD19 que recayeron o son refractarios. Se administra como una sola infusión intravenosa (IV) en uno de cuatro niveles de dosis, que se prueban en orden creciente. Este estudio de fase 1/2 evalúa la seguridad, la búsqueda de la dosis, la farmacocinética y la eficacia; no se indica una medida de resultado principal específica.
who_for: Age 18 to 90 years (Part 1) or 13 to 90 years (Part 2)
Relapsed or refractory CD19-positive leukemia or lymphoma, as defined in the protocol
CD19-positive expression
AAV antibody level within protocol-specified requirements
Kidney, liver, heart, lung, and blood count values within protocol-specified ranges
not_for: AST or ALT liver enzymes more than 2 times the upper limit of normal
History of thrombotic microangiopathy, cardiomyopathy, or sensory neuropathy
Pregnant or breastfeeding women
Acute GvHD grade 2 to 4, or chronic GvHD of any grade
History of hypersensitivity or toxicity related to corticosteroids; or chemotherapy within protocol-specified discontinuation timelines

NCT06768905.summary_en: This study tests 131I-Apamistamab, given before a CD19-targeted CAR-T cell therapy, in adults with relapsed or refractory diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (non-Hodgkin lymphoma). Patients receive a single 50 mCi dose of 131I-Apamistamab 5 to 7 days before a single CAR-T cell infusion. The main outcome is not stated; the record says the study aims to determine safety, efficacy and tolerability, and it is listed as Phase 1/Phase 2.
NCT06768905.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa 131I-Apamistamab, administrado antes de una terapia con células CAR-T dirigida a CD19, en adultos con linfoma difuso de células B grandes recidivante o refractario (linfoma no Hodgkin). Los pacientes reciben una dosis única de 50 mCi de 131I-Apamistamab de 5 a 7 días antes de una única infusión de células CAR-T. El resultado principal no se indica; el registro dice que el estudio busca determinar la seguridad, la eficacia y la tolerabilidad, y figura como Fase 1/Fase 2.
who_for: Relapsed or refractory DLBCL or high-grade B-cell lymphoma after at least one chemoimmunotherapy regimen that included an anthracycline and CD20-directed therap
Age 18 years or older.
Relapse or refractory disease confirmed by a repeat biopsy within the last 12 months.
ECOG performance status 0 to 2.
Considered a candidate for standard CAR-T therapy.
not_for: Pregnant or breastfeeding patients.
Heart function with LVEF below 40%.
Active autoimmune disease or active graft versus host disease needing systemic T-cell suppressive therapy.
Positive HIV, hepatitis B or hepatitis C test, with listed exceptions.
Prior treatment with radiopharmaceuticals for a lymphoma indication.

NCT03463954.summary_en: This study tests Novilase laser therapy, a device that destroys breast tumors using image-guided laser, in women with breast cancer tumors 15 mm or smaller. Each participant receives image-guided laser ablation of the targeted tumor through the skin, then an MRI and excision 4 to 6 weeks later. The main outcome is the rate of complete ablation, judged by pathology and MRI, compared with a performance goal of 80% based on lumpectomy.
NCT03463954.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa la terapia con láser Novilase, un dispositivo que destruye tumores de mama mediante láser guiado por imagen, en mujeres con tumores de cáncer de mama de 15 mm o menos. Cada participante recibe ablación con láser guiada por imagen del tumor objetivo, a través de la piel, y luego una resonancia magnética y una escisión a las 4 a 6 semanas. El resultado principal es la tasa de ablación completa, evaluada por patología y resonancia magnética, comparada con una meta de desempeño del 80 % basada en la lumpectomía.
who_for: Women aged 18 or older who can give written informed consent.
Single (unifocal) breast tumor no longer than 15 mm, confirmed by needle core biopsy.
Tumor clearly visible on ultrasound or mammography and on MRI.
Weight 300 lbs (136 kg) or less, with no significant comorbidities affecting life expectancy.
Agrees to follow standard radiation or adjuvant therapy as prescribed.
not_for: Pregnant or breast-feeding.
Contraindications to gadolinium contrast or MRI, or severe kidney disease.
Advanced stage breast cancer, or lobular, sarcoma, phyllodes, Paget's, or metastatic tumor.
Known BRCA positive, or triple-negative tumor (ER, PR and HER2 negative).
More than 25% intraductal component on core biopsy, or only DCIS with microinvasion.

NCT06590961.summary_en: This first-in-human Phase 1 study tests UBX-303061 in adults with relapsed or refractory B-cell malignancies. The drug is given by mouth (oral), and how long or how often it is given is not stated. The study evaluates safety and anti-cancer activity.
NCT06590961.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1, en humanos por primera vez, evalúa UBX-303061 en adultos con neoplasias de células B recidivantes o refractarias. El medicamento se administra por vía oral, y no se indica cuánto tiempo ni con qué frecuencia. El estudio evalúa la seguridad y la actividad anticáncer.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older who can give signed informed consent.
ECOG performance status 2 or better.
Relapsed or refractory B-cell malignancy after at least 2 prior therapies, or no available treatment options per the investigator.
Measurable or evaluable disease based on tumor type criteria.
Adequate organ and bone marrow function.
not_for: Previously treated with BTK degradation therapy.
CAR-T therapy within 100 days before study drug start.
Allogeneic stem cell transplant within 6 months, or active graft-versus-host disease.
Known hypersensitivity to BTK degraders or their ingredients.
Impaired cardiac function, clinically significant cardiac disease, or severe bleeding disorders.

NCT05643742.summary_en: The study tests CTX112, a donor-derived (allogeneic) T-cell therapy that uses CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing to target CD19, in adults with relapsed or refractory B-cell malignancies such as lymphomas and chronic lymphocytic leukemia/small lymphocytic lymphoma. CTX112 is given by IV infusion after lymphodepleting chemotherapy; how long or how often is not stated. The main outcome is not stated; this is a Phase 1/2 study of safety and efficacy.
NCT05643742.summary_es: El estudio evalúa CTX112, una terapia con células T de donante (alogénicas) editadas con CRISPR-Cas9 para atacar CD19, en adultos con neoplasias de células B recidivantes o refractarias, como linfomas y leucemia/linfoma linfocítico de células pequeñas. CTX112 se administra por infusión intravenosa después de quimioterapia de linfodepleción; la duración o la frecuencia no se indican. El resultado principal no se indica; es un estudio de Fase 1/2 de seguridad y eficacia.
who_for: Age 18 years or older.
Relapsed or refractory B-cell malignancy.
ECOG performance status 0 or 1.
Adequate kidney, liver, heart and lung function.
Agrees to use effective contraception from enrollment through at least 12 months after infusion.
not_for: Prior allogeneic stem cell transplant.
Cancer involvement of the central nervous system, now or in the past.
Seizure disorder, stroke or bleeding in the brain, dementia, cerebellar disease, or autoimmune disease affecting the central nervous system.
Uncontrolled infection, or active HIV, hepatitis B or hepatitis C.
Other cancer in the last 3 years (non-melanoma skin cancer excepted), or recent anticancer treatment, or immune deficiency or autoimmune disease needing immunos

NCT05909059.summary_en: This study tests a chemotherapy plan called lymphodepleting chemotherapy, given before CAR T cell therapy, in adults with multiple myeloma, lymphoma, or acute lymphoblastic leukemia who have moderate to severe kidney problems. Fludarabine and cyclophosphamide are given through an IV on days -5 to -3 before CAR T cell therapy, with doses lowered based on kidney function. The study is a Phase 2 study that assesses the feasibility of giving CAR T therapy with this dose-adjusted chemotherapy; the primary outcome measure is not stated.
NCT05909059.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa un plan de quimioterapia llamado quimioterapia linfodepletiva, administrada antes de la terapia con células CAR T, en adultos con mieloma múltiple, linfoma o leucemia linfoblástica aguda que tienen problemas renales de moderados a graves. La fludarabina y la ciclofosfamida se administran por vía intravenosa en los días -5 a -3 antes de la terapia con células CAR T, con dosis ajustadas según la función renal. Es un estudio de Fase 2 que evalúa la viabilidad de administrar la terapia CAR T con esta quimioterapia con dosis ajustadas; la medida de resultado principal no está indicada.
who_for: Receiving lymphodepleting chemotherapy before commercial CAR T therapy for multiple myeloma, leukemia, or lymphoma
Adequate bone marrow function to receive lymphodepleting chemotherapy
Renal function at or below 60 mL/min/1.73m2
ECOG performance status 0 to 2
not_for: Relative central nervous system disorders
Active uncontrolled infection or other condition the investigator judges would interfere with the study
Therapeutic-dose systemic corticosteroids (more than 20 mg/day prednisone or equivalent) within 72 hours of CAR T administration

NCT07516366.summary_en: This phase II trial tests botensilimab and balstilimab, two immunotherapy drugs given before surgery (neoadjuvant), in patients with high-risk, non-metastatic clear cell renal cell carcinoma. Botensilimab is given by IV over 30 minutes on day 1 of weeks 1 and 7, and balstilimab is given by IV over 30 minutes on day 1 of weeks 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, and 11, as long as the disease does not progress and side effects stay acceptable. Patients have a nephrectomy 12 to 16 weeks after starting treatment, and the study evaluates safety and feasibility as stated in the official title.
NCT07516366.summary_es: Este ensayo de fase II estudia botensilimab y balstilimab, dos medicamentos de inmunoterapia que se administran antes de la cirugía (neoadyuvancia), en pacientes con carcinoma de células renales de tipo células claras de alto riesgo y sin metástasis. El botensilimab se administra por vía intravenosa durante 30 minutos el día 1 de las semanas 1 y 7, y el balstilimab se administra por vía intravenosa durante 30 minutos el día 1 de las semanas 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 y 11, siempre que la enfermedad no progrese y los efectos secundarios sean aceptables. Los pacientes se someten a una nefrectomía entre 12 y 16 semanas después de iniciar el tratamiento, y el estudio evalúa la seguridad y la factibilidad, según se indica en el título oficial.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older
Biopsy-confirmed, non-metastatic, high-risk kidney cancer with a clear cell component
Scheduled for partial or radical nephrectomy with curative intent
ECOG performance status of 2 or better (or Karnofsky 60% or higher)
Adequate blood counts, liver, and kidney function as defined in the criteria
not_for: Suspected or proven metastatic renal cell carcinoma
Prior systemic therapy for renal cell carcinoma, or prior anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1, or anti-CTLA-4 treatment
Receiving other investigational agents
Pregnant or breastfeeding
QTcF above 480 ms, congenital long QT syndrome, or significant cardiac arrhythmia

NCT07237594.summary_en: This study tests secukinumab, an antibody that blocks IL-17A, in people with metastatic melanoma who had a past immune-related side effect from immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy and are restarting that therapy. Secukinumab 300 mg is given under the skin, first 1 to 7 days before checkpoint inhibitor treatment resumes, then weekly for the first 4 weeks and every 4 weeks after that. The main goal is to measure safety and feasibility; the study is Phase 1.
NCT07237594.summary_es: Este estudio evalúa secukinumab, un anticuerpo que bloquea la IL-17A, en personas con melanoma metastásico que tuvieron un efecto secundario relacionado con la inmunidad por una terapia con inhibidores de puntos de control inmunitario y que están reiniciando esa terapia. El secukinumab de 300 mg se aplica debajo de la piel, primero de 1 a 7 días antes de reanudar el tratamiento con inhibidores de puntos de control, luego cada semana durante las primeras 4 semanas y después cada 4 semanas. El objetivo principal es medir la seguridad y la factibilidad; el estudio es de Fase 1.
who_for: Advanced metastatic melanoma confirmed by tissue examination.
Age 18 years or older.
Prior immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy with grade 2 or higher colitis, hepatitis, or skin rash that led to interruption, stop, or steroid use.
Planned by the treating physician to restart the same therapy or add a second checkpoint inhibitor.
Adequate blood counts, platelets, hemoglobin, and liver enzyme levels.
not_for: Uveal melanoma.
Pregnant or breastfeeding.
Symptomatic brain metastases or carcinomatous meningitis.
Past or current non-infectious pneumonitis that needed steroids.
Active autoimmune disease needing systemic therapy in the past 12 months (checkpoint inhibitor side effects excepted).

NCT06517888.summary_en: This Phase 1/2 trial is testing AAVAnc80-antiVEGF, a gene therapy, in adults with unilateral vestibular schwannoma. Each participant gets one dose into the inner ear of the study ear, using the Akouos Delivery Device, at one of three dose levels. The trial measures safety and tolerability, and it also evaluates how well the delivery device works.
NCT06517888.summary_es: Este ensayo de fase 1/2 evalúa AAVAnc80-antiVEGF, una terapia génica, en adultos con schwannoma vestibular en un solo oído. Cada participante recibe una sola dosis en el oído del estudio, usando el Akouos Delivery Device, en uno de tres niveles de dosis. El ensayo mide la seguridad y la tolerabilidad, y también evalúa qué tan bien funciona el dispositivo de administración.
who_for: Unilateral, progressive vestibular schwannoma in one ear
Vestibular schwannoma larger than 2 mm
Profound hearing loss in the affected ear
Age 18 years or older
Able and willing to follow trial requirements, including a separate long-term follow-up study
not_for: Prior diagnosis of NF2 or bilateral vestibular schwannoma
Prior surgery or radiation therapy for vestibular schwannoma
History consistent with endolymphatic hydrops in the affected ear
Profound hearing loss in the unaffected ear
Investigational drug trial within six months before Day 0, or any prior gene therapy trial

NCT07723703.summary_en: The study tests AMX-883 alone, and in combination with posaconazole, in adults with acute myeloid leukaemia or high-risk myelodysplastic syndrome. AMX-883 is taken by mouth; how long or how often it is given is not stated. The study measures safety, how the drug moves through the body (pharmacokinetics), and early signs of effect (preliminary efficacy); it is a Phase 1 study.
NCT07723703.summary_es: El estudio prueba AMX-883 solo, y en combinación con posaconazol, en adultos con leucemia mieloide aguda o síndrome mielodisplásico de alto riesgo. AMX-883 se toma por vía oral; no se indica cuánto tiempo ni con qué frecuencia se administra. El estudio mide la seguridad, cómo se mueve el medicamento en el cuerpo (farmacocinética) y los primeros signos de efecto (eficacia preliminar); es un estudio de Fase 1.
who_for: Relapsed or refractory AML that failed all available standard therapies, or relapsed or refractory high-risk MDS with 10-19% bone marrow blasts.
ECOG performance status of 0 to 2.
Adequate washout from prior therapies and adequate kidney and liver function.
Adults 18 years or older.
Women who could become pregnant and men must use contraception for at least 120 days after the last dose.
not_for: Acute promyelocytic leukaemia, or chronic myelogenous leukaemia in blast crisis.
Clinically active leukaemia in the central nervous system.
Immunosuppressive therapy after stem cell transplant, or active graft versus host disease above grade 1.
Another active cancer, or cancer needing systemic treatment in the past 2 years.
Long QT syndrome, or family history of long QT or sudden cardiac death before age 40.

NCT05546827.summary_en: This Phase 2 study tests radiation therapy given after starting immunotherapy, before surgery, for sinonasal or anorectal mucosal melanoma. Patients receive combination immunotherapy, such as ipilimumab and nivolumab or nivolumab and relatlimab, followed by radiation therapy in 5, 15 or 20 fractions depending on the group, and then surgery or biopsy. The record does not state a main outcome measure; its stated goal is to learn whether this approach helps patients have better outcomes.
NCT05546827.summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 evalúa la radioterapia administrada después de iniciar la inmunoterapia, y antes de la cirugía, para el melanoma de mucosa sinonasal o anorrectal. Los pacientes reciben inmunoterapia combinada, como ipilimumab y nivolumab o nivolumab y relatlimab, seguida de radioterapia en 5, 15 o 20 fracciones según el grupo, y luego cirugía o biopsia. El registro no indica una medida de resultado principal; su objetivo declarado es saber si este enfoque ayuda a que los pacientes tengan mejores resultados.
who_for: Melanoma of the nasal cavity, sinuses, or anorectal canal, confirmed by biopsy or cytology
Mucosal tumor seen on clinical exam or imaging
No evidence of distant metastasis
Planned for combination immunotherapy such as ipilimumab and nivolumab
Age 18 or older, with ECOG performance status 3 or less
not_for: Previous radiation therapy to the planned target area
Metastatic disease
Pregnant women
Under 18 years of age
Unwilling to use adequate contraception during the study

NCT07032727.summary_en: This study tests combinations of olutasidenib with other drugs, such as cladribine, cytarabine, venetoclax, gilteritinib, or ruxolitinib, in adults with relapsed or refractory IDH1-mutated myeloid malignancies that have a co-signaling mutation. Olutasidenib is taken by mouth, and the other drugs are given by mouth, by IV, or under the skin, depending on the arm; how long or how often is not stated. The study measures safety and tolerability, and this is a Phase 2 trial.
NCT07032727.summary_es: Este estudio prueba combinaciones de olutasidenib con otros medicamentos, como cladribina, citarabina, venetoclax, gilteritinib o ruxolitinib, en adultos con neoplasias mieloides recaídas o refractarias con mutación IDH1 que tienen una mutación de señalización asociada. Olutasidenib se toma por vía oral, y los otros medicamentos se administran por vía oral, intravenosa o subcutánea, según el grupo; la duración o la frecuencia no están indicadas. El estudio mide la seguridad y la tolerabilidad, y es un ensayo de fase 2.
who_for: Adults 18 or older with relapsed or refractory AML, or high-risk MDS, MPN, or MDS/MPN with at least 10% blasts.
Documented IDH1 mutation.
Documented co-signaling mutation in genes such as KRAS, NRAS, PTPN11, FLT3, KIT, JAK2, or CALR.
ECOG performance status of 2 or lower.
Adequate kidney and liver function, and able to sign informed consent.
not_for: Prior treatment with olutasidenib.
Acute promyelocytic leukemia or translocation t(15;17).
Active, uncontrolled leukemia in the central nervous system.
New York Heart Association class III or IV heart condition.
White blood cell count above 25 x 10^9/L, or pregnancy, breastfeeding, or no adequate contraception.
